body:
This fixes the verified run-lifecycle defects on santos/dev2.

- santos/dev2 525b77fde is merged in with a real merge; nothing was rebased.
- The base's `launchWaits` fix in `internal/run` is unchanged.
- Every test named below was written first and failed on the old base 3f46952d4 before its fix.

## What changed, per finding

**1 (blocker): a new request adopted a stale run.**
The old behaviour had two parts:
- `run.Start` wrote the brief only onto an empty root.
- Only a person's stop wrote an ending on the root.

So the next `/task` or `codeaf do` over the same store silently ran the old brief under the new number. Now:
- `plandb.Store.EndRoot` fails the root and cancels what was still open.
- `run.Start` calls it on every ending except these: done, cannot-run, and a context its caller cut. A deadline counts as the limit.
- `Start` refuses a root that already carries a different brief.
- `openBeltRunStore` and `OpenRunPlan` never adopt a store. A store left open is set aside next to the new one as `plandb.db.N`, and its open work is ended as `interrupted`.
- `ContinueRun` carries on only its own root.

Tests:
- TestANewHandOffNeverAdoptsARunNothingIsDriving
- TestEveryRunEndingWritesTheRootsEnding
- TestOpenRunPlanSetsAsideARunLeftOpen
- TestStartDoesNotRunARootThatCarriesAnotherBrief
- TestStartWritesTheRootsEndingWhenALimitEndsTheRun
- TestStartWritesTheRootsEndingWhenTheRootWorkerFails
- TestStartLeavesARunItsCallerCutOpen is a guard and passes on both trees.
- TestEndRootFailsTheRunAndCancelsWhatWasStillOpen covers the new store call.

**5: the dollar limit did not stop peers.**
A worker's final receipt could reach the limit, mark it, and end nothing. Both roads to the limit now go through `reachCostLimit`, which cancels every worker in flight.
Test: TestAReceiptThatReachesTheDollarLimitEndsThePeers.

**6: a hand-off could join a run that had finished.**
A hand-off that arrives while a run is ending, closing or landing now waits for that run to be released, then starts a run of its own.
Test: TestAHandOffDuringARunsLandingStartsAFreshRun.

**7: closing the conversation still landed the work and marked the row failed.**
A run cut because the conversation closed now lands nothing, settles nothing, and writes nothing on its record.
Test: TestClosingTheConversationLandsNothingAndSettlesNothing.

**8: steering was accepted on a finished run.**
A note, pause, amend or priority on a task whose run has ended now answers `that task's run has ended`.
Test: TestASteerOnAFinishedRunIsRefused.

**S3: a part stopped with `x` read `incomplete`.**
`PlanCancel` now cancels with the stop word. The part reads `stopped`, and so does everything the stop took down with it.
Test: TestAPartStoppedFromItsPageReadsStopped.

**9: an interrupted run showed a needs-you mark that nothing could clear.**
It now raises no mark and asks nothing. Home draws the stuck mark for it. It keeps its line: `nothing is driving it; everything it did is kept`.
Test: TestAnInterruptedRowRaisesNoMarkNothingCanAnswer.

**10: joined rows came back after a restart with a false reason.**
They said the working copy was never written down. Only a run's own row can say that now, because a joined row shares its run's copy.
Test: TestAJoinedRowComesBackInterruptedWithoutAFalseSentence.

**13: a review that failed to seat could still end the run `done`.**
When a review could not be seated, the run now answers incomplete, even if its root wrote done. The root's own row in the store still reads done.
Test: TestARootThatWroteDoneStillEndsIncompleteWhenItsReviewCouldNotBeSeated.

**15: notes were handed back twice.**
- A worker is no longer handed its own note.
- A worker launched again on the same task is not handed notes the task already had.
- The task's trajectory records which notes it has had.

Tests:
- TestAWorkerIsNotHandedItsOwnNote
- TestAWorkerLaunchedAgainIsNotHandedNotesItsTaskAlreadyHad

The manual is updated to match: worker-harness, how-tasks-run and adaptive-runs. One wording fix after the merge keeps the probe "how do I pick which folder my next conversation opens in" reaching `home`. The change entry is in `docs/changes/unreleased/`.

Not changed here, because the `codeaf do` door belongs to another lane: an interrupted `codeaf do` still leaves its root open. The next request sets that run aside as `interrupted`.

## Evidence

All runs were on the remote build box, in a fresh snapshot of each revision, and every `go test` used `-count=1`.

RED, on 3f46952d4 plus the new tests:
- All 17 new tests fail for the reason they name.
- The one guard test passes, by design.

GREEN, before the merge:
- `internal/run` and `internal/plandb` pass.
- build, vet and gofmt are clean for run, session, plandb and tui3.

Full `make check TEST_FLAGS="-count=1"` on 888911c05, the merged head: **EXIT 0**.

The two earlier full runs on 888911c05 each failed on a different timing red. The box's load average was about 50. Each red was repeated on 525b77fde and on 888911c05:
- `internal/run` TestNotesBeyondTheBoundWaitForTheNextBoundary and TestANoteIsHandedToAWorkerOnceAndTheScreenStillReadsIt: under load (GOMAXPROCS=1, both trees at once), 4 failures in 400 runs on the base and 6 in 400 on the head. It is the same `stopped at its step cap` failure on both, so it is a load race in the note channel that predates this change.
- `internal/session` TestAChildLandingAfterItsParentSettledReachesTheConversation: 1 failure in 40 runs on the base and 0 in 40 on the head.
- `internal/session` TestARunStartedWithACapStopsAndAsksAtThatCap: a temp-dir cleanup race on the orchestrate road, which this change does not touch. 0 failures in 300 runs on either tree.
- `internal/provider` TestAWireBelowItsPaceWithNothingToSpendSaysSoAndIsSpent: 0 failures in 40 runs on either tree.
- `internal/lane` TestS3ItComesBack and `internal/provider` TestALaterAcceptedStreamCutOutranksThePrimaryRoutingRefusal each failed once, in packages this change does not touch. Neither was repeated.
title: run, session: a run's ending is written where the next request reads it

body:
Brings `santos/dev2` onto `dev`. dev is already merged in with a real merge commit, so this is a fast-forward: dev has nothing that dev2 lacks.

**Status: draft.** The review fixes listed under "Still landing" are going into dev2 now. This PR follows them automatically and goes ready when they are in.

## What this brings

**1. The worker harness, now the default.** A task runs on a bash belt: one loop under both `/task` and `codeaf do`, with a checking seat for the belt check. `CODEAF_TASK_BELT=node` (or `legacy`, or `off`) is the way back to the older node belt. See #1109 waves 1, 2, 6 and 7, and #1335, #1340, #1355, #1207.

**2. Runs as first-class work.**
- A run's life is the conversation's.
- It works in its own copy, and the copy is written down so it can be found again.
- Dollar and time limits end it by one road, and the ending names the limit that caused it.
- A run's dollars reach the conversation's total.
- Work that nothing is driving reads as interrupted, not failed, and can be carried on.
- A stopped task reads stopped everywhere.

About 50 entries, from #1204 through #1305.

**3. Skills, first design (to be replaced).** A memory-backed shelf, `use_skill`, per-message automatic choice, a `/skill` picker that attaches a skill, and a report of which skills a turn used (#1327, #1345–#1348, #1380). This follows the first design in #1277. #1409 builds the settled plan on dev and replaces these pieces after this lands; see the note on #1409.

**4. The chat as manager over the plan store.** The chat role. The chat sees the plan when the person speaks, and notes are a channel into a running worker. See #1205, #1354, #1356 and #1357.

**5. Task page, rail and step rows.** The page and rail door. Step rows are cut from the commands as they ran, step numbers continue across a wake, and a call that did not run has no row. See #1231, #1257, #1260 and #1261.

**6. Pickers.** One fuzzy matcher for every picker, match highlighting, and the caret parks where you type (#1321).

**7. Benchmarks and docs.** The footprint benchmark and its method, resume cost (#1126, #1317), and ADHD-shaped answers (#1209).

**8. Hardening.**
- Heavy-suite locks as kernel file locks (#1264, #1270, #1284, #1324).
- Goroutine ownership at close (#1259, #1267, #1274, #1276).
- Unread and retired profile keys (#1223, #1245).
- The CI gate on this branch (#1362).

## Behaviour that changes on merge

- **Tasks run on the bash belt by default.** Before, `CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash` opted in. Now `node`, `legacy` or `off` opts out.
- `task.parallel` = 0 means no limit on both doors.

## Review

Every feature group above had a feature-level review against its change entry. The findings are being fixed in their own PRs into dev2, each with tests shown failing first and a full `make check` on the merged head.

Already in:
- #1411: run lifecycle (10 findings). A new request never adopts an earlier run, every ending is written on the root, the dollar limit ends peers, close lands nothing, steers on ended runs are refused, interrupted rows are honest.
- #1393: chat manager (9 findings). The digest leads with the live run in the rail's words, `say` and `forward` reach run rows, a key that is read is no longer reported unread, and `Assisted-by` follows `/model`.
- #1395: task page keys, the tab mark, pool judge sweep claims, unowned catalog warms, manual gaps (12 findings).
- The dev merge: a parked parent could wake before its child's review check was seated. Fixed in `internal/run`, 100 stress runs green.

Still landing:
- **`codeaf do`.** It must never commit work it did not make. Spend stays bounded unless the person says otherwise. Project `*.lock` files land.
- **Retry loop.** A server that keeps cutting its answer short is waited on, not re-asked in a tight loop. "One machine" applies only when routing is actually off.
- **Attribution.** Always on: every commit codeaf writes carries `Assisted-by: CodeAF (<model>)` then `Co-Authored-By`. The model is shown as its bare name, with no provider prefix, and it is the one part a person can turn off.

## Evidence

- The merge of dev into dev2 at `525b77fde`: full `make check` EXIT 0, including the Windows cross-builds. Nothing is on the known-red list.
- #1395 at `635c029c6`, #1393 at `449e7921c`, #1411 at `888911c05`: full `make check` EXIT 0 each. CI green on each.
title: santos/dev2 lands on dev: the worker harness as default, runs as work, skills from other harnesses, the chat as manager

body:
Fixes #1383 and #1391.

## What was wrong

- **#1383.** A Codex model had no context window anywhere. The account listing gives every model `context_window: 272000`, and both readers of it dropped the field. A conversation that moved onto `codex/<slug>` kept its previous model's window on the status line and for compaction. On the default engine road there was a second cause: the session asked the catalog of the service it *started* on for a switched-to model's window. The engine ignores the window the surface sends, so nothing else ever set it.
- **#1391.** A Codex call row in the transcript named no endpoint, because the ChatGPT backend names no server.

## What changes

- **The window at the source (`codexauth`, `config`).**
  - Each model keeps the listing's `context_window`, and the fallback rows carry one named constant for the same observation.
  - `ConnectCodex` remembers every row's window, and `CodexRememberedModels` is the one door to that catalog.
  - A row remembered by an earlier build has no window. It takes the fallback's figure for the four ids the fallback names, and any other id stays unknown.
- **The window where it is read (`cmd/codeaf`, `tui3`).**
  - The session's switch lookup asks the process shelf first. The shelf takes a model to its own service's rows, never waits, and takes only its own lock, because it runs under the session's lock. The conversation's catalog answers when the shelf cannot, as before.
  - The start window asks the conversation's own catalog first, as the base did, and the shelf answers what that catalog cannot. Codex publishes no listing, so a Codex conversation's catalog is empty, and a row remembered by an older build is healed only on the shelf. A direct service's catalog refreshes on its own clock while the shelf holds the surface's older copy, so the catalog is the fresher answer wherever it has one.
  - A Codex compartment is re-read whenever the profile is, so a reconnect reaches a running engine.
  - The programs a conversation runs, the generalist and every leaf, get the same start window.
  - The surface keeps the Codex rows with their windows after a sign-in and caches them. On open, its Codex list is brought back into step with the catalog whenever the two differ.
- **The endpoint (`modelsource`, `session`).** The Codex service row declares `ServedAs: "Codex"`, and the session writes that name into a call row when the answer named no machine.
  - This differs from the issue's proposal, which was to put `provider: "Codex"` on every answer. A named answer is evidence in `internal/provider`: it records a lane rating, can strike that lane, and can clear a router-account exclusion. It is also drawn as `via codex` on the live phase line and on task rows. None of that is true of a service that is its own one machine.
  - The first cut of this PR did name the answer, and the adversarial review caught those effects. Codex answers stay unnamed, and a test holds them so.
- **The model warm writes only the router's list.** `warmModels` was handed the catalog the conversation started on. Once a Codex sign-in saves `codex/gpt-5.5` as the chat model, every launch starts there, so both roads overwrote the OpenRouter model list with bare Codex ids. The unfixed build writes `{"models":[{"id":"gpt-5.5"},{"id":"gpt-5.6-sol"}]}`. The warm now always warms the process's own default catalog.
- **Manual.** The Codex section states the window, what a `--host` screen shows instead, and the call rows' endpoint. The call-lines section says why. Two new probes reach those sections.

## Validation contract → tests

| Contract | Test |
| --- | --- |
| The listing keeps each model's window, and both readers save it | `codexauth` `TestW1…` ×2 |
| Fallback rows carry the observed figure | `TestW2EveryFallbackRowCarriesTheObservedWindow` |
| A connection remembers every window, from the listing or the fallback | `config` `TestW3ConnectCodexRemembersEachModelsWindow` |
| A switch asks the new model's own service, and a suffixed id works too | `cmd/codeaf` `TestW4ASwitchAsksTheModelsOwnServiceForItsWindow` |
| A conversation and its programs start on Codex at 272k | `TestW5AConversationThatOpensOnCodex…`, `TestW5ACodexConversationsProgramsAreSizedFromItsWindow` |
| A pre-change profile heals, and a same-address reconnect is re-read | `TestW6A…` ×2 in `cmd/codeaf`, `TestW6A…` ×2 in `tui3`, the latter including a later true 400k replacing the healed 272k, and no rewrite when in step |
| The no-services path is unchanged | `TestW7AShelfWithNoServicesAnswersFromTheLaunchCatalog` |
| A surface with no shelf, the engine road's, switches with the window | `tui3` `TestW4ASurfaceWithNoShelf…` |
| The warm writes only the router's list | `TestAWarmForAConversationOnCodexWritesOnlyTheRoutersList` |
| Codex call rows name Codex, and no lane news or ledger sighting for Codex | `session` `TestE2…`, with a real agent, provider client and Codex transport |
| A router still writes and tells `Alibaba`, and a silent answer writes no key | `TestE3ARouterStill…` |
| A direct service that declared no name writes no key | `TestE3ADirectServiceThatDeclaredNoNameWritesNoEndpoint` |
| No Codex answer carries a server name, in any shape | `codexauth` `TestE4TheTransportPutsNoServerNameOnACodexAnswer` |
| A direct service's own catalog sizes the conversation it opens, over the shelf's older copy; the shelf answers only when the catalog cannot | `TestW8ADirectServicesOwnCatalogSizesTheConversationItOpens` |

## Manual verification

- **Fixture drive of the built binary.** It runs a fake Codex issuer and backend plus a fake OpenAI-compatible router, and all 19 checks pass on the final head.
  - On the default engine road, `/connect` → Codex → sign-in, then a turn on `codex/gpt-5.5`, gives a status line of `5.4k/272k · 2%` and a call row with `"endpoint":"Codex"`.
  - Headless turns on both roads write only `Codex` rows.
  - The router's model list stays free of Codex ids.
  - The router control writes `Alibaba`, a silent answer writes no key, and a router model shows `1M`.
  - In-process, the status line reads `272k`.
  - A profile connected by the unfixed build reads `272k` without reconnecting.
  - No screen draws `via codex` or `(codex)`.
  - Against the unfixed build, the same drive fails on the window, the endpoint and the model list.
- **The real ChatGPT backend**, in a throwaway home with no browser sign-in:
  - The unfixed build remembered no windows, drew no window figure, and wrote every call row without an endpoint.
  - On this branch the real listing's `272000` is remembered for all four models, and the picker shows `codex/gpt-5.5 272k`.
  - A real turn on the default road gives a status line and `/status` context of `11.9k/272k · 4%`.
  - Three real turns, from the screen, headless on the default road, and `--no-host`, all write `"endpoint":"Codex"` rows.

## Independent verification

A second, independent pass drove the built binary at `573a74a57` against the base `b378e9275`. It used its own drive and assertions, and reran on fakes it had first checked against the transport. It passed 14 of 14 checks:

- **Window, fixture.** On the default engine road and `--no-host`, a Codex turn shows `5.4k/272k · 2%` on the status line and in `/status`. The base keeps the boot model's `5.4k/1M · 1%`.
- **Router controls.** Switching back to router models shows `200k` and `1M`.
- **Picker.** It lists `codex/gpt-5.5 272k`.
- **Compaction fires from 272k.** On the engine road, a conversation booted on a 1M model moves to Codex, and the fake backend reports 240k input. This build writes a compaction record (`~240k → ~5k tokens`), and the next request falls from 948 KB to 58 KB. The base does not compact.
- **Old profile.** A profile connected by the base reads `272k` on both roads without reconnecting. After a listing of `400000`, it reads `400k`.
- **Router list.** It stays free of bare Codex ids on both roads. The base writes them.
- **Call rows.** Every Codex turn row names `"endpoint":"Codex"`: TUI on the engine road, TUI with `--no-host`, and headless on both roads. The base writes no key. The router controls write `Alibaba`, and a silent answer writes no key.
- **No `via codex`.** No frame draws it, including frames captured while a Codex answer was still streaming.
- **Real ChatGPT backend.** The live listing's `272000` is remembered for all four models. A real turn reads `11.7k/272k · 4%`. Real headless turns on both roads write `"endpoint":"Codex"`, and the base's row has no endpoint.

The same pass's code review led to the two follow-up commits:

- The start window asks the conversation's own catalog first. It had asked the shelf first, which let a direct service's older surface cache outrank that service's fresher catalog.
- The manual now says what the `--host` meter shows for a Codex model.

## Not in this PR (found by the review, outside both issues' acceptance)

- `codeaf exec`, `run`, the saved-harness runner and the v1 planner still ask the default catalog about a `codex/<slug>` id, so they size from the conservative default.
- Over `--host`, the laptop's meter reads the laptop's own list. When that list has no Codex rows, a switch onto a Codex model keeps the previous model's figure. The far machine compacts correctly, and the manual now says what the meter shows.
- Two journals besides the transcript still name no endpoint for a Codex call: a task's flight rows and a saved harness's headless entry. Neither is a transcript `call` row.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: chat: a Codex model carries its 272k window, and a Codex call row names Codex as its endpoint

body:
## What

Pasting a large document into the box froze the surface. `pastedWords` asked `windowsBackslashWord` about every word by converting **the whole remaining paste** to a string and lowercasing it. A 4,000-line paste (a stack trace, a log, about 180KB and 16,000 words) made about 16,000 copies of up to 180KB each: quadratic, about twenty seconds of CPU on the surface's own goroutine. `TestALargePasteIsOneEditAndNoLayout` measured it as 21s, 6% of the whole tui3 suite. Its CPU profile was 47% `slicerunetostring`, 32% `encoderune`, 17% `strings.ToLower`, all under `app.paste`.

The question now reads at most the sixteen runes it can recognise (`X:\` needs three, `\\wsl.localhost\` sixteen). The rest of the paste path was audited for the same shape: readings are bounded at four, a failed reading stops at its first failed stat, and every other scan is one pass.

## Proof

- **The old splitter's exact output is pinned** as literals, recorded from the old code before the change: plain lines, drive paths, both WSL UNC hosts, single and double quotes with spaces, backslash escapes, mixed lines, and the full 4,000-line trace.
- **A law in PERF.md holds the path linear by bytes allocated**: a 4,000-line paste may allocate at most 10x the bytes of a 1,000-line one. It counts bytes on purpose: the regression was one allocation per word, so an allocation count grows fourfold for the quadratic parser too, and a count-based version of this law passed against it. Mutation-tested: the fixed parser measures 5.1x, the exact old code 15.3x (red), and a worse variant 15.5x (red).
- `TestALargePasteIsOneEditAndNoLayout` keeps every assertion and falls from 21s to 0.01s.
- `make pr-ready` green (touched `./internal/tui3`, the whole package serial with `-count=1`, 317s against 337s before).

Part of the test-speed wave with #1394, #1397 and #1398.

body:
## What

`internal/tui3` (4,804 tests) and `internal/session` (3,681) are serial by construction: the tui3 harness clock is a plain global, so no test can call `t.Parallel()`. `go test` therefore runs each package's thousands of tests one after another. The same compiled test binary run as concurrent processes over disjoint name lists is green and far faster, because the suites mostly wait rather than compute.

`scripts/shard-test.sh` compiles a heavy package once, lists its top-level tests, runs `SHARDS` processes of the binary over round-robin slices of the sorted list, and then:

- verifies every listed test ran exactly once, and fails naming the missing ones otherwise;
- prints a failing shard's whole output and ends with every failing test's name, while the other shards still finish;
- folds the shards into one `test2json` stream for `make test-report`: each test once, the package once;
- refuses a go-test flag it cannot honour (profiles, `-bench`, `-list`, …) instead of dropping it.

It is written for the bash 3.2 and BSD `sed` a Mac ships as well as GNU.

`make test` sends each heavy package there under the one-suite lock and keeps every other package on the unchanged `go test` road, so the pull-request `touched` job and the three `full tests` shards in `ci-full.yml` get it with no workflow change. `SHARDS` defaults to min(8, CPUs); `SHARDS=1` is the old serial run, kept for bisecting a shard-only failure. A `./...` run still holds the lock for the rest of the tree too, so two sessions' tree runs still cannot stack. `TEST_TIMEOUT` stays 15m, now per shard.

`make pr-ready` runs the two shell acceptance scripts (`one-suite_test.sh`, new `shard-test_test.sh`) when a change touches `scripts/` or the Makefile; they take about forty seconds together, so they are touched-only like the Go packages. `one-suite_test.sh` skips its namespace arms where `bwrap` is not installed instead of blocking forever on a holder that cannot start.

## Measured on an 8-core box (dev as of this branch)

| | serial | 8 shards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `internal/tui3` run phase | 341s | 63s |
| `internal/session` run phase | 253s on CI | 106s |
| `make test-report PKGS=./internal/tui3` | | 4,804 tests once, 1 package, 0 failed |

These combine with #1397 (the tui3 harness stops waiting out waiters that cannot answer, 341s to 82s serial); once both are in, most of what is left is compile and real work.

## Proof

- `scripts/shard-test_test.sh` against a fixture module of its own (`scripts/testdata/shardfixture`, never swept by `./...`): every test once over three shards; a failing test surfaces by name and the other shards finish; `SHARDS=1` and `SHARDS=3` agree; a `-timeout` panic names the running test; the folded report equals the serial report; an unknown flag is refused by name.
- `make test PKGS=./internal/tui3`, `make test PKGS=./internal/session` and `make test-report PKGS=./internal/tui3` green; `make pr-ready` green.
- This PR changes no Go file, so its own `touched packages` job runs nothing. The first CI run of the sharded road is the next pull request that touches either heavy package.

## On a two-core runner

Emulated locally with `taskset -c 0,1` (so `SHARDS` resolves to 2) and the touched job's exact line, `make test TEST_FLAGS='-count=1 -p 1' PKGS='./internal/manual ./internal/tui3 ./internal/session'`:

- `internal/tui3`: 2 shards, 195s, green (the touched job measured 337s serial).
- `internal/session`: one shard failed `TestARecallThatLandsBeforeTheFirstWordIsAskedAgainWithIt`. That is a **pre-existing ordering race in the test, not in sharding**: the unmodified binary, run alone on two CPUs, fails it 2 in 40 (4 in 40 on busy cores). Sharding puts two session processes on two cores, which is exactly the load that exposes it. The fix is its own pull request (linked below) and should land before this one.

body:
## What

81% of the `internal/tui3` suite was the test harness waiting out its 150ms waiter budget, not doing work. A full profiled run (`CODEAF_TUI3_CMDPROFILE`) on 2026-09-22 answered 23,507 commands in 1.33s combined and dropped 1,937 at a cost of 288.7s. 934 of the 4,787 tests sat on exact multiples of 150ms.

#463 established that a shorter budget is a bet on the scheduler, so **`cmdBudget` is untouched**. Instead a synchronous fake may now register the exact channels a waiter family parks on and report, on the test goroutine, whether they are open, empty, and without a writer goroutine. Only then is the waiter not started. Everything else keeps today's road:

- a queued value or a close still runs the command and is delivered;
- an owner that does not register, and any family it does not name, keeps the full overlapped budget;
- `watchDriving` / `watchFollowing` (they call test-supplied functions) and the product-written `waitRing` / `waitWake` / `waitStir` are never registered.

`fakeAgent` registers `waitEvent`, `taskFake` adds `waitTask`, and `roomFake` adds `waitRoom` and `waitPilot`. Every surface site that builds one of those waiters assigns the same channel to the app field the harness reads just before it returns the command; the one way they can differ is a waiter for a room or pilot that has since been replaced, whose stale generation means its message would be ignored anyway.

A second commit routes the last two direct `tea.Tick` calls (the pulse beat and the task-pane debounce) through `surfaceTick`. Production still gets bubbletea's tick; the test clock declines them as it already declines every poll at or above the tick budget.

## Measured on an 8-core box

| full serial `internal/tui3` | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| commands answered | 23,507 | 23,509 |
| wall charged to dropped waiters | 288.7s | 11.0s |
| profiled serial wall | 327s | 74s |
| `make test PKGS=./internal/tui3` inside `pr-ready` | 341s | 82s |
| goroutines still parked at the end | 2,238 | 754 |

The answered count is unchanged, so no delivery was lost: the seam removed only waits that could never have answered.

## Proof

- Three new tests assert the seam by the driver's own accounting, never by elapsed time: an empty registered waiter costs zero deadline waits; a registered waiter with a queued event still delivers it and is counted answered; an unregistered waiter is charged the full budget.
- `TestTheHarnessDeliversACommandThatAnsweredHowLongItTook`, `TestTheHarnessStillGivesUpOnTheWaitersItNames` and the two table laws pass unchanged.
- `make pr-ready` green on this branch (touched `./internal/tui3`, the whole package serial with `-count=1`).

Part of the test-speed wave: #1394 takes the relay dead dial out of the laws run; companion PRs shard the heavy suites and make a large paste linear.

body:
Skills installed for Claude Code and Codex now reach codeaf directly, with memory on or off, and the model picks the one a request fits by what the skill is for.

## What changed

- **Claude Code plugin skills are read**, the way Claude Code decides what is live: the plugin is named in `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, `enabledPlugins` says true in the layered settings (home, project, project local), and a project-scoped install counts only in its own project. A plugin reads the skill folders its manifest or its marketplace catalog entry names, and only those; a plugin that names none is read from `skills/`. The plugins folder is never walked, so marketplace clones and older cached versions are left alone. A plugin skill keeps its bare folder name, ranks below every hand-kept skill and above Codex's bundled ones; the decision is written up in `internal/skills/plugins.go`.
- **Codex's bundled skills** in `.codex/skills/.system` are read, below everything else in their scope.
- **Linked skill folders** are followed, which is how `npx skills` and similar installers reach every tool from one copy.
- **Memory off no longer turns skills off.** With `memory.enabled` off the process builds its shelf in a temporary store from the skill folders and removes it on close. Nothing is written to the memory store the person turned off. `use_skill`, the catalog and the per-message carry all work. The #1380 "switched off" line is gone.
- **The catalog lists every skill, by what it is for.** It is in the stable prefix in a fixed order: scope match first, then by name. The recency ordering is gone so the order cannot move between requests. Descriptions are clipped to 160 characters, and the described lines stop at 12 KiB. The names that did not fit follow on one line of up to 2 KiB, and anything past that is counted. The model opens the skill a request fits with `use_skill`. The word-match carry still runs first on every message.
- **The carried-skills line stays visible.** On the chat surface the line reads `skills · <names>`. Once the answer landed, the `▸ worked` chip swallowed it, and even an opened chip did not show it. It now stays under the message, with the chip starting below it.
- **The `/skill` picker and the attachment work on the ordinary launch.** The picker reads the conversation's own shelf. Attach, detach, list and clear cross the session-host connection (`remote.Agent` methods, `Welcome.Skills`, `serveSkills`), where they had been missing. `skillAttacher` leaves the surface-door ledger, and the ratchet is now 21 after the merge with the base's own removal.
- **The attachment is a fact and not a call.** `session.Facts.Skills` carries the attachment down unasked, and the engine announces it after every attach, detach or clear. The chip reads the replica, and the picker asks the shelf and the attachment doors off the update loop (the base's new off-loop laws).
- The shelf holds 400 skills (was 100).
- Manual: `skills-from-other-tools.md` (new), `use-skill.md`, `putting-a-skill-in-front.md`, `skills-a-turn-used.md`, `what-i-remember.md`; six new retrieval probes. Change entry `docs/changes/unreleased/1396-skills-from-other-tools.md`.

**Catalog cost:** each described line is `- name: description`, with the description clipped to 160 characters. That is about 120 to 230 bytes per skill, most often 150 to 180. It is paid once, in the cached prefix. The whole section is bounded at 12 KiB of described lines plus 2 KiB of names.

## Evidence (remote test box; every `go test` with `-count=1`)

- **Red first.** Each new unit test was run against the unfixed implementation with the new tests in place. skills: a compile red, then six assertion reds. resident: two assertion reds. session, tui3, remote and cmd/codeaf: compile reds. The plugin manifest test failed on the earlier discovery code. The carried-line test failed on the earlier feed and fold code.
- **End-to-end, the real binary in tmux, fresh home, both memory settings, on the head:** `TestTUIE2E/foreign_skills_reach_the_conversation` PASS for memory_on and memory_off. Three skills are installed: one in `.claude/skills`, one in `.codex/skills`, and one in an installed and enabled plugin. It asserts:
  - (a) automatic: `skills · tide-almanac` with `QUILLON-TIDE-7431`, then `skills · lantern-ledger` with `LANTERN-LEDGER-2958`;
  - (b) by hand: `/skill orchard` lists the plugin skill with no refusal, Enter attaches it, and a question sharing no words carries `skills · orchard-census` and answers with `ORCHARD-CENSUS-6612`;
  - (c) the transcript records `use_skill` with `"mode":"list"` and `"mode":"get"`.
- **Real installs in a fresh home.** Installed with `npx skills add` (one skill global for Claude Code, one project-level for Codex into `.agents/skills`), `claude plugin marketplace add` plus `claude plugin install example-skills@…` (Claude Code 2.1.278), `claude plugin init` (a skills-dir plugin), and a hand-written `~/.codex/skills` skill. `use_skill` list returned all 15 skills, memory off and memory on. The 12 plugin skills are exactly the set `claude plugin details` lists; the 7 other folders in the plugin's repository, which belong to other plugins, are not offered. A p5.js request opened the plugin's `algorithmic-art` skill, and a harbour-log request followed the Codex skill.
- **Relevance eval** (`TestSkillRelevanceEval`, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, 12 paraphrases sharing almost no words with their skill plus 4 needing no skill, two runs per arm, each request in its own folder). Before is the base build 3f46952d4:

| arm | paraphrases reaching their skill | requests left alone |
|---|---|---|
| before, memory on | 12/24 | 8/8 |
| before, memory off | 0/24 | 8/8 |
| after, memory on | 16/24 | 8/8 |
| after, memory off | 15/24 | 8/8 |

- **Gate on the head 2f87cbc2e.** Build, vet (untagged and e2e) and `make changelog-check` are clean, and the touched light packages (skills, resident, remote, manual, e2e, store, cmd/codeaf) pass.
  - Full `make check` exits 2 and is **not green**. It failed in `internal/run` (TestNotesBeyondTheBoundWaitForTheNextBoundary: step cap), `internal/session` (TestHandingAYourCallToTheModelAndItsResolveAreOneRoad) and `internal/telemetry` (two spool tests).
  - None of these packages' code paths is touched here, and none of these tests failed in the previous full run on this branch. They have not been confirmed against the base.
  - `internal/tui3` passes in that run, including the off-loop laws.

**On hold** since 2026-09-23: #1409 carries the approved skills design, so this branch stops here until Santosh decides.

## Not reached yet

- Claude Code's `disable-model-invocation` and `user-invocable` frontmatter are not honoured; every skill is offered both ways.
- A `SKILL.md` deeper than a direct child of a skills folder is not read. A skills-dir plugin with only a nested `skills/` folder is not read either.
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocation is not followed.
- With `CODEAF_HOME` set, the user-scope folders are read under that folder, not `$HOME`. That is by design (`home.Login`).
- The picker discovers from the local disk even over `--host` to another machine.
- Task workers with memory off do not get the shelf through the executor's own store path.

`TestARelayThatIsNotThereIsItsOwnFact` dials `http://127.0.0.1:1` through `Dial` and through `Register`, each with the 20-second `HandshakeWithin` dialer timeout. ## Per finding

**S4, the digest leaves out the live run (#1357).** `PlanTaskRow` gains `Archived`, set for rows read from an ended run's store, and the digest puts the live run's rows first (`planDigestOrder`). Labels are taken before the reorder, so `#2.1` numbering does not move. Each row's state now comes from `PlanTaskRow.StateWord()`, one mapping from the store's words to the side list's (queued, running, done, stopped, incomplete, your call), and the `tasks` listing and one-task reading use it too. `TestTheRowsWordIsTheRailsWord` parses internal/tui3's `planStateWord` and fails on any word the two map differently. It passes without comparing once tui3 calls `StateWord` itself. Test: `TestTheDigestLeadsWithTheLiveRunInTheRailsOwnWords`.

**S5, `say` and `forward` refuse a run row that exists (#1357).** On a row of the run, `say` is written as a note, and its answer opens "A row of the run takes `say` as a note, so your line went through `note`:". `forward` refuses, saying nothing the conversation holds moves what a run task is judged by, and points at `note` and `stop`. `say` alongside `continue` or `resolve` goes to the old reader, as before. Test: `TestSayAndForwardOnARowOfTheLiveRunAnswerForTheRow`.

**S6, the chat is pointed at a tool it does not have.** The `note` schema text and the note receipt no longer name `revise_assignment`. The schema text also got shorter. The receipt says nothing the conversation holds changes a run task's brief, and names `stop` plus a fresh hand-off. `docs/design/chat-coordination/DESIGN.md` gets dated corrections at the channel table, "Who may write", and change 4's "Today" and "steer". Covered by the S5 test's receipt and the existing note tests.

**S7, `lane.talk.borrow` reported unread.** Added to `nonSettingProfileFields` and the ledger. `TestProfileKeyLedgerLaw` no longer builds its writer set only from the consumed set. It drives every settings row's writer into an empty profile and requires each key that lands to be consumed or retired, and in the ledger. A row that refuses every sample value fails the law instead of being skipped. RED on the base named `lane.talk.borrow` and nothing else.

**S13, `Assisted-by` stale after `/model` (#1325).** `setModel` re-renders the page from the live model. `rerenderSystemLocked` (the clock refresh, anchoring, arming division) renders from the live model too. On the prefix cache: a cache belongs to one model, so the first request on a new model is cold whatever the page says. The re-render uses the page's existing clock stamp (`systemAt`), so the model id is the only thing that changes, and switching back gives the earlier model the exact page it already has cached. A page that names no model (attribution off) comes back identical and message[0] is not touched. Tests: `TestAssistedByFollowsTheModelAfterASwitch`, `TestASwitchBackRestoresThePageByteForByte`.

**M4, two send paths skip the digest.** `SubmitStanding` puts the digest before the standing instruction. `SubmitImage` adds it as its own leading text part, and a new `userMessage.lead` count keeps it out of the journal while the pictures stay. `userMessage.text()` now returns the person's sentence (`said`) when one is set. Before this, the digest was read back as the person's ask by recall, the owed answer and the ask `forward` carries. The vision fallback (a model that cannot see, answered by the vision model) still goes without it: that turn is not the manager reasoning. Tests: `TestAMarkedDraftOpensOnTheRunsRows`, `TestAMessageWithPicturesOpensOnTheRunsRows`.

**M5, the #1357 entry is false about parts.** It now says `stop` and `note` both reach an internal split part such as `#1.2`, by the label the listing and digest print.

**M6, the manual said a note arrives "between steps".** worker-harness.md now says the run looks for unread notes each time the worker finishes a step and hands them over through `Agent.Steer`. A reply being written is cut and asked again. A foreground command of 3s or more moves to the background as a job, and a younger one is let finish. The note schema text, the receipt and the refusal say the same thing.

**M9, #1209 dropped rules without saying so.** From the diff of 7b74ff5a9: the opener and closer bans are still there, and only their example lists were cut ("Sure", "Great question", "You're right", "Say the word and I'll…"). That was the byte trade and it stands. "never hand back half-solved work" was dropped outright, and nothing in the entry or commit says so, so I treated it as unintended and **restored** it: "never a compiling scaffold, a narrowed test or half-solved work". The same section paid for it, and the page ended 4 bytes lighter on both arms, so both waivers fall by 4. The 1209 entry was rolled into v0.4.0 on the new base, so the invalidation is recorded in this PR's entry. `prompt_belt_pages_test.go` had used "Say the word and I'll" as a sentinel only the chat page carries, and after #1209 it tested nothing. It now uses "no closing offer" and checks that each sentinel is still on the chat page.

body:
Fixes four defects a reviewer verified on santos/dev2 `3f46952d4`. Each got a test first. The test was shown red on the base, then green on this head.

## B1: the endless hot retry against one machine (#1358)

`internal/session/loop.go`: under `verdict.Retries()`, the cut branch did `attempt--; continue` before the wait and before the status line. `waitsForEver` fires only on a cut, so a watched one-machine server that kept cutting was asked again in a tight loop for ever. A cut now pays the verdict's wait: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, then 10s from then on. While it waits, the status line reads `no answer N times in Xm · still asking · esc stops`. A pool cut still asks for no wait and still moves on at once. The discard row for a cut is still said before the wait, and it is not said twice.

- Test: `TestAOneMachineThatKeepsCuttingIsWaitedOnAndSaysSo` (internal/session). It uses 40 cuts, then an answer. It checks 41 requests, 40 waits that are all positive and never shrink, a last wait of exactly 10s, and the status line.
- Manual: `internal/manual/chat/models-and-cost.md` has a new section, *My own server keeps going quiet*. The line that said the turn always ends when there is nowhere to go now names this exception.

## S2: the default router pool was called "one machine" (#1343)

`internal/provider/client.go`: `OneMachine` was `served == "" && askedFor(ctx) == ""`. `askedFor` is empty whenever no lane choice was drawn, which includes the router's default pool. `OneMachine` now needs positive evidence of a single machine. That means one of these:
- a pin to one lane, or
- a connected direct service, or
- a base with no router behind it, meaning it is not the shipped router and has never served an endpoints page.

A router's pool is never one machine, whatever the `routing` row says. The routing row steers the router; it does not remove it.

I did not use a literal `routing == off` test for this. `routing off` on the shipped router is still a pool, as `StreamCut.OneMachine`'s own doc says. A person's own server runs under the default `simple` row, so keying on `off` would have undone #1343 for exactly the people it was written for.

- Test: `TestOnlyARequestWithNoPoolIsCalledOneMachine` (internal/provider).

**S2 fed B1.** Here is the reviewer's case: `routing="simple" laneChoiceMade=false askedFor="" Rerouted=false OneMachine=true`. It reached the endless loop for any watched default pool user whose stream died before it named a server, once no fallback model was left. That covers `--one-model`, no chain resolving, and a chain already walked, because the last model in the chain has no fallback. Users who still had a fallback got four immediate asks instead of two, then a hop.

## B2: old checkouts could not see the dual suite lock (#1324)

The directory lock's `pid` named the suite (`go test …`), but an old `holder_alive` only accepts a pid whose command line contains `one-suite.sh`. There are three changes:
- The directory now names the lock HOLDER. The holder names itself when it starts, and its argv[0] carries `one-suite.sh`.
- `one-suite.sh` runs the wrapper with `exec -a "$0"`, so the claim window before the holder starts is covered too.
- `dropDirLock` removes a directory only while it still names the process dropping it, so it never again deletes another tree's `pid` and leaves `since` behind.

The old reader is kept at `scripts/testdata/pre-1264/one-suite.sh`. It is the pre-#1264 script with one change: it will only run against a private lock path.

- Test: shell arm `run_old_reader_sees_current_holder`, which runs the old reader against a live current holder, both before and after the holder names itself. Also Go tests `TestTheDirectoryNamesAHolderAnOldReaderAcceptsAsAlive` and `TestDroppingTheDirectoryLockLeavesSomebodyElsesAlone`.

## S1: a dead directory lock locked the box for ever (#1324)

The flock is the truth. The directory is judged only by a run that already holds the flock, and it is judged by the old checkout's own test. If its pid is not a live `one-suite.sh` process, it is dead. A dead directory is moved aside and claimed again, the same way the old script does it, so two readers cannot both delete it. A directory with no pid gets 500ms to name somebody before it is judged. A live old checkout still refuses the run.

- Tests: `TestADeadDirectoryLockIsTakenBackUnderTheFlock` and `TestALiveOldCheckoutStillHoldsTheDirectoryLock` (Go), and shell arm `run_dead_directory_lock_is_taken_back`. That arm SIGKILLs the holder it started, then checks that the next run goes ahead. `run_refused_by_directory` now uses a real old checkout as the live holder instead of a hand-written pid. `scripts/one-suite_test.sh ARM…` runs named arms alone.

## Found on the way: the one-machine wait wrapped to nothing after 35 asks

On the fixed head, the B1 test still counted **35 waits for 40 cuts**. The cause is in `taxonomy.waitFor`, which doubled with `base << (attempt-1)`. That signed shift overflows an int64 at the 35th ask and returns zero or a negative wait, which the turn loop reads as no wait. So the hot loop came back on the 36th ask even with the loop fix. The shift now saturates, and the one-machine wait holds at 10s for as long as the server stays quiet.

- Test: `TestTheWaitOnOneMachineNeverWrapsToNothing` (internal/taxonomy), asks 5 to 500. The old test stopped at 20, which is why it never saw this.

## Also

- `scripts/one-suite_test.sh`: `run_order` and `run_host_b_after_cell` now wait for the lock line before reading it, the same fix the merged base made to the Go test. On a loaded box `run_order host-first` read an empty line.
- Merged `origin/santos/dev2` (`525b77fde`) with a real merge and no conflicts. The base's re-read in `cmd/codeaf-suite-lock/main_test.go` is kept.

## Evidence (shared build box, fresh clones, every `go test` with `-count=1`)

**RED:** tests-only commit `afa11b8e0` on top of `3f46952d4`.
- `TestAOneMachineThatKeepsCuttingIsWaitedOnAndSaysSo`: FAIL, `waits = 0 ([]), want one in front of every ask after a cut`.
- `TestOnlyARequestWithNoPoolIsCalledOneMachine`: FAIL on two cases. The shipped router with no choice drawn gave `OneMachine = true, want false`. A pin to one lane gave `OneMachine = false, want true`.
- `TestADeadDirectoryLockIsTakenBackUnderTheFlock`: FAIL, `a dead directory lock (pid …) refused the next run`.
- `one-suite_test.sh run_old_reader_sees_current_holder`: FAIL, `the old reader (early pass) ran its suite beside a live current holder: STALE TREE RAN ITS SUITE BESIDE THE CURRENT ONE`.
- `one-suite_test.sh run_dead_directory_lock_is_taken_back`: FAIL, `a dead directory lock (holder …, killed) still refused the next run (status 1)`.
- The existing arms `run_both_locks` and `run_refused_by_directory` were ok on the base.
- On `d3ebe1a74` (the test for the wrap, before its fix), `TestTheWaitOnOneMachineNeverWrapsToNothing` failed with `ask 35 waits -351909h41m29.709551616s, want the 10s ceiling`. The B1 test gave `waits = 35`.

**GREEN:** head `e09755305`.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet` on the touched packages, and `gofmt -l` on the touched files: all clean.
- The six focused tests above pass. So do `TestALiveOldCheckoutStillHoldsTheDirectoryLock`, `TestTheDirectoryNamesAHolderAnOldReaderAcceptsAsAlive` and `TestDroppingTheDirectoryLockLeavesSomebodyElsesAlone`.
- `scripts/one-suite_test.sh` in full, three times in a row: `one-suite namespace and dual-lock acceptance: ok` each time.
- Touched packages: `./cmd/codeaf-suite-lock/ ./internal/provider/ ./internal/taxonomy/ ./internal/manual/` ok. `./internal/session/` ok (304s, through `scripts/one-suite.sh`).
- `make check`: **EXIT 0** (119 packages ok, 0 FAIL, build-cross done).

That EXIT 0 was the fourth `make check` on this head. The box's load average was around 30 to 40 all afternoon. Runs 1 to 3 each failed a different timing-sensitive test in a package this PR does not change, or in a test whose own message calls it a timeout:
- `internal/run` note-channel tests
- `internal/workspace` `TestEightyConcurrentAddsFromSeparateHandlesAllLand` (database busy)
- `internal/provider` `TestARacedArmIsFiledUnderTheOneNameTheLedgerKeys`
- `internal/session` `TestAgreementDoesNotBuyASecondCompletion` ("that is a TIMEOUT") and `TestANewDirectionArrivesWithTheClaimUnspent`

Each of these passes alone, repeated with `-count=3` or `-count=5`, on both this head and the base `525b77fde`.

## What was wrong

`/cost` (and every multi-row note) came out with its first row two cells right of the rest:

```
  · spend        $0.42
  tokens       48.1k in · 3.2k out
  model calls  14
  time         3m12s
```

THE INDENT LAW's pass in `deckRows` skipped any work row whose text already opened on two spaces, meant to keep the fold chip (which baked its own indent in) from moving twice. A note's continuation rows open on exactly two spaces — the lead under the first row's `· ` — so the pass mistook that lead for its own gutter, moved the first row and left the others.

## What changed

- The fold chip lays itself flush and takes its two cells from the pass like every other work row.
- The pass no longer looks at what a row begins with. Every work row moves, so a note's rows, an indented line inside a tool result and a list inside streaming prose all shift together.

```
  · spend        $0.42
    tokens       48.1k in · 3.2k out
    model calls  14
    time         3m12s
```

The `·` on the first row is the note's own marker, the dim lane every answer this surface writes on its own account opens with. It now sits in the gutter column with the table's columns intact under it.

## Proof

- `TestCostRowsKeepTheirColumnsUnderTheGutter` measures label and figure columns in cells across the drawn frame. It fails on the old pass and passes now.
- Focused `internal/tui3` run over folds, notes, harness cards, live steps, tool rows, captions and the gutter: green. `go test ./internal/e2e/` and `make test-laws`: green.

body:
One list of tips, two boxes, two rules. Home rotates through them; a conversation ranks them. All are eventually retired.

**Every tip retires eventually - even if not used - after 6 showings in rotation.**
Users also have the option to disable hints altogether:
```
settings > workspace > disable hints
```

1. `rm ~/.codeaf/notices.json` — wipes your ledger so every tip is new again
2. Launch `bin/codeaf`. The dim line above the rule on home, with a bulb and a cross, is the tip row
3. Press space twice in an empty box to go home, and again from the next conversation — a different tip each time
4. Open a conversation and empty the box. The tip is the lowest rung of the keys row at the foot

note - this branch includes: https://github.com/Agent-Field/CodeAF/pull/1388 (`space space` and `? ask/+ new` revival)

## The twenty-two tips

One table, both boxes. Row 13 is the only home-only row. "always" means from the first minute on home, and after the first exchange in a conversation.

| # | Tip | Appears | Retires |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/compact summarizes the conversation now` | window crosses half | `/compact` finishes |
| 2 | `/cost says what this conversation has spent` | about ten cents spent | `/cost` answered |
| 3 | `esc esc or /rewind takes back an earlier message` | after a long answer | either door lands a rewind |
| 4 | `/files finds files codeaf wrote for you` | after the first export | `/files` reached for |
| 5 | `/resume opens an earlier conversation` | directory has an earlier one | `/resume` reached for |
| 6 | `/standing turns a message into a rule work must follow` | three or more earlier conversations | standing page or order |
| 7 | `/task starts a single-shot task on the side` | after one exchange | `/task` typed |
| 8 | `ctrl+enter makes your message a rule instead of a request` | always | standing page or order |
| 9 | `/manual answers any question about codeaf` | always | `/manual` reached for |
| 10 | `ctrl+shift+t reopens the last conversation tab` | always | a tab is reopened |
| 11 | `type @ to find paths in the current project` | always | the `@` list opens |
| 12 | `/attach sends a file or folder with your message` | always | anything attached |
| 13 | `/project sets the project folder for a new conversation` | **home only** | `/project` reaches a folder |
| 14 | `/export writes the current conversation to a file` | two turns in | an export lands |
| 15 | `/model lets you see and choose models and providers` | always | the model list opens |
| 16 | `/crew sets the models codeaf uses on its own behalf` | always | `/crew` answered |
| 17 | `/budget sets the spending cap for the day` | always | `/budget` answered |
| 18 | `using enter steers conversations · use ctrl+q to queue messages` | after one exchange | a message is queued |
| 19 | `ctrl+t starts a fresh chat in this project` | always | a new chat is started |
| 20 | `/remember carries a fact forward, /forget drops it` | always | `/remember` runs |
| 21 | `/connect links Notion, Slack and other services` | always | connect panel opens |
| 22 | `/autonomy sets how questions are handled while you are away` | after one exchange | `/autonomy` reached for |

Rows 6 and 8 teach the same door and retire together: use `/standing` once and both go.

### Added

- **Home has a tip row**, above the rule over its box, with a bulb and a cross. It never drew one before
- **`/project`**, home only. With a path it pins and opens nothing; bare, it opens the browser
- **`@` on home** — files and folders, ranked as you type, enter puts the path in. `esc` peels the list, then the box, then the screen
- **`/attach` takes a folder**, not just a file. Bare on home it opens the browser

### Changed — commands

- **`/folder` means one thing everywhere**: a folder the conversation is *about*. It never moves the working directory
- **`/manual` is a turn** — the question goes to the model. `codeaf manual` still prints the pages
- **`/project` with a path says nothing now.** Its confirmation was drawn in the refusal slot, which hides home's keys row until the next keystroke — and those keys already end with `project: <path>`. Both refusals still speak
- **Enter on `/attach` in the command list** opens the browser at once

### Changed — other

- **A conversation ranks, home rotates.** First eligible row wins the foot, with a two-turn gap; home's row moves on every visit and every two minutes
- **One ledger, no `priority` column.** Every row draws on both boxes, and a gesture on either retires it on both
- **The cross blanks home's row** until you leave home. The tip put away costs nothing
- **A showing is twenty seconds on home**, one session in a conversation. Six retire a tip
- **The project sits at the right of the keys row**, on both boxes, cut on the right when the keys need the room
- **Eight tip rows were rewritten** in the owner's words, ids and retiring gestures untouched, so nobody is told twice

### Renamed

- **`disable hints`** on the Workspace tab, off by default. The stored key keeps its bytes as `ui.hints`; `internal/config` inverts once

### Removed

- **`/image`** — `/attach` already tells a picture by its name
- **Nine tips, and every feature they named still works.** `ctrl+.`, `alt+1`–`alt+7`, `/search`, `/subharness`: the foot and the `/` list already name them. `ctrl+b`'s came off while copy mode stayed. `/ask`'s came off first, then #1388 removed `/ask`. `/folder`'s was untrue. The second `/attach` row was one too many

### Fixed

- **`/folder picks the folder codeaf works in` was false.** It never did
- **The `@` tip promised a list home did not have**
- **Quoted and escaped paths** answered `no such file`
- **Bare `/attach` on home** said `type the path after /attach`
- **Opening the context sheet** retired both `/attach` tips
- **Stepping through home spent the whole table** in flashes nobody read. A ledger written under that rule is forgiven once
- **The cross re-showed the same tip**, a showing poorer
- **Five manual passages** taught a home door that had moved

### Internal

- **Ids are never reused.** Reworded rows keep theirs; the folded steer-and-queue row took a new one
- **`eventTaskStarted` and `eventTaskPageOpened` still fire.** Nothing waits on them yet
- **Copy mode was deleted on 2026-09-22 and restored on 2026-09-23** — the tip was the thing to drop, not the feature
- **A gate holds `hints-and-tips.md` to every line in the table**, word for word
- **Merged `dev`** (#1384, the working logo). A freeze lays the page out after copy mode owns it — kept on both doors
- **Merged #1388.** Two spaces go home, `esc` is the interrupt again, `/ask` is gone, `ask here` is back. No tip for two spaces: the foot says `space space home` outright. If #1388 lands first, this copy merges away to nothing

## Proof

- `make pr-ready` — the laws and the light gate, then fresh `config`, `manual`, `e2e` and `tui3`
- Built and run by the owner at each step of the wave

`internal/provider`'s `TestTheWarmTranscriptEncodeCostsTheSameAtEightyTurnsAsAtEight/breakpoints` is red on `dev` too, imports nothing this branch changes, and is outside the touched set.

body:
Santosh's report (Slack, 2026-09-22): "esc when a message is waiting does not seem to send it, it seems to just cancel the running one … not sure if this is only when image is attached for followup".

## What was happening

Since #1071 `esc` opens Home, and Home stands the cursor on the conversation before this one, so the reflex `esc`, `enter` is a switch to the previous chat. That switch folded every message waiting above the box into the draft, dropped the picture parked with it, and left nothing to send when the answer ended. Coming back, the follow-up sat in the box as unsent text without its picture, and the turn's close sent nothing.

Reproduced with the real binary in tmux on `dev` c084b60d7, on both the in-process road (`--no-host`) and the engine road: park a follow-up with a picture (plain `enter` parks when a picture is attached; words alone steer into the running turn instead, which is why it looked picture-only), `esc`, `enter`, come back: the block is gone, the box reads the words only, the transcript never gets the message.

## What changes

- The parked queue travels on the aside as itself — words, pictures, pasted documents, standing mark, order — and comes back as the same waiting block with the same hint line. The box keeps only what was typed and unsent before leaving.
- When the turn ends while the conversation is held behind the screen, its watcher's landing edge sends the oldest parked message through the held agent, using the same submit, picture, standing and remote-file doors a front send uses (`parkedStart`), and adopts the returned stream so the next close is the next edge. One message per finished turn, oldest first.
- Session follow-ups (`ctrl+q`) still go first: `Attach` is asked before a parked send, and a running answer is adopted instead of jumped.
- A turn already idle at the stow sends at once. A failed send stays parked with its attachments and notes `submit failed: …` in its own conversation. A send that is crossing while the person comes back is marked so it cannot go twice. The quiet sweep never collects a conversation with something waiting.
- The shared-handle door (a `--host` that cannot dial again) still folds the words into the box because its engine ends the conversation on the swap, and now brings the parked pictures and pastes back onto the tray with them.
- Quitting is unchanged: the draft file still gets the box plus every waiting message's words.
- Manual: the waiting-block page and the Escape section say what leaving does, that `/new` keeps a waiting message with the conversation it was typed in, and name the shared-handle exception; two probes in a person's words reach the page. Stale `esc stops` comments in park.go, followup.go, bargein.go and spellout.go now say `ctrl+c` or Home.

## Verification

- Contract tests in `internal/tui3/parkkeep_test.go`, `switch_test.go`, `sharedagent_test.go`, `keptsweep_test.go`: the queue survives a switch structurally; a picture message is sent through the held agent, not the front one; follow-ups first, one per landing, never twice; idle-at-stow sends now; shared-handle folding keeps chips and pastes; the crash draft keeps the words; a failed send stays parked.
- Hand runs with the real binary and a real model, both roads: park a picture follow-up, `esc`, `enter` onto the previous chat, come back mid-turn — the block is back with `[#1 red.png]` and the message goes at the close; stay away until the turn ends — the message is sent behind the screen and the answer is there on return. Transcripts checked.
- `make pr-ready` green (see the checks).

Not changed here: a picture message replayed from the journal draws the session's `[attached image: …]` sentence beside the chip marker, which is how any resumed picture message already draws.

body: ## What changed While codeaf answers or waits, a single-line chevron-and-dot animation appears immediately below the latest submitted question, after its wrapped text and attachments. A two- or three-word developer caption is composed from compatible action/object families, avoids the last eight opening choices, and rotates every ten seconds through a deck shuffled once per operation. No phrase repeats until the deck is exhausted. Dim ink separates the playful caption from factual work updates. Work details and the answer grow below it; the indicator scrolls with the question and disappears on completion. The input area has no added activity row. The component reserves nine terminal columns for every pose and two columns before following content. With its two-column inset, its label starts at column 14 relative to the content area. The caption has its own 28-column reservation plus a two-column gap before future content. A slow decoding ripple briefly replaces one letter at a time with two symbols over 160 ms, resolves for 80 ms, and pauses for 1.8 seconds between passes. Every substitution is one terminal cell. Accessible tiers keep static text. Token counts and rates do not affect this layout. The top-left header carries a stationary `>● codeaf` wordmark. Chat, task transcripts and adaptive-run pages share `tokens.WorkActivity`. It offers ten motions with 28 timed poses each, explicit named or random selection, and operation-local state. Steering and provider retries keep the turn's choice. Frames are read-only and use the existing clock; there are no extra timers or background painting. The animation stops for questions, inactive or disconnected tasks, and copy mode. ASCII, monochrome, linear and small-window views retain compact text. Includes manual, design and performance documentation, plus the numbered change entry. ## Validation - Focused chat/task lifecycle, harness, approval, header and composer geometry checks pass locally. - Caption grammar, length, recent-history exclusion, render stability and decoding readability and fallback checks pass. - All 280 poses preserve the label column and anchor below a wrapped question. body:
Fixes #1379.

A person with eighty-one SKILL.md folders on disk asked the chat whether it could use skills and was told codeaf has no such mechanism. The binary carried the wave. `memory.enabled` was off.

Every part behaved as designed. The launch import returns when memory is nil, the catalog renders zero bytes for an empty shelf, and `use_skill` is withheld rather than present and refusing. The model was left with no shelf, no verb and no sentence about either, so it reasoned from the silence and denied a shipped feature.

## The rule this adds

Absent-not-broken stops a model planning a reply around a call that can only refuse. It does not stop a model reasoning from the absence. So it gets a companion clause rather than an exception: **when a capability is withheld by a setting, something has to say so.**

Otherwise "absent because impossible here" and "absent because it does not exist" are the same silence.

## What changed

- The catalog renders one line when the machine holds skills this session cannot reach, naming `memory.enabled` and saying the skills exist.
- The door measures that once at launch. A prompt prefix may not walk six folders per render.
- A machine with no skills still pays nothing. That is what the emptiness law is actually about: a number nobody has yet, not the difference between empty and switched off.
- The `/skill` picker reads the folders rather than the shelf, so it listed skills that could not be attached. Each row now carries the reason **beside** the folder's own warning rather than instead of it.
- `use-skill.md` gains a heading answering the capability question in both states.

## Proof

Both new tests were run **red against the unfixed tree** before they were kept:

```
--- FAIL: TestTheCatalogSaysSkillsAreSwitchedOffRatherThanMissing
    a machine with skills and memory off rendered nothing
--- FAIL: TestTheSkillPickerSaysWhyARowCannotBeAttachedWithMemoryOff
    the row does not say why choosing it does nothing:
    › ○ alpha-flake      chase a flaky test · project
```

Gate on the build box at `410fea62b`:

```
gofmt clean   build 0   vet 0   change entries 107   laws 0   manual gates 0
internal/session  ok  (full package)
internal/tui3     ok  325.396s
cmd/codeaf        ok   93.272s
```

## Not in this

body:
Closes #1345.

## What was true

On the bare hosted road (`codeaf chat`, the engine in another process) a person typed `stop it` over a running task. The model's `tasks … stop` looked the row up through the task graph and the project's finished-work index, and a live bash-belt run is in neither until it ends, so the tool answered `No task "1" in this project` and the model paraphrased that as `I've stopped.` while the rail kept `1 running`. The run's own page could stop it, because the page hands the rail's number straight to `Cancel`. v0.3.0 stopped the run and printed `Stopped.`.

## What is true now

A stop resolves its number or title-derived name against the live run first (`liveBeltTaskByToken`, the run's root and joined rows, the same ids and titles the rail shows) and then takes the existing `stopOneTask` → `CancelWithReason` road: the stopped root is written to the store, the run's context is cut, the branch is kept, the stopped frame is published. Every failure now begins `Could not stop task …:` and says why, so a refusal or an empty receipt can never read as success. `internal/manual/chat/task-controls.md` says so.

## Verified

- `internal/remote/hosted_stop_test.go`: a real `session.Agent` over the real loopback wire with a blocking run fixture and an HTTP/SSE model stub that sends exactly `tasks {"id":"1","stop":true}`; asserts the success receipt the model saw, the stopped rail frame, the cancelled store root, and exactly two model requests. Red before, green after.
- `TestTasksToolStopsARunsOwnRowBeforeItHasEnded` (session seam) and the stop-refusal test now demanding `Could not stop task "404":`.
- Hand proof on the built binary, hosted and in-process: `stop it` → row `stopped`, `1 running` gone within seconds (frames in the fix worktree).
- `make pr-ready` green (session 331 s, remote, tui3, manual gates).

Found in the 2026-09-21 staging verification of 17ae56d34.

body:
Closes #1370.

`TestNothingArrivingAfterTheStopIsDrawn` compares two whole rendered frames.
The head draws the time of day on every frame (`pulse.go`'s `pulseClock`, off
`app.now`), so the wall clock was inside that comparison without anybody
putting it there, and the test failed whenever its two captures straddled a
minute boundary. Measured at one failure in eighty one runs.

## The fix

`stoppingApp` now builds its surface on a held clock, the way
`stopbound_test.go`'s `boundedStopApp` already does. The seam existed:
`app.now` reads `a.clock` and falls back to `time.Now`, so this is one
assignment and no new mechanism.

IT IS PINNED IN `stoppingApp` AND NOT IN `newTestApp`. `newTestApp` has calling
files in the hundreds, and pinning the clock there changes the observable time
for every test in the package at once, including the ones asserting on elapsed
durations and relative words. That may be the better end state, but it is a
package-wide behaviour change and it is not this.

## Red before green

Two reds, both on `89dacca80` with nothing else applied.

The shipped test, which is red at nanosecond resolution rather than at the
minute boundary:

```
--- FAIL: TestTheStoppedSurfaceReadsAClockThatDoesNotMoveOnItsOwn
    two readings of the stopped surface's clock differ by 64ns, so the head can
    move between two frames nothing happened between
```

And the reported failure itself, made deterministic by pinning the clock 200ms
before a minute boundary and walking it across during the test's own 0.45
seconds. This ran on the base tree and is not part of the change:

```
--- FAIL: TestRedOnBaseTheReportedFlakeMadeDeterministic
    the frame moved after the stop:
    was:
     codeaf                                          wed 3:43am
    now:
     codeaf                                          wed 3:44am
```

Nothing else on the frame differs, which is the whole diff the gate saw.

## The guard, which is on the fix and not on the product

There are two repairs here that produce the same green: pin the clock, or stop
comparing the part of the frame the clock is drawn in. The second one also
stops the test noticing a real change to the head after a stop, which is inside
what it exists to catch.

So the comparison now has a name, `stoppedFrame`, the test above uses it, and
`TestTheStoppedFramesComparisonStillCoversTheHead` drives the held clock across
a minute boundary and insists the compared frame sees it.

That guard was checked by mutation rather than by assertion. Narrowing
`stoppedFrame` to drop the head, which is exactly the cheap repair:

```
--- PASS: TestNothingArrivingAfterTheStopIsDrawn
--- FAIL: TestTheStoppedFramesComparisonStillCoversTheHead
    a minute passed and the compared frame did not move, so the head is no
    longer inside the comparison
```

The cheap repair leaves the original test green and this one red, which is the
only arrangement that makes it a guard.

## Is anything else in the package exposed

The class is not "a test that reads the clock", it is a whole-frame string
comparison containing a field that moves on its own, so the search is for
frames captured twice and compared rather than for `time.Now`. There are two
such comparisons in `internal/tui3`:

- `stopping_test.go`, this one.
- `roomclick_test.go:132`, `TestAPressOnNothingInTheConversationDoesNothing`,
  which compares `frame(a)` whole.

The second one is NOT exposed, and that is measured rather than reasoned: its
frame does carry a clock word, and `roomApp` already holds its own clock
through `taskApp`, so the field cannot move between its two captures. One site,
fixed here, and no class issue owed.

## Checks

On one box under its heavy-suite lock, `-count=1` unless stated.

```
go test -count=200 -run '^TestNothingArrivingAfterTheStopIsDrawn$' ./internal/tui3/
go test -count=200 -run '^TestTheStoppedSurfaceReadsAClockThatDoesNotMoveOnItsOwn$|^TestTheStoppedFramesComparisonStillCoversTheHead$' ./internal/tui3/
go test -count=1 ./internal/tui3/
```

```
ok  github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/internal/tui3   90.896s   (count=200, the reported test)
ok  github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/internal/tui3  141.141s   (count=200, the two new ones)
ok  github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/internal/tui3  325.673s   (count=1, the whole package)
```

`bash scripts/laws.sh` exits 0 across 27 packages. `gofmt -l ./cmd ./internal`
prints nothing.

The whole package is in there because `stoppingApp` has seven callers across
two files, and a helper that now pins a clock is a change to all of them.

body:
`generate_video` and `generate_music` both refuse an empty prompt on their own
first line. `generate_image` did too, and stopped.

## How it went

The check was in the base of both trunks. It left in `2b46a3a5b`, "the web pair
and the picture hand are plain functions a command line can share": the block
around it moved into the extracted function and the check did not come with it.
The commit message does not mention the guard, nothing else in that change
touches validation, and the two sibling doors still have theirs. It was
collateral, not a decision.

NOTHING WENT RED, because nothing was asserting it. That is the whole reason it
survived three days and a fifty six file merge review.

## Why this door and not another

It is the paid one. A provider asked to draw nothing still bills the call, and
the answer it sends back reads as the provider having a bad minute rather than
as a caller having sent an empty string. So the cost is real money and a
diagnosis pointing the wrong way.

The guard is in `GenerateImage` rather than on the belt, because that function
is shared: `internal/session`'s tool calls it and so does `cmd/codeaf`'s
`image.go`. Put on the belt it would leave the command line door refusing
nothing.

The request now carries `prompt`, the value the guard read, rather than
trimming `parsed.Prompt` a second time at the call. Two readings of one prompt
is how a door starts refusing calls it then sends anyway.

## Acceptance

`internal/session/tools_image_prompt_test.go`.

THE ASSERTION THAT MATTERS IS THAT NOTHING WAS SENT, not that the sentence is
right. On `9321a8556` as it stands:

```
--- FAIL: TestThePictureHandRefusesAnEmptyPromptAndSendsNothing
    the picture hand sent 3 request(s) for a prompt that was not there
```

Every sentence assertion in that test PASSED on the base. All three empty calls
were refused, by the provider, after being paid for. A test that only checked
the words would have gone green over the defect, which is the shape this is
worth writing down for: the door said the right thing and the money was already
spent.

Three cases: no prompt at all, a prompt of spaces, a prompt of one newline.

`TestAPromptWithWordsInItStillReachesThePainter` is the control, without which
the test above passes on a door that refuses everything. It also pins that what
reaches the painter is the TRIMMED prompt, which is the second half of reading
it once.

The nine existing `TestGenerateImage` cases still pass, which is the evidence
the shared function was not disturbed rather than a claim that it was not.

## Checks

On `9321a8556`, on one box under its single heavy-suite lock, `-count=1`:

```
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/internal/session	248.773s
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/cmd/codeaf	99.246s
```

`cmd/codeaf` is in it because it is the other caller of `GenerateImage`, and a
guard checked only where the belt calls it is checked in half the places it
runs.

`bash scripts/laws.sh` exits 0 across 27 packages. `gofmt -l ./cmd ./internal`
prints nothing.

body:
The number 15 was written down three times for one limit:

- `SlackReadThread`'s doc, as the word "fifteen"
- the `limit` query parameter, as `"15"`, which is the one that actually applies it
- the tool description a model reads, as `"15"`, in a different package

The third is the one that goes stale in silence. If somebody changes the limit, the call still returns whatever Slack returns and the model still believes whatever the sentence said, so nothing fails and nobody finds out. `connect.SlackThreadLimit` is now the one place and both sites reference it. This is CLAUDE.md's one-source-of-truth rule, whose own worked example is the `propose_task` 40/200 pair.

**The description is still a compile-time const.** Both operands are string constants, so `"Read one Slack thread in order, up to " + connect.SlackThreadLimit + " messages. ..."` folds at compile time. Nothing moved into `init`, the declaration stays usable everywhere a const is, and the rendered text is byte for byte what it was:

```
Read one Slack thread in order, up to 15 messages. The channel id and ts are the final line of a slack_search result; ...
```

`internal/session` already imported `internal/connect`, so no new edge.

**No test.** A `strings.Contains(slackReadThreadDescription, connect.SlackThreadLimit)` assertion would hold for every possible value of either side and could never fail. The compile-time concatenation is the mechanism; a test on top of it would be a test that cannot fail, which is the shape #1306 is about.

### The settings rule that rides with it

`Setting.read` now states the same argument where it has teeth. A row's `read` returns **what the product will actually use**, not what is stored: where a value passes through a resolver, the row reads the resolver, so a person who types something the resolver will not honour watches it change in front of them.

That is what makes a lossy store safe, and it is the only thing that does. `persistedCount` (#1369) collapses unset and zero the moment the value is written, and nothing downstream of the row can recover the difference, because downstream never sees what was typed. The row typing the default back at the person is the whole safety argument, so it belongs on the field that does it rather than in the helper that depends on it. #1369 and this now point at each other.

### Checks

On Spark, fresh clone of `santos/dev2` at `d91bb63ae`, `~/src/wt-slack15`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `gofmt -l ./internal ./cmd` | empty |
| `go build ./...` | 0 |
| `go run ./cmd/codeaf-changes check` | 0, 100 entries well formed |
| `go test ./internal/connect ./internal/config ./internal/guard ./internal/namelaw` | 0 |
| `go test ./internal/session` | ok, 249.6s |
| combined | `COMBINED_RC=0` |
| em dashes on added lines | 0 |

`internal/tui3` and `cmd/codeaf` are out of scope: neither reads the constant or the description, and neither file in them changed.
