body:
A `/task` node ended reading `paused — it resumes`, its state still running, with no ending on the
record and nothing naming what had cut it. Work carried on for eight minutes afterwards on a node
nothing was waiting for.

## What was wrong

The codebase already knows this failure. `internal/session/task_run.go` carries a comment headed
*THE NURSERY LAW*: a part's job row lives in its **owner's** registry, and `jobRegistry.shutdown`
cuts that row's context through `job.signal`, which takes the `stop` handle and never the explicit
one that only `jobRegistry.kill` calls. A part cut that way reads its own cancel as a process
quitting, lands on `settleUnfinished`'s paused road, and returns `""` so the state stays
`TaskRunning` for a recovery that is not coming.

`workTaskNode` guards against it with `defer node.graph.stopChildren(node.id)`. **The design body
did not.** It closed its thread with a bare `_ = child.Close()` and called `stopChildren` nowhere.
That thread is not a leaf: `newTaskAgent` hands it the family's graph and its depth, so it carries
`propose_task` and `tasks` on its belt and can own parts of its own. Every part the thread handed
out was therefore cut down with it, unmarked, and landed paused. `runTaskNode`'s own
`stopChildren` runs only after the body has already closed the thread, so the mark arrived too
late to change the road the part took.

## What changed

**The design's thread stops its parts before it is closed.** `designHarnessNode` now carries the
same guard `workTaskNode` has, registered *after* the close's defer so it unwinds *before* it, on
every road out of the function. It reuses `TaskGraph.stopChildren`, which deliberately leaves
settled children alone, so the ordinary road where every part already settled finds nothing to do.

**A node's context never ends without a reason on the record.** Even with the first change, the
`ctx.Err() != nil` road can still be taken, and it used to write nothing at all — no ending, no
cancelling party, no reason. A node machinery cut where it stood now carries a new
`TaskEndingInterrupted` and a report saying the cut came from outside the work. It still does not
move the state and still leaves the checkpoint resumable: an interruption is not a finding about
the work, and that has not changed. What changed is that it is no longer silent, so a person can
tell an interruption they caused from machinery that cut the work.

Nothing existing would carry that: `store.UserCancelReason` is the resident's person-cancel
journal string and names a person, and the person's own road is already covered by the
`wasStopped` arm through `TaskEndingStopped`. The machinery cut had no word at all, so this is a
new `TaskEnding` value rather than a new field.

Because `TaskNode.end` is first-cause-wins, the record clears `Ending` on requeue, so a resumed
attempt does not inherit a reason that was never its own.

**`task_run.go`'s `spendLedger` comment is not a third instance.** It discusses the same ordering
— a stopped parent is closed and folded before `stopChildren` runs — but as the *reason the
mechanism exists*, and it already redirects the ledger to the graph's home agent. Checked and left
alone.

## Evidence

Both changes were pinned by a failing test first, and both failures are the real ones:

```
--- FAIL: TestAPartAThreadHandedOutIsNotLeftPausedWhenTheDesignCloses (0.06s)
    a part the design's thread handed out was cut down unmarked and left reading as resumable work:
      state   = "running"
      ending  = ""
      stopped = true
      report  = "paused — it resumes"

--- FAIL: TestAMachineryCutNodeAndAPersonsStopDoNotReadTheSame (0.00s)
    a run machinery cut the work on says nothing about what ended it
```

Three commits, in order: the reproduction, then each change.

Verified on the Spark cluster over ssh at this PR head:

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/session/`
- `go test ./internal/session/ -run 'TestAPartAThreadHandedOutIsNotLeftPausedWhenTheDesignCloses' -count=1` — ok
- `go test ./internal/session/ -run 'Nursery|StopChildren|Paused|Unfinished|Settle|Interrupt|Ending' -count=1` — ok, 10.8s

One thing worth a reviewer's eye: change 2 surfaces `Ending` for a node in the *running* state,
where previously only a `failed` node carried one. The rerun-from-branch road was the risk — it
calls `node.end(...)` and sends the node round again — but both continue paths set the state to
`TaskQueued` and clear `ending` first (`task_continue.go:144` and `:441`), so a node that is
actually re-running cannot show a stale reason.

A decision card raised under `--yolo` put itself up and waited. `--yolo` means nobody is
watching, so a card that waits is a run that hangs until something else times it out.

## What changed

`internal/session/tools_ask.go` now turns a `PolicyAsk` card that carries a default into a
`PolicyDecide` one when the run is unattended, so it takes its own default and carries on. The
posture read is `Config.Unattended`, which `cmd/codeaf/chatv3.go:1056` sets from `opts.Yolo` and
from nothing else — so this cannot reach an interactive or a headless run.

Two neighbouring cases are deliberately untouched:

- **A card with no default still parks.** It has nothing to take. That is the headless branch
  just above, which hands such a card back as `your call`.
- **An assumption card is not this road.** Its default is its options standing and it already
  carries the away-policy clock, so it never arrives here as `PolicyAsk`.

The answer is written through the existing `defaultAnswer` / `headlessAnswerLine` pair, so the
record says the default was taken automatically rather than chosen by a person.

## Evidence

The test was written and committed **before** the fix, and fails on the tree without it:

```
--- FAIL: TestACardUnderYoloTakesItsDefaultAndSaysSo (2.00s)
    tools_ask_test.go:80: the card waited under --yolo instead of taking its default
```

Two commits, in that order: `9c548800` pins the behaviour, `876aa8bf` makes it true.

Verified on the Spark cluster over ssh, from a fresh clone of this PR head:

- `go test ./internal/session/ -run 'Yolo|Ask|Card' -count=1`
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/session/`

The 2.00s in the failure above is the card actually waiting — the test spends the real timeout
before it gives up, which is what the run was doing in the field.

Adds the scheduled workflow that mirrors the Model Pool's signed index document onto the `model-pool` orphan data branch, plus the signature verifier it runs. Nothing else: no product code, no relay Worker (that ships with the Pareto crewing PR into `santos/dev`, #1093).

## What it does

Every six hours, and on manual dispatch, the job fetches `https://codeaf.agentfield.ai/pool/index.json` and its detached Ed25519 signature, verifies the signature against the public key (a literal, no secret needed), and commits both files unchanged under `pool/` on the `model-pool` branch. The branch holds the signed document and its signature only: no count, no leaderboard, no extracted statistic.

## Why it goes to `dev` on its own

GitHub only runs a workflow that exists on the default branch, so the mirror cannot start until this file is on `dev`. The relay is already live and the `model-pool` branch exists (created by hand today, refreshed hourly from a stand-in job until this workflow takes over).

## Evidence

- Both files are byte-identical to their copies on `feat/auto-crew` (#1093), where the relay's 58 node tests and the verifier run.
- Workflow requests `contents: write` itself; the repository's default token permission is read-only.

body:
Fixes the 400 Santosh hit on a custom connection: `local-proxy/gpt-5.5 is not a valid model ID`.

## What was wrong

A service connected **while a conversation is open** never reached that conversation, on the session-host road that interactive `codeaf chat` takes by default.

`v3Process.setModelSources` carries a freshly resolved profile to the agents the process is holding — `for _, agent := range p.agents`. Two doors register what they build (`chatv3.go` for the boot conversation, `chatv3_process.go` for `/new`); `cmd/codeaf/engine.go` never has. `git log -S"proc.track" -- cmd/codeaf/engine.go` is empty.

So on a session host that list is empty, `agent.SetSources` is never called for the conversation that is open, its `modelsource.Set` keeps only its default member, `Set.For` finds no matching `Written` segment and falls through to `s.services[0]` **with the model id still qualified**. OpenRouter answers 400 about a model nobody publishes, which the taxonomy classifies as `OurBytes` and the surface says as *"the request could not be sent as it was"*.

**This is pre-existing, not introduced by #1089.** Any mid-session `/connect` of any service on the hosted road has it. Custom connections are simply the first case where a person routinely connects mid-session and is switched onto it in the same breath, by the preferred-model move.

## Evidence

`~/.codeaf-test2/logs/calls.jsonl` on the reporting machine:

```
turn  local-proxy/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001  400
API error (400): local-proxy/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 is not a valid model ID
```

That wording is OpenRouter's. The proxy's own wording for an unknown model is `unknown provider for model ...`, confirmed by curl — which is how the request was proved to have gone to the default service rather than to the connected one. The same proxy answers 200 for the bare id.

Three-way tmux repro on a fresh profile, which is what pins the cause rather than the symptom:

| | before this change |
|---|---|
| connect mid-session, turn in the same conversation | **400** |
| `/new` in the same process, then a turn | works |
| restart the binary, then a turn | works |

`/new` and a restart both clear it because both build a fresh agent from the refreshed process settings. That split is what rules out the config layer: `config.ClientConfigFor` → `modelsource.Set.For` resolves correctly against the real profile (`BaseURL=http://127.0.0.1:8317/v1`, `Model="claude-haiku-4-5-20251001"`, `Direct=true`).

There is **no** fallback onto another provider after the 400. The `deepseek`/`openrouter` rows beside the failure in the log are the separate title and router lanes, which run alongside every turn and end `context canceled` when it dies. No billing moved.

## The change

Paired register/forget, tied to the engine session's lifecycle.

- `internal/remote`: new `Engine.Closed func(agent WrappedAgent)`, called once per closed conversation at **both** close sites — `Session.shutDown` (after `agent.Close()`, never on the `already` return) and `Session.swap` (after `previous.Close()`, the road `/new` and `/resume` take without touching `shutDown`). Nil is a door that retains nothing. No wire message, no wire version bump, no protocol method.
- `cmd/codeaf/chatv3_process.go`: `forget`, the pair of `track` — removes by pointer identity under `p.mu`, order-preserving, clears the dropped tail so a retained agent cannot outlive its conversation.
- `cmd/codeaf/engine.go`: `proc.track` after `openV3Agent` **and** inside both the `Fresh` and `Open` closures. Without those two the defect returns for a conversation opened by `/new` over the wire — which is the road a person takes precisely when they have just connected something. Plus the `Closed` closure that forgets.

The forget half is not decoration: an engine daemon outlives every conversation it serves, so tracking alone would grow the held list for the life of the process.

## Tests

| test | fails before the fix? |
|---|---|
| `cmd/codeaf` `TestTheEngineDoorTracksEveryConversationItBuildsAndForgetsIt` | **yes** — *"bootEngine builds 3 conversations and tracks 0"* |
| `cmd/codeaf` `TestATrackedConversationIsReachedAndAForgottenOneIsNot` | no — pins `forget`'s semantics, which did not exist before |
| `cmd/codeaf` `TestOpeningAndClosingConversationsLeavesTheProcessHoldingNothing` | no — eight open/close cycles, asserts `len(p.agents) == 0`; the leak guard |
| `internal/remote` `TestEveryClosedConversationReachesTheEnginesClosedDoor` | no — pins `Closed` on both roads, once each, with agent identity |
| `internal/remote` `TestAnEngineWithNoClosedDoorStillClosesAndSwaps` | no — nil door takes both roads |
| `internal/session` `TestAServiceConnectedMidConversationServesTheNextTurn` | no — the wire contract the engine road was failing to invoke: the connected host is asked, with its own key, and the wire model is **bare** |

Being straight about that column: only the structural law fails on the unfixed tree, because the defect was a missing call rather than wrong logic. Verified by applying `forget` and `Engine.Closed` to a detached checkout at `f1a9299f3` while leaving `engine.go` alone — the law failed with the message above and everything else passed. The structural test is the one that would have caught this originally and is the one that catches its return; it reads the door with `go/ast`, so it lands on the laws gate.

`internal/session/TestAServiceConnectedMidConversationServesTheNextTurn` is the mirror of the existing `TestRemovingAServiceEvictsAndDisarmsItsClient`, which covered removal only.

No manual page changes: nothing in `internal/manual/chat/services.md` claims a connection takes effect only on the next conversation, so there is no stale denial to remove. No new command, key, tool, default or limit.

## Testing

All on Spark from a fresh clone, per the standing rule — nothing was run on the laptop beyond `gofmt`, `go build` and single-test runs.

body:
## Why this must land

The relay half of this audit is already live in production (website2.0 #62, `be802e874`, deployed 18:02Z on 2026-09-17): agentfield.ai now drops any event that cannot name its codeaf version. The binary half is this PR. Until it is merged to dev and carried through the staging build and the next main release, released binaries still spool and post `unknown`-version events (the relay now discards them, so the data is silently thinner rather than wrong), the Go smoke tests still mint a fake install on every suite run, and a hosted `codeaf chat` still reports zero turns, model calls and tool calls in `session_ended`. **Needs merge to dev, then include in staging and the next main release.**

Fixes from auditing the anonymous usage counts against the first day of real data in PostHog. Four defects were real; the rest of the design held. Relay side: website2.0 #62 (merged and verified in production).
## Fixed here, each pinned by a test

1. **A hosted chat reported zeros.** A local `codeaf chat` attaches to the workspace's session host, a separate process, so the counters that tick where the loop runs never reached the chat process that sends `session_ended`. In production 27 of 35 chat sessions carried 0 turns, 0 model calls and 0 tool calls; the 8 with numbers had run with `--no-host`. The chat process now counts from the events it receives from the host (turn done, tool end, tool failed, retrying), and only when the session is hosted, so an in-process chat is not counted twice.
2. **Events without a version could leave the machine.** The opt-out ladder keeps an unstamped build off, but a test can force the ladder on and the events then carry `codeaf_version: "unknown"`. 44 such events reached production from one Go test. The send path now drops any event whose version is missing, empty or `unknown`, whatever switched the ladder.
3. **Smoke tests counted as installs.** `exec_smoke_test.go` builds a real binary stamped `v0.0.0-smoke` and runs it with a fresh home, so every suite run minted a new install id and sent `first_run`. 49 of the day's 84 raw install ids were this. The smoke environment now carries `CODEAF_TELEMETRY=off` and an empty endpoint, and a test proves the binary writes no telemetry state.
4. **The hosted door handed back two handles.** Wrapping the hosted boot agent with the counter tee (fix 1) but returning the bare agent from `Resume` and `Fresh` made the surface hold one conversation under two names, and a conversation opened beside the first was not counted at all. The agent is wrapped once and every door hands back that one; `besideAgent` carries the same tee. Pinned by `TestTelemetryTheHostedBootAgentIsCounted` and `TestTelemetryAConversationOpenedBesideIsCounted`, and the pre-existing hosted-resume identity test.

Test-only plumbing: a test binary is unstamped, so with fix 2 the lifecycle tests saw their events dropped; `telemetry.VersionForTest` stamps a version for one test, the same way `EnableForTest` turns the ladder on. No production path changes.

## Audit findings that were not bugs

- **Install id** lives at `<state root>/telemetry/install_id`, under `CODEAF_HOME`, not the profile. It survives upgrades and profile switches; it changes only if the state root moves, which is what the id is defined by. `first_run` is sent once per id and no id has more than one in the data.
- **Double sends.** The relay derives PostHog's `uuid` from the event id, so a batch resent after a partial failure deduplicates at ingestion. No duplicate uuids exist in the data.
- **Both doors.** `execute` runs the lifecycle once per process; `do`, `exec`, `run` and `plan run` count in-process (verified live: a clean task arrived as `done`/exit 0 with its model-call band, an interrupted one as `interrupted`/exit 3). Child processes the binary spawns (`engine`, resident, watchdog) are not session commands and emit nothing.
- **Version stamping.** Release builds stamp `rev` with the tag, so `channel` derives as stable, rc, staging or dev; `make build` stamps the commit, which reports as a source build with channel `unknown`. Unstamped or dirty builds never send.
- **Opt-out.** `CODEAF_TELEMETRY=off`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, the project file and `codeaf telemetry off` each write nothing at all; pinned by the existing gate tests and checked live with `codeaf telemetry status`.
- **Leaks.** Every property key ever seen on a `codeaf:*` event in PostHog is on the allowlist; the relay strips anything else.
- **Rate limits.** None at the relay beyond 50 events and 64 KB per batch; abuse would show as volume, not as broken data. Left as is.

## Verified

On Spark (host `spark`, plain ssh, 20 cores) in a fresh `git clone` checked out at this exact head, `681e2adf1e832fdfa9676f8d3764dd2754567b50`: `make check changelog-check test-laws` exit 0, 126 packages ok, no failures (log `~/src/af-tel-check.log`, 18:23Z to 18:29Z). `internal/telemetry` and `cmd/codeaf` also pass under `-race`. Nothing ran on the laptop.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## What failed

On the published `staging-20260917-fa252d69d6dc` line (PR #1060), neither
`codeaf update` nor `/update` could finish over the real network. Both ended
with:

    error: read the release response: context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout or context cancellation
    while reading body); install a release with: curl -fsSL https://agentfield.ai/get/codeaf | bash   EXIT=1

Deterministic, 3/3, by two independent drivers.

The cause is arithmetic. Both doors built the release client with
`update.NewClient(rev, 3*time.Second)` — the budget for the small launch check
— and that became `http.Client{Timeout: 3s}`, which in Go covers the WHOLE
exchange including every body byte. The same client downloaded the release
asset: `codeaf-linux-amd64` is 57,532,578 bytes and a plain curl of it takes
about 8.6 s here. Three seconds could never cover it. `--check` passed
everywhere because its response is a few KB, and every earlier hand test used a
local mirror that serves 57 MB in milliseconds.

## The new clocks

`Client.Timeout` is gone. The transport bounds only what has made no progress —
a 5 s dial, a 5 s TLS handshake, a 10 s wait for response headers — and every
call takes its deadline from its context:

| Call | Clock |
| --- | --- |
| launch check and `codeaf update --check` | 3 s, whole exchange, from one `CheckTimeout` constant both doors read |
| release metadata during an install (latest / list / checksums) | 10 s each |
| the asset download | no whole-exchange clock: 30 s with no bytes arriving fails, 15 minutes overall is the ceiling |

A dead connection still fails with a sentence; a slow one now succeeds. No Go
deadline text reaches a person any more: a stall says `downloading
codeaf-linux-amd64 stalled — no bytes for 30 s`, the ceiling says `took longer
than 15 minutes`, late headers say `did not start arriving within 10 s`. The
terminal road still ends with the curl line and the chat road still offers it.
The stall window, the ceiling and the metadata window are injectable, so the
new tests prove each clock against real slow, silent and trickling servers
instead of waiting out the shipped durations.

## Proved on the real network

A `v0.1.0`-stamped build from this branch, against the real
`github.com/Agent-Field/CodeAF` releases:

**Terminal** — `time codeaf update` printed

    codeaf: installed v0.2.0 at /tmp/.../codeaf
    codeaf v0.2.0 built 2026-09-15 13:26 · go1.26.5 linux/amd64

in **7.5 s real**; the installed file is 57,532,578 bytes and reports v0.2.0.

**Chat** — the launch drew

    codeaf v0.2.0 is out · you have v0.1.0 · /update installs it and restarts · or: curl -fsSL https://agentfield.ai/get/codeaf | bash

and `/update` drew its three notes,

    downloading codeaf v0.2.0 for linux/amd64…
    checksum matched · installed at /tmp/.../chat-codeaf
    restarting on v0.2.0…

then restarted onto the same conversation — the transcript's marker exchange
came back under `· resumed ·`, `/status` moved from `build v0.1.0 built
2026-08-31 20:00` to `build v0.2.0 built 2026-09-15 13:26`, and its `file` row
named the same `transcript.jsonl` before and after.

## Why it blocks

#1060's update road is unusable on the line that is published today, so this is
a blocker for promoting staging to main: whoever installs that build cannot
update out of it from inside codeaf.

## Gates

`gofmt -l cmd internal` (empty) · `go vet ./...` · `go build ./...` · windows/amd64
and darwin/arm64 cross-builds · `make build` · `make test-laws` ·
`go test -count=1 ./internal/update/ ./cmd/codeaf/ ./internal/manual/ ./internal/e2e/` ·
`make test-focus PKGS=./internal/tui3 RUN='Update|Notice|Command'` · `make test-quick` —
all green. The chat manual's update section states no timeout, so it needed no
correction.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

# The worker harness — one loop under `/task` and `do`

This replaces the engine behind `/task` and `codeaf do` with one worker, one
shell hand and a plan store the binary carries. It is the replacement in
docs/design/worker-harness/DESIGN.md. The branch was merged into `santos/dev` on
2026-09-18 and the waves ended there; everything since has landed on `santos/dev`
as small pull requests, each named below. This body describes `santos/dev` at
3a154ceaa, at product height, and #1108 is the running index.

## What a person gets

- **`/task` becomes a run.** `/task <brief>` starts a run on the plan store
  instead of a node of the conversation's own tree. It answers at once with the
  run's id, the run's root page is the store, and a second `/task` joins the
  live run as a child of its root. When the run ends the conversation is woken
  with the outcome, the result the root reported, and where the work went.
- **`codeaf do` becomes a run with nobody attached.** Same store, same
  supervisor, same worker and the same exit ladder (`0` done · `1` could not run
  · `2` ran and did not finish · `3` a limit stopped it · `4` needed an answer),
  with the same `--json` envelope and usage ledger.
- **The plan store is in the binary.** `internal/plandb` is one SQLite store,
  written by the Go driver already in `go.mod` — never a separate install. A
  worker reaches it as `plandb` in its shell, bound to the run's own store on
  every command.
- **Steering rides the store.** Notes, pause/resume, cancel, amend and priority
  are writes to the plan, and a run worker reads them in its next frame. Hard
  verbs (cancel cascades to descendants and dependents; pause holds a subtree
  out of the frontier) are enforced by the runtime whatever the model does.
- **A text reply no longer ends a task; the task ends when `plandb` says
  done.** A worker that answers in words with no command is told `no action
  executed: answer with one bash call; finish with plandb done <your id>
  --result '…' when the acceptance holds; wait with plandb wait when you are
  blocked on another task` and goes round again; four such replies in a row
  fail the task; `plandb wait` parks it with its claim released. Three tests
  that scripted the old text ending were rewritten to finish in the store:
  `TestBashWorkerPublishesTheLiveStepWhileItsCommandRuns`,
  `TestDoOnTheRunEngineCompletesABriefAndNamesTheRootResult` and
  `TestDoOnTheRunEngineLeavesTheUsageLedgerToTheSession`.
- **A parked task comes back once, when its wait is over.** A worker that
  parks with `plandb wait` is launched again only when everything it waited on
  has finished, or at once when a child failed or was cancelled; a child being
  claimed, started or noted while a sibling still runs is not a reason. A root
  whose children all landed done is never closed failed.
- **The seat a person named is the seat every launch takes.** `--model` seats
  every leaf and `--plan-model` every planning task, wakes included. The check
  seat is resolved from `--check-model`, then `CODEAF_CHECK_MODEL`, then a pinned
  seat, then the profile (#1207). Before this, every wake of
  a root ran on the profile's mastermind row whatever the flags said.
- **The spend block.** Every model call a run makes lands one row in the store's
  ledger tagged with the task, the model and the seat it ran on. The spend page
  draws the run's task spend by seat, and reads it back with `plandb spend --by
  seat` (also `chat`, `project`, `model`, `task`), with `--since 7d` to bound the
  window.

## Landed since the merge

Each line is a small pull request on `santos/dev`, gated by a full check on the
build box on the exact commit.

**Work and its review**

- **One way to put work out.** A typed `/task`, `codeaf do` and a task the chat
  starts by itself take the same road (#1205).
- **A copy of its own for every run.** A run no longer works in the person's
  folder. Its work comes home as one commit when the run ends, unless a person
  stopped it, in which case it stays on the run's own branch (#1232, #1250).
- **The review contract.** A worker declares its own checks, and a review holds
  only on a recorded, zero-exit run of every declared command (#1220). A declared
  check is one uncomposed command, read the way a shell reads its quotes: an
  escaped character inside double quotes is text, and a shape the reader cannot
  settle is refused (#1215, #1273).
- **No `done` before the review.** A run counts a piece of work as finished when
  its worker has come home, not when its row says so, so every finished piece is
  reviewed before the run answers, whatever order the workers came home in. A
  worker that ends its task in the middle of a command comes home when that
  command ends, at most 600 seconds later. A review that cannot be added ends the
  run as `incomplete`; it is never skipped (#1275). A parked task is finished
  only by a worker woken for it (#1271).
- **A task's step numbers continue across a wake** (#1261), and the dim line
  under a row is only that row's own (#1265).

**Stopping, limits and money**

- **A person's stop reaches a run** in one write, keeps the work on the run's
  branch and buys no model turn (#1250). A stopped task reads `stopped` wherever
  its state word is drawn (#1258).
- **A time limit ends a run** (#1262), and **a dollar limit holds while a worker
  is still working**: spend is counted as each call is paid for (#1268).
- **A run's dollars reach the conversation's own total**, as they arrive and on
  every ending, so the conversation's spend limit, `--max-cost`, `/cost` and the
  status line no longer leave runs out (#1280).
- **A run is handed what is left** of the smaller dollar limit the person set,
  `--max-cost` included, less what the conversation has already spent (#1281).
- **An ending a person caused is not a fault.** A run a limit ended says which:
  `a time limit you set stopped it` or `a dollar limit you set stopped it`. The
  first limit reached names the ending (#1279).
- **A worker that has stopped making progress is told once, then ended.** The
  same command coming back with the same answer brings one note; three more
  identical steps end the task with `the same command came back with the same
  answer 6 times in a row: the work was not moving` (#1266).
- **A cancelled command is ended by the call that ran it.** A cancel that arrived
  as a command started could leave it running under no parent (#1282).

## How to try it

**The harness is behind the switch `CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash`.** With it unset the
build is unchanged and the shipped engine serves every road; with it set, a
`/task` is a run on the plan store, a task worker carries one shell, and
`codeaf do` takes the run road.

```
CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash codeaf            # then type:  /task <brief>
CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash codeaf do "<task>"        # one headless run, then exit
CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash codeaf do --json "<task>" # the machine-readable envelope
```

A run worker's belt is one shell hand. It coordinates through `plandb`
(`plandb add`, `plandb split`, `plandb task note`, `plandb task overview`,
`plandb done --agent <name> --result '…'`), and it reaches codeaf's non-shell
hands through the binary — `codeaf patch`, `codeaf doc`, `codeaf web fetch`,
`codeaf web search`, `codeaf image` — each on the same code path its tool runs.

**What to try.** Set `CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash` and open `codeaf`. First, type
`/task <a brief with two or three parts>`: the task rail draws the run's plan
as a tree — each task indented under the one that requested it, a held task
under what it waits on — and, under the one that is running, its live step — the running glyph, `$` and
the command the worker is executing at that moment, with `N steps · $` beneath
it; open the task page and it follows the newest step as it lands until you
scroll up, and resumes following when you reach the bottom again. Second, steer
it: on the task page type a note and press enter; the page confirms it and the
note is read at the worker's next step, and the task's record shows the step
that picked it up. Notes, pause, resume and cancel all ride the plan store, so
a task steered from the page and a task steered from `plandb` on the command
line are the same task. Third, the door with nobody attached:
`CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash codeaf do "<the same brief>" --json` runs the same loop
headless and prints the envelope — the root's result, the landed files and
branch, the node count and `spend_usd`; `plandb spend --by seat` reads the same
run's ledger back.

## Measured — the six calibrated cells

One seat per arm, the same model on both, a $5 cap per run, on the shared build
box. `shipped` is the shipped engine; `harness` is this branch. n=3, and every
figure is the median of the three.

| cell | shipped $ | shipped wall | harness $ | harness wall | pass shipped / harness |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c1 | 0.0075 | 14s | 0.0057 | 26s | 3/3 · 3/3 |
| c2 | 0.0299 | 273s | 0.0102 | 66s | 3/3 · 3/3 |
| c3 | 0.0140 | 114s | 0.0042 | 43s | 3/3 · 3/3 |
| c4 | 0.0105 | 98s | 0.0037 | 19s | 3/3 · 3/3 |
| c5 | 0.0477 | 359s | 0.0230 | 131s | 3/3 · 2/3 |
| c6 | 0.0259 | 231s | 0.0056 | 48s | 3/3 · 3/3 |

The harness is cheaper on all six cells and faster on five; the one cell it
loses (c1) is the cheapest and shortest, by tens of seconds. It also drops a
cell — c5 passes 2/3 where the shipped engine passes 3/3 — which is why the grid
alone is not the readiness bar.

Median output tokens per call: **476 shipped, 217 harness**.

## Measured — repository feature tasks

Each task was handed a repository at a pinned base commit and a feature to build,
with a 45-minute wall and the same model on both arms.

| task | harness, review round (a02845661) | shipped (7231347eb) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bandit, incremental cache | **PASS** 89/89, $0.19, 22m | 82/89, $0.24, 45m (wall) |
| bandit, interprocedural taint | 84/85, $0.18, 26m | 83/85, $0.19, 41m |
| awilix, async container initialization | 23/24, $0.06, 6m | 23/24, $0.27, 45m (wall) |
| cattrs, partial structuring recovery | **PASS** 69/69, $0.08, 8m | **PASS**, $0.21, 45m |

With the review round on, the branch is at or above the shipped engine on every
task on pass count and below it on cost and wall on every task, by three to ten
times; the bare loop before the review round was cheaper still but passed one
in four. The runs before it and what each exposed are in
docs/design/worker-harness/BENCHMARKS.md, including the read-only comparison
that showed the bandit cache miss was a worker ratifying its own reading of
the ask in a test — which is what the review round now reads against the ask.

## Known gaps

- **The readiness bar is one run deep.** The repository table above is one run
  per task; the bar is n ≥ 3 on the same pinned model with no task where the
  shipped engine wins on any of pass count, cost or wall. The six-cell grid
  (n=3) still shows one cell (c5) where the shipped engine passes 3/3 to the
  harness's 2/3, measured before the review round.
- **The review round now fires on a root that worked alone.** Until 2026-09-18 a
  solo root that wrote its own `plandb done` was never checked, so every
  repository number above that predates that fix measured an unreviewed run.
- **The review round is one round deep.** A finding opens one `fix:` task and a
  finding on that fix task is a note, so a run cannot loop; a fix that changes
  a behaviour the check did not cover is not caught (bandit taint, one case).
- **The harness is behind `CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash`.** With it unset the shipped
  engine serves every road. That is the shape for the owner's hands-on test.
  Once the owner is happy the default flips: the run road serves `/task` and
  `codeaf do` with the variable unset, the variable stays for one release as
  the way back to the shipped engine, and then it goes with the engine it
  selected.
- **Three things are the owner's to decide and are unchanged until he does.**
  What ctrl+c, `/quit` and a closed window do to a run: today only the stop on
  the task's own row stops it, and an engine ended by a signal in the middle of
  a command leaves that command running. Whether an incomplete run's work is
  merged into the person's folder: today it is. The side list's foot: today its
  `done` group also holds stopped and incomplete work, so the foot counts them
  as `done`.
- **A person's stop of one part is not yet a fact of its own in the store.** It
  is written as a cancel, the same write a cascade makes.
- The manual pages and the prompt corpus are updated with the branch; per-task
  models (`add --model`), the project and machine dashboards, and terminal
  `attach` are later views on the same store.

## Words on the screen

Every word the harness shows a person was read against the chat manual before
this body was written. On the task rail and the task page: *task*, *step*,
*note*, *queued*, *waits*, *running*, *done*, *incomplete*, *your call*,
*node*, *slot*, *branch*, *session* — all already the manual's. In the run's
own sentences (a task's record, a failure reason, the `do` envelope): *run*,
*plan*, *store*, *worker*, *root*, *landing*, *landed*, *result*, *spend*,
*cap*, *wall*, *seat*, *parked*, *wake*, *trajectory* — all already on the
manual's pages. Two sentences were new, and both are now quoted on the
`worker-harness` page rather than renamed, because they are what the belt
says to the model and the record has to show the words the model was told:
`no action executed: …` and `4 replies in a row carried no action`.
*Harness*, *belt*, *envelope* and *leaf* are design and manual words and
never drawn on a screen. The rail's live step line and the page's
following of it (`$ <command>`, `N steps · $`, `queued · waits: <what>`) are
spelled from the same list.

## State

**Merged into `santos/dev`, where it stays behind its switch.** Nothing here
reaches `dev` until the owner's hands-on test: #1108, the pull request from
`santos/dev` into `dev`, stays a draft until then. The numbers above are read
before the code, and the bar is the table, not a sentence.
title: WIP: the worker harness — one loop under /task and do

body:
Integration branch `santos/dev` into `dev`. Draft: it is the running index of what the branch carries, and it stays a draft until the worker harness is complete, the independent end-to-end pass on Spark is green, and Santosh has tested it himself.

## State

- Level with `dev`. Everything through #1192 already reached `dev` as #1194 on 2026-09-18, and `dev` has been merged back each time it moved (#1116 mirror workflow, #1195 /connect custom row, #1196 v0.3.0 changelog).
- Every landing below is a squash gated by a full `make check` on Spark, fresh clone, on the exact commit. The check has cross-compiled every release target since #1254.
- The worker harness is off unless `CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash` is set, so the default road does not move.

## The worker harness

One loop under `/task` and `codeaf do`, with a plan store per run, a plan seat, a work seat, a check seat, and a review round after each piece of work (#1109).

- **One way to put work out.** A typed `/task`, `codeaf do`, and a task the chat starts by itself all take the same road; a landing wakes no model turn, and a reply comes only when an answer is owed (#1205).
- **A copy of its own for every run.** A hand-off no longer works in the person's folder; the work comes home as one commit when the run ends (#1232).
- **The review contract.** A worker declares its own checks; a holds verdict rests on a recorded, zero-exit run of every declared command, and the basis is kept with the task (#1220, replaces #1206). A review is seated on the crew's checking seat, resolved from `--check-model`, `CODEAF_CHECK_MODEL`, a pinned seat, then the profile (#1207). A declared check is read the way a shell reads its quotes (#1215).
- **No lost or doubled work.** A run's result is read from the store when the root's worker returns late (#1210); a dispatch pass no longer reclaims the leaf it just released (#1225); a `codeaf do` run whose root finished itself still gets its review (#1233, #1243); a parked task is finished only by a worker woken for it (#1271).
- **Conversations keep their tasks.** A reopened conversation reads back tasks born from a run's plan, never overwrites a checkpoint it could not read, never reuses an id (#1213); every run a conversation made stays readable (#1234); the tasks tool reads a run's tasks from the run's own record (#1222).
- **No done before the review.** A run counts a piece of work as finished when its worker's return has been taken in, not when its row says done, so every finished piece gets its review round before the run answers, whatever order the workers came home in. A review that cannot be seated ends the run as incomplete instead of being skipped (#1275, with the store's half in #1271).
- **A quoted check is read as the one command it is.** One quote scanner sits under both check readers; an escaped character inside double quotes is text, and any shape the scanner cannot settle is refused (#1273).
- **A long declared check says why it was refused.** A check over 1000 bytes is refused with its cause and its own measured length; the limit governs admission only, so a check already recorded stays on the checker's door (#1283).
- **Proposals and endings.** A refused proposal is told every problem at once (#1214); a landing's report counts as evidence the ask is finished (#1212).

## Stopping and limits

- **A person's stop reaches a run.** The stop ends the run's task and everything open under it in one write, cuts the run's context, keeps the work on the run's own branch, puts nothing into the person's folder, and buys no model turn; ctrl+c is read above a page that is loading or open (#1250). A stopped task reads stopped wherever its state word is drawn (#1258).
- **A time limit ends a run.** A run is handed what is left of the conversation's time; work in flight is ended and its endings are absorbed (#1262).
- **A dollar limit holds while a worker is still working.** A worker tells its run what it has banked as each call is paid for, without ever waiting on the run; a dollar is counted once, and what a run counts as spent never goes down (#1268).
- **A run's dollars reach the conversation's total.** The run hands its owner its running total whenever it rises, with or without a dollar limit, and the conversation closes on the run's final figure before any ending splits off, so every ending counts once (#1280).
- **An ending a person caused is not a fault.** A run ended by a limit says which one, `a time limit you set stopped it` or `a dollar limit you set stopped it`, with no fault colouring; the first limit reached names the ending, the tasks that ending cut read the same way, and a task that failed by itself keeps its own reason (#1279).
- **A run is handed what is left.** A run's dollar ceiling is the smaller of the conversation's dollar limits, including one typed on the command line, less what the conversation has already spent, so a second run gets the remainder after the first (#1281).
- **A cancelled command is ended by the call that ran it.** A cancel that arrived as a command started could leave it running under no parent; the cancel arm now sends the kill itself unless the call was adopted or already reaped (#1282).

- **A worker that has stopped making progress is told once, then ended.** The same command coming back with the same answer, with nothing moving under the worker's own task, brings one note from the belt saying what the worker can do; three more identical steps end the task with a reason a person can read. A task blocked on another task is parked, not ended (#1266).

## The task page and the rail

- The plan as a tree on the rail, a line saying what is happening now, a bounded read-only question about a run, a work tab that lists runs (#1204); a task's page opens from its row, and a run has a row of its own with its parts under it (#1231).
- A conversation whose engine runs in another process, which is the default, reads and steers its run over the wire (#1230).
- Step rows show the work: the run's bookkeeping is left out, commands are cut by byte span and never retyped, rows keep their recorded numbers (#1257); numbers continue across a wake (#1261); a call that never ran has no row, and a refused action is one dim line (#1260); the dim line under a row is only ever the row's own (#1265).
- Speed: a press on a run's row opens its page in under 0.2 seconds (#1251); a slow connection to the engine no longer freezes the screen (#1255); a stalled stream paints at the spinner's pace (#1235).
- Typing on a task's page goes to that task, never to the model as a message (#1244); a letter typed into a note never raises the stop card, and a finished task offers no verb the store would refuse (#1240).

## The engine host and sign-in

- A headless message or an opened task row that lands while a host is coming up reaches it, at no cost when no host is starting (#1272).
- A reconnect reuses its registered identity and reports a finished sign-in only after its listener is released (#1236).

## The profile

- Keys in `config.json` that nothing reads are said once, in the conversation, and never for a key the product itself writes or retired (#1223, #1239, #1245).
- Two profile writes compose, in one process (#1242) and across two processes, on every platform the repo builds for (#1248).

## Nothing keeps writing after the process closes

- The place sweep's note is sealed at close (#1227); the standing ticker belongs to the process and a pass in flight is cancelled at once (#1256); the usage writer is owned and closed at quit (#1259); the pool judge sweep is stopped and joined, and a landing the close interrupts is judged on the next start (#1267); the model catalog's own warm is cancelled and joined, and a fetch that lands after the cancel no longer writes (#1274); each process owns its place sweep, and close cancels the walk and joins it, so nothing is renamed or removed after close returns (#1276); a usage flush says whether it drained or reached its ceiling, and one ledger path's writer can be stopped and joined (#1285).
- A law lists every goroutine a conversation process starts and requires each to name its stop and its join (#1267, #1269).

## Tests and tooling

- The heavy-suite lock is a kernel file lock that works across process namespaces (#1264) and follows the suite, with a refusal that never calls a holder gone (#1270); the lock is held by a small holder beside the suite and never inherited by what the suite starts, so a process a test leaves behind cannot keep the machine locked (#1284). The full check cross-compiles every release target (#1254).
- Tests made independent of machine load or of the machine's state: #1203, #1211, #1221, #1226, #1228, #1229, #1237, #1238, #1246, #1247, #1249, #1252, #1263, #1278. A repeatable drive of a run on the real binary in hosted mode lives under `scripts/` (#1241).

## Also on the branch

- The lazy lexer registry (#1193). Answers lead with the action, number their steps and end on one next thing (#1209).

# Already on `dev` through #1194, kept for the record

What follows reached `dev` on 2026-09-18 as #1194 and is unchanged since.

## What a person gets

| Feature | What it does for you | How you use it | Where it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crew model family: open or all | The three crew words (frugal, balanced, max) answer from open-weight models only, or from every model including frontier ones. | `models.crew.source = open\|all` (default `all`), or the open/all switch in `/crew`. | On `santos/dev` (#1073) |
| Pareto crewing: crews computed from the live catalog | Crew presets are computed from OpenRouter's prices and quality indexes on the cost-quality front, refreshed daily, instead of a hand-picked table. Any seat can be `auto`. | `/crew catalog`, or `models.crew.pick = catalog`. | On `santos/dev` (#1093, squash 2fb296bf1) |
| Pick mode: `table`, `catalog`, `learn` | Choose the fixed table, today's catalog, or a crew learned from judged runs, per role (worker, checker, planner). | `/crew table\|catalog\|learn`, `models.crew.pick`. | On `santos/dev` (#1093, squash 2fb296bf1) |
| Learn: judged runs move the picks | After each chat `/task` run an independent judge scores every seat (billed to a `judge` seat). Scores go to your own sheet and feed the picker next time, blended with the pool by observation count, so your own runs improve your own picks first. Starts from a seed built from 145 real runs, so learning works on day one. A seat you type by hand is judged too. | Automatic under `pick = learn`. `codeaf pool show` lists what the picker knows. | On `santos/dev` (#1093, squash 2fb296bf1) |
| Model Pool: collective, text-free evidence | Every install can share its score rows through a relay and pull a signed index back, so everyone picks better because the others ran. Rows are computed numbers and ids under a per-install nonce: never code, prompts, paths or identity. | `model_pool on\|read\|off` (default `on`, notice shown once). `codeaf pool show\|status\|verify [--json]`. | On `santos/dev` (#1093, squash 2fb296bf1) |
| Public relay and GitHub mirror | The relay Worker ships in-repo under `relay/` with a runbook; it is live at `https://codeaf.agentfield.ai/pool`. The signed index is mirrored to the `model-pool` branch of this repo so anyone can watch it update. A team can run its own private relay with its own key (`CODEAF_MODEL_POOL_RELAY_URL`, `_MIRROR_URL`, `_PUBLIC_KEY`). | Nothing to do; works out of the box. | On `santos/dev` (#1093, squash 2fb296bf1) |
| The paper | `docs/design/model-pool/pareto-crewing.pdf` ("Pareto Crewing"): the objective, estimator and picker, with figures from real runs. | Read it. | On `santos/dev` (#1093, squash 2fb296bf1) |
| Named, multiple, switchable custom connections | Connect several OpenAI-compatible endpoints (local models, proxies), each with its own name, key and model list; switch between them, including mid-session; rename one and every stored pick follows. `/model` groups models under each connection's name. Switching onto a keyless default service is refused with a reason. | `/connect` → **Custom OpenAI-compatible API**; `/settings` → Providers → add / edit / active connection. | On `santos/dev` (#1092, squash 825ef2c41; Santosh e2e-tested locally against a local OpenAI-compatible proxy) |
| Worker harness: one loop under `/task` and `do` | The internal hands (patch, doc, web, image) become one worker loop with a plan store, shared by the chat `/task` door and `codeaf do`. | No new surface; fewer steps and lower cost per task (smoke: 4/4 parts in 28 steps vs 3/4 in 42). | #1109, draft, wave 1 landing |

Bug fixes on the branch (question answer-box keys, landing answer fate, retry avoiding the failed upstream, recovery evidence, taxonomy lane read, and, with #1092, mid-session `/connect` now reaching the live conversation on the engine road, a pre-existing hole) are not listed above; each has its own change note under `docs/changes/unreleased/`.

## Known limits, stated on purpose

- The learned picker is greedy on its estimate; there is no exploration yet, so a model that is never picked is never scored. The next algorithm pass (Thompson sampling, hierarchical cap, drift) is a follow-up PR.
- The judge runs on the chat `/task` door only; `codeaf do`, `ask` and remote sessions do not feed the pool yet.
- The pool index is read at start-up (24 h cache); `codeaf pool verify` pulls a fresh copy, read at the next start.
- A pool cell becomes readable at 3 rows, from one install or three (the paper says three installs); follow-up.

Live at `https://codeaf.agentfield.ai/pool` (healthz 200, index signed, `codeaf pool verify` good). The `model-pool` branch exists and carries the current signed index (refreshed hourly by a stand-in job until #1116 puts the workflow on `dev`). the settle turn a landing note wakes under `task.settle auto` runs under the checker's own bound, a call ceiling and a share of the run's cap, one call for a clean tree with no declared check, and records "not settled within its bound" instead of running to the wall, which had been a one-to-two-dollar tax on most headless runs (#1183); the chat-side `tasks` text and a resumed session's record line name a failed or unverified node's kept `task/<slug>` branch and its verdict word, the same two words the headless envelope carries (#1184); the identical-effects test is deterministic, its forty saves carrying distinct call signatures so the turn's repetition guard cannot end the turn and the leash is the only thing the assertion is about, which closes a margin-of-one race that had read as a load flake since #284 (#1185); a non-verified `codeaf exec` or `codeaf run` names its kept branch and verdict in its envelope through the one result-envelope seam the three headless doors share, so do, exec and run answer alike (#1186); a task worker parked on a command it started (a bash call the 30-second background clock promoted to a job) waited the node's whole allowance when the job never ended, which is what held a DOE run silent for 53 minutes under a live cap; the park now has a bound of its own, a third of the allowance, posts "the park was not settled within its bound" and hands the turn back while the command keeps running, with the diagnosis at docs/notes/yolo-task-worker-parked-on-promoted-bash.md (#1187); the model pool runbook's plan line says metered, not capped (#1188, #1189, docs only); the status row says `working` while the door's task subtree turns, read from the same signal the tab strip draws from so the two cannot disagree, with the manual's screen and task-page sections moved to match (#1191); a job subtree is cut when it passes a CPU or process bound, 60% of the machine sustained for 30 s or 128 processes when nothing else bounds it, the process backstop alone under a cgroup or affinity quota, and the run learns it as "the job subtree was not settled within its bound", which is what a model that spawns infinite loops under a dollar cap had escaped (#1190); a note records what a task's audit step can execute and where that boundary is set, the declared checks plus read-only git and coreutils, which is why a brief that declares no check leaves a cautious auditor nothing it may run (#1192, docs only); the prose lexer registry loads a curated set of forty languages on first use instead of parsing all 279 of chroma's lexers at init, plain text for the rest, which takes about 3 ms off cold start and 2 MB off the binary, with chroma's files and licence carried beside the copies (#1193). title: santos/dev: crew family, Pareto crewing and the Model Pool, custom connections

body:
`/model` lists 600 models. You can't scan it. This makes it scannable.

## Before

```
inference-net/schematron-v2-turbo        $0.03/$0.15 per M · 128k
~openai/gpt-astra-latest                       $10/$50 per M · 1M · sees
inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-vl   $0.06/$0.18 per M · 131k · sees · watches
nex-agi/nex-n2.5-mini:free                                 262k · sees
```

Every figure correct. No two rows put the same fact in the same place.

## After

Real renders, owner's live catalog, 108 cols. Opens alphabetical:

```
 › /model filter by name
  model ↓                                   in/M   out/M  window   elo  inputs
  deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1              $0.25   $0.95    163k  1135
  deepseek/deepseek-r1                      $0.7    $2.5     64k
  deepseek/deepseek-v3.2                   $0.27    $0.4    163k  1187
› deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash               $0.07   $0.14      1M  1220
```

**`alt+s` sorts by the next column, `alt+shift+s` walks back.** Every column is two
presses — its own direction, then reversed — so one key reaches every order:

```
  model                                     in/M  out/M ↓  window   elo  inputs
  ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-micro         $0.017    $0.11    131k
  deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731          $0.06    $0.12      1M  1252
  openai/gpt-oss-20b                       $0.03    $0.13    131k   947
```

**`→` opens a model's providers — two levels, their own table, their own sort:**

```
  deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash  coreweave   0.4s      1M   24
    auto                                           auto-route based on /settings — coreweave now
    openrouter
      provider    first ↓  t/s    $/M    up  note
›     coreweave      0.4s   24  $0.28   99%  tail 3s
      cloudflare     0.8s   58   $1.3  100%  no tools
      deepinfra      1.2s   27  $0.18   99%  out ≤ 65k
      default
```

Narrow frames fall back to the old tail — it's better per row, only worse down the
page.

## What else moved

**Columns, not verbs.** `sees` / `hears` / `watches` / `draws` / `films` / `speaks`
were six invented words each carrying a side *and* a thing. Now the catalog's own
nouns under `inputs` / `outputs`. Blank = text in, text out.

**Enter no longer closes the list.** It applies and stays open, so you can compare
two models and change back. `esc` closes.

**`auto` and `openrouter` sit together** — they're the two things you're choosing
*between*, and under `simple` routing they send the same thing. Dropped the bullets
(they claimed a distinction the wire doesn't make) and the dim paragraph that
re-printed each row's own numbers in prose. `enter` on `openrouter` opens it and
lands on `default`, which reads as "these exist, and you've chosen not to pick".

**The filter box searches names. Only names.** It used to also take `@cloudflare`,
`<1s`, `>50t/s`, `$<0.3`, `fp8`, `tools`, `fast`, `cheap` — a query language you had
to read a manual page to know existed. Those were questions about facts, and the
facts are columns now, so you can just look. Type `$<0.3` and you get an empty list,
not a silent reinterpretation.

**`→`/`←` stop fighting the caret.** They're the tree's keys unless you're mid-typing
(within 600ms of the last change to the box). Leaving an open fold used to cost one
press per character typed. Any edit takes the caret back, and `ctrl+b`/`ctrl+f` do it
without changing your query.

**One order for the foot, at every level** — grouped by what each key *moves*:

```
↑↓ pick · ← back · → providers · alt+s sort · enter <verb> · ctrl+t effort · esc
```

**Four things were plain broken.** `→ providers` and `ctrl+t` did nothing on home's
model list while the UI advertised both. The provider heading was drawn but not
counted, so the fold could overflow. `←` on `default` closed two levels at once.
And `openrouter` didn't name `→ providers` when nothing was measured, though the key
worked.

## Two bugs worth calling out

**The sort read the wrong lane.** `via`, `first` and `t/s` cells come from the lane a
row *names*; the sort asked `bestLane` instead. So rows with **blank** cells carried
real numbers into the sort and the blanks didn't group. One reading now serves both.

**An alphabetical default buried the best match.** `gpt` returned
`anthropic/claude-gpt-echo` above `gpt-5-classic` — the search itself going wrong.
The name column now orders by relevance first, alphabetically only inside a tier.

Both found by trying it against the real 521-row catalog rather than a fixture.

## Proof

`make pr-ready` + `make test-laws` green. 51 new tests, 30 new manual probes.
Manual updated, including a page that says the filter grammar is gone and points at
the columns instead — the old keystrokes are in its heading so they still retrieve.

Also fixes two `cmd/codeaf` update tests that failed on every macOS laptop and
passed in CI (`t.TempDir` gives `/var/...`, which the update door resolves to
`/private/var/...` on purpose). Product untouched.

Still red on clean `origin/dev`, not mine: `TestTheOpeningHintNamesBothDoors`,
`internal/release`'s ledger test (#1060).

body:
## What

The wordmark on the first screen — the setup block and the greeting — is drawn `CodeAF`, four rows tall, with the capital `A` and `F` on the same line as the `d`'s ascender.

```
          ╷     ┌─┐ ┌──
┌─  ┌─┐ ┌─┤ ┌─┐ │ │ ├─
│   │ │ │ │ ├─╴ ├─┤ │
└─  └─┘ └─┘ └─┘ ╵ ╵ ╵
```

## Why

`┌─┐ / ├─┤ / └─┘` is not an `a`, it is two closed bowls of equal size stacked on each other, and two equal closed bowls are an `8`. That was the second-to-last glyph of the product's own name on the first screen of every fresh install. The owner's call is for the two letters at the end to stand up out of the word as capitals.

A capital's top is the ascender's top, and three rows of box-drawing could not give it that: a bar is drawn at the *middle* of its cell and a stem reaches the cell's *edge*, so the `d` stood half a row over any capital however it was formed, and a stem in the bottom row hung half a row under the bowls' baseline the same way. The fourth row is that half a row made whole. The x-height letters live in the lower three rows; the capitals and the `d`'s ascender start in the top row, the ascender as the half-stroke `╷` so its top is the capitals' bar; and every stem that ends on the baseline ends as `╵`, which stops where `└─┘` does.

**The word is spelled `codeaf` and drawn `CodeAF`.** `product` is unchanged, the glyph table is still keyed by its lowercase letters, the ASCII fallback still gets the word `codeaf`, and the lowercase spelling law over sentences, titles and `--help` is untouched. Only the letterforms under two of its letters differ from the text.

## Also in here

- `internal/manual/chat/empty-screen.md` had been drawing the retired `aforge` letterforms — with the pre-terminal `e` — under the label "the codeaf wordmark". The name law walks text and cannot see a name spelled in box-drawing, so that page had been wrong in pictures since the rename. It draws the shipped forms now.
- The greeting's centring test read the unit's left edge off the wordmark's first row, which is now the cap line the x-height letters leave blank; it reads the second row. The assertion is unchanged.

Turns `dev` green. `TestASuccessfulHandoffJournalsTheRungThatSuppliedTheBrief` (`internal/session/carryladder_test.go:118`) failed in a full `make check` on `dev` at `da6e7a0e`: the worker's brief was the running model's draft instead of the mastermind's written handoff. It passed when run alone. Test-only change; no product code moves.

## Cause

The suspect was an errand (namer, title) stealing a scripted step, as in #392. That is not what happens. The mark's drawing is a sidecar (`sidecar.go`): it starts at the boundary that crosses the net and the turn goes straight on. How many rounds pass before the drawing lands is up to the scheduler, and a scripted round costs nothing. On a busy machine the turn ran 41 to 54 rounds against a 53-step script, the writer's ask landed past the end, the scripted completer answered with its past-the-end line `(unscripted)`, the handoff rung read as degenerate, and the carry ladder fell back to the draft.

## Fix

`checkpointAgent` now puts the existing `watchReadings` watch on the turn, and the checkpoint and carry-ladder tests submit through `watchedContext`. `answerWhenQuiet` holds each request that carries the belt until the readings beside it have landed, the order a real turn has, where a real model spends seconds per step. No assertions in existing tests change.

Regression test: `TestAHandoverWaitsForTheDrawingBesideItInsteadOfRacingIt` holds the drawing back by 200 ms and requires that the turn does not spend its script racing it and that the writer's rung still supplies the brief.

## Evidence (Spark, over ssh)

- Negative control: with the `watchReadings` line removed, the new test fails 3/3 (`the turn made 54 rounds while the drawing was in flight`). With it, 20/20 pass.
- `TestASuccessfulHandoffJournalsTheRungThatSuppliedTheBrief` 200/200 under 40 CPU burners with the fix.
- Full `go test -count=1 ./internal/session/`, **twice**, each from a fresh clone of `8f7fb007afe9a4a5e06cf1a005c4603b4a80cdee`: both `ok` (178.8 s, 179.5 s).
- The later commit on this branch adds only the changelog entry.

#1099 (`fix/session-git-holes` → `dev`) touches the same package. Whichever lands second should rerun `internal/session`.

body:
`codeaf do` works in the person's own directory, so its job root's workspace is
`OwnedByPerson`. `leafOutputHint` offered that root the overflow-document
address `exec.SuggestPathFor(node.ID, title)` — a workspace-relative
`task-<n>-<slug>.md` — while every intermediate leaf was already pointed at the
run's scratch. A root that took the offer left an untracked file at the root of
the person's tree. `Workspace.RecordChanges` observed it, `Workspace.Artifacts`
filed it, `jobArtifacts` joined it into the record the delivery gate is held to,
and the gate read a file the request never named as part of what was handed
over and refused the delivery; the run then ended incomplete over work that was
complete and committed.

There is no separate mechanical clean-tree check to exempt, so the fix is the
writer's, not the reader's: where the workspace belongs to the person, the job
root's file invitation is resolved through `Workspace.ScratchPath`, the same
address an intermediate leaf gets, and the withdrawal for a directory already
standing at that name is measured at the scratch spelling. The final message
still carries the deliverable.

Nothing is excluded by name. `Workspace.record` drops any path outside the root,
so a note written at the offered scratch address is never in the record; a file
that turns up in the person's tree while the leaf runs is still observed and
still lands in that record, whatever it is called.

Tests beside the touched package cover the three halves: a personal root is
offered a path under the run's scratch and the tree it was judged in is left
empty; a file appearing in the person's tree at a name wearing the same shape
still joins the record; a directory at the offered scratch path still withdraws
the invitation.

body:
Anonymous usage counts for codeaf: on by default, a notice printed once, off with `CODEAF_TELEMETRY=off`. The contract is `docs/TELEMETRY.md`; this PR is the whole pipe from the binary to the relay's door.

## What is sent

Four events, all coarse: `first_run` (once per install), `session_started`, `session_ended` (banded counts of turns, model calls, tool calls, failures, cost, duration, stop reason, exit code) and `fault` (a 16-hex fingerprint of codeaf function names at the crash site, never the message). Common properties are version, channel, OS, arch, usage context (local, CI, container) and install method. The distinct id is a hash of a random install id; no person profile is created and geolocation is off.

Never sent, and tests prove it: prompts, code, file names, paths, repo names, keys, email, IP, machine name, model slugs, raw error text. The relay strips unknown keys as a second wall.

## How it works

- `internal/telemetry`: the events, an allowlist, a local spool (`~/.codeaf/telemetry/spool.jsonl`, 50 per POST, 7-day age, 1000-line cap), one deadline-bounded flush at exit, and the opt-out ladder. Session counters are three atomic adds on the hot paths and count whether or not telemetry is on; only sending asks the ladder.
- `cmd/codeaf`: lifecycle in `execute` for chat, resume, do, exec, run and `plan run`; `codeaf telemetry status|show|on|off`; fault events from `reportFault` (main) and from `guard.Recover` through a hook (goroutine).
- `internal/config`: the `telemetry` setting row. A project file can only turn it off, never on.
- `scripts/install.sh`: records how the copy was installed and prints the notice; sends nothing.
- `scripts/release_downloads.py` and a daily workflow: public GitHub release download counters as one gauge event per asset per day.

## Off switches, in the order checked

`CODEAF_TELEMETRY=off|0|false`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, `telemetry = off` in the project file, `codeaf telemetry off`, an empty `CODEAF_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT`. Unstamped or dirty builds and test binaries never send. Nothing is sent before the notice has been shown.

## Verified

- Full `make check changelog-check test-laws` on Spark on this exact head (job id and result in the last comment). One failure is pre-existing on `dev` and untouched here: `internal/release` `TestPublishedPinExamplesGiveVersionToBash`, because `README.md` on `dev` no longer carries a `| VERSION=` pin example. It fails the same way on a clean `dev` checkout.
- A stamped build of this head ran two real task sessions against the production relay: a clean one arrived as `done` with exit 0 and the model-call band filled; an interrupted one arrived as `interrupted` with exit 3. The relay's own checks (schema, size, enum, unknown-key stripping) were exercised end to end.
- `internal/telemetry` and `internal/guard` pass under the race detector. Binary size stays under budget.

## Known limits

- `turns` is counted where the chat loop seals a turn, so task sessions report the 0 band for it.
- The notice is not printed under `--json` or when stderr is not a terminal in chat mode, and until it has been printed nothing is sent.

body:
## What failed

A node call that failed on the upstream machine OpenRouter routed it to was
retried up to three times as the same request. Each fresh attempt was built
with fresh knobs and — under the simple routing row — no `provider` object on
the wire at all, so the router's own default routing answered every attempt
the same way, all three landed on the same upstream, and the node ended with
`after 3 node call attempts: provider ended the response with
finish_reason=error` having produced no work.

## What the retry now does

An attempt that failed on a NAMED upstream — a relayed 5xx (`APIError.Provider`,
which is where a `finish_reason=error` reply is normalized to), or a cut stream
(`StreamCut.Provider`) — records that machine and the next attempt asks the
router not to use it. The names accumulate across the attempts of one call, so
the third attempt avoids the machines that failed the first two.

- The list rides the call's context (`provider.WithRetryAvoid`) the way every
  other per-call fact does, and is read once into `callKnobs`. It is built in
  the node's own retry loop, handed over per attempt, and gone when the call
  ends — nothing reaches a later call or a stored setting.
- On the wire it is `provider.ignore`, merged into whatever preference object
  the request already composed rather than replacing it: the sort word, a
  ranking and a demand all survive beside it. `only`, `order` and `ignore` are
  narrowed through one shared field law (`providerPrefs.strike`), which the
  per-call refusal list already followed, so two lists cannot carry two answers
  about how the three fields fit together.
- A machine a demand still names is never also written into `ignore`, and a
  demand the veto emptied stops being a demand.
- A person's pin for the model wins outright: nothing is ignored.
- A base that has not shown it carries a preference object, and a routing row
  of `off` — including the direct, one-road services that resolve to it — are
  left exactly as they were, so those requests are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- A failure that names no machine changes nothing; the retry goes where it
  always went.
- When every attempt fails, the final error names the machines that were tried.

Every request that does not fail this way carries an empty list and is
unchanged.

## Tests

New tests beside both touched packages: the retry carries the list and
accumulates it; a cut stream's name is carried; a failure naming nobody avoids
nothing; a relayed 4xx names no machine; the list does not outlive its call, at
the node loop and at the request body alike; the veto goes out on the next body,
rides beside a ranked road, stays off a road that asked for no preference
object, and never empties a demand it joined.

## How it was tested

Spark job `20260917-063523-000531`, revision `e1d0e75248273cbb1eddfac983313fcc7ff871b0`:
`go build ./...`, `go vet` and `go test -count=1` over `./internal/exec/...`,
`./internal/provider/...` and `./cmd/codeaf/...` — all green.

```
ok  internal/provider    71.7s

ok  cmd/codeaf           71.7s
```
