One pull request to `santos/dev`: **Pareto crewing** (the crew picker), the **Model Pool** with its judge, relay and mirror, the **paper**, and the fixes folded from #1097–#1102. `santos/dev` (through #1105) and `dev` (through #1106) are merged in, so this diffs cleanly against its base.

**Status:** ready for review on head `fd29d79a5`: full `make check` green on Spark at `cf4ea354c` (107 packages, EXIT 0), and `fd29d79a5` adds one runbook sentence on top (docs only). `santos/dev` `825ef2c41` (#1092) is merged in at `dc180fdfb`. Not to be merged until the owner has looked.

## What this brings

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Pareto crewing | The crew is picked on the cost-quality front, per role and per task, from evidence rather than a fixed table: `picked from` = `table` \| `catalog` \| `learn` | `internal/crewpick`, `internal/config/auto.go`, `/crew`, settings sheet |
| The judge | After a chat task lands, a model outside the crew rates each seat's work; the numbers feed the next pick and are billed to the `judge` seat | `internal/pool/judge`, `cmd/codeaf/poolrecord.go`, `session.Config.TaskLanded` |
| The Model Pool client | Signed, versioned index read daily with a cache and an embedded seed; a text-free outbox pushed under a per-install nonce; `model_pool` = `on` \| `read` \| `off`; `codeaf pool show \| status \| verify` | `internal/pool/{index,pull,poolcfg,outbox,record,tally}`, `cmd/codeaf/pool*.go` |
| The relay | One edge function, one store of per-install daily count/sum/sum-of-squares triples (rows folded in, the join for copies between stores), one hourly Ed25519 signing job, a per-install quota; a GitHub Actions mirror of the signed index every 6 h to the `model-pool` branch | `relay/`, `.github/workflows/pool-mirror.yml`, `docs/design/model-pool/RUNBOOK.md` |
| The paper | *Pareto Crewing*: objective, front and knee, the pool's statistics, the estimator and its constants, the Thompson picker with role-level feedback, the deployment; two referee reports and the response beside it | `docs/design/model-pool/pareto-crewing.pdf` |
| Seat on every usage row | `seat` (reflex, low, worker, high, mastermind, talk, judge) derived at the bank | `internal/session/usage_seat.go` |
| Fuel at the catalog's price | with a fallback table for the nine shipped ids, pinned by a test | `internal/config` |
| Folded fixes | `do` re-dispatch room (×3/2 per attempt, `redispatches` in the envelope); no git command without a directory, linked-worktree share; coverage round bought once, `core_done_seconds` in the envelope | #1098, #1099, #1100 (#1097 superseded by #1105's `provider.FailedLane`) |

**Pareto crewing in one paragraph.** The five seats (reflex, low, worker, high, mastermind) come from one of three places, chosen on the settings sheet under `picked from` or with `/crew`: `table` (default) is the rows we ship; `catalog` recomputes the three budgets from today's published prices and benchmark indexes — each seat priced on its own token shape, scored on the seat's own weighting of the intelligence, coding and agentic indexes, crews on the pareto front of bill against quality, `frugal` the cheapest, `max` the best, `balanced` the knee on a log-bill scale; `learn` is `catalog` with measurements on top — the pool's index, the seed shipped in the binary and the install's own judged runs enter each seat's score as a prior weighted by observation count, `N/(N+30)`. `crew` still says how much to spend, `models.crew.source` (open | all) which family; a tier row may say `auto` (catalog for that seat alone); a hand-typed model id always wins; every seat's rung says where its id came from.

**What leaves an install, and the switch.** `model_pool` is `on` by default. What is sent is computed, text-free numbers about the models the install ran (role, model, a number, judge, door, size bucket, day) under a per-install nonce — never code, prompts, paths or an identity; `codeaf pool status` shows exactly what is waiting. `read` uses the pool and sends nothing; `off` sends nothing, judges nothing, and picks from the catalog alone (`CODEAF_MODEL_POOL=off` for one run). A private relay is a copy of `relay/` under your own keypair: `CODEAF_MODEL_POOL_RELAY_URL` and `models.pool.public_key` point an install at it (runbook, "Run your own relay").

## How to e2e test this

Build the head in a fresh worktree and use an isolated profile:

```
git fetch origin feat/auto-crew && git worktree add ~/af-test origin/feat/auto-crew && cd ~/af-test
go build -o bin/codeaf ./cmd/codeaf
export CODEAF_HOME=$HOME/.codeaf-test CODEAF_PROFILE_DIR=$HOME/.codeaf-test
bin/codeaf pool show          # mode on · default, relay/index/submit addresses with sources, "built-in seed of <day>", own sheet: none
bin/codeaf pool status --json # can_read/can_send, index source "seed", own cells 0, pending 0, relay reachable or not
bin/codeaf                    # chat, in any small repo
/crew                         # crew word, family ‹open · all›, picked from
/crew learn                   # picked from = learn (/crew catalog, /crew table); /settings → Providers: crew · picked from · family · tier rows · model pool · pool key
/task <a small, checkable task>
```

The launch line under the task names the pick. What it chose on Spark on 2026-09-17 (head 4a3c5499b, family all, crew balanced), verbatim:

```
crew → balanced · learn · brain gpt-6-astra · hands gpt-5.6-sol · checks claude-fable-5.1
```

The task landed and committed in 5m19s; about a minute later (the judge runs on its own goroutine) the profile held:

```
$ cat $CODEAF_HOME/pool/own.json
{"schema":1,"cells":[{"metric":"role_quality","role":"worker","model":"openai/gpt-5.6-sol","dims":{},"n":1,"sum":100,"sumsq":10000}],"wins":[]}
$ cat $CODEAF_HOME/pool/outbox.jsonl
{"schema":1,"day":"2026-09-17","nonce":"5b6413931f5a7c52489fd894d000665f","payload":{"schema":1,"metric":"role_quality","role":"worker","model":"openai/gpt-5.6-sol","score":100,"judge":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731","door":"task","size":"M","day":"2026-09-17"}}
$ grep '"seat":"judge"' $CODEAF_HOME/v3/usage.jsonl
{"at":"2026-09-17T12:29:37-04:00","day":"2026-09-17","model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731","seat":"judge","calls":1,"in":747,"out":12132,"usd":0.01634292}
$ bin/codeaf pool show | tail -1
own sheet: 1 cell, 1 observation
```

(That run scored only the worker: both judge questions shared one 90 s deadline and the first answer took 64 s. Fixed on the same day and pinned by two tests — each seat's question now has its own 90 s — so a run on this head shows one cell per seat: worker and high.) The next `/crew` and the next task read those cells; a seat's rung turns `learned` when its own measurement outweighs the catalog. Then:

```
CODEAF_MODEL_POOL=off bin/codeaf   # /task … : no judge call, no rows, no judge usage row
bin/codeaf pool verify             # fetches with TTL 0 and checks the signature under the built-in key (relay must be up)
codeaf do "..." --json             # envelope carries redispatches and core_done_seconds
```

Set one seat only: a tier row = `auto` on the sheet or `models.tiers.worker=auto`.

## Testing

All runs on Spark over ssh in fresh clones of the pushed head; logs under `~/src/trees/check-<sha>.log` on the host.

- `~/src/trees/check-cf4ea354c.log` (this head minus one runbook sentence): full `make check`, 107 packages ok, EXIT 0, binary under the size budget; `14c36add3` (same Go code, before the priming script's user-agent line) passed the same run. Before it: `check-dc180fdfb.log` (the `santos/dev` `825ef2c41` merge) — build, vet, gofmt, cmd/codeaf, remote, catalog, config, manual ok; `check-0e0024ec5.log` full `make check`, 107 ok, before the last-judge line, the seed regeneration and the priming script; `check-9ee021a1c.log` the same on the head before the runbook's last two notes. The first full run on `96da9689c` (104 ok) caught two gaps, both fixed on the way: a change-note title over 100 characters and `CODEAF_MODEL_POOL_MIRROR_URL` missing from the env registry.
- `check-622af4f02.log`: cmd/codeaf pool/judge tests ok with the per-seat time-share tests. `check-0f984f981.log`: internal/tui3 ok after the pool-key row got its tab. `check-8a55527c4.log` (client A merged): cmd/codeaf, config, manual, the seven pool packages ok; tui3 caught the missing tab. `check-7b02b7ecf.log`: judge per-seat timeout, cmd/codeaf ok. `check-b9f18fa67.log` (relay): 50 node tests, manual, cmd/codeaf ok. `check-4a3c5499b.log`: build, vet, gofmt, cmd/codeaf, session, manual, config, pool/... ok. `check-651e753ed.log` (santos/dev + dev merge): session, exec, provider, taxonomy, manual, config ok. `check-8d92e4551.log`: full `make check`, 105 packages ok, before the hook/relay/client work.
- Proof run: `~/src/doe/peer/c036/` on Spark (result.json, own.json, outbox.jsonl, judge-usage.jsonl, crew-before/after frames, scrollback).
- End-to-end on `cf4ea354c` against the primed relay, 12 steps, all pass (report on the test host: `~/src/e2e-learn-2026-09-17.md`, with `KNOWN-LIMITS.md` and `evidence/INDEX.md`; 18 runs). The loop closes: a `/task` lands → a judge outside the crew scores each seat → the own sheet and the outbox fill → the rows reach the relay and the next publish → a fresh install reading that index picks differently under `learn` than one reading the built-in seed (the worker seat moves from the seed's flash model to the pool's `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`). Two residual notes, not blockers: a bare `auto` tier row labels its rung "computed from the catalog" rather than `learned` even when the measurement carried the pick; and the pool-picked worker lands on the current branch about two runs in three, the third ending on its task branch (the follow-ups below).

Change notes: every `1093-*` entry under `docs/changes/unreleased/`.

## Seed

`internal/pool/index/seed.json` (and the paper's Figure 6, `data/seed-cells.csv`) is regenerated at this head (`4e1e2e7fd`) from every scored run to date: 15 cells from 194 runs, up from 14 cells / 145 runs at the last regeneration. What moved, at the seat level: on the worker seat `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (83.3, n=34) now sits clearly above `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` (67.4, n=90) and `z-ai/glm-5.3` (72.5, n=38), and `meta/muse-spark-1.3` leads (94.1, n=15); on the check seat `qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902` (92.0, n=23) leads, `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` is at 87.1 (n=29) and `moonshotai/kimi-k3` at 86.2 (n=27), and `anthropic/claude-opus-5` is unchanged at 83.3 on n=4 (not enough to rank). A caveat that the paper states and the index carries as `n`: the cheaper workers were dealt smaller tasks (size is a covariate, not balanced), so a worker-seat gap between a flash model and a full one is partly a size gap. Those are the computed, text-free numbers the binary ships; the learner weighs them by `n` against the catalog prior.

The relay is primed from the same runs: `relay/tools/prime.py` turns the two scoring ledgers (kept outside the repository) into ordinary row submissions — the seed's own seat and score mapping, one install nonce per originating session, judge id `codeaf/reviewer` — and posts them once. Done on 2026-09-17: 385 rows over 10 install ids accepted, and the publish that followed is index version 1789681435 with 19 cells, mirrored to the `model-pool` branch — so an install that reaches the relay reads numbers on day one instead of an empty document. One probe row sent while diagnosing the edge's user-agent block is in the store too (the worker cell of one flash model holds 91 observations where the seed holds 90); left as is, one row in ninety. Nothing is counted twice: an install holds one index document at a time (`index.Fallback` — the cache when it parses and is not older by generated day than the built-in seed, else the seed; tested in `internal/pool/index`), never a blend of the two. The paper's architecture section says the same.

## Relay

Deployed from this branch's `relay/` (Worker `codeaf-pool`, KV id in `wrangler.toml`, signing key in the platform secret store, hourly cron plus publish-on-read, observability as in the dashboard). Live: DNS is in, `/pool/healthz` answers, the first index (version 1789669815, empty cells under `min_installs = 3`) was published and verified under the built-in key, and after priming the current one is version 1789681435 with 19 cells — on Spark, `pool status` from this head's binary says `relay: reachable · index version 1789669815` and `pool verify` says `signature good`. The mirror workflow can be dispatched only once its file is on the default branch, so the first mirror commit follows this merge; until then the mirror address answers 404 and the client reads its cache or the seed. `docs/design/model-pool/RUNBOOK.md`: `cd relay && wrangler kv namespace create POOL` → id into `wrangler.toml`; `… | wrangler secret put POOL_SIGNING_KEY` (the private seed lives outside the repository); `wrangler deploy`; the DNS placeholder record for `codeaf.agentfield.ai` (proxied); Actions write permission; one dispatch of the mirror workflow. Until then every install reads the built-in seed and its own runs, and `pool status` says the relay is unreachable.

## How the team joins

1. Build from `santos/dev` once this lands (`make build`, then `bin/codeaf`). Nothing to configure: `model_pool` is `on` by default, the relay and mirror addresses are built in, and the signer's public key is compiled in.
2. What the defaults already do: every `/task` that lands in a chat-door conversation is scored by a judge model outside the crew (billed to the `judge` seat, shown in `/usage`); the scores go to the own sheet (`<profile>/pool/own.json`) and, as text-free rows, to the outbox, pushed at start-up and after each judged run. The crew's seats still come from the shipped table until you switch the row.
3. To let the numbers pick the crew: on the settings sheet set `picked from` to `learn` (or type `/crew learn`; stored as `models.crew.pick`). `learn` = the catalog's cost-quality front blended with the pool's measurements by observation count (`N/(N+30)`), your own sheet included — so each judged run moves your next pick. `catalog` is the same without measurements; `table` is the shipped rows. A hand-typed model id on a tier row always wins.
4. What you will see: `codeaf pool status` prints `relay: reachable · index version N`, the index line (generated day, age, min installs), `own sheet: K cells, M observations`, `pending P` rows in the outbox and the last judge line (model, seats scored, or the candidates tried and why); `codeaf pool show` prints the mode and each address with its source; `codeaf pool verify` fetches with TTL 0 and checks the signature under the built-in key. A new index document is read at the next start.
5. Where to watch on GitHub: the `model-pool` branch, `pool/index.json` and its `.sig`, mirrored from the relay; the badge on the README's Model Pool section shows when it last moved. It carries the signed document only — no count, no leaderboard.
6. Opting out: `model_pool = read` keeps the judge and the own sheet local and sends nothing; `off` asks no judge at all and reads nothing (`CODEAF_MODEL_POOL=off` for one shell). `picked from = table` at any time returns the crew to the shipped rows.

## In, and not in

In: catalog crew and its knee; `picked from` and the ladder; shrinkage blend `N/(N+30)`; index reader, signed pull, cache, seed; outbox, install nonce, push at start-up and after each judged run; the judge, its deterministic choice, the chat-door hook, the `judge` seat; own sheet feeding the next pick; settings (`model_pool`, `models.pool.public_key`, `picked from`); relay code, mirror workflow, runbook; the paper.

Not in (follow-ups, separate pull requests):
- The learner's cleverer pass: the Thompson draw in the picker (`explore` setting), the hierarchical cap ℓ with its moment estimators in place of the count fold, drift forgetting, the settled probability π*, the crew-as-a-group pair term — all specified in the paper.
- The judge hook on the headless doors; `codeaf do` taking `auto` crews through the same seam. Seen on this head (e2e step 12, `~/src/e2e/peer/c088/do.stderr`, `homes/D12/logs/calls.jsonl`): under `picked from = learn` with the pool read, `codeaf do` still seats its worker from the table row (`work z-ai/glm-5.3-flash (crew balanced, table)`) while `exec` and the chat door on the same profile pick the pool-learned worker. Suspect: `do` resolves its seats keyless before the run (`cmd/codeaf/do.go`, `config.LoadKeyless` → `useAutoSeats` → `ResolveSeats`), so on a profile with no catalog cache the rows never arrive inside the 3 s bound and the seat falls to the table rung as designed — `exec` loads with the key first. Fix PR after the merge.
- The fixed table becoming generated output checked by a test.
- Relay deploy and the first mirror commit (above).
- Seen in the e2e rerun on this head, not blockers, fix PRs after the merge: (a) a `/task` under `learn` implemented the change and passed its tests, then ended `paused — it resumes` with no takeover, no `/new` and one codeaf on the home; ~44 s earlier the mastermind seat had failed twice with `context deadline exceeded` (the picked model, then its fallback), the node paused at "formatting and checking focused packages" with no model call after it, and its record has `canceledBy`/`cancelReason`/`endedBy` null and merge aborted — suspect: the planner seat's deadline cancels the task's lifecycle context (evidence on the test host: `~/src/e2e/homes/A2/v3/projects/…c077…/transcript.jsonl`, `logs/calls.jsonl`). (b) A decision card ("how should it proceed", land vs leave) stopped a `/task` under `--yolo` (c059 in the same harness); under yolo a question must not stop the node, or must take the default. (c) A worker committed to its task branch but the merge to the current branch failed, so the task did not land and the judge was never asked (c082, and the c077/c059 shapes; evidence on the test host: `~/src/e2e/homes/C2`) — a failed merge should still be a landing the judge sees, with the merge failure as the finding. Read again from the record: that run ended `unverified` because the process was stopped while its work was being checked, and a node closed by a process exit takes the store's road, which has no judge — so the real gap is (d): a record left `unverified` by a dead process is never judged afterwards; a start-up pass over the previous life's unverified records could hand them to the judge. A real merge conflict is judged today (every final state reaches the hook).

title: Pareto crewing: the crew picker, the Model Pool with its judge and relay, and the paper

body:
Closes #1089.

`/connect` → **Something else** used to hold exactly one custom connection: the id was the
literal `custom`, so connecting a second custom service replaced the first, the display name
was auto-derived with no way to type your own, and an IP-literal host produced a name nobody
could read. This makes a custom connection a named, repeatable thing, and makes the one the
conversation is talking to something you can flip from either door.

## What changed

**Ids are the persistence vocabulary; the written name is the routing prefix.**
`internal/modelsource` mints `custom` for the first connection and `custom-<slug>` for each
one after, so several coexist and `persistConnectedSource` no longer upserts them onto each
other. `SourceSlug` reads a host whole instead of taking its last dot-separated label, so
`127.0.0.1` answers `127-0-0-1` (not `0`), IPv6 literals keep their groups in order
(`fe80::1` → `fe80-1`, `::1` → `ipv6-1`), a zone id is cut before the host is read, and a
literal that reduces to nothing falls back to the plain custom id.

**One backend, two doors.** The validate-and-persist step lifted out of
`internal/tui3/modelservices.go` into `internal/config/custom.go` (`PrepareCustomSource`,
`ActiveConnectionFor`, `RenameConnectionModels`), so `/connect` and `/settings` → Providers
both call it rather than each carrying its own copy. The add row is offered on both surfaces
whenever a connection can be added — including on an empty profile — and carries an id no
real connection can mint, so it can never collide with one.

**The active connection is derived, never stored.** It is read from the conversation's live
model, not from a slot in a shared profile file, so two conversations on different
connections each see their own. Enter on the active-connection row walks a ring that includes
the default (non-custom) connection, so switching back is the same single action as switching
away. A switch that arrives while a turn is working is deferred and spent when the turn
settles; the panels refresh only when a settle actually moved the conversation, so an idle
settle no longer sends an open panel's cursor back to the top or clears a standing disconnect
confirmation.

**A rename carries everything it named.** Role models persist in the crew tier rows, written
with the connection's name as their prefix. `RenameConnectionModels` re-prefixes every stored
row and writes them in one atomic profile write, validating each new value first, so a rename
cannot half-apply and leave some roles pointing at a name that no longer exists.

## Acceptance (issue #1089)

| Acceptance bullet | Where |
|---|---|
| Connect a custom service and be prompted for a name; it shows up under that name | name step in the connect flow, resolved through `Collides`; `connectionswitcher_test.go` |
| Connect a second custom service; both coexist | per-instance ids in `internal/modelsource`; `custom_test.go` |
| An IP-literal address produces a sensible name | `SourceSlug`; `modelsource_test.go` table |
| Add, rename and switch the active connection from `/settings` → Providers without opening `/connect` | `internal/tui3/settings.go` Providers rows on the shared `internal/config` door; `addrow_test.go` |
| A custom connection fronting a non-OpenAI-dialect model completes a turn | the `provider`-object-off retry already reaches a custom base; pinned here by `internal/provider/refusal_test.go` so it cannot regress |

**`/model` groups models by connection** — the last of the issue's "Where each piece lands"
items. The picker already grouped by connected service (`modelsFor` in `internal/tui3/palette.go`);
what this PR adds is the coverage that keeps it true for *several* custom connections:
`TestTwoCustomConnectionsGroupApartInThePicker`, `TestRenamingACustomConnectionMovesItsPickerHeading`
and `TestACustomConnectionWithNoListKeepsItsPlaceInThePicker`.

**Switching onto a keyless default service is refused**, the way an empty model list already is,
so the switcher can no longer hand the conversation a state whose first send opens a key door
nobody asked for. One helper, `defaultServiceHasKey`, now answers that question for both the
switcher and the key prerequisite.

**A minted custom id carries only plain characters** (`modelsource.IDWord`): lowercase, runs of
anything else become one dash, and a name that reduces to nothing answers `connection`. The
written name and every id already persisted are untouched.

## A mid-session connect now reaches the conversation that is open

Interactive `codeaf chat` runs its conversation on an `engine --daemon` process. That door
registered nothing it built, so a profile broadcast reached no conversation and an agent kept
the account set it was born with. A service connected mid-conversation therefore matched no
member of that set, and its qualified model id fell through to the default service with the
prefix still on it — a 400 about a model no router publishes, read by the person as *the
request could not be sent as it was*.

| in one `codeaf chat` process | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| connect, then a turn in the same conversation | 400 | works |
| connect, `/new`, then a turn | works | works |
| connect, restart the binary, then a turn | works | works |

**This is pre-existing and not introduced by #1089.** Any mid-session `/connect` of any service
on the hosted road behaved this way; custom connections are simply the first case where a person
routinely connects mid-session and is switched onto it in the same breath. The fix is a paired
register/forget tied to the engine session's lifecycle: the engine registers every conversation
it builds — boot, `/new` and `/resume` — and releases it through a new `Engine.Closed` door,
told on both roads a conversation ends. Registering without releasing would grow the held list
for the life of a daemon that outlives every conversation in it, which its own test pins across
eight open/close cycles.

**No billing moved.** The 400 names no upstream, so it classifies as a malformed request
(`ActionReshape`) and ends the turn. The deepseek and openrouter rows beside it in `calls.jsonl`
are the separate title and router lanes, which run alongside every turn and end with
`context canceled` when the turn dies. The turn itself never retried onto another model.

**What the evidence is worth.** One test fails on the unfixed tree: a structural law that reads
the engine door with `go/ast` and counts the conversations it builds against the ones it
registers (`bootEngine builds 3 conversations and tracks 0`). The others pin pieces that did not
exist before the fix, so they cannot fail first by construction. That law is brittle — it counts identifiers inside a function named `bootEngine`, so a refactor that moves
the build behind a helper would make it pass while the defect returned. Its failure messages name
both numbers so a reader can see what it actually checked. A behaviour-level equivalent would
need a live wire harness and would pass before the fix anyway, since the held list is only ever
empty on the engine road.

## Evidence

- `make check` green on this exact head, run on the Spark cluster over ssh from a fresh clone of
  `191cf579a70cbd70ee1db80efdf2caa46ecaec5d`: **99 packages ok, 0 failures**, binary
  53,149,961 bytes (under the 54,600,000 size budget).
- The branch carries `santos/dev` merged in at `3b97f50c`, so that run covers exactly what would
  land rather than a stale base.
- The engine fix was additionally proved on its own head before it was merged here: `cmd/codeaf`,
  `internal/remote` and `internal/session` each green from an isolated clone, plus
  `scripts/laws.sh` over 117 files and 27 packages.
- ~3,000 added lines, of which more than half are tests: `custom_test.go`,
  `connectionswitcher_test.go`, `addrow_test.go`, `modelservices_test.go`,
  `modelsource_test.go`, `refusal_test.go`, `chatv3_track_test.go`, `closeddoor_test.go`.

## What the review passes changed

The branch went through an architecture review, a correctness review, and a final read-only
review of the whole diff, each followed by a fix pass for the findings that were verified
against the code. Three of those are worth calling out, because each is a behaviour a reader
would otherwise have to trust:

- **An open panel re-ranked on every settled turn**, sending the cursor back to the top and
  clearing a standing disconnect confirmation. The refresh is now gated on a settle that
  actually moved the conversation — `TestASettleWithNothingToSpendLeavesTheConnectPanelWhereItWas`.
- **A rename during a working turn could silently eat a pending switch.** The person presses
  enter on the switcher row, is told the move waits for the turn to finish, then renames a
  connection — and the promised move disappeared. The re-spelling of the frozen live pick is
  bookkeeping and may now claim the deferred slot only when it is empty; a pending move always
  wins, carried under the new name if the rename was its own. Three tests cover the three
  cases (pending on another connection, pending on the renamed one, nothing pending).
- **Nothing tested that a second add mints a second id.** If the mint had regressed to
  answering `custom` again, `persistConnectedSource` would have replaced the first connection
  by id and the suite would have stayed green while the "both coexist" acceptance bullet
  broke. `TestPrepareCustomSourceMintsAFreeIdForEveryAdd` now walks `custom`,
  `custom-<name>`, and the numeric tiebreak twice.
title: connect, settings: named, multiple, switchable custom connections (#1089)

## What

The identity codeaf stamps on the commits it lands was `codeaf <codeaf@localhost>`. No git host can link `codeaf@localhost` to an account, so every branch codeaf landed failed the CLA check on the author line — CLAassistant reported "codeaf seems not to be a GitHub user".

The author is now `codeaf <agentfield-bot@users.noreply.github.com>` — the same identity the `Co-Authored-By` trailer already names. The two older local addresses (`codeaf@localhost`, `aforge@localhost`) stay recognised by `taskCommitIdentity`, so task work from before this change still lands as the harness's own.

## Why the address and not the identity

The author line is load-bearing, not decoration: a sibling landing reads it to tell the harness's own forward progress from a person's intervening work (`internal/session/task_branch_protection.go` says so). So this moves the address rather than removing the marker.

## Changes

- `internal/session/task_branch_protection.go` — `codeafGitEmail` is the bot address; the old pair joins `aforge@localhost` as legacy, and `taskCommitIdentity` recognises all three.
- `cmd/codeaf/chatv3_place.go` — the session-opening empty commit uses the same address.
- `internal/manual/chat/how-tasks-run.md`, `internal/manual/chat/permissions.md` — the identity as documented.
- `internal/session/attribution_test.go`, `task_rename_compat_test.go`, `cmd/codeaf/chatv3_place_test.go` — pin the new author and assert the legacy pairs still classify.

## Tests

- `go build ./...` — clean
- `gofmt` — clean
- `go test ./internal/session/ ./internal/exec/ ./cmd/...`

body:
Closes #1077.

## The defect

A landed task's `your call` was re-raised byte-identical on every node move while the node stayed unverified, even after the person answered it — the session that reported it accepted the same card twelve times in an hour. Three gaps made the loop:

1. The raise consulted nothing about the answer. The replay road got that consultation in #1036; the raise door (`EventTaskUpdate` → `publishLandingQuestion`) never did.
2. The card never said what became of the last answer, so the twelfth read as though the first eleven were ignored.
3. An in-flight accept did not suppress the re-raise, so the answer's own settle notices brought the card back within seconds, with no new fact.

## The fix

- **`TaskNotice.Settling`** names the resolution in flight over a landed node, in the claim's own words, copied from the graph's own claim fields at the one place node-update notices are built (never stored — no second source of truth). A notice naming a resolution in flight raises nothing and withdraws nothing — except a changed decider, which redraws at once with the new holder — and `resettle` hands the settle's claim back inside its locked write, so a settle's own terminal notice still raises. The two claim doors (a settle and a merge round) refuse each other, and neither may start over the other's claim.
- **The raise consults the record the way the replay does**: `landingQuestion` runs `decidedAlready` over the decision diary, and a re-raised card leads its reason with the answer's fate — `accepted 18:20 · nobody could check it` — composed by `landingAnsweredStamp` in the lane's own vocabulary. The take-down before every mint keeps the re-raise honest: the bank held the old card against the raise's own law, so a terminal notice could re-emit a flight stamp after the flight ended.
- **Replayed-card answers record decisions** whenever the synthesized question can be read back, closing the 14-receipts-vs-12-records gap so the fate survives restarts and fresh windows; an answer whose question cannot be read back (the restore race) writes nothing, per the record door's own law.
- **Killed re-audits and failed merge rounds release-then-emit**, so the question comes back with the answer's fate on it — the kill and the round's failure live on the job row and the node's kept report — instead of being held down or silently swallowed.
- **tui3 draws the reason row when it is news** the newest done card cannot have; the card already draws the ask's own reason.

One ordering note: the record is written after the lane takes the answer (a decision recorded for work that never resolved would refuse the next question for no reason), so the settle's *own* terminal notice raises without the fate on a first answer; every raise after the record exists carries it.

## Verification

`go build ./...`, `go vet`, and the seven #1077 tests (fate stamp, hold-down + terminal raise, decider redraw, terminal-stamp retirement, claim doors, notice naming, tui3 fate row) green, plus the full `internal/session` and `internal/tui3` suites on the Linux test box. One known unrelated failure on the dev machine: `TestLegacyRegisteredWorktreeResumesLandsAndCleansUp` fails identically on clean `origin/main`.

Three review rounds done (engine correctness; record and surface; final hygiene) with their findings fixed on the branch.

—
Drafted with [agentfield ai](https://agentfield.ai/github?utm_source=github&utm_medium=pull_request&utm_campaign=drafted_with) · reviewed and owned by the author
title: An answered landing carries its answer's fate, and an in-flight settle holds the question down

`https://agentfield.ai/get/codeaf` has served `scripts/install.sh` from this repository's `main` since 2026-09-16, the day the repository went public. Two pages still said otherwise; this change makes them true.

## What was true, and what is true now

- **`internal/manual/chat/running-from-the-terminal.md`** (compiled into the binary, read by the chat's `manual` tool) said the repository is private, that the raw installer answers 404 to anyone not signed in, and that `https://agentfield.ai/get/codeaf` "is not serving yet". The section now opens with the proxied line the README prints, describes the raw GitHub line as the script under it, and states the channel path (`/dev`, `/staging`, `/rc`) beside the `bash -s --` flags. The heading is unchanged, so every probe that reached it still does.
- **`docs/GUIDE.md`** headed the installer section "The installer, and what it is waiting on", said the route was "written and unmerged", called a source checkout "the road that works today", and said the repository has no rc or staging publication. The installer now comes first under `## Install` (the README links `#install`), the clone line no longer says it needs repository access, and the channel sentence is stated as a condition rather than a date: a push to `dev`, `staging` or `main` publishes that channel's build, and a channel with nothing published stops with `no <channel> build has been published yet`.

Both pages now say to pipe into `bash`, not `sh`: the script uses `set -o pipefail` and `[[ ]]`, and `sh` is dash on Debian and Ubuntu, which rejects both. The manual also says what the proxy refuses — a script without its channel line exactly once, or a body that is not a shell script, is a 502 rather than the wrong thing — because that is what the route does.

Not changed, because it is still what the code does: "Nothing self-updates: run the line again when you want a newer build." There is no `internal/update` on `dev`.

## Verified

The proxied line was run for real against the live site into a scratch home: `curl -fsSL https://agentfield.ai/get/codeaf | bash` exited 0 and installed v0.2.0; `/get/codeaf/dev` installed that day's dev build; the bare body is byte-identical to the raw script; each channel path differs from it by exactly the channel line.

`make pr-ready` is green (laws and manual gates; no Go file changed, so no touched packages). `go test ./internal/manual/ ./internal/namelaw/` pass.

Adds a model-family toggle to the crew: the same three preset words (`frugal`, `balanced`, `max`) can now resolve against either the open-weight table this build ships, or the whole catalog with closed/frontier models in it.

## What changes

- **`models.crew.source`** (new setting row, `model family`, right under the crew row). Values `open` (default) and `all`. Profile-only, like the tier rows.
- **`crewAllModels`** in `internal/config/crew.go`: the same three presets answered from the whole catalog. The open table is byte-for-byte untouched, and a profile that never answers the row resolves exactly what it did before.
- **`CrewModelsForSource(source, preset)`** plus `CrewSourceAt`; `CrewModels(preset)` keeps its signature and delegates with `open`, so no existing caller rippled. `CrewAt` and `ApplyCrew` resolve through the source row, so the crew word and the five ids it summarizes can never be drawn from different families.
- Manual paragraph under the crew section.

## The two families

**open** (default, unchanged):

| seat | frugal | balanced | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| reflex | `mistralai/mistral-nemo` | `mistralai/mistral-nemo` | `mistralai/mistral-nemo` |
| small work | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` | same | same |
| worker | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` | `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | `z-ai/glm-5.3` |
| careful | `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | `moonshotai/kimi-k3` | `moonshotai/kimi-k3` |
| mastermind | `z-ai/glm-5.3` | `moonshotai/kimi-k3` | `moonshotai/kimi-k3:high` |

**all** (new):

| seat | frugal | balanced | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| reflex | `google/gemini-2.5-flash` | `google/gemini-2.5-flash` | `google/gemini-2.5-flash` |
| small work | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` | same | same |
| worker | `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` | `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` | `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` |
| careful | `google/gemini-3.8-flash` | `anthropic/claude-opus-5` | `openai/gpt-6-astra` |
| mastermind | `anthropic/claude-opus-5` | `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` | `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` |

Both tables keep the crew's existing laws: the worker column is the spend dial, and the careful seat is a different vendor from the worker in every preset (asserted by a test over both families).

## Design notes

- The toggle changes what the preset words **mean**, not the five ids on disk. Flip the family and re-pick the crew; until then the crew word reads `custom` against the new family, which is true.
- Ids picked off the catalog's own published Artificial Analysis scores (intelligence / coding / agentic) against blended price, seat by seat by the work each seat does.

## Not in this PR yet

- The `/crew` picker's open/all selector (sibling slice, in flight).
- The `docs/changes/unreleased/` entry needs the real PR number: `make changelog-new PR=<n> KIND=added SLUG=crew-model-family`.

## Verification

`go build ./...` clean. `go test ./internal/config/...` green, including: the careful-seat-different-vendor invariant over both families; the all family pinned to the locked ids and passing the tier gate; an untouched profile resolving the open family byte-for-byte and an unknown source word reading open silently; flipping to `all` and re-applying a preset writing the all ids and reading `balanced`.

—

Drafted with [agentfield ai](https://agentfield.ai/github?utm_source=github&utm_medium=pull_request&utm_campaign=drafted_with) · reviewed and owned by the author

## Scope note: what "law 1" means here

The review loop was briefed that a profile which never answered resolves
byte-identically to before. That is true of the **family mechanism**: with no
`models.crew.source` row, nothing about resolving a preset changed.

It is **not** true of the **roster**: the open table's frugal mastermind and its
balanced careful and mastermind seats moved in this same PR, and so did the
shipped default crew (which is exactly the balanced row). A never-answered
profile now gets `kimi-k3` where it used to get `qwen3.8-27b` and `glm-5.3`.

That move is deliberate and disclosed: it is in the change entry, and the manual's
open table shows the new ids. It is kept in this PR rather than split out because
the roster decision and the toggle were made as one piece of work. If a reviewer
would rather see them apart, say so and the roster change comes out into its own
PR with its own entry.

Home now replaces its flattened tasks section with **sessions**, showing the fifteen most recent conversations. Its heading opens the renamed **Sessions** tab.

Home and conversation screens used different message-box controls, navigation could act on a stale mouse selection, and task activity was spread across competing lists. This change aligns the controls, makes Escape a consistent way back, and keeps Home, tabs and the chats menu in sync.

## UX changes

- **Broader explicit task retry:** stopped, interrupted, errored and incomplete ordinary tasks, quick tasks, designs and saved workflows can retry in place. Quick tasks retain their checklist and previous finding; designs and workflows restart through their original runners. New design/workflow records persist restart inputs across process restarts. Successful/running tasks, read-only views, and separate background-job/adaptive-run summaries do not offer the task retry action. Legacy records without runner inputs fail with an actionable explanation.
- **Conversation-first Sessions tab:** only running and completed sections, newest recorded activity first by default; clicking age reverses the order. Each conversation and all its tasks move together as work starts or settles; queued, waiting and unanswered work stays in running. Trees start fully expanded, Home titles and conversation bullets are shared, missing metadata never promotes tasks into top-level rows, and time windows retain complete trees. Tree connectors show ancestry, collapse arrows sit immediately after titles in the left/name column, and project has a separate column instead of a title suffix. Removed the redundant tasks prefix and retired sort shortcuts. Filtering preserves category and selection follows rows as activity reorders them.
- **Less duplicate spend information:** Home’s spend heading stands alone; today’s cost and allowance remain on the top line. Panel charts and the heading’s link are unchanged.
- **YOLO for interactive conversations:** unconfigured interactive conversations use `allow`, including remote conversations. Ordinary destructive operations such as file overwrites, `rm -rf build`, `git reset --hard` and `git clean -fdx` can run without asking. Tool-specific rules and the critical-command floor remain in force. Headless runs default to prompting/refusing unless explicitly authorized through local `--yolo` or saved approval settings. Invalid saved values fall back to asking. A headless connection cannot reuse an already-open interactive agent.
- **Shared message boxes:** the seam shows the full model identifier in bold color, separately styled `model:effort`, approvals and a project control with hover feedback. Home uses Option/Alt+P for project. Both surfaces use Option/Alt+E for effort and Option/Alt+A for approvals. Shift+Enter inserts a newline, including correct cursor and placeholder behavior on Home. Project selection is sticky across keyboard and mouse controls; paths preserve their absolute root or home-directory tilde and truncate on the right.
- **Clear submission and commands:** Enter on an unselected Home draft starts a conversation; `/ask` submits to a Home answer pane with an animated activity indicator. Slash commands appear alphabetically in a scrollable, live-filtered list above the seam on both surfaces. Removed `/approvals`, `/yolo` and the old Home submission rows. Folder pastes remain text after an attachment refusal; the project-start offer only arms on a folder pasted into an empty Home box and expires on the next non-Enter input.
- **Predictable navigation:** Escape backs out of the current layer and ultimately reaches Home. Double-space navigation is removed. Conversation footers say `esc home`, task conversation footers say `esc main`, and the Sessions, Spend and Settings tabs say `esc home` at rest. Filters and editors retain their own dismissal hints. Clicking Home’s “since you left” heading opens Memory.
- **One conversation list and one title:** Home has one deduplicated Sessions list with the fifteen most recent conversations, combining open tabs and saved history; closed history is dimmed. Closing a conversation also closes its tab and chats-menu entry. One generated five-to-eight-word title supplies both Home and tabs, truncated to fit; prompts label new conversations until naming finishes, and empty unsent tabs are not saved. Bullets distinguish answering, unread and unanswered-question states.
- **Questions on the relevant row:** removed the “needs you” heading and empty placeholder. An amber question mark identifies the conversation or task awaiting an answer, with its answer actions preserved. Questions without a visible matching row remain reachable as unheaded rows; compact layouts avoid duplicate conversations.
- **Consistent row actions:** the latest mouse or keyboard navigation owns the single selection. Right opens actions in Home’s description column. The empty Home message box advertises `→ options` first in its footer, including compact Home. Conversation and task actions use `x close`, `n new in project`, `o open folder` and `p copy project` where applicable; closing preserves history and running work.
- **Task interface cleanup:** incorporates `codex/task-interface-cleanup`, including the fixed conversation sidebar header, task creation order, simpler sidebar chrome and retrying incomplete tasks from their task screen. Task pages and Home keep current task records reachable.
- **Approvals and provider context:** live approval choices persist in conversations and work over remote connections; Home’s choices carry into the new conversation. Engine reattachment replays the last serving provider. The integrated workflow and current `dev` changes are included in this branch.

Manual pages and change entries accompany the behavior changes. Modifiers display as Option on macOS and Alt elsewhere.

- **CI regression repairs:** credential replies cannot become draft tab titles, Sessions retains its running animation and short-window priority, task decisions do not duplicate their question mark on a parent conversation, and Settings displays its live model filter. Older tests now assert the requested titles, navigation, list structure and selection behavior.

- **Latest dev integration:** merged `dev` through `49b4a58fb`, preserving the Sessions trees and message-box controls alongside the new task runner. Run tabs keep their own view without duplicating or renaming conversations in Home, Sessions, or the chats menu. Settings filters keep their cursor in the visible field; the compact task rail cannot reorder the cached Sessions tree. The new headed model picker retains its provider controls and sorting independently of Sessions. Draft model reasoning is reflected in Home’s seam, with explicit message-box effort taking precedence.

## Review fixes

- Saved approval posture and effort are restored through the shared direct/picker/engine opening path. The gate is restored before agent construction; restoration failures stop opening rather than silently using a permissive default. Explicit `--yolo` wins without changing the saved choice, and restored conversation choices do not become the default for new conversations.
- Remote protocol 17 rejects version 16 peers before changed question clarification/replacement semantics can cross. Remote headless callers identify themselves, and incompatible interactive/headless reuse is refused before the connection takes ownership.
- Closing a Home tab consults live conversation ownership instead of treating its identity-only close-stack entry as another window.
- Model control tokens are rejected from generated titles and ignored when reading old saved titles.
- Removed deleted task-state wording, rewrote the change entry to describe only final behavior, corrected the project-shortcut description, and clarified YOLO's actual scope in the UI and manual.
- Proposed standing preferences and design rules are separated into draft [#1334](https://github.com/Agent-Field/CodeAF/pull/1334) for owner confirmation.

## Validation

- Focused regressions pass for approvals, headless defaults, picker reopening, ownership after closing, title tokens and remote protocol compatibility.
- Manual retrieval regression and focused model-picker, sorting, composer and Home effort regressions pass.
- Full local `make pr-ready` passed on `78ddda475`: build, vet, formatting, packed manuals, changelog, manual retrieval, repository laws, and fresh tests for all seven touched packages.
- All GitHub checks passed on `78ddda475`: [PR gate run](https://github.com/Agent-Field/CodeAF/actions/runs/35643247021) plus CLA status.
- `make build` rebuilt the canonical `bin/codeaf`; `--version` confirms `78ddda475`.
- Separate draft #1334 passed local `make pr-ready` and all GitHub checks; it remains a draft pending owner confirmation.
title: UX changes: home navigation and consistent message-box controls

## What this does

Commits after `fd84adfc`: merge from `dev` resolving the two conflicts (`DESIGN.md` takes #1046's amendment with the bench-host wording reapplied; the `CONSTRAINTS.md` delete wins over #1064's edit), the two cited folders restored, `test/ux` removed, the change entry added and then corrected. `make pr-ready` green locally (no Go file changed; laws and the light gate pass); CI green on `98b8dd5b`.

body:
Round 1 (initial cleanup) of #1065; round 2 follows.

Scope is sections A–D of the issue, plus what the repository rules or review required.

## Taken over

The review fixes are four commits on top of `c8346300`:

- `prompt: the messages-from-codeaf list names every note codeaf writes`
- `session: no change skips judgment only when it answers the reader`
- `test: the model stub replays the no-change fold`
- `prompt: the standing-news tag stays with the event, not on the page`

The third commit adds a deterministic replay through the real binary: eleven `read`
rounds, a 30-row answer, one rejecting completion-reader call, and one exact
`[no change]` reply. The headless and tmux runs both reached that complete path.

## What changed

**A. Harness**
- **The completion check sees more of the answer.** `checkpointSaidBytes` goes from 600 to `8 * 1024` bytes, or less when the person's request already fills most of the digest. `checkpointClipSaid` takes the room that is left. If it still has to cut, the text ends with `[clipped by codeaf: N of M bytes]` instead of a bare `…`, and the marker counts toward the limit.
- **New reply token.** `session.NoChangeReply = "[no change]"`, read in one place by `IsNoChangeReply`.
- **When the token counts.** In `checkpointReopen`, `answeredNoteUnchanged` reads the transcript. The token counts only as the very next reply to the check's own `[carry on]` note; a volatile session note in between is skipped over. It does not count after tool calls, after the person's own message, after a load or ask nudge, or with other words beside it. When it counts, the turn ends with no further check call.
- **After a token reply.** Only a token that answered the reader's note suppresses the route judge and gives memory learning the answer before the token. In every other context, the token is judged and learned from as an ordinary reply, and another completion check can run.
- **Where the token is hidden.** Display remains deliberately context-free. The transcript keeps the token for the model, while `entryRows` gives every tool-less exact-token reply 0 rows and the live feed empties every such reply at its response boundary (`feed.confirmResponse`), whether or not it counted for the completion check. Either way, `deriveWorkfolds` leaves the settled answer before it in view. `workfold.go` is unchanged.
- **Old journals.** The previous carry-on note is kept as `explainingCheckpointCarryOnLead`, so journals that contain it still hide it.

**B. Prompt text.** `checkpointCarryOnLead` uses the issue's four lines. `checkpointRemainsAsk` adds that text marked as clipped is never evidence the person saw a cut-off answer.

**C/D. `internal/session/prompts/system.md`**

`# Tone` and `# Delivery` are replaced by four sections, and the five rules they carried are restored inside them.

- **`# The answer`**
  - Once a turn ends, only its last message stays in view. The plan and the one-sentence status before each tool batch are still shown while the turn runs.
  - The deliverable goes in that last message. Evidence and blocking details stay complete.
  - Restored: match the person's task and vocabulary; state uncertainty at the claim it affects and choose the safe option.
  - "Done" is never a compiling scaffold or a narrowed test, and half-solved work is never handed back.
- **`# Answer or change`**
  - Questions, options, comparisons and tables are answered in the reply itself, not in a file, unless the person asks for a file.
  - No edits until the person asks for a change.
  - Renamed from `# Words or work`, which collided with the existing `## Work or words`.
- **`# When corrected`**, as the issue wrote it.
- **`# Messages from codeaf`**
  - Names the user-role tags codeaf writes into the conversation: `[carry on]`, `[taking stock]`, `[silent]`, `[stuck]`, `[folded …]`, `[context compacted]`. It no longer claims that any other opening is the person's; `[image #N]` is identified only as the person's attachment.
  - Does not name the tool result's `[held]`, the private reader's `[still asked]`, or standing news's `[something you set up fired]`: that line carries its own instruction under the event, and `TestTheSteeringLineReadsAsNewsAndNotAsARequest` refuses a second copy on the page (the prompt diet's WITH THE EVENT class).

Other prompt changes:
- `…act and offer to unwind it` now continues `when the person asked for a change`.
- `NEVER yield while actionable work remains` becomes `Don't end the turn while work the person asked for remains`.
- `promptprofile.go`: all four sections survive the lean profile. `Messages from codeaf` also has an explicit `keeps: true` row.

**Prompt budget raised, on purpose.** Against `origin/dev`, fixed grows from 53,276 to 55,280 bytes and lean from 45,051 to 47,055: 2,004 bytes on both arms. Each arm already had 15 bytes spare, so each waiver rises by 1,989: `fixedPrefixWaiver` 5,291 → 7,280 and `leanPrefixWaiver` 13,566 → 15,555. Both sit exactly on the new measurement, with the original dated note extended by the review measurement. body:
`ctrl+k` is kill-to-end-of-line in every shell on the machine. Here it opened a card. This gives the letter back to the message box and moves the conversation switcher one modifier across.

## What works now

1. **`ctrl+k` kills to the end of the line** — message box, home's box, every filter box. The pair to the `ctrl+u` that has always killed to the start.
2. **`alt+k` opens the switcher** (`opt+k` on a Mac). Card, keys and behaviour otherwise unchanged.
3. **`alt+shift+k` walks it backwards — in every terminal.** `ctrl+shift+k` could not, and was bound on maybe half of them.
4. **Home's rule names it**: `alt+w folder · alt+o model · alt+k chats · / commands`.
5. **`Chats ▾` is deleted.** The `+3` overflow count stays, dim and inert.

## Why the switcher moved and not the edit

Every `ctrl+<letter>` on this surface is spent. Only `h`, `i` and `m` are free, and the terminal already spends those on backspace, tab and enter. So the edit had nowhere to go and the card did.

`alt+` is the modifier the places are already built on. `k` is the letter people have learned.

## What the move bought

`alt+shift+k` is escape-then-`K`, a different byte from `alt+k`'s escape-then-`k`. `ctrl+shift+k` and `ctrl+k` were the **same byte**, so the reverse gesture needed a terminal that had taken the kitty disambiguation flag. Now it needs nothing.

## What it costs

A Mac whose Option key composes accents: `opt+k` types `˚` and no card appears. Same setting every other `alt+` chord here already needs.

Handled rather than left to be found: `˚` is on the dead-key table, and it is the one character there read in a **conversation** as well as on a place — because it is the one chord bound in both. The hint slot says `opt types a letter · turn on option as meta`.

Linux and Windows pay nothing. Alt is already meta there.

## 3 bugs found on the way

1. `ctrl+k` reached the composer but **not home's box** — five boxes hand-roll their own key switch and all five were missing it. Home is where a launch lands, so that was the first box anyone would try it in.
2. Home's rule, the question chip and two key-sheet rows drew `alt+` on a Mac while the rest of the surface drew the Mac spelling. They were built straight out of their constants and never went through `chordSpelling.say`.
3. `config.KeyQuickSwitch`'s doc said the setting governed the switcher's own chord. It has always governed `ctrl+tab`.

## 2 new laws

- **`killpairlaw_test.go`** — fails any key switch answering `ctrl+u` without `ctrl+k`, naming file and line. Two exceptions named with reasons (string fields with no caret).
- **`chordspellinglaw_test.go`** — renders the conversation, key sheet, all seven places and the key map on a Mac's spelling, fails on any `alt+` reaching the frame. A frame test, not a source test: every constant is *supposed* to say `alt+`; what was wrong was the path from constant to paint.

Both verified to bite by reverting a fix and watching them fail.

## Separately: opt+ replaces ⌥

Every modifier on a Mac keycap carries a word **and** a symbol — Control is `control` and `⌃`, Option is `option` and `⌥`. "What the keycap says" never chose between them, and this surface took the word for one (`ctrl+`) and the symbol for another. `opt+` is `ctrl+`'s own move made twice.

Bindings untouched. `opt+` is four cells, exactly as `alt+` is, so every ladder that fits a chord on Linux fits it on a Mac. `⌥` measured as one cell and was not reliably one cell on screen — U+2325 is East-Asian Ambiguous. It was also the one person-visible mark reached as a string literal rather than through `tokens.GlyphSet.Glyph`.

`⌘` is still a glyph and is now the only one.

## Manual

`keys.md`, `screen.md`, `home.md`, `commands.md`, `places.md`, `tasks.md`, `getting-started.md`. New section answering *"why not the option symbol"*, seven new retrieval probes, and the stale claim that `ctrl+k` saved a harness design from inside its room is gone — that row was deleted long ago.

## Proof

`make pr-ready` green, including the full `internal/tui3` suite (315s). Laws, manual gates and the light gate green.

At rest `ctrl+c` ends the session on the keystroke that lands, over every picker, panel, room, page and paste bracket — leaving is never modal. The arm is gone: no first press that only warms the door, no 1.5-second window, no `ctrl+c again to quit` in the hint slot.

Mid-turn nothing changes. `ctrl+c` is still the interrupt and that press is spent on the model, so a two-tap mid-turn stops the answer and then leaves.

## What the arm was protecting, and what it cost

Three of the four things the double press bought are bought by the exit path instead, which is where they always belonged:

- **The draft and everything parked above it** are written down by `app.quit` itself — so they are owed to a real SIGINT and a closed window too, neither of which was ever going to press a key twice. `TestAQuitInTheGapAtTheEndOfATurnKeepsWhatWasParked` pins the case the arm was written for: a press in the gap between `EventTurnDone` and the stream closing now leaves *and* puts the parked message in the draft file.
- **Work a session host is running outlives the window** whatever this surface does (`workOutlivesExit`).
- **Mid-turn is unchanged**, so the two-tap that started the whole argument still stops the model on its first press.

The fourth is genuinely spent: **nothing on the way out names running work any more.** A person who leaves with tasks running inside this terminal is not told so first, and a `ctrl+c` struck by accident at rest ends the session. What they typed comes back at the next launch; what those tasks were doing does not. `ctrl+w` on a tab with work in it still raises a card and still asks.

## The code

- `input.go` — at rest the key calls `a.quit()`.
- `quitarm.go` is deleted. `leavingDraft`, all that is left of it, is `leaving.go`. Gone with it: `app.quitArm`, `armQuit`, `quitArmed`, `disarmQuit`, `quitSweep`, `quitHint`, `quitArmWindow`, the frame-clock wakeup they needed and the armed-door rung in `hintWord`.
- The work-counting helpers move to `tabclose.go` as `workCount` / `workCountWord` — the close-a-tab card is the one place that still reads them.
- Strings: `landingKeysWord` is `esc interrupts · ctrl+c quits · ? for help`, the `/help` row is `ctrl+c         quits everything · mid-turn it interrupts instead, like esc`. README and `internal/e2e`'s word table follow.

## The manual

Nine chat pages updated in the same change. Three retrieval probes went red on the way — `it asked me the same thing twice`, `how long does stop take`, `does closing one conversation quit codeaf` — and were fixed in the pages, never in the test: the askers' words are in the `## ` headings now.

## Proof

`make pr-ready` green on this laptop, including the full `internal/tui3` suite (315s) and the laws.

body:
The owner's ask: tell people a new version is out, give them the command, and —
better — let them update from inside the chat and come back on the new build.

## What a person sees at launch

A stable build that is behind the newest stable release gets one dim transcript
line, and nothing else changes:

```
codeaf v0.2.0 is out · you have v0.1.0 · /update installs it and restarts · or: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

It carries both versions, the command, and the curl line, because the ask was
that the command be given. The look is a command, not an opening read, so the
first frame is drawn before the network is asked anything; three seconds is the
whole budget, and offline, refused, rate-limited or malformed all draw nothing.
The answer is cached for a day beside the profile, though a cached newer release
still shows the line at every launch — the reminder is the point.

## Who is prompted

Only someone who could sensibly be behind. A stable tag when a greater stable
exists; a release candidate once its stable line is published. A `dev-*` or
`staging-*` channel build, a `make build` sha and an unstamped binary make **no
request at all** — a channel build is deliberately newer than stable, and a
source build belongs to whoever built it. `codeaf update --check` still answers
on those, naming what the running build is.

Opt-out: `CODEAF_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` silences the launch check only; `/update`
and `codeaf update` still work. Headless doors never check.

## What /update does

Names the tag, then the checksum and where it landed, then restarts:

```
· downloading codeaf v0.2.0 for linux/amd64…
· checksum matched · installed at /path/to/codeaf
· restarting on v0.2.0…
```

Already newest says `you are on the newest codeaf, v0.2.0` and stays. It refuses
while a turn or a task is running, and once started, one shared guard stops a
second `/update` or a new turn from beginning underneath it — the restart must
never quit on top of live work. The restart happens in the door, after the frame
is down and the terminal is back, and re-execs with this launch's own arguments
plus `--session` on this transcript, so the same conversation reopens.

## What `codeaf update` does

`--check` prints one line and exits 0 (newest), 3 (a newer one exists) or 1
(could not ask). Without it, installs stable by default, or `--rc`, `--dev`,
`--staging`, `--version <tag>`. A source build refuses in place and names its
path instead of replacing something a developer is holding. An unwritable target
is left alone and offered the curl line; sudo is never attempted.

## Hand-verified, and how

The repository is private, so `releases/download` cannot be reached anonymously.
The real `v0.2.0` assets and release JSON were mirrored to a local HTTP server
and reached through `CODEAF_GITHUB_API` / `CODEAF_GITHUB_DOWNLOAD`, with a
binary stamped `v0.1.0`. Through tmux, against that mirror: the launch line
appeared; `/update` printed the three notes above; the process restarted; the
restarted build reported `v0.2.0` and resumed the same transcript; `codeaf
version` then printed one line naming `v0.2.0`. Full commands and frames are in
the lane's verification record.

Not verified here: Windows (cross-build only — the `ReplaceFileW` path has a
contract test but has never run on Windows), and a real anonymous download from
a public repository.

## Two things found on the way

The engine kept its twenty-second torn-link grace on a *deliberate* detach, so a
cleanly closed window looked attached long enough to keep a freshly installed
codeaf behind the engine the old one had already left. Fixed here.

`scripts/install.sh` and `internal/update` were reading the same release list by
different rules — the shell accepted any `dev-*`/`staging-*` tag and semver parts
with leading zeroes. They share one grammar now; #1056's publish-time ordering is
untouched, only which candidates are eligible.

## Review

Two adversarial review rounds against the contract. Round one found three
blockers — a `/update` race, `Authorization` surviving a redirect to another port
on the same host, and an ignored Windows rollback error. Round two found two
survived: the guard was missing from the home page's Enter road, and
`ERROR_UNABLE_TO_MOVE_REPLACEMENT_2` is a documented *partial* failure that can
leave no file at the target. Both fixed, each with a test that fails without the
fix.

body:
Two halves of one fault. The second is what made the first visible.

## The budget was not a budget

`folderIndexWalk`'s clock check stood **below** the walk's `!entry.IsDir()` return, so a file never consulted it. The walk therefore got a turn to stop only *between directories*. The comment over the constants said so out loud — "checked before traversal and at each directory" — and that reading was the defect, not a description of it: the directory that ends a home walk on a Mac is `~/Library/Caches`, one directory holding hundreds of thousands of files, and a bound never read while those stream past is not a bound.

Measured on the owner's laptop, before this change:

```
scanFolderRoots took 5m58.281175834s and found 1144 roots (budget is 3s)
```

The check moves above the file return. The constants' comment now says what the code does.

## The suite walked the developer's own home directory

`tui3_test.go`'s `TestMain` moves the state root and says in so many words that it leaves `HOME` alone, because this package *draws* `~` in front of paths and those readings are about the real one. `scanFolderRoots` does not draw `~` — it **walks** it, with `os.UserHomeDir`, which is the one thing that seam does not cover.

So any test that opened the folder picker indexed the whole home directory of whoever ran it: six minutes on a laptop, nothing at all on a runner whose home is empty. A test that passes there and fails here is exactly what `TestMain` exists to prevent, and it is how `TestThePicksLandingMidBrowseKeepTheChoicesAndThePreview` came to panic on the driver's five-second budget while CI stayed green:

```
panic: the harness waited 5.00s for (*app).askFolderStore.func1 and it never answered
```

`folderRootScan` is now the seam, for `opener.go`'s `processOpener` reason, and `TestMain` answers it with nothing.

## The test

`TestTheBudgetIsMeasuredAgainstEveryEntryAndNotOnlyDirectories` drives the clock rather than racing one — the thing being proved is *where the walk stops*, and a wall-clock threshold is a coin toss on a loaded box. The clock spends a second of the budget per reading, over a tree of one file-filled directory followed by a repository. A directories-only walk reads that clock four times and never runs out, so it reaches `z-repo`; an every-entry walk runs out among the files and never gets there. Verified failing against `dev`'s ordering, passing with the fix.

## The manual

`choosing-a-folder.md` said the index is built in the background and refreshed about once a day — still true — and said nothing about the walk being bounded, which was fine while it ran to the end of the disk and is not fine now that it stops. It now states the three stops and the way past them.

## The dead sentence is deleted

`folderIndexWord` wrote two sentences — "there was more to look through than this list holds", and a count of the folders a permission refused — and **no surface has ever called it**. Three tests asserted its wording, which is what kept it looking alive.

A person-facing sentence no door reaches is worse than absent: to anyone grepping for it, it reads as a promise the product keeps. It does not. `folderIndexAnswer.Bound` and `.Denied` are the facts, they are still set, and the three tests now stand on those — including the prefix-of-the-truth law, which was written about the answer and is now attached to it.

A picker that says out loud what it could not see is a real thing to want, and it is a change that adds a door rather than one that deletes a corpse.

## Proof

`make pr-ready` green, including the full `internal/tui3` suite at 315s — which is the first time it has been green on that laptop today. `TestThePicksLandingMidBrowseKeepTheChoicesAndThePreview` now passes in 0.5s.

## What

The thinking chip above the message box — `ctrl+v`, and a press on the cell —
walked five stops and wrapped from `max` back to `low`. `auto`, the state a
shipped install is actually in, was the one stop the walk could not reach: a
conversation dialled up once had to be put back through `/effort auto` or the
ladder's top row, which means leaving the control you are standing at.

It walks `effortNextClearing` now — the wheel the model picker's `ctrl+t` and a
task's own rung have always turned. One press past `max` hands the conversation
back, and the walk begins again at `low`. `/effort auto` and the ladder's top
row still clear it in one move from any rung, which is what somebody five rungs
away wants.

A standing item's rung is now the only scope whose wheel never lands on
absence; it is cleared in the item's own document, which is why.

## The note that clearing writes

Clearing was rare while `/effort auto` was the only door, and one of its notes
was wrong: on a machine whose `thinking` row in `/settings` is set, a cleared
conversation falls back to *that row*, but the note blamed a level dialled onto
the model and pointed at `ctrl+t` — a chord that would not move it. That
sentence is one press away now, so it is fixed:

| What catches the cleared rung | What the note says |
| --- | --- |
| nothing | `thinking · auto · the model decides` |
| the `thinking` row in `/settings` | `thinking · auto for this chat · <rung> · the thinking row in /settings decides now` |
| a level on the model (`ctrl+t`, `--reasoning`) | the existing note, naming the model and `ctrl+t` |

Telling the second from the third means asking the agent for the model's own
level rather than reading a table that answers `""` for "not told yet" — the
same seeding a keystroke is already allowed (`app.modelOwnLevel`).

## Proof

- `make test-quick`, `make test-touched` (`./internal/manual ./internal/tui3`) — green.
- Four new tests in `internal/tui3/effortchip_test.go`: the six-stop walk, the
  press off `max`, the install-row note, and the model-level note.
- Two new manual probes: *does the thinking cycle go back to auto*, *I cleared
  the thinking rung and it still says high*.
- Manual pages updated in the same change: `keys.md`, `models-and-cost.md`,
  `screen.md`, `running-on-another-machine.md`.

One unrelated red appeared on the first `test-touched` run —
`TestThePicksLandingMidBrowseKeepTheChoicesAndThePreview` panicked on the 5s
work budget in `askFolderStore` while the box was loaded — and the same suite
was green on a clean re-run. It touches nothing this change does.

Two installer defects found this afternoon by driving the published staging build through `scripts/install.sh`.

## 1. The channel picker took GitHub's list order, which is not publish order

The `rc|dev|staging` arm fetched `releases?per_page=100`, walked the tags in file order and broke out on the first one matching the channel. GitHub does not list releases in publish order. Observed today with `--dev`: it chose `dev-20260915-e2ae913b7d0c` (published 13:43Z) while `dev-20260915-56a22c20ec53` (14:56Z) and `dev-20260915-4b6ec83cfbfa` (15:21Z) both existed — a stale build, installed silently, with nothing on screen to say so.

The whole list is read now and the candidate with the newest `published_at` wins whatever its position, falling back to `created_at` when a release has no publish time. A new `extract_dated_tags` helper emits one `<stamp> <tag>` line per release using the same no-`jq`, POSIX-awk approach `extract_tags` already used; it stops at the release's `assets` so an asset's own `created_at` can never decide the pick. Ties (including releases carrying no timestamp at all) keep the first met, so behaviour is stable.

`--stable` (`releases/latest`) and `--version <tag>` are untouched, and the channel-matching patterns are unchanged.

## 2. The refusal named only a rate limit

The repository is private today, so an anonymous `--dev` call gets a 404 and took the `api_problem` path — which told the person about a rate limit that was not the problem. Both causes are named now:

> `GitHub's API could not be reached or refused (a rate limit, or a repository you cannot read?); pin VERSION=<tag>, or export GITHUB_TOKEN`

That sentence has exactly one home in the tree; nothing else quoted it.

## Validation contract

- For `--rc`, `--dev` and `--staging`, the installer chooses the matching tag with the newest `published_at`, regardless of list order.
- A `null` or absent `published_at` falls back to that release's `created_at`.
- An asset's timestamp never decides the pick.
- A release with neither timestamp is still a candidate but ranks below any that has one; ties keep the first met.
- `--stable` and `--version <tag>` are unchanged, as is `no <channel> build has been published yet`.
- An API refusal names both a rate limit and a repository the caller cannot read, and still names both ways out.

## Proof

`TestInstallerPicksTheNewestChannelBuildWhateverTheListOrder` drives the real script against the `httptest` fake with the oldest `dev-*` tag listed **first**, and is **red against the unmodified script** on all three subtests (`newest_published_at`, `created_at_replaces_null_published_at`, `staging_uses_timestamps`) and green after. `TestInstallerNamesBothReasonsWhenTheAPIRefuses` covers the 429 and a new private-repository 404 mode.

Gates: `bash -n scripts/install.sh`, `go test -count=1 ./internal/release/`, `make test-laws` — all green.

## What was true

Nothing in this repository reproduced the licences of the code compiled into the binary, and `.github/workflows/release.yml` published only `dist/codeaf-*` and `checksums.txt`.

That is a live obligation, not a tidiness point. `internal/pair/cpace/LICENSE` is BSD-3-Clause and `internal/pair/pairing.go` links that package into every build; clause 2 asks for the notice "in the documentation and/or other materials provided with the distribution" of a binary. `internal/connect/ampcatalog/providers.json` is a `//go:embed`ed copy of the amp-labs catalog. Every Go module in the build carries the same shape of obligation. None of them had a notice anywhere, and the repository goes public with a stable release.

## What is true now

**`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` at the repository root** — 57 sections: the 55 modules `go list -deps ./cmd/codeaf` names, plus the vendored CPace and the embedded amp-labs catalog. Each section states its version, its licence identifier and the licence text verbatim from the module's own source. Every one of the 57 has a licence file; none was unidentifiable.

**`cmd/codeaf-notices` generates it from the build itself**, so it cannot be written by hand and cannot quietly go stale. `generate` writes it, `check` says whether regeneration would change it. Like `codeaf-changes` it is a developer's binary and never a verb on `codeaf`, so the product pays nothing for it on the `SIZE-BUDGET`. Output is deterministic — two runs are byte-identical.

**A law in `cmd/codeaf-notices`** reads the same module set and fails when a compiled module has no section, when either copied component is missing, and when the committed CPace licence text is no longer reproduced word for word. No network (`GOPROXY=off`), and it decides in a third of a second, so `go.mod` cannot grow past the notice.

**The release carries it.** The build job copies the file into `dist/` before the checksums are written, so `checksums.txt` covers it and the publish step — which already uploads `dist/*` — attaches it to every release on every channel. `internal/release/workflow_test.go` asserts both lines. The installer needs no change: it looks up only the row naming its own asset.

One line in the README install section and one in `docs/rules/promotion.md` under Releasing.

## Validation

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go build ./...` | pass |
| `go vet ./...` | pass |
| `make fmt-check` | pass |
| `go test ./cmd/codeaf-notices/ ./internal/release/` | pass |
| `make test-laws` | pass |

Proved by hand, not just asserted: deleting the `github.com/flynn/noise` section fails the law naming that module; altering one line of the reproduced CPace licence fails it too. `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged and no dependency was added — the generator is standard library only.

The diff deliberately stays clear of the `Test release surface` step, which #1047 changed; this branch is rebased on top of that merge.
