body:
The repository goes public with a first stable release, and three of its prose
surfaces are about to become false in ways a reader cannot check. One of them is
compiled into the binary, so a model reads it as the only account of this program
that exists. A fourth thing was never written down at all.

Every claim below was read out of the tree, not remembered.

## The channels, as they are

`.github/workflows/release.yml` maps a push to `dev`, `staging` or `main` onto a
`dev-*`, `staging-*` or rc publication, and marks everything that is not stable
`--latest=false --prerelease`. Stable is only ever a person dispatching `Release`
on `main`. The README said instead that the repository "currently has no rc or
staging publication" — true when it was written, false as of today's promotion.
It now describes which branch event publishes which channel, and says in one
clause why the bare curl line still stops with `no stable build has been published
yet`: `--stable` is the default and reads GitHub's `releases/latest`, which
excludes prereleases.

## Conditions, not dates

The raw-URL installer road answers 404 **while** the repository is private and
works **once** it is public with `scripts/install.sh` on `main`. That is now
written as a condition in both the README and the manual, so the sentence is true
on either side of the flip. `https://agentfield.ai/get/codeaf` is still not
serving, so the working road goes first and the proxied address is described as
the form that will be supported once it serves — rather than labelled "the
preferred form" at the top of the list, which sent a reader to a dead URL first.

## The manual page is the model's only source

`internal/manual/chat/running-from-the-terminal.md` said the repository is private
today and the published URL answers 404. It is compiled into the binary, so that
was about to become a confident wrong answer. Its first section is rewritten in the
same conditional truths; every existing `## ` heading is kept word for word, and
the manual gates confirm all twenty-five probes that route to this page still
reach it.

## Disclosing the rtk fetch

Neither the README nor any page under `internal/manual/chat/` mentioned that
codeaf downloads and installs a third party's executable. `codeaf do` starts one
background attempt (`cmd/codeaf/chat.go:2142`, reached through `errandRun`) to
fetch the pinned `rtk` v0.45.0 from `github.com/rtk-ai/rtk` when none is already
resolvable and `CODEAF_RTK` is unset. It is now stated in both places, with the
bounds exactly as the code spells them: two minutes for the whole fetch, 64 MB per
response, sha256 against the published `checksums.txt`, four platform pairs, mode
`0700` at `$CODEAF_HOME/bin/rtk`, nothing waiting on it, one log line either way,
and `RTK_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` on every call. `CODEAF_RTK=off` refuses it.

This change describes the behaviour. Whether it should be opt-in is the owner's
call, not this pull request's.

## Branch rules and the free plan

Three files said branch rules are unavailable until the org moves to GitHub Team.
GitHub Free supports rulesets on **public** repositories, so the true condition is
"GitHub Team **or** the repository is public" — which is tomorrow. `.github/rulesets/README.md`,
`docs/rules/ci.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are corrected minimally, and the rulesets README
now says to apply both rulesets the day the repository goes public rather than only
inviting a check.

## Proof

Prose and manual pages only — no Go source, no workflow, no `LICENSE`, no
`BENCHMARKS.md`.

```
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/internal/manual	1.791s
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/internal/tui3	0.260s
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/internal/session	0.602s
make test-laws: 115 files in 27 packages — all 27 packages ok
```

## What

The first staging build after the ledger's deletion (#1012) published nothing: the `Release` workflow's `test` job died at its first line with exit 2 and no output. Under `set -euo pipefail`, `skip="$(awk … .github/known-red.txt 2>/dev/null | paste …)"` over a file that does not exist is an exit inside an assignment, and the step ended before `go test` ran. Every channel but `dev` runs that job, and `dev` skips it by design, so nothing on `dev` could see it — staging, rc and stable builds were all blocked.

- The ledger is read only when it is there, the way `scripts/laws.sh` already reads it; an absent or empty ledger leaves `test_args` empty.
- `internal/release/workflow_test.go` now runs the step's real prologue under `bash` with `set -euo pipefail` in four ledger states (absent, empty, comments only, one name) and asserts the step lives and the name becomes `-skip`. Verified red against the old workflow, green against this one.

## Validation contract

- With no `.github/known-red.txt`, the release-surface test step reaches `go test` with no `-skip`.
- With an empty or comment-only ledger, the same.
- With a ledger naming a test, `go test` receives `-skip ^(Name)$`.
- The workflow never reads the ledger unguarded again (the contract test refuses `known-red.txt 2>/dev/null`).

Seen live: staging run 34984927706 (`test: failure` at 0.3 s, `build`/`publish` skipped).

Home's law 2 was **act left, watch right** — the person's three panels on the left, the machine's four on the right, whatever any of them held. On a quiet machine that drew six whispering headings over a screen that was five sixths scaffolding, with the one panel that had rows boxed into a third of the width.

The column is now a reading of what the panel holds.

- A panel **with rows** stands in the **field** — the columns left of the last one, filled from the top left corner down.
- A panel **with nothing in it** stands in the **rail** — the last column, flush with the right edge, as its heading and its whisper.
- `projects` and `spend` are **pinned** to the top of the rail whatever they hold, because their height is the same on every machine on every day. One blank row separates that pair from what is only quiet today.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/079a6e61-fa10-4370-a295-9d1998276eb4



### What it costs, taken knowingly

Home's geography moves now, and nobody can learn that `running` is on the right. The **rank** inside each column never moves, so the cost is to one axis and not both. The owner ruled this on 2026-09-15 after reading a real quiet home.

### Two consequences that needed their own call

- **The field fills rather than balances.** Balancing put the cursor's panel in whichever column had room, so `↓` off the tab bar landed on a different panel at 120 cells than at 200 — and the landing is the same line at every width, because a landing that moves with the frame is one nobody can build a habit on. Filling from the left keeps it stable, and never spreads two short columns over a wide screen. The middle column at three is the descriptions': a row's sentence stands beside it there, and a question raised from home stands there as a card; no panel of headings is laid in it.
- **`←→` now step over a column with nothing to stand on.** Without it the rail was out of the arrows' reach entirely on a wide quiet frame — `projects` and `spend` drawn on the screen with no key that walks to them.

### The one person-facing sentence that moved

Home's resting foot gains `ctrl+o open folder`. That clause was already there on any machine whose right column had rows (§6.6 refuses to leave a door invisible when `→` crosses columns instead of opening a row's verbs); what changed is that the rail always has rows, so the condition is always met. The design's four keys still open the sentence and `esc` is still not on it.

### Proof

`make pr-ready` green — the light gate plus the full `internal/tui3` suite (318s). All 399 home tests pass. Six tests were rewritten to pin the new law rather than the old one, and two were added: the rail's group gap, and the descriptions' middle column at three.

`docs/design/home-mission-control/DESIGN.md` carries the amended laws 2, 3 and 6 and says what each of them used to say. The manual's `home.md` is redrawn under the new geography, its opening sketch included.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### After review

The review's three blockers and four should-fixes are in `006fbd6a3`: a `scheduled` row draws its one sentence per kind at every width, as the line under the cursor where there is no middle column; an open fold reads `3 fewer · 40 more` and names no place, because `enter` on it toggles the panel and the heading is the door to the place; `enter` on an order made from home lands standing on that order; the tagged e2e fold test waits for `N more`; and the manual's retired roster, resting foot, fixed-columns claim and the `elsewhere` / `made from home` refusals are rewritten to what the code does. `make pr-ready` green again.

## What

The publish job copied the whole `## <tag>` section of `CHANGELOG.md` into the release body. GitHub refuses a body over 125,000 characters, and the first roll-up in this repository (v0.2.0, 612 entries with their folds) renders at 1.7 MB — so tomorrow's stable dispatch would have built six binaries and then failed at `gh release create`.

- `codeaf-changes notes <tag>` prints the section whole when it fits, the headline layer (every `- **title**` line and kind heading, folds removed) with a pointer to `CHANGELOG.md` when it does not, and a cut at a line boundary when even that is too long. A tag with no section exits non-zero with nothing on stdout, which is the workflow's existing fall-back to generated notes.
- `release.yml` asks that command instead of the awk copy; `internal/release/workflow_test.go` refuses the awk coming back.
- `docs/rules/changelog.md` and `docs/rules/promotion.md` say what the page carries when the section is bigger than a body may be.

## Validation contract

- A section under the cap is printed exactly as written, up to the next `## ` heading.
- `v0.2.0` never answers for `v0.2.0-rc.1`; a missing section is a refusal with empty stdout.
- Over the cap, every entry's headline line and every kind heading survive, no fold survives, no triple blank lines, and the body ends with the pointer line.
- When even the headlines do not fit, the cut is at a line boundary and the pointer is still last.
- The shipped cap leaves room under 125,000 for the install paragraph the workflow appends.

Proved on the real thing: the rendered v0.2.0 section (1,697,248 bytes) becomes 99,895 bytes of notes with all 612 headline lines kept.

body: **The spend place (`alt+3`) was a chart, two ragged tables and a door that went to the wrong screen. It is one cut of the ledger at a time, in four columns, with a control that swaps the cut — and the doors open the thing.** ## Before ## After > The screenshot below is from an earlier round of this branch — the layout is current, but the headings now read `by model` / `by topic` and only one is drawn at a time. ``` 14 days came to $2.10 · 28.9M tokens · loudest day: $2.03 sep 14 (bandit-algorithm) ← by topic → ← the cursor is on the heading · bandit-algorithm task 7 $0.63 · deepswe model discussion chat aforge-v2 $0.38 by standing order · repo-watch 88 firings $0.01 a run $0.88 ``` --- ## The bug you can't see in a screenshot `enter` on a row of *what it was for* **did not open that thing**. - a task opened the tasks *place* — then left you to find your own row in a list of everything this machine has ever run - a conversation opened **home**, the switcher, with the conversation you named nowhere on it Both go through the doors the rest of the surface already uses now. A task opens **its own record card**. A conversation is **brought forward** if this terminal has it, otherwise opened beside the one you're in. A promise opens the standing place **on that order**. A thing the record no longer holds **refuses where it stands** instead of walking you to a page about everything. A test was asserting the defect. It waited for `pageHome`. --- ## One cut at a time `by model` and `by topic` are the same money added up two ways — every dollar under one heading is also a dollar under the other — so a page drawing both asked you to read one bill twice. The page draws one. It opens on `by topic`, the question you walk in with. Walk the cursor onto the heading and it wears arrows: **`←`, `→` and `enter` step between the two.** The arrows appear only there, because `→` on every other row opens that row's verbs — a key is drawn where it is bound. An empty window keeps the control, or `by model` would have no way back. Standing orders keep a heading of their own under `by topic`: a promise is one of the things money was *for*, so it's a third heading rather than a third cut. ## Why the bars went A bar was a model's share of the dearest one — a reading the figure at the end of the same row already gives. It cost a reserved column, plus a second reservation in front of it so a role word on one row couldn't shove it out of line. The list is sorted dearest first. That is the chart. ## Why the figures moved right What a row **is** is read from the left. What it **cost** is read by comparison with the row above — and a comparison is made on a figure's right-hand edge. So the facts travel together in a block and the names run out to meet them. That block ends **where the chart ends**, on the `today` point. Money used to be flushed to the frame, which on a wide terminal put the one figure every row is read for forty cells from the counts it belongs with. **A row gives up its words before its figure.** A long name pushes the fields behind it, but only as far as the cells the money needs. ## Numbers - **Money is a column of cents with a floor.** Under a cent reads `$0.01` — not `$0.0068`, not the words `under a cent`. The head line, `/cost` and the Spending tab keep exact arithmetic; a floor is a column's rule, and a total in a sentence has nothing to line up with. - **Thousands are marked everywhere.** `$4,210.55`, `$50,000`. The page used to draw `128,400 calls` and `$4210.55` on one row. - **Token volumes got a `B` rung.** A fortnight of agent work read `7062.1M`. Now `842` · `12.4k` · `1.2M` · `3.2B`. ## Words - `a task` → **`task`**, `a conversation` → **`chat`**. Column words, not sentences. - The headings are `by model`, `by topic`, `by standing order`. They were sentences that named the page's subject again before getting to the point — and the tab already said `spend`. - `under a cent a run` is gone; a promise's per-firing figure goes through the money column's rule, so it reads `$0.01 a run`. ## Smaller things - **Twenty rows under `by topic`, not three.** Three is a headline, not an answer to the question this page is for. - **The loudest day lost its row** and became the head line's last clause. - **The head reserves the zoom clause** before its own optional facts. A key crowded off this line is not hidden, it is **unbound**. - **A missing project draws nothing**, not `.` — `filepath.Base("")` answers `"."`, and that was reaching the screen. - **Narrow frames give up whole fields**, in a named order of worth. Never a figure with its tail cut off. Never the money. --- ## What the review caught Three blockers, all real, all fixed in `6d3d656`: 1. **A task row could open another conversation's task.** The join matched the index's `SessionID` — the conversation that ran the work — against `SubjectSpend.Session`, which is the task node's *own journal id*. The exact-pair arm never fired on real ledger data, so every row fell through to an id-only match, and ids restart with every conversation. `SubjectSpend` carries `Root` now and the join is `(id, Root)`. The fixture and the test were green because they spelled the ledger a way no ledger is spelled; both write the real shape now. 2. **The money could be truncated.** Fields were laid left to right and the row trimmed to the frame at the end, so a long name or project cost the row its tail. And `spendProjectCap` reached the measure and not the draw — a cap that moves the table and bounds nothing. 3. **The cut's control vanished on an empty window**, because it lived only on a heading over rows. Plus the three smaller notes: the head line's floored formatter, the silent fallback on a stale target, and `places.md`. --- ## Checking it ``` make demo-home ``` Then `alt+3`. The fixture carries a heavy stretch — five-figure call counts, billion-token volumes, money in the thousands — so the columns are at full width. ## Notes - Manual updated in the same change (`internal/manual/chat/models-and-cost.md`, `places.md`), as the manual law requires. - Deleted: `spendBar`, `spendModelBarCap`, `spendReading.modelCols`, `roleCol`, `spendReading.subjectCols`, `loudestRow`, `loudestRowIn`, `spendDoorWord`, `spendOpensWord`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## What was happening

A Finder window kept appearing on the owner's Mac at `~/<worktree>/internal/tui3`, closed, and appeared again.

`open ""` on a Mac is **not** an error. The platform resolves the empty path to the calling process's own working directory and puts a Finder window on screen. So `startOpener("")` did not fail — it opened a file manager, silently.

The caller is the sign-in handoff: `connectAuth` passes `ev.AuthURL` straight to `openConnectFlow`, which hands it to the platform. An `EventConnectAuth` carrying no URL therefore opened a window onto whatever folder codeaf was started in.

Under `go test` that folder is the package's own source directory — and `salience_test.go`'s table drives **every** event kind through the conversation's pump, `EventConnectAuth` among them, with no `AuthURL` and no stub over `processOpener`. So every run of `./internal/tui3`, in every worktree, opened a Finder window on that worktree's `internal/tui3`.

## The evidence

`com.apple.finder`'s `FXRecentFolders` on the owner's laptop decodes to four entries, one per checkout that has ever run the suite, each at `internal/tui3` and nothing else from those trees:

```
~/<worktree-a>/internal/tui3
~/<checkout>/internal/tui3
~/<worktree-b>/internal/tui3          (worktree since removed)
/private/tmp/<worktree-c>/internal/tui3
```

`open` raises an existing window rather than making a second one, which is why it read as one window shoving itself in front of the person over and over rather than as a pile of windows.

Reproduced by putting a logging shim named `open` ahead of `/usr/bin/open` on `PATH` and running the suite: exactly one call, `args=[]`, `cwd=<checkout>/internal/tui3`. Bisected to `TestALensLowersSalienceAndNeverDropsAFact`, which reproduces it alone.

## The change

- **The guard is in `startOpener`, not at the call site.** All six doors into the platform deserve it, and a rule that appears in two places drifts. It returns the sentence a `PATH` miss already says — a person is owed the same answer either way, and the link written under every handoff is still the way through. No new person-facing string, so no manual page moves.
- **`salienceRun` now takes `watchOpener`**, so no row of that table can reach the machine running the test whatever door a future kind grows.
- **`opener_test.go`** asserts the refusal *with a working opener on `PATH`* — a machine with no opener refuses for a different reason and would pass with the guard deleted. Verified failing without the guard, passing with it.

## Proof

Rebased onto `dev` after #1041, so the module path and the product name in these comments are `codeaf`.

The light gate and the laws are green. The full `internal/tui3` suite is green in 316s **except** `TestThePicksLandingMidBrowseKeepTheChoicesAndThePreview`, which fails identically on clean `origin/dev` with nothing of this branch applied:

```
panic: the harness waited 5.00s for (*app).askFolderStore.func1 and it never answered
```

That is `scanFolderRoots` walking the real `$HOME` and overrunning the driver's budget — not this change, and not something this branch can fix. Flagged separately.

body:
## The product is codeaf

One name, one spelling, everywhere a person, a model or a build meets it: the binary is `bin/codeaf`, the command is `codeaf`, the module path is `github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf`, the state root is `~/.codeaf`, the variables are `CODEAF_*`, the manual calls itself codeaf, and a structural law on the pull-request gate (`internal/namelaw`) fails the build the day the old name reappears in a live surface. Santosh asked for this before Wednesday's soft release; it is one pull request so nothing lands half-renamed.

## Nothing an existing install has breaks

- `~/.aforge` is adopted on the first start of the new binary: renamed to `~/.codeaf`, with `~/.aforge` left as a link to it, so conversations, keys, settings, the engine socket and an old `~/.aforge/bin` on PATH all still resolve. If the move cannot happen, the old folder is read where it is. Nothing moves when `CODEAF_HOME` or `AFORGE_HOME` is set.
- Every `AFORGE_*` variable is still read, for one release, whenever its `CODEAF_*` spelling is unset. Product code reads them through one door (`internal/env`) and a law keeps it that way. Skills and the standing timer's unit files carry both spellings.
- A repository's `.aforge-v3/config.json` and its `.aforge-v3/` task folders are still read; new writes go under `.codeaf/`. Nothing rewrites a person's repository on its own.
- Task commits are authored `codeaf`; commits an earlier build authored `aforge` are still recognised as the task system's own.
- The standing timer installs under its new unit names and removes the old `aforge-tick` units, so no machine ticks twice.
- The installer targets `Agent-Field/codeaf`, falls back to the old repository name until GitHub is renamed, and installs older releases' `aforge-*` assets as `codeaf`.

## What the chat knows

`starting-codeaf.md` gained `## The old name`: what happened to aforge, the adoption, the variables, and that "CodeAF" in the benchmark threads was swe-pro's harness, a different program. Probes for those questions are in the manual's test table.

## Deliberately not in this pull request

body:
**One idea: the switcher card and the tab row are the same list, read two ways.** Six commits follow from that; the seventh is spacing.

**The card is now `alt+k` (`opt+k` on a Mac).** #1062 is folded in and closed as subsumed — it moved the switcher off `ctrl+k` so that key could be kill-to-the-end-of-the-line, and it deletes the `Chats ▾` control on the tab row. Both PRs edited the same three files and #1062 deleted `hopOpenAll`, which this one edits, so one resolution beat two.

## What you'll notice using it

1. **`enter` works from home.** It used to switch the conversation *behind* home and leave home standing, so the key looked dead while it had quietly swapped what the screen was drawn over. `hopTake` now ends in `hopLand`, which comes down off whatever place is showing — home, tasks, standing, memory, spend, search, settings.
2. **Rows are in tab order.** Leftmost tab is row 1, so `3` on the card is the third tab. The cursor still starts on the last conversation, so `alt+k` `enter` still means "back where I was".
3. **Close a tab, the row leaves the list** — down behind the fold, still held and still running, `enter` brings it and its tab back. By the `×`, by `ctrl+w` in the conversation, or by `ctrl+w` on the card.
4. **The foot is `→ show closed` / `← hide closed`**, and one dim `closed` marks where the tabs stop, spaced the way the head's `open` is.
5. **Long names fit.** The name column takes the spare width instead of `nothing new` taking it, with two cells of air so a name that fills its column never runs into the clause.

## Wording fixed

- `ctrl+w put away` → **`ctrl+w close tab`**. `put away` is home's `ctrl+e`, which ARCHIVES a conversation until its name is typed — a durable act one keystroke away from this one. The card's own receipt already said `tab closed`.
- **Every `✕` row says why it refuses**: `open in another window`, or `that folder is gone`. `hopRest` asked the disk about the folder for the glyph but left the field the clause reads false, so one of the two cases drew the refusing mark with nothing beside it.

## Removed

- The wrapped title block under the list. It only ever repeated the selected row's own name, only appeared when that name happened to be long, and cost the rows under it their places on a short card.
- The `Chats ▾` control at the right end of the tab row, with #1062's own reasoning: `→` opens the fold and a second door is a second thing to keep in step. `hopOpenAll` goes with it.

## Found in review, fixed

- **`ctrl+w` on a conversation this window never opened closed nothing and said it had.** `hopTabbed` asked `tabShut` alone, and nothing ever dismissed a conversation this terminal has not held — so the map was silent and silence read as "it has a tab". It now asks `row.open` too. `hopReading` never noticed because every row it splits is one the keeper holds; `hopAway` did.
- **The seam's three lines were charged whether or not it was drawn.** On a short card the window lost three rows, the rows it lost were the closed ones, and `→ show closed` made the list SHORTER and showed nothing. They are given up in order now — the air, then the word — and a card too short even for the word draws the closed rows without it.

## Under it

- `hopReading` splits its rows on `hopTabbed`, which asks `tabShut` and never the drawn strip — the strip is a frame behind the keystroke, so a card rebuilt from it after its own `ctrl+w` kept the row it had just closed.
- `hopStripOrder` lays the rows out the way the strip is; the recency walk survives as the tie-break for a conversation with no tab.
- `hopFirstStop` is a method now: it walks the previous-stack, because row zero stopped being the conversation `tab` would go to.
- `hopOpenRows` is the figure the reading returned rather than a walk of rows, which gain the rest of the machine when the fold opens. The head's `3 of 12` is how many TABS are on the row.
- `hopSubjectCol` is gone: the clause has the fixed column (`hopNoteCol`) and the name takes what is left, up to `hopSubjectMax`.

## Paperwork

`make pr-ready` green on the head commit — the light gate plus the full `internal/tui3` suite with `-count=1`, 317s. Fourteen tests added or rewritten in `hop_test.go`, each verified to fail without its change. Six change entries carry the invalidations.

`keys.md`'s switcher section broke the manual's retrieval gate by growing too long after three changes landed in it; the layout and the ordering are now sections of their own. The card drawing on that page is regenerated from `hopCardLines` rather than hand-patched, which is also how the one conflict with #1041's `codeaf` rename was resolved — nothing else in the branch spelled the product name.

## One defect found on the way, already fixed on dev

`internal/tui3`'s suite walked the developer's real `$HOME` — `askFolderStore` → `scanFolderRoots` starts at `os.UserHomeDir()`, and `TestMain` deliberately leaves `HOME` alone — so on a cold cache or a loaded box that scan blew the harness's five-second budget and panicked, taking the whole test binary down and reporting the package red at ~60s. It cost this branch several false reds. #1058 landed the seam (`folderRootScan`, answered with nothing in `TestMain`) while this was open, and it is gone.

body:
`ctrl+e` on home put a conversation away correctly and instantly — and then the row sat there for several seconds before it went. The owner met it as a UI that lagged its own message: `put away · type its name to find it again` printed under a row still on the screen.

## Why

Home's `ctrl+e` writes and then re-reads the world on the spot, and says so in its own comment — *"The world is re-read on the spot so the row moves under the hand rather than on the next sweep"* (`internal/tui3/home.go`). But that re-read goes `refreshHome` → `readWorldKnown` → `worldSeam` → `hostWorld.world`, whose **first law is that it answers from what is held** and starts a refresh behind itself. The write, meanwhile, was a bare `client.Archive` straight to the engine, which told that cache nothing.

So the rebuild redrew the row exactly as it was, and the row went only when a later beat's `fetch` had returned *and* a later beat rebuilt: `hostWorldEvery`'s two seconds of allowed staleness plus up to two of tui3's own three-second `homeEvery` beats.

**This was never only a `--host` fault.** An ordinary local `aforge` has taken the engine road since `v3TakeHostRoad` stopped requiring a host that was already answering, so `chatv3_local.go` builds its surface through the same `hostOptions`, and `localDoors` overrides neither `World` nor `Archive`. A fault in the far-machine caching layer was reaching every launch on the laptop.

## The fix

`hostWorld.archive` is `Options.Archive` now: the write over the wire, then the held copy corrected and the entry aged out so the next reading still asks the engine what it really thinks.

That correction already existed one type over — `hostStanding.save` does exactly this for the ambient side, and its comment states the law: *"A WRITE THAT LANDED IS PUT STRAIGHT INTO WHAT IS HELD, and that is what keeps the row from redrawing stale in the beat before the next fetch returns."* `hostDuty.age` had precisely one caller in the tree before this. This is that law applied to the one write home makes against the world.

The match is on the directory spelling the row came with and is deliberately not cleaned first: over `--host` that is a path on the engine's machine, which this laptop's separator has no business rewriting.

## Proof

Three tests in `cmd/aforge/chatv3_host_test.go`, all of which fail on `dev`:

- `TestPuttingAConversationAwayCorrectsWhatHomeDrawsAtOnce` — holds the far end still (the state the surface is in for the whole of that window) and asserts the very next reading, the one home rebuilds from, already has the row away; and that the duty was aged so the engine is still asked.
- `TestARefusedPutAwayLeavesTheConversationOnHome` — a refused write changes nothing here.
- `TestBringingAConversationBackCorrectsTheHeldWorldToo` — `ctrl+e` from inside the archive is its own undoing, in the other direction.

`make pr-ready` green.

body:
## What this is

When the person asks for something that lives in one of their accounts and that account is not connected yet, the chat connects it on its own in **one question**, and the same turn carries on once the sign-in lands.

The chain already existed (`services` → `use_service` → the connect card → the browser → the wait → the account's tools armed for the next request of the same turn) and was proved end to end on the real binary against a fresh profile before any of this was written. What was not seamless, and what changes:

- On the shipped approval default the person answered **three** questions before the browser: `ok to run services`, `ok to run use_service`, then the connect card. The first two are gone. `services` is a listing that changes nothing, so it joins the read-only lift; `use_service` is lifted by a sibling predicate named for what it is — a tool whose own question is its consent — because every tool it arms is gated on its own. An explicit `services:prompt` or `use_service:prompt` rule still asks; a deny blanket still denies; `AlwaysAsks` is untouched.
- The model was told its new tools arrive "on your next turn", which reads as "stop and wait for the person". The tool description and the success result now share one constant: `The account's tools are in your tool list from your very next request, which is still this turn — carry on and use them now`.
- The only cue that the person has accounts at all was one tool description. The `use_service` belt fact now says the person has accounts it can act in, never to answer "I don't have access to your X" before calling `services`, and that an account not connected yet is asked for through `use_service`. It is a belt fact rather than a line in `system.md` because the prompt names only the tools the call carries; the bytes were paid back out of two sentences that were said twice, so both prefix budgets sit below dev's.
- `2 not now`, five minutes of silence, and typing something else all reached the model as "The person did not agree". They are three sentences now, and the typed words ride into the tool result verbatim so the person's new instruction is acted on instead of swallowed. An answer that lands at the five-minute boundary now beats the clock instead of being reported as silence.
- Pressing `esc` during "waiting in your browser…" left the spinner and a dead link on screen for the life of the session, outside the render cache. The card settles as "connection didn't complete" when its turn ends.
- Typing words at a browser connect question drew "checking your <Name> key…" for a service that has no key.
- A failed sign-in printed the OAuth `state` nonce and "authorization error: state does not match" to the person, the transcript, the model — and, through the `/connect` panel and the Connections tab, on the surface's own door too. Every browser road now crosses one deny-by-default boundary in `internal/connect`: internal failures become `the sign-in came back wrong and nothing was connected`; a vendor refusal keeps only its plain-words reason.
- The manual said aforge never opens a browser for you (it does, and writes the link down with a copy affordance so a machine with no browser still has a way through) and that two credential writers can lose each other's last change (stale since the store lock). Both corrected; `permissions.md` lists `services` and `use_service` where it lists what runs without asking.

The connect card remains the one place the person agrees to connect an account.

## Validation contract

| Item | Behaviour | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Shipped default: `services` and `use_service` reach the connect card with no tool-approval question; an explicit prompt rule still asks; deny still denies | `internal/approval` tests; hand test on the real binary with `tools.approvalMode` unset |
| C2 | After a mid-turn connect, the very next model request of the same turn carries the account's tools and the model calls one; no human message intervenes | session test reading `request.Tools` on the second step, run under the shipped prompt posture so its zero-consent assertion bites; hand test with a key service |
| C3 | The model is told to carry on now, from one constant shared by the description and the result | session test; the sentence seen verbatim in the transcript |
| C4 | Refused, never answered, and moved on are three sentences; moved on carries the words verbatim and nothing is stored | session tests for all three; C4c hand-proved (the model answered the new question) |
| C5 | A sign-in still waiting when its turn ends settles as "didn't complete"; no row keeps spinning; the port is released | tui3 test; hand test after `esc` |
| C6 | Words at a browser question open no key card | tui3 test; hand test |
| C7 | No nonce and no exchange vocabulary reaches the person or the model, on any road | connect and session tests (deny-by-default boundary, mutation-checked); hand test grep over the transcripts |
| C8 | With a hub the prompt says accounts exist and how to reach an unconnected one; without one it says nothing | `prompt_belt_test.go` both ways; prefix-budget tests |
| C9 | The manual is true and every probe still reaches its page | the three manual gates; two probes hand-checked through the `manual` tool |

Mutation checks: deleting the approval lift fails the same-turn test; deleting the boundary-answer receive fails the race test; inverting the deny default fails the nonce test.

## Proof

- `make pr-ready` green (approval, connect, manual, session, tui3; zero failures).
- Every intermediate commit builds and vets (`git rebase --exec` over the branch).
- One read-only adversarial review round found seven blockers, all reproduced before being fixed; the two that mattered were the surface's own `/connect` door still printing the raw callback error and a manual heading that pushed the answering section out of the search window while the probe stayed green.
- Hand tests on the real binary, engine road, fresh profile with no approval row set; captures kept internally.

## What only a person with a browser can still verify

- The real Slack or Google sign-in happy path: sign in, `✓ Slack connected as …`, and the same turn answers the original question.
- A workspace that requires admin approval; a vendor-side Deny; whether the link is clickable in your terminal.
- On WSL the surface's auto-open reaches the **Windows** browser through wslu's `wslview`, so the loopback callback has to cross Windows → WSL localhost. Not changed here; worth knowing when a sign-in "can't be reached".

## Out of scope, left as follow-ups

- A key with no health check still reads as connected until the first call (most catalog rows have none); needs a new seam through `connect.Status`.
- The loopback failure page is still a raw `500 authorization error`; oauth2cli has no failure-page hook.
- No visible clock on the five-minute ask and the five-minute browser ceiling.
- `--once` through a running daemon waits five minutes instead of saying nobody is watching.
- A damaged `credentials.json` removes accounts silently.

body:
## What a person sees now

Approve a task, look at another tab, come back: the assignment is there with
**your answer under it** — `start it · approved` — and nothing to answer. The
conversation behind it takes the keyboard again, so it scrolls.

Before this, coming back re-asked the same question, every time, for as long as
the turn that proposed the work was still running.

## Cause

A turn's backlog is every event that turn has sent, kept verbatim so a surface
arriving mid-turn reads the work from its first line (`eventHub.attach`). A
**card** in it is the one event that is not a report of something that happened
but a question about something that has not — and the replay handed it over
whatever had since been decided.

So `EventTaskProposal` went out again on every re-attach. `app.proposeTask` found
no card for that id (the atomic replay's entries stop at the turn's floor, so the
running turn's card exists only in the backlog), built one, and raised the
question — a question the engine had already recorded an answer for and would
therefore never close. And because a question takes the keyboard where it is
drawn (#919), the conversation underneath it could not be scrolled while it
stood. **Both symptoms, one cause.**

## Fix

- `questionAsked` names the question a card put in front of somebody, in the
  lanes' own keys — consent, a task proposal, a standing card, a harness offer,
  a connect ask. `eventHub.attach` is handed what is still being asked
  (`Agent.stillAskedLocked`, the banked words read under `a.mu` at the moment of
  the attach) and leaves out a card whose question is no longer one. The backlog
  stays a faithful log of the turn; what is filtered is the REPLAY.
- A proposal **restates itself when it is settled**: `taskWait.decided` sends the
  card again with `TaskNotice.Decided` on it, the moment anybody answers — a
  person, another window, or the countdown — beside the restatement
  `taskWait.withdraw` already made for the other ending, at the one place both
  roads pass through. A card that states its own outcome is not asking anything,
  so the replay keeps it in the open card's place.
- The surface draws it as what it is. `taskVerdict` is the one reading of
  approved-and-redirect that the window whose key answered and the window
  replaying a decision both take.

The first commit alone would have left the forming block saying
`not started · the call was refused` over work that was running
(`app.refuseFormingCard` reads a `propose_task` result with no card as a
refusal), which is the second commit's whole reason.

## Before / after, on the real binary

Driven as a person in tmux on the Spark against `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`:
two tabs, a task-start question answered by hand while the turn went on running,
then `tab` away and `tab` back three times.

**Before** (`~/af-taskq-evidence/before4/3-midturn-back-1.txt`, and identical on
rounds 2 and 3):

```
  ╭─ ? ◆ Go program printing first 20 primes, with test ───────────
  │ Write a small Go program in /tmp/atq/before4/w that prints the first twenty primes, plus …
  ╰──────────────────────────────
─ conversation about saying only the word one · deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash · ⠿ auto ·
╭─ ? wants to start a task: Go program printing first 20 primes, with test ─────
│ ▸ 1  start it
│   2  no
╰─ ↑↓ choose · enter take it · esc later ──────────────
  c change · ? ask back · 1–2 jump
 › say what to change… (enter sends it)
```

The second symptom is visible in that same before-run: the `tab` I sent to
switch tabs went to the QUESTION instead — round 2 shows the pointer moved from
`1 start it` to `2 no` and the tab never changed. A question takes the keys where
it is drawn, so nothing aimed at the conversation reached it.

**After** (`~/af-taskq-evidence/after5/3-midturn-back-1.txt`, identical on rounds
2 and 3):

```
  ╭─ ? ◆ Go program printing the first twenty primes, with test ────────────────
  ╰─ start it · approved
    ⇉ Go program printing the first twenty primes, with test
    · this one wants more hands · handing it over with everything found so far
─ conversation naming with one-word response constraint · deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash · ⠿ auto
 ›
```

No question. The card carries the answer. The box is the conversation's again,
so the keys are too.

## Spark evidence

Worktree `spark:~/af-taskq`, revision `7ccfdd12f`. `go build ./...`, `go vet
./...`, `make test-laws`, `go test ./internal/session/ ./internal/tui3/
-count=1` — all green (`spark:~/af-taskq-tests2.log`, session 192s, tui3 312s);
`./internal/remote/` and `./internal/enginehost/` green at `20fc1fee7`
(`spark:~/af-taskq-tests.log`). Captures under `spark:~/af-taskq-evidence/`.

## Tests

- `internal/session`: `TestAnAnsweredProposalIsNotAskedAgainOfASurfaceThatArrivesLater`,
  `TestAProposalNobodyAnsweredIsStillAskedOfASurfaceThatArrivesLater`.
- `internal/tui3`: `TestAProposalDecidedBeforeThisWindowArrivedIsDrawnAnsweredAndNotAsked`,
  `TestADeclinedProposalDrawnOnALaterAttachSaysSo`, `TestAProposalNobodyHasDecidedIsStillAsked`.

All deterministic — a held clock, no sleeps, no model.

## Manual

`internal/manual/chat/questions.md` gains
*"You answered it, then switched tab and came back — is it asked again?"*, in the
words somebody would search for, and it says what is still there when you return
and what is not.

`questionOtherKey` routed keys by hand and bound a short list, so in a question's own answer box the usual text-editing keys did nothing: `cmd+←`/`cmd+→` never reached the ends of the line, `cmd+delete` never killed to the line start, and `opt+delete`/`ctrl+delete` never deleted a word — while the message box directly beneath the question answered to every one of them.

## The ruling

Issue #1023, item 1, ruled 2026-09-14: **the person-facing word for the thing behind a model that answers a request is `provider`.** One model id is served by many machines; this surface called one of them a *lane* while the wire, OpenRouter's own refusals (`provider.only`) and the owner all said provider. Items 2–5 of #1023 are not in this pull request.

Vocabulary only. `internal/lane`, `LanePin`, `laneAutoSaid`, `lanes.go`, `lanes.json` and the `lane.talk` / `lane.guard` settings keys are unchanged — a name a person never reads costs nothing to leave alone, and renaming a key on disk would move somebody's pin.

## Every respelled string, old → new

**`internal/tui3/settings.go`**

| old | new |
| --- | --- |
| row label `lane` | `provider` |
| `lane · <model>` (the fold's own sheet label) | `provider · <model>` |
| `↑↓ move · → or tab lanes · enter choose · esc cancel · type to filter` | `… → or tab providers …` |
| routing `about`: "one model is served by many **endpoints** … no pinned **lane** … a pinned **lane** … no **machine** to name" | … many **providers** … no pinned **provider** … a pinned **provider** … no **provider** to name |
| speed guard `about`: "asked of the next-best **machine**" | "next-best **provider**" |
| prompt profile `about`: "for an **endpoint** that reports a window" | "for a **provider** that reports a window" |

Earlier builds called the same thing a lane …`) and a handful of headings — `(this used to be called the lane)`, `Pinning one provider yourself (pinning a lane)`, `a machine that cannot take tool calls`, `a machine that will not serve my model`, `all providers slow, which older builds spelled all lanes slow`, `Providers (lanes) on a custom base URL`, `the lane I pinned`, `endpoint routing, lane routing, all the same row`.

body:
## What the row shows now

`generate_image` was the one hand whose step row said nothing about itself: no
target and no model, because the tool is in no gloss table and its file is
usually a name the tool chose rather than one the caller wrote. The row was
`generate_image` and a clock.

It now reads:

```
├─▶ generate_image circle.png · seedream-5              1.2 MB · 2.4s
```

- **the file** is the substance and takes the primary ink;
- **the image model** is a qualifier behind the middle dot and recedes to dim —
  the parameter hierarchy `toolview.go` already states for a `read`'s line range
  and a `bash` call's `cd` prefix;
- the word is the **short** spelling (`modelui.ModelWord`), the one this surface
  already uses for a model everywhere else. No fourth spelling was invented.
- **unknown model → nothing.** No placeholder, no dangling separator.

Opening the step (click it, or ↑/↓ + enter) shows what went IN, as prose:

```
│ "a small red circle, flat vector, centred on white"
│ 1024x1024
│ from art/sketch.png
│ drawn with seedream-5
│ <the picture>
│ /…/circle.png   1024×1024 · 1.2 MB
```

The prompt leads, quoted, wrapped, capped at twelve lines with the existing
`… N more lines` foot. Under it one dim line per other input the call actually
gave — an input nobody gave has no line, because "default" is a word this
surface is not in a position to fill in. A **running** generation shows the same
block above its clock: a prompt is readable long before the picture is.

## Where the name comes from

One road, no new field on the wire:

| fact | road |
| --- | --- |
| the file | the call's `path` argument, else the path out of the result — through `app.picturePath`, the rule the picture preview already used |
| the model that drew | the tail of that same result line, `… , generated on <model>` — written by `internal/session`'s `describeGeneratedImage` from the same `model` variable the request carried |
| what was asked for | the call's own `model` argument, from `Event.Args` |

The model is **chosen inside the tool**, after the call's word is resolved
against the live catalog, so the result is the only place the answer exists. The
surface does not re-derive it and does not show the session's default as a
stand-in — a hosted task room's row is drawn by this same composer from a node
whose default this window was never told.

`internal/session/tools_image_test.go` pins the contract between the two
packages: the model that rode the request is exactly what stands after
`, generated on ` at the end of the result's first line, for the slot default
and for a picked word alike.

## One thing deliberately NOT built

The brief asked for `asked for X · drew with Y because <reason>`. **That case
cannot happen.** A model word `generate_image` cannot use is REFUSED before a
penny is spent (`no image model matches "xyz"`, `fish-audio/s1 makes speech, not
image`) — the tool never silently substitutes. Writing that branch would be
describing machinery that does not exist. What does happen and is shown is
`asked for best · drawn with seedream-5`: the request and the answer, both real,
both off roads already there.

## Evidence

Laptop: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l internal/ cmd/` clean.

**Spark gate** — `~/af-imgmodel`, detached on `feat/image-step-names-model`:

```

...

ok  	internal/config	2.731s
ok  	internal/manual	1.565s
ok  	internal/provider	71.358s
ok  	internal/session	185.161s
ok  	internal/tui3	312.669s
PRREADY_EXIT=0
```

and after the manual follow-up commit: `ok internal/manual 1.660s`,
`ok internal/e2e 0.343s` (the untagged needle gate).

**Real-model drive** — `bin/aforge chat --debug` in tmux at 200×50 on Spark,
`moonshotai/kimi-k3`, a real OpenRouter key, ~$0.25. Screens under
`spark:~/af-imgmodel-evidence/`.

The row, after a real generation (`success3/`, verbatim):

```
    ▾ drawing red apple into apple.png
    ╰─▶ generate_image apple.png · seedream-5-0-pro
    │ ▸ apple.png · preview  [open original]
```

The same row **while it ran** — the file from the arguments, no model yet:

```
    ╰─▶ generate_image apple.png
```

The opened step, on a call whose generation was refused by the image model
(the first drive, verbatim — wrapped at the frame, not truncated):

```
    ╰─▶ generate_image circle.png
    │ ▾ circle.png · collapse  [open original]
    │ "A single solid flat red circle, perfectly centered on a plain white background. Minimal flat vector graphic st
    │ (#E02323), no outline, no shadow, no texture, no other elements. The circle occupies about two thirds of the fr
    │ 256x256
    │ /tmp/srimg/v3/projects/-tmp-srimg-w/9c2324791eb01c13/work/circle.png
    │ Image generation failed (bytedance-seed/seedream-5-0-pro): API error (400): …
```

— the prompt quoted and wrapped, the one input the call gave, then the picture
block. No model line, because that call produced no picture to attribute; the
model it tried is in the failure the same block shows, and the manual now says
so in as many words.

**Not verified by hand:** the `drawn with <model>` / `asked for … · drawn with …`
line in a real terminal (covered by `internal/tui3/imagemodel_test.go`; the drive
that produced a successful picture would not stay on the row long enough to open
it without re-sending the prompt, so the capture was abandoned rather than paid
for). A real `--host` / task-room row — the composer is shared, so it should
follow, but it was not driven. The phone tier.

**Owed, not in this change:** a FAILED generation could name its model as a
qualifier too — the fact is in the result, in a different sentence shape. Doing it
properly means one marker spelled the same way in every outcome of
`describeGeneratedImage` and its failure strings, which is a respell of
person-facing text and belongs in its own change.

body:
Closes #1022.

## Problem

Four things, all from the same drive.

1. **The chip said `@morph` while three turns were answered by Sail Research.** The status chip, the settings panel's `lane` tail and the picker fold's mark were drawn from the profile row; the wire asked the transport. The two disagree the moment the wire retires a pairing.
2. **A routing change landed on the next session.** Settings → Providers → `routing` wrote `config.json`, and the `lane` row beside it went on explaining `auto` in the launch word on the same screen.
3. **`AFORGE_DEBUG=1 aforge` wrote `run.json` and no request bodies.** Four launches; `aforge chat --debug` wrote them all.
4. **The lane fold had no way back to `auto`** (≈16 `↑` presses past every machine, and one too far lands on another model's row where `enter` switches the model), and its filter box filtered models, not machines.

## Cause

1. `app.pinnedNow` asked `provider.PinnedFor`, but `laneNow`, `sheet.laneWord` and `armLanes`'s `picker.pin` all read `config.LanePinned` / `config.LaneAt` — the row on disk, which a retirement never touches.
2. `applyV3Governance` read the routing row and wrote it onto `session.Config.Routing`, which `newProviderClient` handed every client as `provider.StaticRouting(...)`. A **handed-down** answer beats the row `InstallRouting` puts in place, so the conversation's clients were pinned to the word on disk at launch. `app.routing` and `sheet.routing` were launch snapshots too.
3. `v3TakeHostRoad` was given `debug: *debug` — the flag. With only the environment pin set, the launch took the host road, and the host process (never told to record) made the calls while this process wrote the header.
4. `applyLaneChoice` only ever pinned; `picker.rank` cleared `p.unfold` before matching anything.

## Fix

- **One door for the pin.** `provider.PinNow(model)` answers the machine a request will demand *and* the machine a person's row still names that nothing is asking for, read together under one lock, with the model folded by `lanePinFor` — the same normaliser the retirement was written with, which also closes the surface-spelling seam noted on #1019. `PinnedFor` is its first half. `tui3`'s `laneInForce` is the one reading every naming site makes: chip, `laneNow`, `picker.force` (beside `picker.pin`, which still tells the fold's three rungs apart), and `laneRowTail`. A retired pairing draws `auto (morph cannot serve this model)` on the model row and marks `auto` in the fold; the `lane` row itself is left exactly as written, because pinning again puts it straight back.
- **The routing row is installed, never handed down.** The profile door no longer sets `cfg.Routing`; it installs the row (`config.InstallRoutingRow`, the half of `InstallLaneRows` the panel calls alone) and the session's clients read it live. `Config.routingInForce()` states the same rule for the gates on this side (the lane beat). `app.routingRowChanged` re-installs and re-reads `app.routing` / `sheet.routing` on the write.
- **The record's switch decides the host road**, not one of its three doors: `debug: trace.Enabled()`.
- **The fold's two gestures.** `enter` on the machine in force unpins (keyed on what the wire would demand, so `enter` on a stood-down machine re-pins, as the manual promises); the hint slot reads `enter unpin · ← back · esc`. Typing while a fold is open matches that model's machines first, through the same `tokenScore` the model list uses, and falls through to the models when nothing matches.

## Manual

`models-and-cost.md` (the "next session" claim and the model row's tail), `lanes.md` (a new section for the two gestures, and what the retirement does and does not touch), `commands.md`, `keys.md`, `debug-record.md` and `staying-on-that-machine.md` (a recording launch keeps its conversation in this terminal, by the pin as by the flag).

## Evidence

- `internal/provider/pinchip_test.go` — the law: over every state of the row (auto, openrouter, pinned, retired, re-pinned, base that carries no choice), what a surface may name equals what `drawLaneChoice` demands for a call a person is reading.
- `internal/tui3/pinchip_test.go` — the surface reads the transport and not the row; `laneRowTail` over its states; the unpin toggle and its hint; the fold's filter; a routing cycle reaching the transport, `app.routing`, the `lane` row's explanation and the fold's sentence on one frame.
- `cmd/aforge/recordroad_test.go` — the host road is decided by the switch (AST law) and refuses a host while the record is on.
- `cmd/aforge/routinglive_test.go`, `internal/session/routinglive_test.go` — the door hands down no row and installs one; a session with no row of its own follows the live one, a session carrying one keeps it.
- Spark gate (`make test-laws`, `make pr-ready BASE=origin/dev`) and a real-model drive: pasted into a comment below.

## Not verified

- **The #1022 anomaly itself was not reproduced.** The issue reports it once in five sequences, and it is still not reproduced here; the reproduction attempt is reported in a comment. Item 1 ships the law regardless — after it, no surface can name a machine the wire is not asking for, which is the state the report describes whatever produced it.

body:
Closes #1020.

## The problem

`TestAnsweringLetAforgeDecideTwiceStandsRatherThanRefusing` (`internal/session`) failed on the Spark beside a real-model TUI drive with

```
the second press enqueued -2 more lines for the model
```

A **negative** delta is not a press that sent something; it is a queue that shrank between two reads.

## Reproduction

On an otherwise idle Spark, at `origin/dev` @ `649392ad7`, the race detector was enough — no second workload needed:

```
$ go test ./internal/session/ -run TestAnsweringLetAforgeDecideTwiceStandsRatherThanRefusing -count=50 -race -timeout 20m
--- FAIL: TestAnsweringLetAforgeDecideTwiceStandsRatherThanRefusing (0.00s)
    tools_tasks_test.go:681: the second press enqueued -2 more lines for the model
--- FAIL: TestAnsweringLetAforgeDecideTwiceStandsRatherThanRefusing (0.00s)
    tools_tasks_test.go:681: the second press enqueued -2 more lines for the model
--- FAIL: TestAnsweringLetAforgeDecideTwiceStandsRatherThanRefusing (0.00s)
    tools_tasks_test.go:681: the second press enqueued -2 more lines for the model
--- FAIL: TestAnsweringLetAforgeDecideTwiceStandsRatherThanRefusing (0.00s)
    tools_tasks_test.go:684: the node is not held by aforge after two presses
FAIL	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/session	0.730s
```

Four failures in fifty, **no data race reported** — the queue read is properly locked — and a second face of the same defect on the very next assertion.

## The cause

Both faces are the turn the press itself wakes, and both are the product doing exactly what it says:

- `Agent.HandUnverifiedToModel` (`internal/session/task_audit.go:2637`) puts its line on the queue through `enqueueSteering`, which is a **wake** note (`agent.go:2961`), so `enqueueNote` calls `wakeLocked` (`agent.go:3091`) and a turn starts on its own goroutine.
- That turn's first act is `Agent.drainSteering` (`agent.go:2683`), which empties the whole queue into the transcript. **That is the `-2`**: the queue held the landing note and the hand-over note, and the drain took both between `said := len(steeringQueue(agent))` and the read after the second press.
- That turn's **end** runs `Agent.handBackUnsettled` (`agent.go:1722` → `task_run.go:4411`), which gives every node the model did not settle back to the person via `givesBackLocked`. **That is "the node is not held by aforge after two presses."**

So this is not a defect in the door — it is a test that was subtracting two queue lengths a goroutine was moving underneath it, and reading a node's owner while the end-of-turn floor was moving it. `askDelivered` (`asklane_test.go:35`) already carries exactly this reasoning for a conversation's answers: *"a wake starts a turn the instant the note lands, so a test that only read the queue would be reading a race."* The two hand-over tests were the ones that had not learned it. The sibling `TestHandingTheSameDecisionOverTwiceSaysItIsAlreadyHandedOver` has the identical exposure on both faces and is fixed in the same change before it is met.

## The fix

No production code changes.

1. **The observation moves to a door the drain cannot shift.** `timesSaidToModel(agent, line)` (`jobs_test.go`) counts how many times one line has been put in front of the model — what is still queued **plus** what a drain already recorded — and counts *occurrences*, not messages, because the drain folds session news into one authored user message (`coalesceSessionNotes`). Both tests now assert the thing they actually mean: the model is told about one decision **exactly once**. `steeringQueue` is untouched and still right for the tests that are about the queue itself.
2. **The woken turn is held open while the second press lands**, by running both tests on `holdingCompleter` (a completer that waits for its context and answers nothing). That is the scenario each test is written about — a card drawn before the hand-over reached it, pressed *while aforge is holding the decision* — and it takes the end-of-turn floor out of the race rather than hoping to win it.

## Proof

All on the Spark, at `f3b05b80f`.

**The same loop that failed four times in fifty, now clean** — and it is the sibling test too, which had the identical exposure on both faces:

```
$ go test ./internal/session/ -run "TestAnsweringLetAforgeDecideTwiceStandsRatherThanRefusing|TestHandingTheSameDecisionOverTwiceSaysItIsAlreadyHandedOver" -count=50 -race -timeout 20m
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/session	19.532s
```

**Under load** — the same `-count=50 -race` loop at `GOMAXPROCS=2`, started beside a full `go test ./internal/session/ -count=1` on the same box, which is the shape the original failure was met in:

```
# the loop, beside the suite
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/session	16.279s
EXIT=0

# the suite it ran beside
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/session	182.464s
EXIT=0
```


## Gate

`make test-laws` and `make pr-ready BASE=origin/dev` on the Spark, at `f3b05b80f`:

```
./scripts/laws.sh
laws: 111 files in 25 packages
... 26 packages ok ...
LAWS_EXIT=0

make --no-print-directory test-touched
touched: ./internal/session
./scripts/one-suite.sh go test -timeout 15m -count=1 -p 1  ./internal/session
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/session	184.001s
PRREADY_EXIT=0
```

body:
The README was an install page: four `curl` lines that answer 404 to anyone who is
not signed in, and nothing about the product. This replaces it with a README that
sells the chat flow and is honest about what a reader can actually run today.

## What changed

- **The product first.** What aforge is — a terminal session you talk to, that reads
  and edits files, runs commands, hands work to tasks you can walk away from,
  remembers, and takes slash commands — then a **real captured session** on the
  default model before anything about installing.
- **A section on which folder it works in.** The launch order out of
  `cmd/aforge/chatv3_layout.go:84`, the owned-workspace case, and `/workspace` as the
  door — the thing a first-time reader hits first and the old README never mentioned.
- **Install tells the truth** (below), with channels, installer flags and the
  first-run screens folded into `<details>`.
- **Chat, tools, tasks, models and money, the in-binary manual, headless, remote,
  contributing** — each short, with the long tails folded.
- `internal/manual/chat/running-from-the-terminal.md` carried the same four dead
  `curl` commands, so the manual law makes it the same change. Its first section now
  says the same true thing; every `##` heading is untouched, so the probe table still
  reaches it.
- Numbers appear only where a cited constant backs them. The two places shipped text
  disagrees with itself (`--parallel` 8 versus 32; `--budget` 150,000 versus
  `--token-budget` 220,000) are left out rather than picked.

## What is live and what is not

| Road | State |
| --- | --- |
| `git clone` + `make build` → `bin/aforge` | **works today**, for anyone with access to this repository |
| `curl -fsSL https://agentfield.ai/get/aforge \| bash` | **not serving** — the route is Agent-Field/website2.0#59, open |
| `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/main/scripts/install.sh \| bash` | **404 anonymously** — the repository is private, and `scripts/install.sh` is not on `main` |
| `--rc` / `--staging` channels | no rc and no staging release has been published |

The README says each of those in one sentence, in that order, without apology. The
proxied form is documented as the preferred one because it survives a repo rename.

## How every claim was checked

Two ledgers, both from independent lanes.

- A **193-row claims ledger**: one row per command, flag, path, key, slash command,
  tool name, number and behavioural sentence, each with the code citation and a
  runnable recipe. Every row was run: **188 PASS, 5 UNTESTABLE-TODAY** — anonymous
  clone of a private repo, the three unmerged proxy channel routes, and a real
  `--host` session needing a second machine.
- A **refutation pass** that re-ran all 193 mechanically, then by hand, and drove the
  real binary through a fresh first-run in tmux. It knocked three rows down, and all
  three are fixed in the second commit here: the permission card (the ledger's grep
  had matched a stale comment), `aforge models` listed as keyless (it exits 1 with
  `aforge needs a model to work with.`), and a first-run quote from the branch a
  reader with a browser never sees. It also refuted a claim that the captured screen
  was impossible, by reproducing it: same message, same model, byte-identical cache
  line.
- **The captured screen is real.** `bin/aforge` built from this branch, driven in
  tmux against `~deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-latest`, in a throwaway `AFORGE_HOME`.
  So is the permission block, recaptured at 100 columns for this change.

## Gates

`go test ./internal/manual/ ./internal/tui3/ -run 'Manual|Probe|Corpus' -count=1` —
green. `make test-quick` — exit 0. `make pr-ready` — green. Ten in-page anchors and
nine relative links all resolve.

## Owner actions this surfaced

- **There is no `LICENSE` file.** The README deliberately claims no licence; that
  silence is the visible symptom.
- **The product slug is provisional.** `/get/aforge` bets on `aforge` surviving as at
  least an alias.
- **Promote `dev` → `main`** so `scripts/install.sh` reaches `main`; `origin/main` is
  from 2026-08-17 and has no `scripts/` directory at all.
- **Merge Agent-Field/website2.0#59** and flip the repository public — the two halves
  of the curl road.
- Discussions are disabled, so there is no community destination to link; no Community
  section was added.

## Two defects found on the way, not fixed here

1. `aforge --help` files `aforge models [--refresh]` under the group heading
   `Look at what happened — read-only, no key, nothing spent`. `models` needs a key.
   The README no longer repeats it; the binary's own help still does.
2. `aforge why self` and `aforge why <task-id>` exit 1 on a fresh home with
   `error: there is nothing at <home>/graph.db.` — no key demanded, but not a
   graceful empty state either.

body:
## Problem

A person pinned `kimi-k3` to DeepSeek through `/model` and was answered by Morph, Alibaba and others while the status line still read `@deepseek`. The provider-choosing stack — the belief chooser, the routing gate (#1003), the hedge arms, silent pin retirement on the saved account exclusions — could overrule the row a person wrote, and the picker, the status line and the call log disagreed with the wire. The owner's ruling: that algorithm is slow, weird and wrong. Take it out of the request path and make what is shown, what is selected and what is recorded be exactly what went on the wire.

## What changed

**`simple` is the routing row this build ships** (cycle `simple → latency → price → off`; the three old rows remain opt-in):

- No pin → the request carries **no `provider` object at all**. No probes, no chooser, no gate, no hedge, no takeover, no stall rescue. OpenRouter's own routing answers.
- Pin → exactly `{"provider":{"only":["X"],"allow_fallbacks":false}}`, one ask. A stall still gets the `switch to auto?` question, which is a question and not a rescue.
- `config.DefaultRouting` and `provider.DefaultRouting` are both `simple`, tied by a test; an unwritten or unknown row resolves to it in one place (`config.RoutingWord`). The per-intent split (a person's turn by speed, an errand by price) is deleted, and `routingFor` collapsed into `routing`.

**The routing row reaches every client this process builds.** The harness, the subharness, `read_document`, `view_image` and each `/model` panel member were assembled through `Config.ClientConfig`, which never carried a routing answer, so they ran `latency` whatever a person wrote; one of them retired the DeepSeek pin process-wide on the saved account exclusion before any wire was asked. Now `provider.InstallRouting` is installed once by `config.InstallLaneRows`; a client handed a source keeps it.

**A pin is refused by the wire, not by a memory, and the person is told.** The pinned ask goes out even when `account-exclusions.json` already covers the machine; the 404 retires it through the existing door. The sentence (`DeepSeek cannot serve this model; routing on auto for this model until you pin again`) used to travel as machinery narration and the turn's work chip folded it away; it now has its own kind end to end (`provider.StreamRowNews → session.EventRowNews → a told note`) that the fold refuses to hide.

**The pin governs the calls it is named for.** `lane.talk` scopes to calls a person is reading (`knobs.role.Visible()`, the same predicate that decides whether they are told): the turn and `aforge exec` (whose door now stamps `RoleLeafAttached`); the title, memory reflex, route question, document hands and subharness nodes go bare. Before this a pinned turn paid three 404s, one per errand model.

**The call log says what each attempt carried.** A widened retry names no lane and `relaxed` lists what actually came off (`provider.only`, then `require_parameters`, then `ignore`); the row that ends an attempt reads that attempt's own knobs.

**The `/model` lane fold's `auto` row says what the routing in force does** through one door (`laneAutoSaid`): under `simple`, `openrouter's own routing; aforge stays out`, no predicted machine, no `no rescue` chip; the settings sheet's `lane` paragraph and the `auto (x now)` tail read the same door.

Manual pages (`lanes.md`, `commands.md`, `models-and-cost.md`, `screen.md`), `docs/CHAT-V3.md` and three change entries updated in the same change. `internal/session/prompts/system.md` says nothing about routing.

## Evidence

Every test ran on Spark, none on the laptop. Each lane's head passed the packages it touched (`provider` ≈71 s, `session` ≈180 s, `tui3` ≈311 s, `cmd/aforge` ≈68 s, config, e2e, manual, ci, laws); the integrated head's `make test-laws` + `make pr-ready BASE=origin/dev` result and the final real-model drive (empty profile, Morph pin, DeepSeek pin, `latency` opt-in; picker ↔ status line ↔ call log ↔ request body) are posted as comments below before this leaves draft.

Real-model drives so far (`--debug` request bodies, ≈ $0.05 total): no pin → body has no `provider` key, one call; Morph pin → `{"only":["Morph"],"allow_fallbacks":false}`, `served: Morph`; DeepSeek pin → demand on the wire first, 404 `…permits only: deepseek.`, one demand per turn, bare retry rows `relaxed:["provider.only"]` with no lane, the sentence on screen and still there after the next turn, `⠿ auto · via streamlake`.

## Consequences worth the owner's eye

- **The warm-cache pin is not sent under `simple`.** OpenRouter's own routing may hop machines between turns, so the prefix cache from #1015 is not pinned to one provider by default. The manual's warm-cache section is qualified accordingly.
- The lane beat (free sheet refresh) still runs under `simple` so `/model`'s fold has machines to pin; paid probes are off.
- `aforge exec` now waits with a person's patience on every routing row, which follows from stamping its role.

## Not in this PR

- #1020: `TestAnsweringLetAforgeDecideTwiceStandsRatherThanRefusing` red once under load, negative steering delta.
- `app.pinnedNow()` keys `PinnedFor` on the surface's model spelling while retirements key on the wire slug (pre-existing).
- The picker's `openrouter` row still reads `let the router balance on price` under `latency` too (pre-existing).
- The retirement sentence is not journalled, so it survives the session but not a reload.

body:
## What this fixes, measured

A planning chat (issue #912) burned **2.4M input tokens vs 41k output (59:1), $1.41, 14.5 min**: 18 sliced `read` calls on one 5180-line file, endpoints rotating to 5 different machines, first `[taking stock]` note at round 3, compaction that freed 6%, and 44% of spend invisible in the transcript. Every fix below answers one measured number from that session (+ the follow-up router audit).

## The fixes

- **First-rung floor** (`checkpoint.go`) — the route race used to drag the first `[taking stock]` mark down to the boundary it landed on (fired at round 3 over 43 KB); the mark now waits at `checkpointPrice/checkpointRatio` (round 5), with a probe test pinning the floor against race-at-any-round.
- **Read dedupe** (`heldreads.go`) — a `read` whose range is fully covered by what this conversation already holds answers with a one-line pointer instead of re-paying bytes; spans carry a fingerprint of the message text, so stub/fold rewrites invalidate coverage by themselves; changed files (mtime+size) read fresh.
- **Fold old slices** (`turnfold.go`) — repeated reads of one file keep the newest slice whole and fold the older ones to `read offset/limit` pointers, inside the existing per-step fold.
- **Billed arms leave call lines** (`sessionfile.go`, `loop.go`) — hedged rescue arms and cut-stream retries, previously banked but invisible, leave a `call` row with an `arm` marker; a mid-session model hop now seals one usage line per answering model (was: all calls rolled onto the last model).
- **Cache pin in the enforced set** (`lanes.go`) — the affinity pin used to die whenever the speed frontier dropped it (`provider.order` advisory, honored 29%); it now joins the demand unless patience-refused or the person pins a lane themselves.
- **Shaped takeover gate** (`routefirst.go`) — the OpenRouter-takeover gate counted any refusal as evidence, including refusals of *our own narrowed demand*, so a takeover fed on itself; only a refusal of a bare (router-default) request counts now.
- **Stale-build launch sweep** (`taskpresence.go`, tui3) — the third binary-shadow incident in this repo's history: one fail-open presence sweep at launch names live sessions on an older rev, with the pids — warn, never blocks, never kills.

## Verified

- `go build ./...` green; focused tests for every fix green with `-count=1`; `make test-laws` green (25 packages).
- Live sessions on the branch: single endpooint held with `cacheRead ≈ input` (97–100%), dedupe pointer firing, marks at the ladder geometry, takeover storm gone.
- TUI e2e: 12 subtests pass; the 5 reds **also fail on clean `origin/dev`** — filed as #1014 (not our regression).
- Effort/wire auto verified unchanged: no `reasoning` field is stamped for default chat turns; OpenRouter auto governs.

## Notes

- Change entries 1004–1010 in the wave's vocabulary, one per fix.
- #1014 tracks the five rotting e2e needles on dev.

Fixes #912
Fixes #913

## What

Burns the known-red ledger to zero. `TestEveryLockInTheGuardedTreeUnlocksFromADefer` — the one remaining entry in `.github/known-red.txt` — is green on a clean tree.

This is the provider half of the lockdefer burn started in #431:

- **47 sites across 13 `internal/provider` files** (`armwatch`, `connectivity`, `hedge`, `lanepin`, `offer`, `phase`, `pool/wall`, `prefcarry`, `quirks`, `receipt`, `streamguard`, `waitreport`, `withdrawn`).
- **7 `cmd/aforge` stragglers** (`chatv3_beside`, `chatv3_local`, `chatv3_modelshelf`, `chatv3_process`).

Every site was the snapshot / test-and-set / then-release idiom with the `Unlock` on the success path. Each became a small method that holds the lock from a `defer` for its whole body and answers what the caller needs, with the slow or re-entrant tail left outside (so no self-deadlock). **No logic, ordering, or under-lock field access changed.**

## The ledger burns to zero

That was the last known-red entry, so per the ruling in `docs/rules/ci.md` the ledger is deleted, not edited:

- `.github/known-red.txt` deleted.
- `internal/ci/knownred_test.go` (the ratchet) deleted with it — the file's own header says *"the commit that deletes the ledger deletes this file with it."*
- The shared `repositoryRoot` helper it defined moves to `internal/ci/root.go` so the remaining ci tests keep their door.

The Makefile (`KNOWN_RED := $(shell grep ... 2>/dev/null)`), `scripts/laws.sh` (`[ -s .github/known-red.txt ]`), and `ci-full`/`release` workflows all read an absent ledger as "skip nothing", so the gate is green with the file gone.

## Proof

- `TestEveryLockInTheGuardedTreeUnlocksFromADefer` — **PASS** (zero loose sites).
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./cmd/aforge ./internal/provider/...`, `gofmt -l` — clean.
- `go test ./internal/provider/... ./internal/provider/pool/... ./cmd/aforge ./internal/guard/ ./internal/ci/` — **ok**.
- `make test-laws` — **ok**.
- Manual gates `go test -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/` — **ok**.

## Notes for review

- Non-trivial extractions worth a second look: `hedge`'s `decide` (winner-flip-`close(decided)` kept atomic, losers cancelled outside), and `climbTheLadder`/`giveLadderArmTheVoice` (split across the re-entrant `startArm` to avoid nesting).
- `chatv3_modelshelf`'s two identical refresh sites folded into one `stock` helper (one source of truth) — flagged in case a purely per-site refactor is preferred.

body:
Lane D of the `simplify` wave: two behaviour changes, both about work that a
person was made to wait through for no reason they could see.

**Stacked on #996** (`fix/auxiliary-inventory`), which is the bug-fix half of
the same lane; this PR's base is that branch, so the diff here is lane D's
behaviour changes alone. Merge #996 first and this rebases to nothing.

## 1. The judge no longer holds the seal

The end of a turn waited for BOTH end-of-turn readings. One of them — the
work-or-words judge — stood between the model's last word and the seal, blocking
on a cheap screen plus, on a yes, a mastermind confirm. The answer was already
fully drawn on the person's screen. Parked behind that wait were the seal, the
usage row, the next Submit and the follow-up drain.

The turn's job was never to know whether the ruling had arrived. It was to say
when one may be spent, which it still says, and then walk away:
`judgeRace.takeAtTheEnd` (which blocked) is `judgeRace.spendWhenItLands` (which
does not). A yes that lands after the turn ended starts its task then.

That needed a lifetime for a reading that outlives the turn that bought it —
`afterTurn` in `sidecar.go` — because the judge's whole effect is to start a
task, which lands outside the turn anyway. A reading that refuses to be taken
still releases what was held for it, and a reading beside a turn stops writing
into a conversation that has closed.

The status line's `whether that should be work` is deleted, because the wait it
named no longer exists. Only the reader that can RE-OPEN the turn is still
waited for.

## 2. `reaskMs` — the recall's re-ask is priced

This is an instrument, not a fix, and it is here because the ≤50 ms law can be
satisfied by a request that is then thrown away. On a turn where the person
waited **7,389 ms** for their first word, `sendMs` read **1**. The recall had
cut its own request and asked again, and nothing measured the gap.

`journalPace` now carries `sealMs` (the model's last word to the seal) and
`reaskMs` (how long the request a recall threw away was on the wire), in place
of `sendMs`/`firstWordMs`/`stepGapMs`. The share of turns that pay for a
cut-and-re-ask still cannot be derived from one ledger row — that is stated in
the change entry rather than claimed as closed.

## The law

`loop_speed_test.go` asserted two figures; it asserts three, and the third is
the one that matters here: **the seal must not be held by any reading whose
answer could be spent afterwards.** `afterturn_law_test.go` is new and on the
laws gate.

## Proof

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt` clean.
- Laws, session, tui3, config, roles, manual, replay and cmd suites on the
  Spark against this exact head (tail in a comment below).
