body:
Closes #998.

## What was wrong

`TestQuestionsE2E` has been **14 of 18 red since #933** (`23f5da1eb`), which took
the brackets off every key on this surface. The line draws `▸1 delete it`; the
suite waited three minutes at a time for `[1] delete it`.

The untagged gate that exists precisely so this cannot happen (#184) stayed green
throughout, because it was looking at the half of each needle that had not moved:

- nine needles in `internal/e2e/questions_e2e_test.go` were **inline literals**,
  which the table's gate cannot see at all — it only reads `tuiwords_test.go`; and
- **eleven rows of the table itself** spelled `[c] change` in `screen` while their
  `source` said only `change`. The gate greps `source` against the surface's own
  sources, so it checked the word and never the key in front of it.

The second half is the larger share and is not in the issue's own list:
`questionLaterKeyWord`, `questionTakeThePickWord`, `questionChangeKeyWord`,
`questionUndoKeyWord`, `questionTickKeyWord`, `questionBlankKeyWord`,
`questionPairAWord`, `questionPairBWord`, `questionMoveItWord` — plus the four
landing answers used by `TestTUIE2E` and `TestTaskStatesE2E` (`settleAccept`,
`settleNotRight`, `settleTellIt`, `settleConflictNo`), rotted the same way.

The paid run then found two more of the same shape, one layer down:

- **the chip.** `questionChipTail` waited for `question · alt+a`. The status line
  leads with the question's own head — `? delete the build directory? · alt+a` —
  and spells `1 question` only where there is no head. Its `source` was `alt+a`,
  so the gate was green on it exactly as on the brackets. The row is its own name
  now: the tail, ` · alt+a`.
- **the aiming rule.** `o`, `c`, `x`, `?` are each the first letter of a word
  people type into the box, so the block does not take one from somebody who has
  not yet aimed at the question (`questionAimKey`; the manual says it in a
  person's words). Six scenarios pressed `o` to open a page, the `o` went into the
  message box, and each waited out its patience for a page nobody opened — with
  `› o` on the screen it printed.
- **the room's foot.** It waited for `nothing chosen yet` on a freshly opened
  page. Since #789 the page opens where the block's pointer stood, so it says
  `answering 1 postgres`.

## The fix — one abstraction

A row that is offered on a key now **names the key**, and one function puts the
two together:

- `tuiWord` gains `key`; `say` returns `tuiWord.spelling()` — the word alone on a
  plain row, `keyedWord(key, word)` on a keyed one.
- **`keyedWord` is the one place this suite writes the gap between a key and its
  word.** The nine pasted answers go through it, so `delete it` stays the
  scenario's own word (the model was steered to offer it) and the `1 ` in front of
  it stays the product's grammar.
- Nineteen rows are respelled onto it. The one-space column is pinned by
  `internal/tui3`'s own tests, not read off a screenshot — `relanding_test.go`
  asserts `a resolve it   n drop it   s tell it`, `papercuts_test.go` asserts
  `a accept` / `n not right`.
- `aim` is the gesture, spelled once: `↓` then `↑`, because an aim may not be an
  answer — `enter` takes the pick and `esc` puts the question away — so the walk
  is walked straight back and the pointer ends where it started.

## The law that keeps it

`TestNoNeedleSpellsAKeyTheSurfaceStoppedSpelling` (untagged, `go/ast`, 0.02 s)
walks every screen-reading call in the package — `awaitQuestion`, `screenSays`,
`screenSilent`, `screenEchoes`, `r.waitFor`, `statesAwait` — and refuses a
**needle-position** literal that brackets a key or pastes a numbered answer onto
its word. It reads the table as data (so a bracketed `screen` is caught too) and
the suite as source.

Needle positions are named per door rather than "every literal in the call",
because the last argument of the three assertions is a *moment* — prose for
whoever reads the failure. Every other literal is left alone on purpose: the
suite's own header says a sentence the **model** wrote is a coincidence, not a
source of truth.

Both halves were proved to fire, on the Spark, against this branch:

```
--- FAIL: TestNoNeedleSpellsAKeyTheSurfaceStoppedSpelling (0.02s)
    tuiwords_test.go:1171: questions_e2e_test.go:334: screenSays waits for "[2] leave it", and this
      surface stopped bracketing its keys in #933. Say it with keyedWord(<key>, <word>), or with
      say(t, …) where the word is the product's.

--- FAIL: TestNoNeedleSpellsAKeyTheSurfaceStoppedSpelling (0.02s)
    tuiwords_test.go:1175: questions_e2e_test.go:984: awaitQuestion waits for "1 overwrite it",
      which pastes an answer's key onto its word. The key grammar is the product's and moves
      without this file: say it with keyedWord("1", "overwrite it").
```

Manual: `internal/manual/chat/questions.md` said a key is drawn `[1] allow once`.
It is drawn `1 allow once`.

## Evidence (Spark, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`)

Untagged gate, on the merge candidate — green in a third of a second:

```
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/e2e	0.353s
```

`internal/manual` green (`ok … 1.723s`). `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` clean;
`make changelog-check` clean.

`go test -tags e2e -run TestQuestionsE2E -count=1 -timeout 60m -v ./internal/e2e/`,
three paid runs, tmux `af-e2eneedles`. **4/18 on `dev` → 16/18**, and the
timeouts are gone (`ALineAsks…` 212 s → 13 s, `AQuestionWhoseSubjectWentAway…`
187 s → 10 s, `AnotherWindowAnswers…` 200 s → 22 s):

```
--- FAIL: TestQuestionsE2E (522.58s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ALineAsksAndTheKeysAnswerIt (13.37s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ACardCountsDownToItsPickAndEnterTakesIt (9.13s)
    --- FAIL: TestQuestionsE2E/TheRoomComparesAnnotatesAsksBackAndSends (265.03s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ACardWithABlockUnderEachAnswerArrivesWhole (29.67s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ASentenceWithHolesIsFilledIn (17.52s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/AChecklistTicksSeveralAnswers (17.75s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/PairsAreAnsweredOneRowAtATime (13.99s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ADialIsMovedWithTheArrows (14.76s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ARatifiedActSaysWhatItDidAndHowToUndoIt (5.81s)
    --- FAIL: TestQuestionsE2E/AssumptionsStandUntilOneIsStruck (8.65s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/TwoQuestionsInOneStepAreOnePanelWithTabs (20.74s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/FourReadsInOneBatchAreOnePermissionFrame (17.74s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/AnotherWindowAnswersAndTheFirstSaysWho (21.93s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/AQuestionWhoseSubjectWentAwayIsWithdrawn (10.70s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/AProjectRuleDecidesAChoiceAndTheRowWearsIt (15.75s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/HeadlessTakesTheDefaultAndSaysSo (18.18s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/TheOrdinaryRoadCarriesAQuestionAndItsAnswer (17.67s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/TheOlderBlocksHaveNotMovedOntoTheObject (4.19s)
```

## It is not 18/18, and the three reds are product defects, filed

Not needles. Each one is something the suite could not reach while it was waiting
for screens that no longer existed, and each is reproducible:

- **#1005** — a question whose answers do not fit the row is drawn as a row
  anyway, with an answer cut off. `questionRowFits` exists, its own doc says the
  chooser asks it, and `grep -rn questionRowFits internal/tui3/` finds no caller:
  the ladder's last rung is `return true`. Fires 3 of 3 runs
  (`AssumptionsStandUntilOneIsStruck`). Fixing it changes which drawing questions
  get across the product, so it wants the owner's eye and a full `internal/tui3`
  run — not this PR.
- **#1006** — an ask-back on a turn-blocking question lets the turn end, and the
  question is withdrawn out from under the person: `⊘ … — no longer needed · the
  turn moved on without it`, with their answer half-composed. Fires 2 of 2 runs
  that reached it (`TheRoomComparesAnnotatesAsksBackAndSends`).
- **#1007** — `ask`'s `options` sent as a JSON string carrying `blocks` is still
  refused (`options takes a list; it arrived as text`); `unwrapEncoded` does not
  fire on the nested shape. Model-dependent, ~2 runs in 3
  (`ACardWithABlockUnderEachAnswerArrivesWhole`, green in the run above).

So #998's acceptance is met in substance — the suite waits for the screens the
surface draws, and a law stops it drifting again — and the remaining red is real
findings rather than rot.

## What changed

The `lane` row's default (`auto`) ran aforge's own lane chooser on every request — paying the measurement budget to second-guess a router that balances well most of the time. Now `auto` lends the routing to OpenRouter: requests go out with the legacy preferences (sort word, strike-ledger order, price ceiling) and the router picks the machine.

**aforge takes over when the router lets go.** A per-model gate (`internal/provider/routefirst.go`) counts routing refusals (429s, permit-only 404s) and answers that came back unusable (thread lost, tool markup, cut stream). Two of either in a short while arms the chooser for a 30-minute window: the request then carries the chooser's closed set exactly as a pin would. Good answers count the evidence back down; the window lapses and the router routes again.

**Never a cold guess.** The belief ledger learns from every named lane's answers regardless of who chose (`noteLane`, `noteLaneOutcome`), so when a takeover comes the chooser ranks lanes it has been watching, not strangers.

- `pinned: x` unchanged — a person's word outranks both
- `openrouter` = `auto` without the safety: same router routing, aforge never intervenes
- the takeover says itself once, parked until a watched call, in one sentence
- manual (`lanes.md`, `models-and-cost.md`), settings hint, and picker note updated in the same change (manual law)

## Proof

- `internal/provider`, `internal/lane`, `internal/e2e`, `internal/config`, manual gates: green on the laptop
- `make pr-ready`: running on Spark
- live DeepSeek call: next

## Takeover thresholds (judgment call)

2 refusals (5-min window) or 2 bad answers (30-min window) → 30-min takeover. Seeded from the strike ledger's own cooldown and the count a person has already been offered by the time they'd reach for `/model`.

body:
## Why this kept happening

The owner sees this on every launch inside the aforge-v2 checkout:

```
engine: Santoshs-MacBook-Pro is still running an older aforge and something is still going in it — let that finish, or run aforge engine --stop on Santoshs-MacBook-Pro
```

**The remedy in that sentence stops the wrong engine.** `aforge engine --stop` with no `--workspace` resolves to the **home directory**, never to the workspace being complained about. So copying the line exactly as written, from inside a checkout, stops the healthy home host and leaves the offending one running — and the line comes back on the next launch. Forever.

That is how one host survived twenty-two hours and eight rebuilds of advice. Measured live before the fix: a daemon started 2026-09-11 11:23 from a dirty build, still holding the aforge-v2 workspace, answering wire **14** while this build speaks **16**. `remote.Version` went 14→15 at `ed8371321` and 15→16 at `319c949e9`, both after that process started, so it legitimately spoke a wire this surface cannot read. Retire asked it to go, it answered busy, the versions differed, and the harsh sentence fired — correctly. The window then ran in-process with no engine behind it, every time.

`aforge engine --stop --workspace <the checkout>` retired it at once.

## The fix

Both arms of `staleEngineHostSentence` now spell `--workspace <path>`, taken from the host's **own** answer (`remote.HostSelf.Workspace`) rather than from what this process thinks it opened — the sentence is about the machine that will not let go, so the words a person types have to name what *it* is holding. A host too old to fill that field keeps the bare command rather than being handed an invented path.

`sessionHeldElsewhereSentence` in `chatv3.go` already spells the flag for exactly this reason, and its comment names `staleEngineHostSentence` as its voice. The voice was the one place not doing it.

## What this deliberately does not change

The version-mismatch branch itself. Refusing to splice a wire-16 surface onto a wire-14 host is right, and the gentler `busyEngineHostSentence` road cannot honestly be offered across frames this build cannot read.

## Two things found on the way, filed rather than fixed here

1. **A dirty tree makes every rebuild a new engine identity.** `buildinfo.Identity()` returns the bare revision only when the tree is clean; dirty, it appends the build timestamp, and `make build` computes dirtiness from `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal` — so **untracked files alone** make every rebuild a different engine. That is by design and is not this bug (a build mismatch alone lands on the gentle sentence), but it is worth knowing.
2. **A host can be pinned non-idle by a connection whose peer is gone.** `binary.replaced()` only retires an idle host, and the offending daemon held an accepted connection whose peer endpoint belonged to no process on the machine. That is why it could never self-retire. Separate defect, mechanism unconfirmed, filing separately.

`go build ./...` clean; `go test ./cmd/aforge/ -run 'Stale|Engine'` green. The manual page quoting both sentences is updated in the same change, with a paragraph on why the flag has to be typed.

body:
Home's foot box grew to fit its draft and no further, so the commonest state — a question one sentence long — drew a **single row** between the rule above it and the hint below it. Reported as too thin to notice and not reading as somewhere to type. One row of text bounded by two rows of chrome has no mass of its own.

`homeDraftFloor` is three, and it is the **same three** as `homeDraftRows`. That makes the typing area a block of one height: it does not grow under the hand as a sentence wraps, and the list above it does not step down a row when it does. A box that changed height while somebody typed into it was the other half of the same complaint, and both are answered by one number rather than two that have to be kept apart.

The rows are padded **below** the draft, never above. The caret's row is derived by subtracting the block's height from the rows placed, so a pad at the bottom moves both by the same amount and the caret stays on the letter it is on.

## The empty box is three rows too

The first cut left an untyped box at one row, on the argument that three blank rows held open would be a cockpit. That was wrong on its own terms: the one thing on this screen a person types into should be a block they can see *before* they have typed anything, and a box that jumped from one row to three on the first keystroke shifted the list up under the hand reaching for it. The resting rows are the box's silhouette and not its surface — the press span stays empty, so a click on them falls through to the place underneath exactly as a click on the resting row always has.

## Three things the suite caught, all of them real

**The floor is the CONVERSATION'S floor, not home's.** The chat's foot and a place's foot are the same rows, and `esc` between them may not move any of them — `TestWalkingBetweenAChatAndThePlacesMovesNothingAtTheFoot`, a defect PLACES-AUDIT lane K found and fixed once already. A floor that held on home alone put it straight back. So `boxFloor` is asked by the chat's `inputBlock` — which `inputHeight` and the drawing both go through, so the rows reserved and the rows drawn cannot disagree — and by every place's frame. **On a frame tall enough for it, a conversation's transcript is two rows shorter than it was.**

**The floor is spent out of rows the frame has to spare, never out of the smallest frame's body.** Held open unconditionally the three rows cost home a whole panel off the bottom of its column at 80×24, made an empty place draw its rule where its whisper had been, and let a long roster squeeze the rail's standing section out. Three laws exist to catch exactly that and all three did. `boxFloor` compares the body the floor would leave against the body an 80×24 frame has under a one-row box — twenty-six rows and taller — written as that comparison rather than as the number, because the number is a consequence of the head and the foot and would rot the next time either moves.

**`draftBlock` allocated its block at the rows it held rather than at its cap**, so every pad reallocated on every frame of a scroll. `TestOneScreenScrollOfFourThousandLinesStaysInsideTheAllocationLaw` priced it at 235 against a ceiling of 230. Allocated at `maxRows` the pad lands in room already there — the ceiling is untouched.

Five laws had `- 3`, `- 4` or `placeFootRows` written into their own slicing, which was fine while the box was one row everywhere. `placeFootRowsAt(height)` is that arithmetic once, and each of them asks it; `placeFootRows` itself moves out of `placelaws_test.go` and into `pages.go` beside the code that spends those rows.

## `aforge engine --stop-all`

The other half of the same afternoon. The stale-engine refusal names one workspace, and a person who does not know *which* of their folders is the problem was left reading a directory of hashes. `enginehost.Held` reads the plain-text `workspace` file each host writes beside its socket, and the sweep stands every one of them down, naming each as it goes. A directory whose host has already gone is counted rather than printed, so a sweep does not bury the one line that matters under thirteen saying nothing was there.

```
stopped holding /Users/santoshkumar
12 workspaces had nothing holding them
the next connection in any of them starts fresh from this build
```

## Proof

Everything ran on Spark, per the standing order — nothing heavier than `go build` on the laptop.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `go test ./internal/tui3/` | **ok, 311s, 0 failures** (8 → 20 → 8 → 0 across four honest rounds) |
| `make test-laws` | green |
| `make test-touched` | 57 packages, 0 failures |

Driven by hand against a seeded demo home at both heights. 100×40 at rest draws three rows; 100×24 at rest draws one and keeps every panel; at both heights the rule is on the same line before and after the first keystroke, so the foot does not move under the hand.

The chat's own foot was **not** verified by hand — the demo home has no key, so sending a message drops back to first-run setup. `TestWalkingBetweenAChatAndThePlacesMovesNothingAtTheFoot` covers it at three sizes and is green, but that is a test rather than a screen anybody watched.

## What was red

`internal/session`'s `TestHandingTheSameDecisionOverTwiceSaysItIsAlreadyHandedOver` fails
on plain `dev`, 3 runs in 30 under `-race` (`GOMAXPROCS=2`), as
`the second press enqueued -2 more lines for the model` — the steering queue shrank by two
between the fixture's two reads. Its sibling
`TestAnsweringLetAforgeDecideTwiceStandsRatherThanRefusing` is the same shape and the same
race. It is one of the faces #997 names on #959.

## The cause, and the product defect under it

Handing a decision over WAKES A TURN on an idle session, and against a scripted model that
turn's whole life is microseconds: it drains the steering queue before its request and the
floor hands every model-held landing back after it. The fixture was reading both facts
while a real turn moved under it.

Under that is a defect nobody had seen. A press lands on the steering queue, and a queue is
read at a STEP boundary — so a card pressed while the turn's last request is already out
reaches **no request at all**: the note is recorded at that turn's end drain and answered
by the turn that wakes for it. The floor took the hold back at the end of the first turn
anyway, which put the chips back on the card within milliseconds of the press and then
handed the model a decision the person was holding again. Two hands on one question is the
exact thing the receipt exists to prevent.

## The fix

**The queue is the fact.** A hand-over note still waiting on the steering queue is a
question nobody has been given, and `handBackUnsettled` leaves that hold exactly where it
is; the note carries the landing it hands over so the floor can ask. It is assignment.go's
own law about a line said to a node, said about a decision handed to the model — a line
accepted after the last drain was never in front of anybody. No second state is written
down, and the floor still falls at the end of the turn that *reads* the question.

**And nothing beats after the conversation has closed** — the second face the coordinator
asked for, `phasenews_test.go:389` vs `phasenews.go:508`. A held stage is re-said on a
ticker until it ends, and a session closed mid-stage left that goroutine running: it posted
a conversation's stage after the conversation had gone, and under the detector it was a
live goroutine reading this package's own beat while the next test wrote it. `Close` ends
the stage properly (so a surface takes the clock down) and `tellPhase` refuses a closed
session, which is #997's law one lane over and the same law as `steer_grace.go`'s grace and
`asklane.go`'s clock.

**The fixture states its window rather than racing it.** `modelHoldsTheTurn` parks the
model inside its call: no queue drains while a turn is inside a request, and no second turn
starts while one is running. It is not a tolerance and not a sleep.

## Law tests

- `TestAPressNoRequestCarriedKeepsTheDecisionForTheTurnThatReadsIt` — the floor run by hand
  at the instant an in-flight turn would run it, with the press still on the queue. It
  fails on `dev`'s floor with `a turn that never carried the note took the decision back
  off the model`, and it also asserts the floor still falls once the woken turn has asked.
- `TestNothingBeatsAfterTheConversationHasClosed` — no beat outlives the session, and a
  phase armed behind the close arms none either.

## Manual

`tasks.md` and `task-rooms-after-restart.md` both said a handed question comes back at the
end of *a* turn. They now say which turn: the one that actually reads it.

## Evidence — every run on the Spark (nothing heavy on the laptop)

| # | what | revision | where | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | RED repro: `-run '^TestHandingTheSameDecisionOverTwiceSaysItIsAlreadyHandedOver$' -count=30 -race`, `GOMAXPROCS=2` | plain `origin/dev` @ `82624af79` | `/tmp/af-red-handover`, log `/tmp/af-red-repro.log` | **3 FAIL / 30** — `tools_tasks_test.go:638: the second press enqueued -2 more lines for the model` |
| 2 | GREEN, same run plus the four tests added/touched, `-count=30 -race`, `GOMAXPROCS=2` | this branch @ `08c28ee2b` | tmux `af999load`, log `/tmp/af999-load.log` | **ok 59.2s**, run beside the full suite (Spark load avg 8.1) |
| 3 | whole `internal/session` suite, `-count=1` | this branch @ `08c28ee2b` | tmux `af999full`, log `/tmp/af999-full.log` | **ok 182.2s, 0 FAIL** |
| 4 | re-run of (2) on the final head of that base (comment-only commit on top) | `e0b38094e` | `/tmp/af-red-h4` | **ok 56.7s** |
| 5 | REBASED onto #997's reworked head `05f3066e8` (owed stamp / ctx-threaded reading / `taskdelta_law_test.go`): seven touched tests `-count=30 -race`, `GOMAXPROCS=2` | this branch @ `26b525b2f` | tmux `af999r2l`, log `/tmp/af999r2-load.log` | **ok 55.8s**, beside the suite |
| 6 | whole `internal/session` suite `-count=1` on the same rebased head | `26b525b2f` | tmux `af999r2f`, log `/tmp/af999r2-full.log` | **ok 185.8s, 0 FAIL** |

detector, at `GOMAXPROCS=2`, with another suite running beside it.

Laptop only ran what the owner's order allows: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt`,

body:
## What was red

`internal/session`'s load-dependent reds name a different test each full run (#959). The one this lane was given — `TestAPickTakenByTheClockReadsAsProvisionalAndRunsWithNobodyParked` — is now held still, and it never fails on an assertion at all:

```
--- FAIL: TestAPickTakenByTheClockReadsAsProvisionalAndRunsWithNobodyParked (0.00s)
    testing.go:1464: TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat /tmp/TestAPickTaken…/001: directory not empty
```

**13 failures in 5000 runs** of that one test on the Spark under load (`GOMAXPROCS=2`), every one of them that message. 490 of the temp directories were left on disk, and each one contained exactly one file: `told.json`.

## The cause

`Agent.refreshElsewhere` (taskdelta.go) is the reading that tells the model what the other windows on this project have been doing. It was started from the turn loop as a bare `go` of its own, taking no context and answering to nobody. Nothing joins it, and `Agent.Close` does not wait for it — it cancels the turn and goes — so the reading stamps `told.json` into the conversation's folder after the session has closed. In a test that folder is a `t.TempDir()` being removed, and the write lands in the window between `RemoveAll` emptying the directory and unlinking it. The red then names whichever test happened to own that directory.

It is a product defect and not only a test artifact: the stamp says *this session's model was told*, and it advanced ahead of the index walk, so a session that closes with the reading in flight moves the stamp over a day of other windows' landings **no model ever read**. That conversation never mentions them again.

## The fix — three changes, one cause

- **The reading goes through `readBeside`** (sidecar.go), the one door for a reading beside the work. That file exists because four such readings each had their own idea of what a cancellation means; this was a fifth with none. It is handed the reading's own context and **obeys it** — before the walk and again before the assignment — and it is counted by the beside-watch, so a fixture waits on the fact. `tellsElsewhere` is asked at the call site too, so a task node's turn and a conversation with no folder enrol no no-op reading.
- **The stamp is owed under the lock and written behind the path** (`Agent.toldStamp`, placemeta.go's `stampWriter`, settled by `Agent.SettleWrites`). `a.mu` is the lock a steer, a cut, a named interruption and every drain take before a request leaves; a stat + marshal + write inside it is the exact shape #876 lifted out of the meta stamp, and the ≤50 ms law cannot see it because `paceAgent` never sets `Place.Dir`. The owe is registered while the session is still open, which puts it ahead of `closed` and therefore inside the settle `Close` already performs.
- **A closed session does neither**, checked at the reading's *first* lock acquisition so it does not even walk the index. That is the ask lane's own law about a clock that ran out after the door shut (`Agent.askClockRanOut`, #963), said about a reading.

Also: `NoteTold` only moves forward (read-compare-write) — two readings written behind the path can land out of order, and an older stamp landing last would re-read landings the model was already told about, which `deltaRemember` then de-duplicates into news nobody is ever told.

## The laws that guard it

- **`TestTheToldStampIsOwedAndNeverWrittenOnThePath`** (new `taskdelta_law_test.go`, on the laws gate of every PR): every `NoteTold` call in the package sits inside an `Owe` closure. It has to be structural — `offpath.Write.Owe` starts its performer at once, so "the file is not there yet" is a race with that goroutine, not a property. Both the shape it refuses and the shape it asks for are planted, so the law is held to naming one and passing the other.
- **`TestTheElsewhereReadingWritesNothingOnceTheSessionHasClosed`**: the reading is started through `readBeside`, held on a channel across a real `Agent.Close`, released, and joined through `besideWatch.quiet` — then everything owed is settled before the negative is asserted, so it is not a race in either direction.
- `TestACloseLandsTheStampTheReadingOwedBeforeIt`, `TestTheToldStampLandsThroughTheSettleDoor`, `TestAReadingLetGoOfBeforeItRanReadsNothing` cover the close, the settle door and the context.

## Evidence — all on the Spark, head `f9d5d7da4`

| | before (`origin/dev` 82624af79) | after (`f9d5d7da4`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-run '^TestAPickTaken…$' -count=5000`, `GOMAXPROCS=2`, under load | **13 red**, 490 temp dirs left, each holding `told.json` | **`ok … 7.541s`, 0 red, 0 dirs left** |
| the delta tests + both law files, `-race -count=200`, `GOMAXPROCS=2` | — | **`ok … 634.733s`** |
| `go test ./internal/session/ -count=1` beside `./internal/tui3/` | `FAIL` (rotating names) | **`ok … 181.786s`** |
| `make test-laws` (incl. the new law) | — | **`ok internal/session … 6.882s`** |
| `go build ./... && go vet ./internal/session/` | — | clean |
| CI `PR gate` | `touched packages` red on `TestAPersonsTurnIsNeverBoundedByTheWall` (#967's flake, not this change) | green on `002254339` and `05f3066e8`; `f9d5d7da4` running |

`internal/tui3` in the same run is red only on `TestPermissionsFromOneStepAreOneFrame`, the known dev red another lane owns — red in the before-baseline too.

The proof run also caught a regression this change introduced in its own fixtures: three hand-built agents that call the reading directly and are never closed left the newly-deferred write unsettled, which reproduced the same `directory not empty` one level down (200 runs under `-race`). They settle in their own cleanup now — the contract `Close` meets for a real session.

## Seams

- **#999 (`fix/handover-twice-race`)** lands `Agent.writeIfOpen`, the one door for *write nothing into a conversation that has closed*, already carried by the memory pass and the phase news. The order of landing is #997 then #999, so this PR keeps its own inline check — shaped for a one-line swap: the lock, the `closed` check, the three lines it guards, the unlock, nothing between. The comment at `taskdelta.go` names #999 as what replaces it.
- **lane A's `simplify-A`** adds `Agent.gitAhead` (gitfacts.go, `offpath.Take`) — a reading beside the work with no context and no join at `Close`. It writes only its own channel, so it cannot reach a `TempDir`, but it is exactly the shape this PR closed. When #997 lands, that lane rebases and gets the context-and-join treatment there.

## What this does NOT close

#959 is wider than this one writer. Two more faces of the same family were measured on the way and are **not** fixed here:

- `TestHandingTheSameDecisionOverTwiceSaysItIsAlreadyHandedOver` — `the second press enqueued -2 more lines for the model`: a fixture counting the steering queue while a woken turn drains it.
- A real **data race** under `-race`: `phasenews_test.go:389` writes a package-level variable that a previous test's `beatHeldPhase` goroutine is still reading (`phasenews.go:508`). Cross-test shared state plus a leaked goroutine — the same shape as this PR's bug, in another file.

Both belong in #959 rather than in this lane.

body:
Three findings from an audit of this build's auxiliary machinery. All three are
things the code reports about itself incorrectly; none changes what any model is
asked or answers.

## 1. `RoleCompaction` was a priced dial wired to nothing

`Agent.compact` takes `_ context.Context` and makes no model call — a compaction
is two mechanical rearrangements of text the session already has, and the
summariser was deleted long ago. `RoleCompaction` survived it: a constant, a
`TierHigh` assignment, a description, and a row on the Providers tab offering a
person a model for a call that never happens. `TierHigh`'s own five-minute
patience was derived from "a compaction summary over a full window".

Deleted, with the settings and manual text that offered it, and the patience
re-derived from the auditor — the call on that tier that really does read a
great deal before it writes.

## 2. Nine of eleven callers of this package's model door reached the wire anonymously

The guardian, vision, the shaper, the spell-out, the subharness intake, the run
planner, the harness designer, the ceiling's handoff draft and a saved program's
own AI step all called `completeWithModel` with no `provider.WithCallTag`
anywhere above them. 2,309 of the 2,839 untagged finishes in the ten days to
2026-09-10 are this package's, and with them the answer to "what was this build
spending that model on all night".

The tag was a context value a caller could forget, and forgetting it is silent.
It is an argument now — `callPurpose` — so a call with no purpose does not
compile, and the door is the only thing in the package that calls
`provider.WithCallTag` (the turn, the ask tool and the errand ladder each used
to stamp their own).

`auxiliary.go`'s claim that `callRole` is "the one door all auxiliary provider
calls pass through" was the false one, and now says what is true: it is the one
door every **errand** passes through, and it names what is legitimately not an
errand and why.

`nohiddenwork_test.go` is the law and it is on the laws gate: a blank purpose
fails the build, a `WithCallTag` outside the door fails the build, and the walk
fails if it stops finding the door at all.

## 3. The prefix gate weighed a belt nobody runs

`fixedPrefixBudget`'s doc comment has always said it bounds "the belt the
shipping conversation door assembles". The fixture under it had no memory store,
no accounts hub, no standing items and no saved programs: 18 tools, 39,073
bytes, green with eight kilobytes to spare. A configured machine carries 23 and
weighs **53,025** — 5,025 over the 48,000 cap the gate was enforcing. Invisibly,
every day. Same shape as #576.

The gate now weighs the belt shape named `shippedBeltShape`, the same "fully
wired" definition `prompt_belt_test.go` uses, through one shared helper, and
both arms — fixed and lean — weigh the shipped shape rather than a thin fixture. The figure becomes a
ratchet at the measurement with no headroom, 48,000 stays as the stated target,
and the test prints the shortfall on every green run.

**The 5 KB is filed, not fixed:** `stand` alone is 9,607 bytes, more than a
quarter of the tool block and nearly twice the next heaviest. Trimming a schema
changes what the model is told, not a byte count, so it belongs to whoever owns
the standing belt.

## Seams reported, not worked around

- **Three roads build their own `provider.NewClient`** — the standing sentinel,
  the memory tidy-up and the document reader — and never touch this door, so
  they are outside the errand ladder. They have no `*Agent` to reach it through.
  They are no longer outside the PURPOSE law: it now requires `withPurpose` on
  every own-client completion, per call, and the negative was planted on the
  Spark (each of the three stripped in turn, each failing by file:line).
- **Four of the nine are genuine errands** — guardian, shaper, spell-out, intake
  — that could go through `callRole` and gain the ladder's fall-through, the
  tier's patience and a journal row. That asks a second model on failure, which
  is a behaviour change and does not belong in a fix PR.
- **`subharness_intake` builds its window on `context.Background()`**, so a
  person's interrupt does not cut it. Fixing it is part of the `callRole`
  conversion above.

## What this PR deliberately does not do — issue #1010

An altitude review found the shape is one level too shallow in three places, and
all three are cross-package. They are filed as **#1010**, with **#928 as the
spine**, and they mostly DELETE what this PR adds:

1. **The purpose belongs on the wire, not in a package convention.** This PR's
   law can only see `internal/session`; five other packages reach a model by
   other roads. `provider.NewClient` taking the purpose, and `calllog.Record`
   refusing an untagged row, deletes `withPurpose`, `purposeInherited` and the
   own-client second pass entirely, and makes the law one sentence module-wide.
2. **#928: `lane.Role` rides on the record.** `cmd/aforge-replay`'s `roleOf`
   table is a hand-maintained join this PR had to grow by four rows and correct
   twice. `provider.WithCallRole` beside `WithCallTag` deletes the table — and
   with it the one rename this PR carries, `purposeSentinel = "standing-check"`,
   which moves a word collision rather than fixing it.
3. **The prefix variance is removed, not measured around.** `widestBelt`,
   `bare.WidestGrepDescription` and the two normalisations in
   `prefixbudget_test.go` exist only because `grep` and `load_capability` say
   different sentences on different machines (169 bytes). One description
   everywhere with the machine fact delivered at runtime deletes all of that.
   That one needs the belt's owner: `bare`'s stated law says the opposite.

Both holding actions now name #1010 where a reader meets them
(`clientdoor.go`'s `purposeSentinel`, `prefixbudget_test.go`'s residue note).

## Proof

- `go build ./... && go vet ./...` clean.
- Laws, manual, roles, session, tui3 and cmd suites on the Spark (see comment).
- Real-model run on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` checking `calls.jsonl` has a
  role on every auxiliary row and none untagged (see comment).

body:
**THE CHROME NAMES THE MODEL THE ENGINE IS ON.**

`a.model` is the **dial** — what the person last picked, what the next message
will use. What the engine is talking to right now is a different fact. The two
part company the moment somebody picks a model while work is running, and on
2026-09-11 a person read both answers side by side for seventeen minutes: the
model cell drawn from the dial, the `via` machine drawn from the request in
flight, neither cell wrong on its own terms.

### What changed

- **One source.** `session.Agent.TurnModel()` publishes `a.riding` — the engine's
  own record of what the step in flight is talking to — with the emptiness law on
  it, so an idle conversation answers `""` and the caller decides what to draw.
  No second latch: #935 already held this fact, and two mechanisms for one shape
  is the thing the bar refuses.
- **Every cell beside the model reads it**: the seam's model word, the waiting
  line, both `via` sightings, the lane rider, `/status`'s model and lane rows
  (one reading now, not two), the `@lane` pin, and the press targets behind the
  chip — so what lights is what the press acts on.
- **The rung is the rung of the model the cell names** —
  `Agent.ResolvedEffortFor(model)`. Reasoning levels live per model id, so the
  old cell drew one model's name beside another model's level.
- **The pictures are made safe by the move, not by the picker.**
  `Agent.ridesOnLocked` is the one door the model the work is talking to changes
  through, and the scrub hangs off it, firing only when the model actually
  changed. `Config.SupportsImages func(string) bool` becomes
  `SeesImages func(string) ModelSight`: sending needs a positive `sees`,
  scrubbing a positive `blind`.
- **`auto` is respelled `⠿ thinking auto`**, because `auto` is also the lane
  dial's word and was read as "lane: auto" twice.
- **Over `--host`** the fact crosses as its own fact on the photograph the rung
  already rides (`Facts.TurnModel`, `Welcome.TurnModel`, wire **16 → 17**);
  against an older engine the seam draws the dial alone rather than guessing.

### Laws

`internal/tui3/wiremodel_law_test.go` is a package-wide ratchet — every function
reading `a.model` is named with the reason it means the dial, and the list only
shrinks — plus a law that `turnModel` asks the engine and never the news desk.
`internal/session/turnmodel_law_test.go` pins the single writer of `a.riding` and
the four doors that must keep reaching it.

### Proof

Real-model tmux drives on the Spark, dev and this branch back to back, in the
comment below: dev's seam flips to the picked model the instant the pick lands
while the old model is still writing the answer (4/4 samples naming a model
nothing was talking to); this branch holds the answering model across the tool
call and falls back to the dial only when the turn ends (3/3, 0 flips). An
earlier drive held it for 75s across several tool batches while the `via` rider
moved wafer → baidu.

Suites on the Spark: `tui3`, `provider`, `remote` green; `session`'s one red per
loaded run is a different test each time and every one passes 3/3 in isolation.

**Do not merge — this is for review.**

Fixes the `internal/tui3` red on plain `dev` at `82624af79`:
`TestPermissionsFromOneStepAreOneFrame` — *the permission frame does not say "safe answer"*, in 0.00 s.

## The cause, in one sentence

#946 (the permission frame) and #985 (the gate grades its own calls) landed within a day of each other and disagreed about one row: #946 was cut before the grading, so it drew `safe answer` on `deny all` **only while the pointer was on `deny all`** — the same sentence at the time, because #933 opened every permission on the refusal — and #985 then made an ordinary call open on `allow all`, which took the mark off exactly the frames where the pointer stands on the act.

Neither PR was wrong on its own; the merge was. Both halves were stale, so both moved.

## What changed

**The code — the frame lost the safe answer, so the code is fixed.**
`deny all` is the answer that loses nothing *by construction*: the frame forms only where every member has one (`questionGrantAndSafe`), and the row sends each question its own. So it now says so on every frame it draws, wherever the pointer stands. That is **one rule with the panel of one's**, not a second one — `questionPanelOption` has always marked any hands-only answer that loses nothing regardless of the pointer, and a single costly permission never stopped saying `safe answer`. The fix deletes a condition rather than adding one.

**The test — its pointer expectation was #933's rule, which is no longer anyone's.**
It read a `StakesCostly` set as opening on `deny all`. Per #953's change entry, verbatim: *"A permission's pointer opened on `deny` for every call — #933's deny-first-while-ungraded rule. It now opens by the stakes: `deny` on an irreversible call, `allow once` on an ordinary one."* `TestEnterOnAPermissionSplitsOnTheStakes` already holds that down for a question asked alone, and `questionGroupStart` is that rule read over the set rather than a second one. The test now asserts the pointer the grading puts there **and, separately, that the refusal is named though the pointer is not on it** — the two are different claims and the old test conflated them.

The frame's own pointer law is untouched: a frame holding a call nobody graded still opens on `deny all` (#933's middle case, kept), which `TestTheGroupPointerIsEachQuestionsOwnReadOverTheSet` covers.

## The corroboration that this is a code bug, not just a test fix

`internal/e2e/questions_e2e_test.go` waits for `safe answer` on a frame of **four ordinary reads**:

```go
screenSays(t, screen, say(t, "questionGroupSafeWord"), …)
```

After #985 and before this change, no row on that screen says it — so `TestQuestionsE2E` would have gone red on the next live run. The assertion is unchanged here; only its stale reasoning is.

## The stale prose, hunted down

Four places still explained the deny-first pointer as current. Each now says what is true and what expired with the grading:

- `internal/manual/chat/permissions.md` — the grouped-frame section said the pointer starts on `deny all` "so `enter` on a frame you have not moved denies them all". It now reads the pointer off the stakes, matching the single-permission section above it, which was already correct. **The manual law:** the frame's diagram moved its pointer too.
- `internal/tui3/questionset.go` — the header diagram showing `▸ 3 deny all`.
- `docs/design/questions/GALLERY.md` — the caption said the pointer opens on `deny all` "until the calls are graded (#953)". That condition has now landed. The `.ansi`/PNG captures are pre-grading records of a real run and are left as such, with the caption saying so rather than a regenerated screen implying otherwise.
- `internal/e2e/tuiwords_test.go` — the needle's reason was "DENY-FIRST UNTIL THE CALLS ARE GRADED".

Nothing was added to `.github/known-red.txt`.

## Noticed, not touched

`docs/design/questions/DESIGN.md:186` and `TestAGroupedPermissionOffersNoLifetimeRow` both say the grouped frame's lifetime row comes back "the day the grading lands (#953)". The grading landed; the row did not come back, and the test did not fail. That is a separate loose end from the same pair of PRs, out of scope here.

## Proof

- `make test-focus PKGS=./internal/tui3 RUN='^TestPermissionsFromOneStepAreOneFrame$'` — red before, green after.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, gofmt clean.
- `go test ./internal/manual/ ./internal/e2e/ ./internal/iconlaw/` and `make test-laws` — green on the laptop (all sub-minute).
- Full `./internal/tui3` suite on the Spark — evidence in a comment below.

A second pass at making this repository presentable in public: the planning
dumps that accumulated at the root go, the plan documents that had already been
superseded by shipped contracts go, captured raw experiment data goes where a
kept report already carries its findings, other people's machine paths come out
of the files that survive, and the Go the compiler can prove nothing reaches is
deleted.

Nothing a build, a test, a Makefile target, a CI workflow, a script or an
embedded corpus reads was removed. Every removal is proved by the gates below,
and two expected deletions were **dropped** when that proof failed — they are in
"deliberately left" with the reason. An adversarial pass over the finished branch
then found nine more defects; all of them are fixed in the last three commits, and
what it found that this change may not touch is listed at the end.

## What went

| bucket | files | what |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| junk | 1 + ignore rule | the tracked `internal/.DS_Store`; `.gitignore` now refuses another |
| root planning folders | 115 deleted, 2 moved | `ideation/` (6), `issues/` (14), 15 of 17 `audit-notes/`, `perf-report/` (48), `test/ux/` (33) |
| plan documents | 9 | `docs/coordination-design.md`, `docs/home-design.md`, `docs/host-parity.md`, `docs/host-parity-commands.md`, `docs/remote-files-plan.md`, `docs/small-models-sota-2026.md`, `docs/sub-10b-sota-2026.md`, `docs/design/folder-experience/WAVE.md`, `docs/design/test-speed/PLAN.md` |
| captured raw design data | 207 | `docs/design/pin-doe/{cells,golden,sealed.json}` (196), the Claude Design export under `docs/design/home-rethink/` (11) |
| personal paths | 22 + 180 scrubbed | `bench/oneroad/**` shell and python defaults, `bench/parallel/bench-rank.py`, kept `docs/design/polish` and `pin-doe` reports, seven production comments, a private host name, a provider's internal pod address, and 169 retained frame captures |
| orphan Go packages | 11 | `internal/voice` (677 + 387 lines), `internal/gate` (362 + 524 lines) — zero importers anywhere |
| unreachable functions | 53 files | all 68 functions `deadcode -test ./...` proved unreachable from every `main` and every test |

668 files changed, 678 insertions, 38,030 deletions (including the three follow-up commits after the adversarial pass). About 2.0 MB of tracked
content and **2,928 net lines of Go**.

Two documents moved rather than died, because live code cites them:
`ideation/provider-routing.md` → `docs/design/routing/provider-routing.md` (cited
13× from `internal/lane`) and `harness-research-notes-set2.md` →
`docs/research/harness-research-notes-set2.md`. Every citation moved with them.

### The frames, scrubbed without moving a single column

169 of the 1,167 retained terminal captures carried a developer's home directory,
in visible fixed-width text and inside OSC-8 hyperlink targets. `santosh` and
`example` are both seven characters, so the substitution is length-preserving: the
3,291,647-byte total is **identical** before and after, and every column, every
truncation point and every escape payload is byte-for-byte what it was.

Two law tests got *stricter*, not weaker: `internal/guard/sweep_test.go`'s
`guardedPackages` and `spawnAllowlist` and `internal/provider/funnel_law_test.go`'s
`funnelKnownSecondTransports` each carried an exemption for a file in the deleted
voice package. The exemptions went with the files.

## What was deliberately left, and why

- **`docs/design/polish/frames/`** (1,167 captured frames, 3.3 MB) — the obvious
  candidate, and it stays: `scripts/gallery.py` reads them and about fifteen kept
  `docs/design/polish/*.md` audits link to them by name. Deleting them would
  dangle hundreds of evidence lines. `scripts/frame.sh` regenerates them, so a
  later change that also rewrites the gallery and the audits can take them.
- **All raw `bench/` ledgers** (`ab-routing`, `probelab`, `routerlab`, ~7.5 MB) —
  also stay: `analyze.py`, `replicate.py`, `merge_results.py`, `summarize.py`,
  `assert-b2.py` and `panel/anchor_battery.py` read those exact files. Removing
  them would leave scripts that cannot run.
- **`harness-research-notes.md`** stays at the root: three of its citers
  (`internal/session/task_audit.go`, `task_run.go`, `task_store.go`) are touched
  by open pull requests, so their path text cannot be rewritten here.
- **`audit-notes/design-law-v2.md`** (cited by `internal/session/session.go`, an
  open-PR file) and **`audit-notes/headless-regression-audit.md`** (named by a
  changelog entry) stay, so the folder survives with two files instead of
  seventeen.
- **`docs/remote-access-plan.md`** and **`docs/conversations-design.md`** stay:
  deleting either needs an edit to `docs/REMOTE.md` or to a changelog entry, both
  off-limits here.
- **`cmd/harness-design`'s `driver.Plan` / `driver.Exec`** looked dead and are
  not: `orchestrate.go:53-54` assert `_ orchestrate.Planner = (*driver)(nil)` and
  the same for `Executor`.
- **`internal/registry`** stays whole — its test is a law that parses
  `internal/head/toolbelt.go` by literal path — and so `toolbelt.go` stays.
- **Test-only code was not touched.** The large cohorts that looked removable
  (`internal/head`, `internal/tui2/tokens/format.go`, `internal/resident/brief.go`,
  `internal/tui3/folderindex.go`, `internal/store/message_parts.go`) each still
  carry live non-test declarations — `head.go:353` calls into `absorb.go`,
  `folderplace.go:1235` calls into `folderindex.go`, `message_parts.go` holds JSON
  hooks four packages import. Nothing there reached the confidence bar, so nothing
  there was removed.
- **`internal/tui3` and `internal/session` keep their unreachable functions.**
  Twenty-seven open pull requests live in those two packages; a deletion sweep
  there buys a few hundred lines and costs everyone a rebase.
- **The Google desktop OAuth client and secret in
  `internal/config/connect_defaults.go` stay**, as asked, and so do the test
  fixtures with fake keys.
- **Three path references are left dangling on purpose**, each a record rather
  than a pointer: `docs/changes/unreleased/199-load-and-midnight-flakes.md` quotes
  the old `ideation/` spelling inside a quotation,
  `docs/changes/unreleased/740-the-test-tooling-tells-the-truth.md` names the
  removed `docs/design/test-speed/PLAN.md` as one of three places a stale claim
  lived, and `docs/design/gate/muse-evidence.json` embeds a verbatim tree listing
  that `internal/revision/grounding_test.go` reads as a fixture. Rewriting any of
  the three would falsify what was recorded.

Thirteen pull requests merged into `dev` while this branch was being built, which
freed six files the collision rule had put out of reach — so the last commit takes
them: `internal/provider/attribution.go` no longer says `internal/voice` reaches
the transcription endpoint, `internal/manual/chat/commands.md` and two `tui3`
comments no longer teach the slash rules with a real person's home, two
conversation-runtime records and one `bench/ab-routing` ledger no longer carry
absolute paths from the machine that made them, and `docs/design/questions/DESIGN.md`
no longer links two `ideation/` drafts that never existed in this tree.

**One file is still out of reach:** `docs/design/workspace-foundation/CONSTRAINTS.md`
names an individual, a personal repository and a conversation link, and an open pull
request owns it. It needs its owner, not this change.

**Test fixtures keep their machine paths**, per the standing rule: `internal/session/taskoutside_test.go`,
`internal/tui3/{home,lanes,slashchip}_test.go` and a few others use a real home path
or host name as fixture data. They are inputs to assertions, not documentation.

## One red, and it is not this change's

`internal/tui3`'s `TestPermissionsFromOneStepAreOneFrame` fails, and it fails on
plain `dev` with none of this branch applied:

```
git worktree add --detach <tmp> origin/dev
go test -count=1 -run '^TestPermissionsFromOneStepAreOneFrame$' ./internal/tui3
--- FAIL: TestPermissionsFromOneStepAreOneFrame (0.00s)
    questionset_test.go:355: the permission frame does not say "safe answer"
```

The test arrived in #946 ("permissions from one batch are one frame") and the
footer wording it looks for moved in #985 ("enter follows the stakes"); the two
crossed on `dev`, which is what `dev` is for. The file does not exist on this
branch's original base, this branch touches nothing in it, and it is **not** added
to `.github/known-red.txt` — that ledger only shrinks. Every other package is green.

This branch has been rebased onto `dev` at `a09847c56`, cleanly, with no conflicts.

## Gates

Every command below was run in the worktree at the branch tip, after the rebase.

| gate | result |
| --- | --- |
| `go build ./... && go vet ./... && make fmt-check` | clean, exit 0 |
| packed manual generate + test + `git diff --exit-code` | `ok internal/manual 1.644s` |
| `go test ./internal/manual/` and `-run Manual` on tui3 + session | `ok internal/session 0.243s` |
| `make test-laws` | `ok internal/workspace 0.025s` |
| `go test -count=1 ./internal/e2e/` (the untagged tuiwords law) | `ok internal/e2e 0.221s` |
| `go test -count=1 ./internal/splitgate/ ./internal/exec/ ./internal/release/ ./cmd/aforge/` | `ok cmd/aforge 82.531s` |
| every other touched package | ok |
| `go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/tui3/` | `ok internal/tui3 308.676s` |
| `go test -count=1 ./internal/session/` | `ok internal/session 212.126s` |
| `make pr-ready` | see the check run |

together.

Reverts 75af6ee57 (#964, "a running stream teaches the ledger mid-stream"), which was merged 2026-09-12 03:11Z with CI three-green and no architecture review. The post-merge review (`~/af-review-964.md`, Opus, against `~/af-speed-architecture-bar.md`) returned REVERT. Not merged; the owner decides.

**Why revert rather than fix forward**

- The headline invariant ("one stream is one measurement, told in chapters, never the same span twice") is false on the primary path. `streamWatch.sighting` (the rebased one) has one non-test caller, `hedge.go:1873`, which is losers only. The winning arm — every ordinary call — settles through `Client.noteVelocity → noteLane` (`lanes.go:743`), which knows nothing of the chapters, so a six-minute stream teaches five chapters **plus** one whole-stream sighting covering all of them. That is verbatim the defect hedge.go documents as fixed ("a lane whose belief moves twice as fast for having been in a race"), now on the dominant path.
- Every partial carries `TTFT: w.first.Sub(w.began)`, and `ledger.see` gates only on `TTFT>0 && Tokens>0`, so one first-token wait is filed N+1 times into `belief.TTFT`, the wait CUSUM and `l.wait.widen`.
- `partialSightingFloor = time.Minute` is a literal with no derivation (bar §9); `ledger.see` takes `noise = variance(prior.Rate)` regardless of span, so a 60 s / 32-token chapter teaches as hard as a whole stream (§10); three constructors now assemble one stream's Sighting (§1, §11); `Ledger().Note → keep → store.log` (flock + append) is now synchronous on the per-delta read loop (the never-block ruling).
- Nothing was measured. L10's replay (#922) showed the chooser already switches ~7× more than its advantage justifies; a belief that moves faster mid-stream risks more churn, and `make replay` on Spark was not run.
- Tests exercise only the loser path; no winner-settlement test, no no-double-count property, no structural law — which is why it merged green.

**Re-land list** (in the review): settlement rebase at ONE door shared by winner and loser; no TTFT on partials; derived cadence; window-scaled noise; `Note` off the read loop; frontier from the lesson not a re-read; a non-overlap law test; `make replay` on Spark showing switches and regret do not rise. #891 §1 stays open for that.

Clean `git revert` of 75af6ee57; the change entry is `docs/changes/unreleased/990-revert-midstream-teaching.md` (renumbered to this PR).

body:
A `/task` the sizing judge called wide, whose first set of parts the reviewer then read together and refused, ran to the end of its life with **no way to divide at all** — however much of the material it opened, and however plainly the parts were there.

The judge used to answer before the node was admitted, so its yes was one of `armDivision`'s signals and the worker was CONSTRUCTED holding `divide_work`. Once #950 moved the judge beside the worker, so that nobody waits through it, that yes arrived after the belt was built and did nothing but draw parts. A refusal is a finding about the parts that were drawn; it never un-judged the width.

## The fix — one door, option (a) of the two the issue names

`armDivisionBeside` banks the judge's answer where the arming reads it and asks `armDivision` the question admission asks — so a harness design, a quick task, a part of somebody else's division and work already armed are refused here by the very lines that refuse them at admission, rather than by a second list that would drift from the first. On a yes it:

1. writes the word through `TaskNode.armAfterAdmission`, the only writer of that word outside admission;
2. appends `divide_work` to the running belt through `armFamily` — the door every late capability comes through, whose append law keeps the prefix cache;
3. re-renders the system prompt through `rerenderSystemLocked`, so the divide page stands under the verb.

In that order, off that one write, so the belt and the prompt cannot be built from different answers — which is the law #936 wrote when it froze arming at construction. It happens **before** the parts are weighed, so every road out of the weighing — the reviewer's no, the floor, the lanes, a yes too thin to be a division — leaves the worker able to hand out what it finds later.

`rerenderSystemLocked` is one function now for the three ways a running agent's config moves: the clock going stale, a conversation anchoring to a project, and this.

## Acceptance

- **e2e, the real `/task` door with a stub provider** (`TestAJudgedWideTaskWhoseFirstPartsAreRefusedStillGainsTheDivideVerb`): the tool names the *wire* carried on the first request (no `divide_work`), then the running worker's own belt and instructions after the refusal (both carry it), with no parts admitted. Red on dev, green here.
- **the control** (`TestATaskTheJudgeCallsNarrowNeverGainsTheDivideVerb`): the judge says no and neither the belt nor the prompt gains anything.
- **the law** (`TestTheArmedWordHasOneWriterOutsideAdmission`): admission, the reload, and this door — no fourth writer, so the two readers can never be rebuilt from different answers.
- `TestAWideTaskStartsItsWorkerFirstAndTheJudgesPartsArriveAsTheReceipt` asserted that the word stayed empty. That assertion *was* the defect written down; it now reads the judge's own word.

The manual says both halves — that a yes counts for the whole run even where the first parts do not hold up, and which work carries `divide_work` at all — and `docs/design/task-start/DESIGN.md` is amended where it said arming is not touched.

Closes #958

`go test -race` was red on clean `dev` in `internal/session`, and no gate in
this repository runs the detector, so nothing said so. Confirmed again on this
PR's base: `origin/dev@9a7ab78cc` reports two `WARNING: DATA RACE` blocks for
`-run '^TestADoneEndingNamesTheCheckItCouldNotRun$' -count=5`, one per subtest,
and the branch reports none.

`Steward.now` and `Steward.started` are read by the product under `s.mu`
(`Budget`, `since`, `wallIsUp`) while the fixtures assigned them with no lock.
On an unattended session that is live, not theoretical: `stewardCheckpointAgent`
builds a session with `Budget{Wall: time.Hour}`, `New` therefore arms the wall
clock, and `watchTheWall`'s first act is `steward.Budget().Left()` — reading the
field a moment before `nearWall` writes it.

## The fix

The field gets one door: `setClock` and `setStarted` take `s.mu` on the write
side, and **every** caller goes through them — the eleven fixture sites, and
`makePrincipal` in `principal_wire.go`. Three fixtures that were taking
`steward.mu` by hand around the write now hold it only for the read they still
need and hand the value to the setter, so nothing takes the lock twice.

`internal/session/stewardclock_law_test.go` keeps every caller on the door, and
it is on the pull-request gate through `scripts/laws.sh`.

## What the lane got wrong, and what changed

The lane (glm-5.3-flash) did the mechanical conversion correctly. Three things
were wrong on top of it:

1. **It committed its own scratch file.** `task-2-x1-ci-race-docs.md`, 146 lines
   at the repository root, in a commit called "what the run left on disk". That
   commit is dropped.
2. **`makePrincipal` was left reaching past the lock.** The lane's own comment
   on the new setters said "the product itself writes neither field after
   `NewSteward`", and `internal/session/principal_wire.go:85` did exactly that —
   `steward.started = a.startedAt`. It is safe today because nothing is reading
   that Steward yet, but a second door that happens to be safe today is how the
   first one stops being the door. It now calls `setStarted`, and the comment
   says what is actually true.
3. **The law matched variables by name.** `isStewardish` returned true for any
   identifier whose name contained "steward", and said so itself: "a new fixture
   that names its steward something else and assigns the field is outside this
   gate and the race is back". That is the hand-kept list the race came out of,
   one file further away. The law now finds its subjects **by type**: it reads
   the package's own declarations for every function whose one result is a
   `*Steward` (four today, discovered rather than listed) and tracks the
   variables they are assigned to, plus the receiver of any method on the type.
   Rewriting it that way is what found #2 above — the name rule had passed
   `principal_wire.go` because the variable there is called `steward` but the
   file was never scanned, being product code. The dead `*ast.FuncDecl` and
   `*ast.SelectorExpr` branches of its `ast.Inspect` switch are gone too.

## Acceptance

Per the issue: the detector, because this race has no road a person can open.

- `go test -race -count=5 -run '<the clock-moving family>' ./internal/session/`
  — ok, 12s, no race report. The family is the eighteen tests in
  `checkpoint_test.go`, `checkmemo_test.go`, `principal_test.go`,
  `turnwall_test.go` and `wallclock_test.go` that move the Steward's clock.
- The same run on a clean clone of `origin/dev@9a7ab78cc` — two races, as filed.
- `go test -run TestTheStewardsClockIsOnlyMovedThroughItsLockedDoor
  ./internal/session/` — ok, and red before `principal_wire.go` was converted.
- `make pr-ready BASE=origin/dev` on the Spark.

`docs/rules/ci.md` gains the section the issue asked for: no gate runs `-race`,
which jobs those are, why, and the command a report is answered with. Its claim
that `grep -rn race .github/workflows/ Makefile scripts/laws.sh` finds the word
only inside "traces" is true on this tree.

Closes #957

Closes #953, and ships the second half of the owner's 2026-09-11 pointer ruling that #933 could not.

## What was true

`consentAsk` stamped `StakesCostly` on every call alike — `rm -rf /` and `ls` — deliberately, with its own paragraph explaining why. So a surface had nothing to read, and #933 shipped deny-first for *every* permission because a safety default that is right in the design and wrong in production is wrong.

## What is true now

`internal/approval` already computed the answer. `AlwaysAsks` is true for exactly the shapes that hold under a blanket allow — bash's critical table and the calls that act in the person's name — and its own comment says why: a memo cannot cover one. That is the same set as "cannot be taken back".

So the gate passes the grade through rather than deriving a second one:

- `consentAsk` reads `approval.AlwaysAsks` and grades `StakesIrreversible`; everything else stays `StakesCostly`. **No string matching on the command in `internal/session`, and no second list anywhere** — the generic-and-meta law.
- The widening `always` is not offered on a grave call, from the same predicate. It would bank a memo the very next call refuses to honour, because these are exactly the shapes the gate asks about every time. One fact, one condition. `deny` keeps key `3`, so the muscle memory holds.
- `questionPointerStart` splits by the stakes alone: `allow once` on an ordinary call, `deny` on a grave one. **An ungraded permission still opens on the answer that loses nothing** — a pointer parked on `allow once` for a call nobody graded is a guess made with the person's one keystroke.

## The test that said the ground had not moved

#933 left `TestTheGateGradesNoCallAsIrreversibleAndMarksDenyTheSafeAnswer` to fail the day the engine started grading, naming the surface test to re-read. It did its job; it is replaced, not deleted, by `TestTheGateGradesAnIrreversibleCallAndMarksDenyTheSafeAnswer`.

Its fixture command changed from `rm -rf *` to `rm -rf /`, and that is worth knowing: **the default policy denies `rm -rf *` outright**, and a denied call is answered in `approve` before any question exists. The irreversible question a surface can actually meet is one the policy still *asks* about — which is the floor's own table. The replication line in the issue was wrong on that point.

## Proof

`make test-focus` on both packages, on Spark:

```
ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/session  0.098s
ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/tui3     0.098s
```

`internal/manual/chat/permissions.md` answers "what happens if I just press enter?" for each case, in the asker's words.

`theControllersWord` (`internal/provider/hedge_test.go`, from #952) hands a lane a
signal to hold its first word on, and only the control ladder closes it. A
controller that never speaks left the lane holding the call open until the test
binary's own deadline, so the reader got a fifteen-minute timeout naming whichever
test happened to be running instead of the silence that caused it — the shape the
fixture exists to remove everywhere else.

**The bound is the scenario's own patience.** `laneRig.patience` is the one place a
scenario states its ceiling, so it is where the hold is armed: the wait runs for that
ceiling times `heldWordSlack` and never for the package timeout. On expiry the hold
opens, so the scenario ends instead of parking a call, and the silence is the failure —
one line naming the controller's silence, the bound it ran to, and the last rung of the
waiting ladder a person was told about (`"nothing"` when there was none, which is the
fact rather than a blank).

The sentence is said from `t.Cleanup` after the watcher is joined, because a `t.Errorf`
from a goroutine that outlived its test is a panic, not a verdict. A scenario that asks
for the word and states no patience is told so there too, since an unarmed hold is the
deadline all over again.

**Proof it catches what it names.** With the ladder deliberately gone quiet,
`TestARescueTheCallCouldNotPayForSaysSoOnTheRow` fails in 0.18s on
`the controller never spoke: no rung of the waiting ladder was reported before 150ms; the last thing a person was told was "nothing"`,
where before it ran to the 15m ceiling.

### Files moved

| File | What moved |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/provider/hedge_test.go` | `laneRig.patience` arms the hold; `theControllersWord` gains the bound, the cleanup verdict and the unarmed-hold guard; new `controllersWord` type, `newControllersWord`, `theWord`, `heldWordSlack`, `arm`, `speak`, `heard`, `silence`, `lastHeard` |
| `internal/provider/hedge_silence_test.go` | new — the regression net, three tests holding the hold away from any scenario |
| `docs/changes/unreleased/<pr>-silent-controller-bound.md` | new — the change entry |

Nothing outside `internal/provider` is touched. Nothing a person sees changed; this is
the wire-test fixture only.

Closes #971

`theControllersWord` in `internal/provider/hedge_test.go` (#952) closed its
first-word signal on a list it kept by hand — `case PhaseAllSlow,
PhaseBelowPace, PhaseSwitching, PhaseSwitchingModel:` — and that list lived
nowhere else. It had already had to grow twice inside #952, and the failure a
missing rung produces names nothing: a lane holds its first word until the
test's deadline.

The list moves onto the phase type, beside `PhaseNews.Waiting()`, exactly where
#970 asked for it. No behaviour changes; it is where one fact lives.

## Which files moved (the provider package has an owner in another session)

Three files, and nothing else:

- **`internal/provider/phase.go`** — one new method, `PhaseNews.ControllerActed()`,
  added directly beneath `PhaseNews.Waiting()`. Its comment says what counts as
  the controller having spoken, and why the two questions stay separate rather
  than one phase carrying both: `first word` is a wait nobody has acted on,
  `trying again` is the relax ladder and not the router, and `asking` is the
  controller deciding *not* to act until a person answers. Nothing existing in
  this file is touched.
- **`internal/provider/hedge_test.go`** — the four-line `switch` inside
  `theControllersWord` becomes `if news.ControllerActed()`, and the helper's
  comment now points at the method. Eight lines, all inside that one helper.
- **`internal/provider/phase_controlleracted_test.go`** — new, and on the laws
  gate (it reads the tree with `go/ast`).

## The two laws

- `TestEveryPhaseAnswersBothQuestions` reads phase.go's own const block and
  compares it against the table **in both directions**: a phase declared without
  a row fails by name, and a row naming a phase that no longer exists fails too.
  This is not decoration — writing it caught `PhasePlanPaused`, which #861 added
  to `Waiting()` an hour before this rebase and which a hand-written table of
  phases would already have been missing.
- `TestTheControllerActedListLivesNowhereElse` walks the checkout for a second
  copy of the case clause. Zero matches outside `phase.go` is the issue closed.

## What the lane got wrong, and what changed

The lane (moonshotai/kimi-k3) added the method and a law file but **never
converted the fixture**, on the reasoning that the fixture "is on #952's branch
and reads the method when it lands". #952 had landed by then, so the hand-kept
list was still on `dev` and the issue was not closed. Its own stop said
`incomplete` while its answer claimed otherwise. Converting the fixture is the
substance of this change.

Its law file was also 194 lines of four tests, two of which pinned the new
method's doc comment verbatim and counted the `switch` statements inside it —
ceremony that breaks on any reword and proves nothing the membership table does
not. Those two are gone; the membership table, which the lane wrote out by hand
as a literal list of eighteen phases (the hand-kept list one file further away),
now derives its subject from the const block.

## Verification

- `go test -count=1 -run 'TestEveryPhaseAnswersBothQuestions|TestTheControllerActedListLivesNowhereElse' ./internal/provider/` — ok

Closes #970

On dev `c495991a4`, **with the gate green**:


The floor did not have one thin probe. It had **nine**, and any one of them

four lanes an evening: #933 lost one question by a hair to a section about a
tick's cell, and because the gate reports one aggregate with no per-question

and both move upward.

`attaching-files` took the asker's words into its **existing** heading and went
first.

`choosing-a-folder` **did not move that way** — the same edit to its heading left
it fourth. Its `/folder` section is four thousand characters and loses on length
normalisation however many of the asker's words the heading carries. A short
section of its own took it first.

That second form is the one #973 proved works, and the correction it forced on
the folklore being passed between lanes this evening: **a new `## ` heading is a
hazard to be measured, not a prohibition to be obeyed.** What is forbidden is
adding one and trusting it.

The first draft claimed the chosen folder's name is on the status line. That
contradicts this page's own law five hundred lines down — choosing a folder makes

Closes #898.

The frame law in `internal/tui3/framedisk_law_test.go` walked `x.method()` only where `x` was spelled as the enclosing method's own receiver, so a package function taking `*app` as a parameter (`placeFrameWithBar(a, …)`) had every `a.…` call inside it dropped. That hid a live `os.Getwd` on every paint (`app.View → placeDraw → placeFrameWithBar ⊘ a.composerRows → … → errandHomeDir → os.Getwd`).

**The reach**

- `surfaceNames`: every parameter typed `*app` is a second spelling of the surface, decided by TYPE, one list with the receiver.
- The planted shape in `TestTheLawSeesEveryShapeOfIndirectionItClaims` turns red if that branch is deleted.

**What the wider reach turned up, and what became of it**

Two findings, both answered in the code. `frameDiskDoors` is the one name it was before this PR — nothing was added to it.

1. **A press closure is not a paint.** The wider walk reached `readDraftKeep` — and the path was fiction: `a.homeCrossChord` asks a running row for its verbs only to NAME them on the hint line, and the stop verb's `do` closure calls `a.closeHome`, from which the walk fell into navigation, `app.stowDrafts` and the draft record on disk. A paint has never pressed that key. So a literal that answers a `tea.Cmd` is the loop's and not the paint's (`answersCommand`, `runsInThisBody`): `app.View` returns a string and nothing in a paint can run a command. 241 fictional nodes off the frame's graph (3156 → 2915); the update-loop walk still walks the press, and the planted package asserts both halves.
2. **The home an errand opens at is read once at `open`.** The first attempt deleted `errandHomeDir`'s `os.Getwd` fallback and answered `.`, which fixed the syscall by making the answer wrong: it is persisted into a standing item's `Workspace` and matched by `filepath.Clean` in `standing.Store.ForWorkspace`, so `.` loses every machine-wide item written by a run that had a home directory, and draws as a literal `.` where the composer's line draws `~`. The fallback is back and the reading moved: `app.errandHome`, learned at `open`, taken by both readers — learned.go's shape for a fact with one name. With the syscalls restored the frame walk is green, which is the proof that nothing on a paint asks for it.

Closes #967, and is the worked example #968 is the convention for.

A test helper failed with **`no node ran`**. What it observed was that nothing arrived on a channel within five seconds. What it asserted was that the scheduler never started a node. On a box with another package's suite running, those are different facts — and the wrong one is expensive.

## What it cost

`TestAPersonsTurnIsNeverBoundedByTheWall` failed **3 times in 54 runs on a clean `dev`**, every one of them beside another suite. Two lanes read the message, believed it, and went into the task graph and the wall law. One of us nearly filed a regression against an innocent merge on the strength of a 0-in-24 versus 3-in-24 bisect — the diff turned out not to touch `internal/session` at all.

The flake was cheap. The sentence cost the hour.

## The change

```go
-	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
-		t.Fatal("no node ran")
+	case <-time.After(awaitPatience(t)):
+		t.Fatal(awaitTimeoutWord("a node to run", time.Since(started)))
```

**The message says what it saw.** How long it waited, what for, that it is a TIMEOUT, and the one thing a reader needs first: *run it alone — a red that only appears beside another suite is this deadline, and a red that survives alone is the seam.* The diagnosis is left to whoever has the graph in front of them.

**The words are spelled once** (`awaitTimeoutWord`) and pinned by a test, because the entire cost of this defect was the wording. `TestAWaitThatRanOutSaysItTimedOutRatherThanNamingACause` asserts the observation is present **and** that `never started`, `no node ran` and `never reached` are absent.

**The deadline is derived, not typed.** `awaitPatience` takes a quarter of what the run's own `-timeout` has left, floored at 5s and capped at 60s. Raising `-timeout` on a loaded box — which this repository already tells people to do (CLAUDE.md, tui3 at 15m) — now buys room here too. A number typed into this file is the stopwatch `PERF.md:24` bans:

> A stopwatch is a fact about the weather. A suite whose red means the box was busy is a suite people learn to re-run instead of read.

**Raising it would not have been a fix.** Five seconds to thirty makes the same wrong sentence take six times as long to arrive.

`heldProposal.await` carried the same five seconds and the same shape of claim (`the held proposal never returned`) and comes into line with it.

## Scope

Between them the two helpers are **63 call sites in 18 files** — I said "six" in #967 and was wrong, having counted `make(ranNodes, …)` constructions instead of `.await(t)` calls. That makes one honest helper worth more than 63 edited messages, not less.

It stays at two helpers deliberately. #968 carries the convention for the rest of the package, with lane F's position on it recorded there: write the convention down, fix this as the example, and let the remaining call sites come into line when somebody is in the file anyway. None of them is red, and what changes the next deadline somebody writes is the convention existing.

## Proof

- `TestAPersonsTurnIsNeverBoundedByTheWall` green; the stage/wall/await group green.
- Both new tests green, and they fail if the message is reverted.
- `make test-quick` green on `c495991a4`.
