body:
Closes #890.

A `propose_task` the belt refused on its arguments spilled the schema's own sentence into the conversation — field names, the offending argument quoted back, *checks must each be ONE command with no shell composition*. That is a repair instruction addressed to the model. It landed on the person as somebody else's mail, beside a card that already said the call was refused.

The row now carries the one fact a person can act on and stays shut. The schema's sentence stays where it already was: in the tool result the model reads and repairs from, and in the transcript behind `ctrl+o`.

## The mechanism, not a message match

`session.ArgumentRefusal` answers with **the loop guard's own eyes** — `argumentRepair`, the same function the guard uses to decide a call is one repair away from working. So the guard and the surface cannot disagree about which failures are the schema talking to the model. A bash that failed out in the world is still the one row whose detail is why the person is looking at the screen, and it still opens itself.

## Where this came from, and what I changed in it

**An aforge lane wrote this** — `~/af-lane.sh 890`, `aforge do` on `z-ai/glm-5.3` through OpenRouter, unattended on the Spark. I reviewed the diff and made two corrections before opening it.

**Dropped:** the lane had also edited `cmd/aforge/usage_test.go` and `vocabulary_test.go` to put a mutex around the help-output seams. That is unrelated to this issue, and the mechanism does not do what its comment claims — it takes the lock in the setup helper and releases it before the test body runs, so two parallel tests still clobber each other. If that seam is genuinely racy it deserves its own issue and a fix that works.

**Kept and committed:** the lane replaced a `time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)` in its own new end-to-end subtest with a wait for a word the turn only produces when it finishes, the way `testAskHere` already waits. That removes five seconds from every run and the flake that arrives when a turn takes six.

body:
**#934 is merged** (`dev@8f45dd5e0`), so this is no longer stacked: the diff is this change alone, rebased onto `dev@91003c79f`. #934 was the seam this needs — the plan, the watch and the body have to be looking at ONE set before the chooser can demand one.

## What was true

`provider.order` is **advice**. With `allow_fallbacks` true the router reads the list, weighs it against its own load and price, and is free to serve the request from a machine the list never named — which it does. Measured over ten days of the call log (L10's replay, 2026-09-11): **the machine this build asked for first served 29 % of the time; the machine a strict preference NAMED served 93 %.**

So every gate the chooser applies — the capability gate, the Pareto prune, the price ceiling with the person's own λ, the quality floor, and above all `beyondThePatience`, which takes out the machines whose expected time to a usable answer is longer than this role will wait — was spending its evidence on a set the router was free to put aside.

## What is true now

`internal/lane`'s **`demandOf`** states that set as `provider.only`: the admitted candidates, minus the ones this choice vetoes, when there are at least two of them.

- **The threshold is the router's own rule, not a number chosen here.** A demand of ONE machine *is* a pin — `only: [x]` with fallbacks off means the request goes to x or it does not go, which is somebody's instruction rather than a belief's opinion — and the rest of the build already reads a one-wide demand as one (`demandedLane`, the single legal same-machine repeat). A belief with one admitted machine therefore makes no demand: it ranks what it has and leaves the router its fallbacks.
- **The ranking travels inside the demand.** `order` says in what sequence, `only` says which machines; the sort word and the strike ledger's order come off, because both rank machines this request may not use.
- **The vetoes are subtracted, not sent beside it.** `only` and `ignore` naming one machine is an empty serving set written by us about a machine we just asked for.
- **A borrowable pin joins the set** rather than leading an order the same object forbids, and comes off the veto list for the same reason. The affinity (cache) pin yields to a machine outside the admitted set — the same law that already made it yield to a refusal, stated positively.
- **The price ceiling comes off** under a demand, as it already did for a pin: the frontier priced every machine it admitted.

**The cost is accepted and named**: a pool whose every admitted machine is busy refuses and the call walks rather than being served by whoever is free. `dropRefusedHere` strikes a refuser out of the belief's demand a machine at a time and drops the demand entirely when the last name goes, with `allow_fallbacks` restored; a demand **somebody asked for** (a person's pin, a rescue's own arm — `demandedLane`, one name) is never narrowed. `keepingServable` is deleted.

## A PIN AND A DEMAND ARE TWO DIFFERENT FACTS — the send-back, and the fix

The review caught the reader this change had missed, and it was one mistake with two faces. `control.Plan.Pinned` was:

```go
plan.Pinned = len(choice.Only) > 0
```

That was the same sentence as "a person named this machine" for exactly as long as `Only` held nothing but a person's strict row. The moment the chooser demanded its own admitted set, **every ordinary routed call read as pinned**:

1. `lane/control/hazard.go` takes the `Ask` road before it even looks for somewhere to go — so a slow call showed the person `switch to auto? (y)` **about a machine they never pinned**, and no rescue went out at all;
2. `hedge.go`'s `walk` returns early on a 429, a 5xx or a broken stream when the plan is pinned — so the primary arm stopped walking, which is the opposite of what this wave is for.

**The fix models the distinction where the plan is built, and carries the fact rather than counting names.** `lane.Choice.Pinned` means "a person named this machine themselves". It is WRITTEN in one place — `drawLaneChoice`'s strict-pin branch, the one reading of the person's own row — and READ in one place, `planFor`. It restores `dev`'s behaviour exactly: on `dev`, `Only` was non-empty at `planFor` time **iff** a person had a strict pin.

Three law tests, each red before the fix:

| test | what it holds | red before |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TestADemandedCallIsRescuedAndAPersonsPinIsAsked` (wire, `lanestub`) | one stall, two choices, two acts: a demanded call **hedges** and never raises a question; a person's pin **asks**, and `y` fires the rescue | `the wait was answered with "ask", want "hedge"` |
| `TestADemandedPrimaryWalksOffAFaultThatBreaksIt` (wire) | a demanded primary whose stream breaks mid-answer walks to the other machine and the whole answer arrives | `decode stream: unexpected EOF` |
| `TestOnlyAPersonsOwnRowPinsACall` (`go/ast`, on the laws gate) | only a person's own row may pin a call, and a pin may never be derived from `Only` | ``planFor derives a pin from `Only` `` |

`TestStrictPinDoesNotWalkToAnotherEndpointAfterTransportFailure` staged a strict pin as `Only` alone — which is now what every routed call carries — so it states the fact instead. It is red without the fix for the right reason (`only:[B]`: the pin walked).

## Acceptance

`internal/provider/demand_test.go`, against `lanestub` with a pool of two whose pools are full (`Profile.Paced` — a 429 naming itself, the commonest named refusal in the ten-day log):

| scenario | asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `TestTheAdmittedSetIsDemandedAndNotMerelyRanked` | body 1 carries `only: [cinnabar, tinder]`, `allow_fallbacks: false`, no sort word, no `ignore` beside it |
| `TestADemandNarrowsToTheMachineThatHasNotRefused` | one pool full → body 2 is `only: [tinder]`, fallbacks still off, and **no later body ever names the refuser**; the healthy machine answers |
| `TestADemandWithNothingLeftInItComesOffTheBody` | every admitted machine refused → no `only`, `allow_fallbacks` restored, both refusers still on `ignore` |
| `TestADemandSomebodyAskedForIsNarrowedByNobody` | a person's strict pin and a rescue's own arm, each left exactly as it stands after its machine refused |
| `TestADemandedCallIsRescuedAndAPersonsPinIsAsked` | the ACT: a hedge for a demand, a question for a pin |
| `TestADemandedPrimaryWalksOffAFaultThatBreaksIt` | the walk a demand is owed |

## The measurement

Both runs are on the Spark, at `dev@b1e743e0d` against this branch's
`7fa503f05` — **patch-identical to this PR's head**, which is those same four
commits carried forward by two rebases (`git range-diff` reports `= = = =`
across both, no content change). The box was carrying other lanes' suites throughout, which is why the
rig was driven **twice in opposite order** (dev→#937, then #937→dev) rather than
once.

### The L3 rig — two throwaway homes, twenty messages, reflex tier pinned

`mistralai/mistral-nemo` pinned as the reflex tier, twenty short questions typed
into a real terminal in tmux, read back off each home's own `calls.jsonl`.

| | dev pass 1 | **#937 pass 1** | #937 pass 2 | dev pass 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| calls with a named server | 75 | 75 | 56 | 53 |
| **served == the machine the row names** | 72/75 = **96 %** | 32/75 = **42 %** | 15/56 = **26 %** | 48/53 = **90 %** |
| whole wait p50 | 679 ms | **589 ms** | **312 ms** | 536 ms |
| whole wait p90 | 2421 ms | 2203 ms | 2358 ms | 2481 ms |
| first token p50 | 337 ms | **298 ms** | **245 ms** | 397 ms |
| machine switches | 41 | 23 | 14 | 16 |

**The served-equals-asked column went the wrong way, and it is the metric that
broke rather than the routing.** `calllog.Record.Lane` is documented as *"the
first entry of the `provider.order` this request carried, or the pin"* — ONE
name. Under a demand the request carries a SET, and `allow_fallbacks: false`
means the router must serve from inside it but is free to choose which member.
So on this branch the column is measuring "did the router pick the machine we
ranked first", while what the demand actually buys — "did the answer come from a
machine this build admitted" — is **true by construction and unrecorded**.

On `dev` the same column is close to tautological in the other direction: the
affinity pin leads `provider.order` with **the machine that answered last**, so
"asked" is largely "whoever served the previous call", and 90–96 % agreement says
the pin is sticky rather than that the routing was honoured. (L10's ten-day
replay of the same field reads 29 % over the whole log; this rig is one model in
a fresh home, so the two are not comparable populations.)

**What did move, in the same direction in both passes:** the whole wait p50
(679→589 ms, 536→312 ms), the first token p50 (337→298 ms, 397→245 ms), and the
machine switches per call (0.55→0.31, 0.30→0.25). Under the demand the router
concentrated on the fastest admitted machine — DeepInfra served 50 of 75 and 42
of 56 on this branch against 38 of 75 and 39 of 53 on dev — which is the set
narrowing doing what it was meant to do. No call was lost: the arms with 20
messages produced the same 75 rows on both builds.

**The one seam that would make this measurable is one field, and it is filed as
#969.** A row can only say `lane`, so "served ∈ asked" cannot be computed for a
demand. Recording the demanded SET beside it — `knobs.laneChoice.Only` into a
`lanes` column on `calllog.Record` (`internal/calllog`, filled in
`internal/provider/calllog.go`) — is the whole of the change, and it is the same
seam #891's own comment asked for ("the census gains served ≠ asked as a family
that can actually go to ~0"). Left out of this PR deliberately: it is a change to
the log's schema and to the census family that reads it, and it wants its own
test. **The change entry carries an `invalidates:` line saying the column has
changed meaning**, so nobody reads 26–42 % in production as a regression.

### `make replay` — the tool cannot host the demanding chooser, and here is exactly why

Run at both heads over the same log
(`LOG=~/.aforge/logs/calls.jsonl SIGHTINGS=~/.aforge/v3/lanes.log`, 995 scored
requests). The two reports are **identical byte for byte** apart from the
`make: Entering directory` line. The `current` row, unattended, on both:

```
| policy    | scored | mean regret | median | p90    | total | agreed | no opinion | unpriced | switches | cache forfeited |
| `served`  |    995 |       7.21s |  0.71s | 15.40s |  2.0h |    99% |         1% |       2% |      336 |     969,273 tok |
| `current` |    995 |       3.91s |  0.35s |  6.39s |  1.1h |    41% |         0% |      11% |      458 |   4,063,054 tok |
```

**Why it cannot tell them apart.** `Policy.Demand(asked) string` returns ONE
machine, and `devChooser.Demand` reads `choice.Only[0]` and falls back to
`choice.Order[0]`. `demandOf` builds `Only` from the ranked `scored` slice, so
`Only[0] == Order[0]` **always** — the demand changes *whether the router may go
elsewhere*, never *which machine is asked for first*. The instrument therefore
sees the same answer from both builds, and it is right to: this is not a ranking
change, and the replay proves that much.

It also could not price the difference even with a wider interface, because the
log it replays was written under `allow_fallbacks: true`. "What would the router
have done had it been forbidden to leave this set" is a counterfactual about the
router, and nothing in the log observes it.

**The one seam that would let it host this:** `Policy.Demand` returning the whole
demanded SET rather than one name, plus a world model that can answer "was the
machine that served inside this set" — which needs the same `lanes` column on the
call row as above (#969). With that one field, both instruments start measuring
the thing this change is about, and neither needs a new mechanism.

## Manual

`lanes.md` gains *"The machines your message may go to are asked for by name — and the provider may not go outside them"*: the set is named and closed, the 29 %/93 % reading is why, what it costs when the set runs out (a move, not an ending), and that a set of one is never made this way because a set of one is a pin. The old "auto ranks what is left" paragraph now says the survivors are asked for by name, and the `switch to auto?` page says out loud that the question is only ever about a machine you pinned yourself — on auto a slow machine in the set is simply left.

## Owed, and stated rather than hidden

- **`PhaseNews.Lane` / "trying Novita".** The waiting line still draws the ordinal. The machine the NEXT body will ask for is the plan's move (`move.Lane` in `dispatch.go`'s retry loop); `notePhase` already takes the context but not the move, so the fill is one argument at three call sites in a file this PR does not own, and it wants its own test. Reported rather than worked around.
- **The wire acceptance for an exhausted demand** is still asserted of the composed object, with the reason in the test's own comment: on the wire a pool whose every machine has refused has no move left, so the ladder strips the preference by itself.

title: Lanes: the chooser demands the set it admitted, instead of suggesting it

body:
## What was wrong

A model a person names while work is running landed at the next **turn**. For a
conversation that is seconds. For a task step it is up to twenty minutes.

Measured, 2026-09-11 14:40:10: a step sat on `waiting · rate limited · 13m 37s`.
The owner picked `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` in the room and typed `continue`. The room
answered **`its next turn takes it`**, and at 14:41:00 the step was still talking
to the model they had moved off. The pick was real and had landed on the agent —
what was missing was anything that made the request in flight let go of it.

The reviewer of #925 found the same thing from the other end: the room and two
manual pages promised "the next request", which `Agent.SetModel`'s own contract
and `runTurn`'s latch made false. This lands the mechanism those sentences need.

## The rule

**A person's word wins in ≤ `lane.SpokenWithin`.** A model change applies to the
request in flight if that request has produced nothing usable yet; otherwise it
applies to the next request. Never the next turn.

## One door, one predicate, one read site

- **`activeGeneration` now carries the turn's own `partialBuffer`**, so
  `productive()` — *has this request produced anything a person could use* — is a
  read of the text already on their screen and in the transcript, not a second
  count of the same deltas. Reaching a machine, parked on a pace, walking a
  refusal, thinking where nobody can read: all one state, and it is a **state,
  never a duration**.
- **`Agent.hearModelLocked`** is the one place a person's model reaches running
  work. It records the word for the boundary and, when there is nothing to lose,
  cuts through `cutGenerationLocked` with a third cause, `errPersonCut`. It
  answers `ModelLandsNow` or `ModelLandsNextRequest`.
- **`cutGenerationLocked` is now the only place a generation is cancelled.**
  `Agent.Steer` used to write the two lines itself; it calls the door now.
- **`runTurn` re-reads the word at ONE site**, the top of the request ladder, and
  starts the fallback chain again from the model the person named.
- **`freshModel`** is the one place a model gets a whole budget of its own — both
  clocks, both counts. The rescue hop's five copied lines are gone; it calls it.

## What a person sees

The room says which of the two happened — `switching now`, or `the next request
takes it` — and never the word "turn". `RetargetTask` carries the landing, over
the `--host` wire as well; an engine too old to answer gets the safe half.

## Laws

- `internal/session/generation_law_test.go` (go/ast) — a second place that
  cancels a generation fails the build.
- `TestAModelNamedWhileNothingHasComeBackIsOnTheVeryNextRequest` — asserts on the
  wire (which model the adapter was handed) and on the clock.
- `TestAModelNamedWhileTheAnswerIsArrivingLetsThatAnswerFinish` — not cut, answer
  kept whole, next request on the new model, nothing reported as a retry.
- `TestStopWhileNothingHasComeBackEndsTheTurnInside` — the person's other word on
  the same clock.
- `TestTheRoomSaysWhenThePickLanded` (tui3) — both sentences, and no "turn".
- The ≤50 ms loop laws still hold; the boundary read is a lock and a string.

## Manual

Five places said "the task's next turn"; all five say what is true now.
`models-and-cost.md` gains the section somebody asks for when they press a model
mid-reply, with both halves, the clock, and the limits.

title: The person's word wins at the request, never at the next turn

body:
## What was true

A lane choice is a **sampled** decision — `internal/lane` seeds its draw with the moment it is asked at, so two asks a microsecond apart are two different answers — and one call encodes its request many times: once per attempt, once for every rung of the relaxation ladder, once more for the object the refusal door re-derives.

Only the streamed door decided a choice up front (`client.go`'s `withLaneChoice`). Everything else drew a fresh one **inside the encoder**, by a contract written into `laneChoiceFor`'s own doc comment: *"A non-streamed call has no watch to agree with, so it decides here."*

So one call could ask for three different sets of machines, and nothing above the encoder could name the set. `control.Plan.Lane` and `Plan.Alts` come from `requestSet(knobs)`, which reads the call's choice; a choice the encoder kept to itself left `requestSet` empty, the plan an OPEN set, and the move generator walking machines the wire had never named. It is the seam #925 took its demand back out over (see its report, *Deliberately not in this PR — issue #891 §3*).

## What is true now

`Client.drawLaneChoice` is **the one draw**, and `Client.withLaneChoice` is its only caller.

`withLaneChoice` is idempotent and asked twice on purpose:

- the **streamed door** asks before the first byte leaves, because the watch that may hedge needs the answer then;
- **`Client.sendShaped`** — the one door every send passes through, where the call's one *budget* is already stamped — asks for every other road to the wire, the raw channel door (`StreamComplete`) included, and hands a call that already has one its own back.

The encoder reads `knobs.laneChoice` and nothing else. A nil choice is a call that decided to prefer nothing, and its request goes out exactly as it did before this package existed.

**Deleted:** the "a non-streamed call makes its own inside the encoder" contract and the code that implemented it; the `request` parameter threaded down through `wirePreferences`, `providerPreferences`, `applyLaneChoice` and `onlyLane` only so the encoder could decide again; and the stale caveat in `onlyLane`'s doc about re-deriving a ranking that may differ from the wire's.

This PR changes **no routing policy**. Same frontier, same ranking, same vetoes — only how many times they are asked for.

## The reproduction came first

`internal/provider/onechoice_test.go`, against `lanestub`, with the belief arriving **mid-call** the way the lane beat really delivers one (a `warmingTransport` warms the ledger when the call's first request leaves; the router answers a fault that names nobody, so the set is not narrowed by strikes and the only thing that can differ between two bodies is what this build decided to ask for).

| scenario | on `dev` |
| --- | --- |
| `TestOneCallAsksForOneSetOfMachinesHoweverOftenItIsEncoded` (the streamed door) | **body 1 `order=[]`, body 2 `order=[quicksilver]`** — a ranking appeared on the second body of one call |
| `TestTheRawStreamDoorAlsoDecidesItsLaneOnce` (`StreamComplete`) | the same, and it never had a choice stamped at all |
| `TestACallThatHadABeliefAsksForItOnEveryBody` (the control) | green on `dev` and must stay green — "one choice per call" must not have been bought by sending no choice |

All three green at this head; the first two verified red with the change stashed.

## The law

`TestOnlyOneFunctionDrawsACallsLane` in `lane_law_test.go` walks the package with `go/ast` and fails the build on a second function that asks the chooser. It rides the `laws` gate (found by that import), and its allowlist is **data with a reason on each line** — `drawLaneChoice` for a call's own decision, `ProbeLanes` because its question is about a *model* rather than about a call. A name that stops asking fails too, so a permission nobody uses cannot sit there.

## Manual

`lanes.md` gains *"The machines one message may go to are decided once — why a retry walks the same set, and why something learned mid-answer waits for your next message"*: the decision is made once and lasts the whole request; what changes between two sends of one message is only the machines that refused *it*; a measurement that lands mid-flight is spent on the next message.

title: Lanes: one choice per call, whichever door the request left by

body:
The question-views wave's first piece (lane P of #830), against `dev` and standing alone on it.

## What a person sees

**One frame.** `internal/tui3/frame.go` is the surface's one framing primitive —
a dim edge, a title and an aside in the top, keys and an aside in the bottom,
every row set to one width, and two plain rules with blank sides on a terminal
that refused box drawing. The question, the `ctrl+k` switcher card and the
onboarding panel are drawn by it. The `/folder` chooser is not, yet, and the
frame's own comment says so: it grew a height-degradation ladder of its own the
same week, and moving it is a change to that ladder rather than a change of
drawing.

**Amber on the marks and nowhere else.** The question's violet (`#C08FE8`) is
retired from both ladders. A question's amber touches `?`, the pointer `▸` and
`◆ recommended`; every word is ordinary ink, every aside dim, and the row the
pointer stands on takes the ground ladder's `selected` rather than a colour. A
law test walks the renderers' paints and fails on a row painted in the hue.

**One chooser.** Which drawing a question gets was four decisions in four
places, each keyed on something different. It is now one ladder of properties in
`questionchooser.go`, read top to bottom, never asking the question's Kind —
what decides how much room a decision needs is what it CARRIES.

**The panel.** The pointer opens on the asker's pick, `◆ recommended` stands at
the right edge, and the pick's reason, confidence and would-switch are one dim
line under the picked row while it is focused. The last row is `something
else…`, which becomes an inline box under the pointer. `esc` folds the question
in place to one titled rule; `space` opens it again.

**Two tiers of keys.** The frame's bottom edge carries exactly `↑↓ choose ·
enter take it · esc later`. Everything quieter stands on one dim row beneath
it, dropped right-to-left as the frame narrows. Every word comes from the one
key table.

**How long an answer lasts.** A permission that offers more than one lifetime
draws them under its answers — `✓ just this once · for this project · from now
on` — cycled by `t how long`, defaulting to the narrowest, never offering a
lifetime the question did not, and absent entirely on a call that cannot be
taken back.

**Where a permission's pointer opens is decided by the stakes** (owner ruling,
2026-09-11): an ordinary call opens on `allow once`, one that cannot be taken
back opens on the answer that loses nothing. It is derived in one place from
`Question.Stakes` and never from the tool's name.

**The receipt** opens with the vocabulary's `✓` and carries a working tail until
the model's first output. It offers no key that has no door behind it.

**The chip** says WHICH question is waiting, not merely that one is; and a
waiting question no longer takes the keys off the place a person is standing on
(#840).

**`/autonomy` has a row where settings are browsed** — Safety, *questions while
you are away*, one row per kind, the same reader and writer as the command. A
setting that changes what the program does on its own is never reachable only by
a slash command.

## Two defects a live drive found

- **The question rules could be written and never read.** `internal/remote`
  carried `SetAutonomy` and no `Autonomy`, and the ordinary launch talks to its
  own engine through exactly that client — so `/autonomy` answered "this
  conversation has no project to keep question rules in" on every machine, with
  the rules sitting in `.aforge/autonomy.json`. Driven, confirmed and fixed.
- **The digits row named a key nothing answers.** `1–3` over the answers `1` and
  `3` — the ordinary shape of an irreversible gate, where the engine drops the
  widening answer — is now `1 3`.

## How it was checked

`scripts/qv-drive.sh` opens this worktree's own binary in a tmux session of its
own, on a throwaway home, with one of `questiondemo.go`'s fixtures named in the
environment. Every view was captured at 120/96/56 columns, in both themes and
both glyph tiers, and the autonomy discovery was driven on a fresh launch: a
person who has never heard of `/autonomy` types "away" into settings and finds
the rows.

Manual, e2e needles and the change entry are in the same commit range. The
evidence split, the two-pane page, the tabs view, grouped permissions, undo on
the receipt and the countdown aside are other lanes' pull requests and nothing
here advertises them.

body:
Closes #920. Follows #918, which wrote the figure once so this change could move one number.

## What moved

`exec.DefaultLeafTokens` goes from 150,000 to **220,000**. Every door reads it, so `aforge exec`, `aforge run` and the chat surface all change with it.

The old figure was calibrated from a turn costing about 11k input tokens and a leaf finishing in 8 to 16 turns. Measured against issue #898 run headless on `z-ai/glm-5.3` (run `04c2404b26072e41`), neither half held.

| leaf | turns | spent | grant then |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Issue 898 frame law fix | 14 | 184,411 | 150,000 |
| finish-issue-898 | 41 | 190,524 | 164,462 |
| Answer remaining offenders | 14 | 268,971 | 211,852 |

The cost was never the stop. It was the re-planning around every landing: five rounds and seven nodes for one issue, 43 minutes, $2.11, and a delivery gate that refused at the end for want of time, while the work itself was correct and committed after the first two leaves.

## One of the three invariants was not real

`TestObservationWindowIsSizedFromContextNotSpend` compared the context-derived window against `DefaultLeafTokens/6` and so appeared to bound the grant under 196,608. But the window has not read the grant since `observationWindow` became `ctxbudget.ObservationBytes` of the model's own context. The division was the test recomputing a **historical** figure — what the spend ceiling used to buy — from a number that had since moved, which made it fail whenever the grant **rose**. A larger grant does not shrink the memory a leaf is given.

That constant is frozen at the 25,000 it actually was. The assertion it supports is unchanged and unweakened.

## The other two are real, and neither moved

Sweeping the constant and running them puts the band at **200,000 to about 241,000**.

- **Floor, 190,000.** `TestACacheDiscountedRunawayLandsOnItsMoney` closes by asserting that cost alone would have bought the leaf several times the work it did. At 190,000 the simulated cost bound and the real run both land at 85 turns, so the comparison stops separating and the test says so itself.
- **Ceiling, 242,000.** The same test's raw bound. At 98% caching a runaway costs about 5.8× the grant in raw tokens, so 242,000 reaches the 1.4M the audited melt-downs reached. 220,000 reaches about 1.28M.

220,000 covers the first two leaves outright with room over. The third had already been lifted to 211,852 by its dependency term and is a job that wants splitting, not an argument for a bigger number.

## A seventh copy of the figure, and a gate for it

`docs/HEADLESS.md`'s `--token-budget` row still said `150000`. It survived #918 because that law watches the *current* number and is blind to a stale copy of a past one — a blind spot #918 states plainly, and I found this one by sweeping for the old figure by hand.

`TestTheHeadlessReferenceStatesTheGrantTheDoorsApply` now reads that row and fails the build when it disagrees with the constant, so the reference somebody reads instead of `--help` is on a gate, as `internal/manual/chat/adaptive-runs.md` already was through the truth table.

## Proof

Spark, worktree at `a6bbd56dc`, `go build ./... && go vet && go test -count=1`:

```
ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/exec    57.886s
ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/manual   1.770s
ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/cmd/aforge       58.936s
```

Both new laws were proved to bite by planting the old figure and watching them name the file, the line and the owner.

Closes #889.

A report that opens with a code fence is the model spelling its answer correctly. The card read that literally and quoted the fence marker itself, so the one row that carries the work's own sentence drew `"```"`.

`firstProseLine` skips leading blank lines and fence markers, with or without a language word after them, and quotes the first line beneath that says something. Two cases it handles on purpose:

- **A report that is nothing but a fenced block quotes its first line inside.** The block is then the answer, and skipping the whole fence would quote nothing, which is the emptiness law doing the opposite of its job.
- **An unclosed fence is a fence still being written.** Nothing inside one has said anything yet, so the reading continues below it rather than treating the rest of the report as inside a block whose end it cannot see.

A report with no prose at all returns nothing and the row falls back to the subtitle, then to the start stamp, which `doneUnder` already knew how to do.

## Where this came from

**This change was written by an aforge lane, not by hand.** `~/af-lane.sh 889` ran `aforge do` on `z-ai/glm-5.3` through OpenRouter, unattended on the Spark, and produced the fix, the test, the change entry and the manual pages in about ten minutes for $3.13. I read the diff, rebased it onto dev, and ran the suites. The runbook for that is `spark:~/AFORGE-LANES-HOWTO.md`.

body:
## The evidence

The owner's own task, 2026-09-11 14:39:17 – 14:40:47, `tag:task` node 2 on
`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Eight consecutive sends came back
`(via Wafer: … is temporarily rate-limited upstream)`, every one carrying
`retry_after: 2`, spaced by the dispatcher's own doubling (0.7 s, 1.4, 2.8, 5.6,
11.2, 22.4, 44.8) — ninety seconds of `waiting · rate limited` while six other
machines on the same model were answering in under five, one of them thirty
seconds earlier in the same minute. Then the work hopped to a model the chain
chose, while the person had already picked one in the room and been told the
change was taken.

Both halves are reproduced as failing `lanestub` scenarios before anything moved
(`internal/provider/namedrefusal_test.go`): on `dev` the first stages eight sends
and 1 m 30 s of waits, the second seven sends of identical bytes.

## What changed

**A named refusal is asked before the status.** `taxonomy.Evidence.Named` is the
one spelling of "one machine owned this refusal", and `classOf` asks it before
any number: a 400, a 502 and a 429 relayed from one pool are one fact and earn
one answer. A 429 that named nobody stops borrowing `the provider could not
serve it` and gets its own shape, `ReasonPaced`.

**A veto that did not take is nowhere else to go.** The dispatcher's exclusion
law used to key on `relayed` — a 4xx that would not otherwise have been retried
— so the commonest named refusal in the log was exempt from it. It now keys on
the veto the body actually carried: when the machine that answers is one this
very body named in `provider.ignore`, routing cannot save this request, and the
refusal is handed back for the ladder and the session's one model hop. The
snapshot is taken at the encode rather than read back at the refusal, because
the veto list is shared by every arm of one question.

**An account's own ceiling is not an open set.** `control.Plan.AccountRefused`
is `ShapeRefused`'s sibling: a router with a pool behind the model paced the
whole key and named none of it, so every machine is behind the same ceiling,
nothing can come off the next body, and the open-set walk's premise is gone. It
earns the comeback it named, once, and then the model. A base that has never
published a pool is deliberately not this — an endpoint with one machine saying
"come back later" is answered by coming back later.

**A person's pick outranks the fallback chain.** `TaskNode.standingModel` is the
model somebody chose in a node's own room and that it is not running on;
`nextNodeModel` moves there instead of walking the adapter's list. A chain
answers "what next when nobody has said", and somebody had.

**And the room says what is true.** `model · <id> · the next request takes it`,
where it used to say `its next turn takes it` — a boundary that can be twenty
minutes off on a long step, which is why the person typed `continue` to try to
force it.

## Laws

- `internal/taxonomy`: a named refusal is `Transport`/`ReasonRefused` at every
  status; an unnamed pace is `ReasonPaced`; `Named()` reads the upstream alone.
- `internal/lane/control`: an account ceiling earns one comeback and then the
  model, is not answerable by a relaxed shape, and has no move at all when it
  named no comeback.
- `internal/session`: a rescue moves to the model the person picked; a model the
  proposal named is not a standing pick.
- `internal/provider`: the three `lanestub` scenarios above, plus the control
  case — a veto the router honours still moves with no wait at all.

## Manual

`lanes.md` "When a machine is too busy" loses the claim that an account-wide
rate limit is waited out for the whole of the role's give-up, and gains the
veto-that-did-not-take case. `tasks.md` and `models-and-cost.md` stop saying a
task's model change lands on its next turn.

## Deliberately not in this PR

Issue #891 §3 — the chooser demanding `provider.only` instead of advising with
`provider.order` — was built and then taken back out. It is blocked on a seam
this PR should not cross; the exact finding is in the report and in a comment on
#891.

body:
## The call the owner watched

`~/.aforge/logs/calls.jsonl`, 2026-09-11, one task node:

```
14:27:50 id e5ba2778 start lane Novita
14:29:16 id e5ba2778 served Morph  ms 86183 ttft 3993 finish tool_calls
         silence_ms 10000 action report reason ceiling refused budget
         prompt 65801 completion 604  cost $0.020
14:32:14 id 730f0d77 attempt 2     served Morph  ms 363005 ttft 5286
         completion 5793   (no action, no reason, no silence_ms at all)
```

604 tokens in 86 seconds, then 5,793 in 363, with a person watching one `[silent]`
nudge. Four things were wrong and each has one idea.

## 0. Sent back once — what the review found, and what closed it

**The person never read `answering slowly`.** Two layers took the word back: the
phase for a wait nothing can be done about was decided twice on one path
(`exhaust`, then `tellFirstPrompt`/`tellTheWait`), and underneath that
`phaseClock.enter` replaced `below pace` with `writing` on the very next token —
instrumented, the sentence lasted ONE token of the eighty-six seconds it was
about. The word is `hedgeRace.theWait`'s one decision now, taken from the act's
reason; the writing may not take it back from the judgement about it; and the
test asserts the LAST phase (`heard.settled`) rather than any phase in the list.

**One rail, one price, two doors.** `hazard.reachable` asks the same purse from
`internal/lane/control` with a different estimate, and the law walked
`internal/provider` only. Both asks are legitimate — before deciding, before
sending — but two estimates for one bound is two rails. The race reads
`control.Alternative.Extra` off the plan (`hedgeRace.altPrice`), so the price is
computed once; the law walks both packages and names both doors; a sibling law
drives the shipped door against a plan priced differently from the frontier.

**The purse was sized in the opposite order to who is waiting.** `GiveUp / λ`
divides by a figure that is smaller for a call nobody watches, so an unwatched
second came out four times dearer: `talk` $1.00, `leaf.unattended` $12.00,
`standing` $24.00. λ/`AttentionValue` is a discount and has to multiply —
`SpendUSD = GiveUp × (λ / AttentionValue) / AttentionValue` — giving `talk`
$1.00 and `leaf.unattended` $0.75. The ordering law is stated PER SECOND across
every role in the table, because patience varies thirty-fold inside each exposure
group and no per-second price can order the totals.

**Six places still described the deleted allowance**, two asserting the opposite
of the law that replaced them. All corrected, and a law greps the live prose of
both packages and both documents for the dead names — a name may be said in the
past tense, not as a claim.

## 1. The purse overruled the hazard

The controller said act. The rail said no — because it was a rolling
**process-wide** allowance (`lane.Budget`: two rescues in any twenty requests,
a tenth of the last hour's bill). A count spread over twenty requests cannot tell
the one that needs rescuing from the nineteen that do not, so it refuses by
arrival order: the rescue it declined cost about two cents against a wait worth a
hundred times that.

That whole mechanism is **deleted**. What a call may spend rescuing itself is its
own, and it is derived rather than chosen:

```
control.Plan.SpendUSD = Role.GiveUp() × (λ / AttentionValue) / AttentionValue
```

How long the wait may still be, times what one second of it is worth to whoever
is waiting. λ is SECONDS PER DOLLAR, so `1/AttentionValue` is the rate at the top
of the scale and `λ / AttentionValue` is how much less this role's seconds are
worth than a watched person's — a quarter, for anything nobody is sitting
through.
`control.Purse` is kept as the interface; its one implementation is
`lane.Spending(plan)`, stateless, asks and never spends — which deletes the
`Allow`/`Affordable` split those semantics forced. `SetLaneGuard(false)` is now
`lane.NoSpending()`. **How many arms a question may have at once is `maxArms = 4`
and is now the only thing counting arms.** The row says `plan cannot pay`, not
`budget`, and `make census` reads the field for the first time.

## 2. A report is still a move

`control.Report` meant "nothing can be started", and then nothing happened at
all. It now asks `control.Next` whether another machine exists and, if so, writes
the serving machine onto the plan's shared move log — so no arm and no attempt of
this question goes back to it. A question with nowhere else to go keeps the only
machine it has.

And the person is told. There was no word for a stream writing too slowly to
read: `writing` is false about the wait, `all lanes slow · still waiting` is false
about the silence, so the surface said nothing. `PhaseBelowPace`, drawn as

```
answering slowly · nowhere faster · 1m 26s
```

## 3. Two filters over one number — diagnosed, measured, and NOT patched here

The flat `Belief.Rate` the chooser ranks on is a SECOND Kalman filter over the
same quantity the four-level chain holds, fed the same observation with the same
noise and reaching a different answer. In the owner's own belief file that
afternoon the chain said **6.0 t/s** and the belief the chooser reads still said
**10.8**. (The brief's `rate/pair x=-4.21` is the pair OFFSET, not a rate; summed
with world+lane+model it is 6.0.)

The cause is in `ledger.see` exactly where the brief said to look, and it is not
the gain — it is that the flat filter's only escape hatch from a state that has
STEPPED is `stepTo`, which runs only when the chain's change point fires, and on
a collapse like this one it cannot. Replayed from the 09:33 series: a run of
consistent sightings drives the flat variance to 0.011 against an observation
noise of 0.36 (a gain of 3%), while the CUSUM peaks at **3.40** against an alarm
of 4.0 and then decays — because a chain that absorbs nine tenths of a surprise
in ONE observation leaves no run of surprises for a CUSUM to accumulate.

**I tried making the flat belief the chain read flat and threw it away**, because
three standing laws in `internal/lane` say it cannot be: `flatten`'s variance is
the sum of four level marginals (1.95 nats after one sighting against a
sheet-primed 0.055), so a measurement WIDENS the belief instead of sharpening it,
and the chain's gain pulls a pair nobody has measured toward a world anchor of
log zero instead of adopting its first measurement outright. Those are three
different quantities wearing one name, and unifying them moves how every lane is
ranked — a `bench/lanelab` question, not a lane's.

So what lands is the diagnosis with its numbers, written at `lane.stepTo` and in
the change entry, plus the replay test from the exact sighting series asserting
the account that DOES matter for this defect: the chain the controller waits
against learns the collapse in one sighting.

## 4. Every attempt is watched, and a stream is judged against what it was promised

A `streamWatch` belongs to an ARM and an arm sends many times. Every once-only
rule on it is right for one send and wrong for a call — `acted` keeps the FIRST
act, so a later attempt's row can never be written. The 363-second attempt 2 was
unwatched by construction. `streamWatch.attempt(now)` re-arms from the plan
before every send; the deadline and the move log belong to the question and are
untouched.

And **#891 §1**: the aggregate credit test measured each gap against `Plan.Gap`,
which `Serving` re-points to whoever answered — so a machine collapsing all
afternoon was judged against its own collapse, and the more this process learned
the weaker the guard got. The bar is now the gap belief the plan was BUILT with:
the machine the choice named. Where the machine that answered is the machine that
was asked for, the bar and the belief are one number and nothing changes.

## Acceptance

- `internal/lane/control` — the substitution fires inside the ceiling (604 tokens
  at 137 ms each against a question sent expecting 60 a second); a machine
  answering at the rate it was asked for is never judged slow; a question sent
  blind is entitled to nothing in particular.
- `internal/provider` (`lanestub`) — the same wire twice: the call's budget
  affords the rescue and the fast machine answers; and it may spend nothing, so
  the row says `plan cannot pay`, the machine is spent for the question, and the
  person reads `answering slowly · nowhere faster`.
- `internal/lane` — the 09:33 series and the 14:29 sighting replayed: the chain
  the controller waits against learns the collapse in one sighting, against what
  the answer itself measured (604/82.19 = 7.35 t/s).
- Five law tests, all proved able to fail by breaking them and watching them name
  the file and line: `TestThePurseIsAskedThroughOneDoor` and
  `TestTheTwoDoorsAskThePurseWithOnePrice` (go/ast over both packages, on the laws
  gate), `TestTheDeletedAllowanceIsNotStillDescribed`,
  `TestEveryAttemptGetsItsOwnController`, and
  `TestNoWatchedSecondIsWorthLessThanAnUnwatchedOne`.
- `TestTheScreenshotScenarioAnswersThroughTheFourthMachine` was **red on dev**
  (`e67f1827b`: died on the first machine's 404, because the walk was bounded by
  that rolling allowance). It is green here, and its stale phase assertion is
  corrected — a walk between machines says `switching` and names where it is
  going.

body:
**DO NOT MERGE** — the owner runs the test binary first (`~/af-promote/bin/aforge`, shasum in the lane report).

Owner's ruling, 2026-09-11 14:20 EDT: *"we should not force a task via a hard turn count; we need to give the model enough in the prompt to choose; when it chooses it needs to weigh whether it is worth it for the task to re-read everything it has."*

## What was measured

A one-line read-only design question (conversation `7598fe73c5ce3a9a`, 13:59–14:08). The chat read home-panel files for ten rounds in 48 s. The round-10 ceiling fired; a mark reader on a 4k-token account said `split`; a handoff writer spent 39 s and 41k input drawing a quick node; the worker opened on the raw sentence, four items and a `CALLS THAT HAVE ALREADY RUN` stub list. Its first six calls re-read the chat's own results (116 KB of stubs), then fourteen more files — **551k input tokens, 24% cached, 393 s, never ticked an item**. Asked why, the chat stopped it and answered from its own earlier reading: *"I over-read. I have what I need"*.

Three faults in one road: the decision made by the wrong party (a summary reader, not the model holding the context), on the wrong signal (a round count, which says nothing about progress), and the move throws the context away.

## The shape

**1. The turn decides, informed.** The rungs below the last one (`checkpointNotes = checkpointMarks - 1`) call no reader and move nothing. They inject ONE note at the turn's next step, through the single ambient door a loop nudge already uses (`enqueueAmbientNote`) — never message[0], no timer, no model call:

```
[taking stock] 10 rounds so far, 9 files opened, 121 KB of results in front of
you. Three roads on, and the choice is yours: answer now from what you have;
carry the rest on in a room, with `quick_task` and `inherit` set, which opens on
this transcript as you are holding it; or hand out the parts you have not read
yet. A worker that does not inherit opens on a brief about your work instead of
on your work, and reads it all again. Nothing has been decided for you and
nothing has been moved.
```

(one line in the transcript; wrapped here, and the three figures are the turn's own.)

**2. Promotion inherits.** `quick_task` gains `inherit` (default false) — a field on #929's `quickAsk`, admitted through `admitQuick`, so the tool and the carry-on road ask for a promotion the same way: the worker is a read-only FORK of the caller's transcript, so its first request carries the caller's messages and tool results verbatim (prefix identical, cache hits) plus the brief as its opening message. One door — `quickAsk` gained a field and `admitQuick` is still the only way a quick node is born. Schema prose:

> `Hand it this conversation so it opens on everything you have already read. Off by default, and refused when your context will not fit its window`

Bounded by a property, not a number: `inheritFits` refuses when the caller's context exceeds `compactThresholdOf(workerWindow)` — **the build's own already-derived line for how far a conversation may grow** — and the refusal names the road still open (hand out with a brief). The window read is **the worker's, not the caller's**: a `task.model` pin or the crew's worker seat hands tasks to a cheaper model every day, so the bound is asked below #929's own resolver, of the model the work will actually leave on (`workerModelFor`).

**3. The carry-on road promotes.** When the net fires, the carry-on goes through the SAME admission door as the tool, with the drawn items as its checklist and the context inherited. The brief road survives only where inheritance cannot go (the rung that fired *because* the context is too big), and there the brief now carries the compiled results themselves under `WHAT THIS WORK ALREADY FOUND OUT` rather than pointers at calls the worker must run again.

**4. The runaway net.** `readMark` survives only as the LAST rung, and no longer asks about rounds. `turnHasRunAway` reads ONE fact — the turn's context has passed the room it can still work in (`compactThresholdOf(a.window)`) — and the other roads to the same ceiling were already written and are not repeated in it: `looped.go`'s nudge ceiling (`handOverLoopingTurn`), `turnwall.go`'s wall (asked ahead of this ladder) and the meter's own disproved completion claim. Each a fact the build already had, with the derivation in prose on the constant. Its reading is a `readBeside` sidecar that may only INTERRUPT (`sidecar_law_test.go` reds an awaited reading on a road that carries the turn on). **A turn reading ten distinct files in 48 s reaches none of these** — pinned by `TestATenRoundReadingTurnIsToldAndNotMoved`.

**5. The prompt, and it comes DOWN.** `inherit` is a verb law now — one schema property, 72 bytes, registered at `quick_task` (class `verb`) rather than as a page sentence — and the road law `quick_task`'s description said word for word after `beltfacts.go` had come to say it is deleted, giving back 145. Measured against `dev 84016ad09` in a detached worktree of it: lean **31,341 → 31,267** and fixed **39,073 → 39,000** on a machine with ripgrep; **31,448 → 31,375** and **39,180 → 39,107** on one without, which is the shape CI measures. Budgets 31,500 and 48,000, and the note itself is in neither figure: it rides the event, at the boundary where it matters.

**A net that fires once says so.** The net measures a condition rather than a boundary, and a full context stays full — and three of `handOverRunningTurn`'s endings LEAVE THE TURN RUNNING (no brief came back, this conversation is holding work of its own, the reader says nothing is left). Without a latch each of those was followed by a fresh mastermind call and an unconditional `cutGeneration` on every remaining step. `checkpointMeter.netFiredAt` records the firing and `netRested` holds the net off for `checkpointPrice` rounds of real work — ONE predicate for all four endings, in the unit the meter already used for a disproved claim, and pinned by `TestADeclinedCeilingDoesNotReadTheWorkAgainEveryRound` (3 readings with the latch over the same script that took 6 without).

## Deleted

`checkpointSplitNote`, `checkpointDecisionSplit`, `checkpointSeamMark`, `quickFromDrawing`'s bare-spec path, the sketch-split gate on the carry road, the stub-pointer section for an inherited worker, and every manual sentence saying a turn is moved at round ten.

## Manual, same PR

`chat/tasks.md` rewritten — *"An answer that runs long is told, and decides for itself"*, *"When a reply is taken out of your hands"*, and a new section on `inherit` — plus three probes in `chat_test.go` (`why did it stop reading and start a task`, `can it keep what it read`, `why did it not become a task`) and the cross-reference in `how-tasks-run.md`.

## Pinned end to end

`inherit_test.go` drives the real runner both ways. A promoted worker's FIRST REQUEST carries its caller's own tool result verbatim, opens on the caller's page plus the one paragraph that is true of a promotion, and is handed none of the `CALLS THAT HAVE ALREADY RUN` section. A conversation too big for the worker's window is refused in a result the model reads, and no worker is started.

## Proof

`make test-laws` (21 packages, incl. `sidecar_law_test.go`, `admission_law_test.go`, `iconlaw`), `go test ./internal/manual/`, the law registry, both prefix budgets, the schema law, `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and focused sweeps across the checkpoint / quick / route / carry / handoff / write-seam families.

## Review, second pass — the nine findings

Coordinator's six:

1. **Lean prefix over budget.** It was, on the base it was really measured against. Cut from the `inherit` description and the `beltfacts.go` sentence until the lean prefix is **31,482 of 31,500** on `dev 84016ad09`; the budget was not touched, and the before/after above is measured on that base.
2. **`how-tasks-run.md` contradicted `tasks.md`** about which tasks inherit a transcript. Its "what a task can do while it runs" paragraph now says the transcript is inherited only by a promotion — `quick_task` with `inherit`, or a reply the ceiling carried on — and that every other task gets one assembled brief.
3. **`readTurnFacts` walked the whole session.** It walks `messages[meter.opened:]` now, and `turnOpenedAt` finds the message the person opened THIS turn with (walking back over the tool traffic to the newest person's message, then over a steer that sits on the ask it steered). `TestTheNotesFiguresCountThisTurnAndNotTheOnesBeforeIt` builds a two-turn transcript with a steer in it and asserts the note counts one file, not three.
4. **`promotedFromTurn` had lost `if read.sketch.handsBack { return nil }`.** Restored, with `TestATurnHoldingCoordinationIsNotPromotedWithItAsAChecklist` — which fails without it.
5. **The change entry overstated `turnHasRunAway`.** Corrected: the function reads context; the loop, the wall and the disproved claim reach the same ceiling by roads that were already written.
6. **`outOfRoom` latched and never cleared.** It stays one-way, and the reason is now prose on the field: the only thing that can put a turn back under the line is a compaction, and a folded transcript is exactly what a promotion must not carry.

The checkpoint owner's three:

- **A — the net had no once-only latch.** Fixed as described above (`netFiredAt` / `netRested`).
- **B — the manual still described the deleted machinery.** `screen.md`'s `taking stock` row, `models-and-cost.md`'s markreader paragraph and role table row, and `tasks.md`'s "looking at the work decides everything else" all say what the code does now. And because `[taking stock]` is now both a status-line phase word and the model-facing note's lead, `screen.md` gains **its own `##` section** separating them (a new heading rather than prose added to an existing one — BM25 length normalisation charges the padded section its own probes).
- **C — `TestARacedVerdictWithoutBreadthArmsNothingOfItsOwn` kept its name and lost its assertions.** Replaced by `TestARacedVerdictWithoutBreadthWritesNoBreadthOfItsOwn`, which asserts what is actually true now: two narrow readings arm no breadth, and either reader saying `Wide` arms it.

`checkpoint.go`'s own header was three claims stale beside this change (a sketch at every mark, a look that costs a call, "nothing is injected into the turn at any mark") and now says what the file does: the notes tell and ask nothing, the ceiling is a property and not a count, and the one reading that must come back is the sidecar's at the net.

## Proof at this head (`d84120b30`, rebased onto `dev 84016ad09`)

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/session/`, `make test-focus PKGS=./internal/session RUN='Prefix|Inherit|Promot|Coordination|LawRegistry'`, the checkpoint / quick / route / verdict / handoff families, `go test ./internal/manual/` (green, `TestHeldOutQuestionsReachTheirPage` included), `make test-focus PKGS=./internal/tui3 RUN='Manual'`, and `make test-laws` (25 packages).

Rebased through #929 (the task-start wave), #973 and #975: `inherit` is a `quickAsk` field, the carry-on road answers a `*quickAsk` with `inherit: true`, and both go through `admitQuick`. There is one constructor, not two.

Spark, isolated clone `~/af-suite-923` at this head, `make pr-ready BASE=84016ad09` behind the box's one-suite lock:

```
make --no-print-directory test-touched
touched: ./internal/manual ./internal/session
./scripts/one-suite.sh go test -timeout 15m -count=1 -p 1 -skip '^(TestEveryLockInTheGuardedTreeUnlocksFromADefer)$' ./internal/manual ./internal/session
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/manual	1.640s
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/session	173.261s
```

Test binary for the owner: `~/af-promote/bin/aforge`, `shasum e66947bc1473cb29becf763a7e55f33a5869de4e`.

## The two CI reds, and what they were

**The lean prefix cell measures an environment-dependent quantity, and that is a defect of its own.** CI read 31,555 where the laptop read 31,484 at the same sha. The cause is `grep`: `bare.grepToolDescription` probes for ripgrep once per process (`exec.LookPath("rg")`) and a machine without it carries the longer fallback description — **134 bytes more** on the GitHub runner, which has no `rg`. Reproduced on the laptop by hiding `rg` and `fd` from `PATH`: the same tree then measures 31,520, matching CI to two bytes. So the honest baseline for this gate is the no-ripgrep one, `dev` sits at **31,448** there, and this PR now sits at **31,375** — 73 bytes below `dev`, in the environment the gate actually runs in. Filed as #981 rather than patched here: a budget whose reading moves with what is installed on the runner cannot be reasoned about by the lane that trips it.

**`TestAContinuationSayingNothingIsLeftDropsTheCeilingHandover` was this PR's own fixture, and the mechanism it exposed is a real boundary.** The turn answers the handover with `NOTHING LEFT TO DO`; `checkpointMeter.believeDone` charges that claim once and arms `askAgainAt = rounds + checkpointPrice`, so ten more rounds of REAL work disprove it and the turn is met again — pre-existing law, pinned by `TestTheRunningModelsSayS0IsBelievedOnceAndThenMet`. This PR widened `checkpointSlack` from `checkpointMarks + 4` (7) to `checkpointPrice + checkpointMarks` (13) so scripts could outlast the sidecar's gap, and 13 tail steps straddle that price: how many of them become rounds of work depends on how many the reading eats, which is why it failed 13/30 on the Spark and 0/30 here. The fixture was asserting the scheduler.

The fix is in two parts, neither of them a rerun:

- `checkpointClaimSlack = checkpointPrice - 1` is the slack for the three fixtures whose turn CLAIMS IT IS FINISHED and carries on (`checkpoint_test.go` ×2, `unattendeddoor_test.go`). By construction they cannot reach the claim rung, so each tests the ending it is named after and nothing else. The constant says why in its own doc.
- `TestABelievedClaimIsMetAgainOnlyAfterAPriceOfRealRounds` pins the boundary **on the meter, with no scheduler in it**: every round of the quiet rings nothing and leaves the net unrested, the round that completes the price rings `checkpointMarks` through the meter rather than the net, the claim is not believed a second time, and a batch that only watched work already out buys none of the price. It fails on a broken latch (`netRested` forced true: "the net was rested 1 rounds after it fired, 9 short of its price").

Spark at this head: `go test -count=30 -run '^TestAContinuationSayingNothingIsLeftDropsTheCeilingHandover$'` → **30 RUN, 30 PASS, 0 FAIL**.

## Folded in from the peer's follow-ups

- **`netFiredAt` was a zero-value sentinel and round zero is a real round** (a turn whose opening boundaries all watch never leaves round zero). The latch is now two fields for two facts, `netFired bool` and `netFiredAt int`.
- **`checkpoint.go`'s new header said "three times the handoff price"** where `checkpointMarkAt(2)` is `checkpointRatio` times it. The figure is interpolated from the constant, not restated.
- **`newQuickTaskSpec` was built twice on the inherit path.** The branch is hoisted: a promotion is built INSTEAD of the plain node, never after it.
- **An empty checklist can reach a promotion, and now the comment makes the argument** the deleted gate's comment used to make against it: a promoted worker holds the whole transcript, so the checklist is a convenience on top of the work rather than the only description of it.
- **`screen.md` listed three firing conditions and there are four.** The believed claim disproved by ten more rounds of real work is named in both places the page describes the moment.

The rest of the review — the two windows behind one line (`TrustedWindowFor`), the transcript walked twice a boundary, the unpinned double-composed page, `awaitReading`'s silent sleep-poll, and `checkpointMarkAt(checkpointMarks)` being production-dead — are filed together as **#979**, with the reviewer's own wording and an acceptance line each.

body:
## Why

Every change to the machine chooser this week — #850, #853, #873 and two lanes still in flight — was judged by a person's screenshot and a ten-row grep. `~/.aforge/logs/calls.jsonl` already holds ~1,000 finished requests a day for ten days: `lane` (asked), `served` (answered), `ttft_ms`, `ms`, `completion_tokens`, `status`, `tag`, `cached_tokens`. That is a bandit replay dataset. We were tuning a bandit by anecdote.

## What this is

`cmd/aforge-replay`, behind `make replay [LOG= SIGHTINGS= SINCE= WINDOW= INCIDENTS= OUT=]`. It walks the log in time order, teaches each candidate exactly the sightings and refusals that had arrived by each moment, asks which machine it would have **demanded**, and prices that answer against what the machine measurably did around that moment — the same `rolePatience.expected` quantity the chooser itself ranks by, read off the log instead of off a belief. Cut by role class, because a second of a watched answer and a second of an unattended errand are not the same second.

Four candidates, each a `Policy` — three teaching methods and a demand:

| | |
|---|---|
| `served` | what the router did (baseline) |
| `current` | `internal/lane`'s chooser as on `dev`, **the real one through `lane.Default`**, never a copy |
| `quantile` | a decayed quantile sketch per (model, machine, role class), read at the role's risk quantile |
| `current+Q` | the same `dev` chooser with a floor under how certain its Kalman may become |

**`internal/lane` is not edited — not even one export door.** `current+Q` goes through `Registry.SetLedger` with a wrapper embedding both `lane.Ledger` and `lane.Hierarchy` (choose.go asks for the second by type assertion) that raises `Posterior.P` on the way out.

Both constants are **measured from the same log**, never chosen: the forgetting half-life from the log's own change-point rate read as a variogram (**10m** — `lane.HalfLife` arrived at independently), and the variance floor from how far a machine's own days differ (**0.2409 nats²**).

## What it found — ten days, 5.8s on Spark

Rebased onto `dev` @ `127fe176c`. **Read the direction, not the decimals**: every figure is recomputed from the log each run, and between the first submission and this head the `current+Q` watched mean went 8.62 → 7.66 → 7.80, crossing `current` twice, while the finding never moved. The change entry therefore states the direction with the estimator error beside it and quotes no figure; `make replay` prints today's.

| watched | scored | mean regret | median | p90 | agreed with what served | switches | cache forfeited |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `served` | 1,154 | **104.79s** | 4.03s | 81.85s | 93% | 1,193 | 17.0M tok |
| `current` | 1,154 | **7.80s** | 0.45s | 16.50s | 29% | 2,366 | 45.7M tok |
| `quantile` | 1,154 | **8.47s** | 3.23s | 14.62s | 11% | **303** | **6.1M tok** |
| `current+Q` | 1,154 | **8.00s** | 0.61s | 16.61s | 27% | 2,608 | 50.7M tok |

| unattended | scored | mean regret | median | p90 | agreed with what served | switches | cache forfeited |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `served` | 2,462 | **62.84s** | 1.23s | 107.37s | 94% | 2,886 | 52.0M tok |
| `current` | 2,462 | **4.37s** | 0.00s | 7.38s | 30% | 3,562 | 83.4M tok |
| `quantile` | 2,462 | **13.24s** | 1.66s | 38.48s | 9% | **710** | **13.6M tok** |
| `current+Q` | 2,462 | **5.13s** | 0.00s | 7.45s | 29% | 3,918 | 91.2M tok |

- **`current+Q` buys nothing.** Inside a 24% estimator error on watched — which is to say no difference, and it has landed on both sides of `current` at different heads — **17% worse unattended** at every head it has been run at, and 10% more machine switches for it. At all three incidents it demands the identical machine `current` does. That is the finding the lane was sent to get, and it is negative.
- **`quantile` is not worth shipping** — 3× the unattended regret, no opinion on half the log — but it reaches a comparable *watched* regret with **303 switches against 2,366 and 6.1M prompt tokens forfeited against 45.7M.** The shipped chooser changes its mind nearly eight times more than its own advantage justifies. That is a finding about `dev`, not about the candidate.
- **The chooser's demand is the machine that served only 29% of the time**, while the machine the preference *named* served 93%. The `allow_fallbacks` gap of #850, measured over ten days.

## The three incidents of 2026-09-11 (derived, never hard-coded)

| moment | asked → served | served cost | best | `current` | `quantile` | `current+Q` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14:27:50 Morph | Novita → Morph | 42.6s | Novita 4.3s | SiliconFlow 5.1s | SiliconFlow 5.1s | SiliconFlow 5.1s |
| 14:32:14 Morph | GMICloud → Morph | 1185.8s | Novita 23.2s | Modal 67.8s | SiliconFlow 29.5s | Modal 67.8s |
| 14:39:04 Wafer ×8 | SiliconFlow → Wafer | 92.1s | SiliconFlow 4.1s | SiliconFlow 4.1s | SiliconFlow 4.1s | SiliconFlow 4.1s |

The shipped chooser already avoids all three. What went wrong at those moments was not its belief — it was that its demand was not what got served.

## Four things that are load-bearing

1. **A machine is never priced from the answer being scored.** The row that served sits inside that request's own window; leaving it in judges the machine that answered against itself.
2. **One common set.** Four candidates scored on four different sets cannot be compared — a policy that declines the hard half wins by declining it. `TestTheCommonSetIsTheSameSizeForEveryCandidate`.
3. **Censored rows are a lower bound, never dropped** (758 of them). Dropping them measures our own hedging policy.
4. **A request whose answer never arrived still asked for something** (4,881 of them). Pricing a refusal as asking for zero tokens made the paced-pool incident rank below a slow but healthy answer.

The report prints **its own error first** — the machine that really served, priced from the window and from its own row, median 24% — so a reader knows how big a regret has to be to mean anything.

## Deleted

`internal/lane/replay_bench_test.go` — a build-tagged bench with λ = 90 everywhere, no role, no common set, no leave-one-out, no censoring and no test of its own. `docs/design/routing/ASSESSMENT-20260911.md` now says its figures are not comparable line for line. The census's own copies of the row reader and of `apiErrorStatus` went with it.

## One abstraction, reused

`internal/callrows` is now the ONE reader of the call log — `Read`, `Row`, the four facts every instrument needs from a line, and `SaidStatus` (what status a router's own sentence names, so the two instruments cannot disagree about a 429 inside an opened 200). `cmd/aforge-census` takes its rows from there and keeps its own argument about what they mean.

## Tested

A 104-row golden fixture with a planted bimodal machine, where the oracle, the served policy and a trivially-wrong one have known regrets, plus nine more laws: leave-one-out, the tail-vs-median reading, the refusal credited to the machine its own sentence names, the tag→role join, the common set, and that no policy is ever taught an answer it could not have had yet. `TestOnlyTheTaxonomyTurnsAStatusIntoAMove` caught a real violation on the first Spark run and is now satisfied by a table. The tag law imports `go/ast`, so `scripts/laws.sh` enrols it and it runs on every pull request into `dev`.

## Rework after review (`e640aa8` → this head)

Four blocking defects, all closed:

1. **The change entry quoted an hour's figures the head's own run contradicted.** It states the direction with the estimator error beside it now, and quotes no number. The rebase proved the point: the watched pair crossed again and every word of the entry stayed true.
2. **`TestAPolicyIsNeverTaughtAnAnswerItCouldNotHaveHadYet` could not fail** — both loops were tautologies over `sort.SliceStable`'s own output, so the instrument's central honesty property was guarded by nothing. It now reads the property from where a policy stands (a recording candidate through `pass()`: what it had been TAUGHT when it was ASKED), builds the case the sort alone decides (an answer landing in the same millisecond a request goes out, asserting the ask is walked first), and asserts that the same check over a deliberately wrong order goes red. Flipping `momentsOf`'s own append order fails it.
3. **The incident table was keyed on `(timestamp, model)`**, which hedge arms and the eight-in-forty-seconds pool burst share, so a candidate row could describe a different request from the one its heading named. Keyed on `asked.index` now.
4. **The tag law never read the build.** It walks the module with `go/ast` now for every tag the build can actually write — `provider.WithCallTag` literals, `errandContext` errand names, and every `internal/roles` constant because `auxiliary.go` writes `string(role)` — and a call site whose tag the walk cannot read is a failure, not a skip. Writing it found **twenty-nine words the build writes that the table did not name** (`video`, `guardian`, `planner`, `title`, `distill`, `quorum`, …), every one of which was reading as an unwatched background errand; each joined the table with the role its own call site declares, and `tool:<tool>` became one rule rather than a row per tool.

Plus the eight non-blocking follow-ups: the calibration figure is stated as a floor on the error; the table says the common set is the intersection of four opinions; `widen`'s doc says why one rate-derived figure floors both axes and what that costs the finding; `lagLadder`'s ends are tied to `stopBelieving`; the half-life fallback law asserts `lane.HalfLife`; the dead `sightJSON` is deleted with a sentence saying why; the report no longer names a `world.around` that does not exist; and the entry says what the deleted bench could do that this cannot.

## Seam owed — filed as #928

**`calllog.Record` should carry a `role` column.** It records the call site's `tag` and never the `lane.Role` the chooser was steered by, so this tool joins them itself in `roleOf`. That join is the weakest thing in the report, and one field on the row deletes it — #928 carries the replication and an end-to-end acceptance that names `roleOf`, `callSiteRoles` and their law as the things to delete. It also removes the one guess: `task` is attached or unattended depending on `someoneIsWatching()` at the moment of the call, which nothing records.

body:
Lane F of the question-views wave (#830), surface half. The answer road: an answer is
drawn the moment it is pressed, every key lands where the person is looking, and a
question nobody was there for is still on the screen when they come back.

Targets `dev` per the owner's incremental ruling; it stands alone there. The engine half
is #910 and is independent of this PR.

## The ten-second freeze, fixed at the cause

A deterministic reproduction first: a scripted wire engine over `net.Pipe`, a real
`tea.Program` whose Update called `ResolveQuestion`, and the surface's news reader exactly
as `tui3.Run` registered it. **10.000362601s** — `remote.callDeadline` to the microsecond.
The client's reader goroutine took the `phase` frame inline and called `p.Send`, which
blocks on an unbuffered channel whose only reader is the event loop — and the loop was
parked inside Update waiting for the very result frame that reader could no longer read.
Only the deadline broke it, and the comment in the tree blamed a busy machine.

Two small mechanisms close it, and the same reproduction now measures **181.056µs**:

- **`doorbell.go`** — one non-blocking coalescing wake door. A foreign goroutine files what
  it has and rings a one-slot channel; the loop holds a standing `tea.Cmd` on it and
  re-arms in the same Update. `ring()` can never block on the UI. `p.Send` from a reader
  goroutine is gone.
- **`offloop.go`** — no wire door is called from inside Update. Every one is asked inside
  an `a.offLoop(...)` literal, on the door line's goroutine, and folded back on the next
  pass, told whether the conversation it was asked of is still in front.

**The question closes on the keystroke with its receipt**, because this window knows what
it just sent; a refusal is the rare road and puts the question back with the engine's own
sentence.

**And the wire sees what a person did in the order they did it.** Commands start on
goroutines of their own in whatever order the runtime feels like, so `D` — which writes
the project's rule AND answers in one keystroke — could have its answer reach the engine
first and re-ask the question before the rule existed. Every door now goes into one FIFO
line, queued *on the loop* under the keystroke that made it and walked by one goroutine.
The loop still calls no door: it appends to a slice and rings a one-slot channel.

## One answering road

`app.answerQuestions([]questionAnswer) tea.Cmd` sends a whole frame's answers through the
door in one command: each row settles on the keystroke with its receipt, the doors are
asked in order on one goroutine, and a refusal comes back against its own row while the
answers that were taken stay taken. The block, the batch sheet, the full page, home's band
and home's needs panel all go through it; five hand-rolled copies of the road are deleted.
(Home's wrote no receipt and left no sent stamp, so its own answer came back down the
questions lane and read as another window's.)

A refusal now re-raises only an answer that actually resolved something, never past a
decision the questions lane has confirmed, and one that arrives after the person switched
conversation is kept and said when the question comes back rather than dropped.

## Keys that did nothing, or landed somewhere else

- **A question takes keys only where it is drawn** — `ctrl+t` then typing `hello there`
  used to grant a waiting tool on the `t`. One predicate governs the keys and the drawing,
  ahead of the block **and** the batch sheet, which had no guard of its own. (#677's fix
  reached `dev` from another lane during this work; the test here still holds it.)
- **The first letter of a sentence belongs to the box.** A verb on the key table (`d`, `c`,
  `o`, `r`, `u`, `x`, `?`, `D`, and the sheet's `s`/`g`) does not reach the question until
  somebody has aimed at it — an arrow, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`, or a click. The hand is the
  question's own **token**, set only when the block actually took an aiming key on a
  settled question, so nothing can inherit a keyboard aimed at a different question. The
  answers' own keys (`1`-`9`, and a letter a lane prints on an option) are deliberately not
  on that road: a key drawn in ink as `[1] allow once` is pressable, always.
- A question raised **while you were away** pins its notice as well as sending it, and the
  first key, click or focus re-delivers what is still waiting.
- A **question page** closes when its question is answered or withdrawn anywhere.
- The **full-page room** scrolls to what the arrows walked to.
- A **checklist** had two cursors; the **second beat** drew none and swallowed every arrow.
- **Under sixty columns** no pointer was drawn at all, so `enter` landed on an invisible row.
- **Click and pointer row maths** was off by the receipt rows above the block.

## The laws

- `TestNoEngineDoorIsAskedFromTheUpdateLoop` — structural, on `make test-laws`. The door
  set is **derived** from `internal/remote` (a method on `remote.Agent` that reaches
  `a.c.call`/`callWithin`/`callAnswered`, transitively) rather than listed, the receiver
  must actually be the agent, nested folds are excluded and method values are caught. It
  also **names what it does not cover**: the doors the rest of the surface still asks from
  Update are written down with where, and the count is a ratchet that may only be lowered.
- `TestAnAnswerOverAConnectionAsksTheFarMachineNothingFromUpdate` — runtime: the client's
  own count of calls made does not move across an Update that answers a question on a real
  socket, and the far machine is then asked exactly once.
- `TestTheDoorsAreAskedInTheOrderTheKeysWerePressed`, `TestClosingTheLineStillAsksWhatIsInIt`.
- Every gate is on counts and outcomes, never a wall clock (PERF.md); the timings are logged.

## Proof

`make pr-ready BASE=origin/dev` and `go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/tui3` green.

A live drive of the real binary in tmux against `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, capturing
every 100 ms: **20 answers to a blocking `ask`, zero `did not answer in time`, the receipt
in the first frame captured after the key on 19 of 20** (the twentieth shows the row with
its clock already held — a capture race of a few milliseconds). Keystroke to row gone,
measured directly: 15–19 ms. #677's replication was re-run on the real binary and the start
page kept every letter; the first-letter rule was shown both ways — `› can you keep it
short` left in the box untouched, then `↓` then `c` opening the change prompt.

The manual is updated in the same change (`questions.md`, `permissions.md`).
