body:
## What was true

`defaultLeafTokens` was spelled in five places: the constant, `aforge exec`'s `--token-budget` default, `aforge run`'s, `chatLeafTokens` in the chat surface — whose comment promised it *"mirrors the headless run defaults exactly"* — and again inside `cmd/aforge`'s usage test. That is an intention where this repository's one-source-of-truth law wants an interpolation, and it meant five numbers had to be recalibrated together by somebody who knew all five were there.

## What is true now

The grant is `exec.DefaultLeafTokens` and every door reads it from there. `TestTheLeafGrantIsSpelledOnce` reads declarations with `go/parser` — not a grep, so a figure inside a string or a comment is not a false positive — and fails the build on a second spelling anywhere under `cmd/aforge`, `internal/exec` or `internal/session`. Proven to bite: planting `const plantedGrant = 250_000` turns it red naming the file and line.

**The value is unchanged at 150,000**, and that is the interesting part.

## The measurement

Issue #898 (the frame law widened to see `func f(a *app)`) was run headless on `z-ai/glm-5.3`, run `04c2404b26072e41`, 2026-09-11. Neither half of the calibration held: the median call carried **14.2k** prompt tokens, not 11k, and the leaves that did the work ran **14 to 41** turns, not 8 to 16. Every one was landed mid-edit.

| leaf | turns | spent | of grant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Issue 898 frame law fix | 14 | 184,411 | 150,000 |
| finish-issue-898 | 41 | 190,524 | 164,462 |
| Answer remaining offenders | 14 | 268,971 | 211,852 |

A grant above the constant is the constant plus `gatheringGrant`'s dependency term; the overshoot past each is the landing reserve at `landingTokenShare`, working as designed. The cost was the re-planning around every landing: **five rounds, seven nodes, 43 minutes, $2.11**, and a delivery gate that refused at the end for want of time — while the work itself was correct and committed after the first two leaves. Every split is paid for twice, once in a fresh planning round and once in the context the next leaf has to be told again.

## Why the number did not move

This branch opened by raising it to 250,000. That turns three tests red, and none of them should be moved to let a figure through:

1. **`TestObservationWindowIsSizedFromContextNotSpend`** compares the 32,768-byte context-derived window against `DefaultLeafTokens/6`, so the grant may not reach **196,608** until the window is re-derived. Moving the comparison would un-pin the category error the test exists for.
2. **`TestACacheDiscountedRunawayLandsOnItsMoney`** holds a 98%-cached runaway under the 1.4M raw tokens the audited melt-downs reached. At about **5.8× the grant**, 250,000 pushed 1,442,112 — exactly what the grant forestalls.
3. That test's closing cost/raw separation **coincides at 190,000**, where the simulated bound and the real run both land at 85 turns, and the test says so itself.

So the grant is load-bearing rather than a knob: moving it means moving the observation window's derivation and re-measuring the runaway bound. **#920** carries that work and this evidence. Until then a lane that needs a bigger grant for one run passes `--token-budget` to `aforge exec` or `aforge run`.

The constant's own comment and `PERF.md`'s "A leaf's bounds" both carry the reading, so the next person to reach for the number meets the ceiling before they move it.

## Checks

`go build ./...`, `gofmt`, `go vet` clean. `internal/exec` and `cmd/aforge` suites on the Spark.

body:
Lane A of the question-views wave (#830), **against `dev`** and standing on its own
there. An answer to the model's own `ask` was only the RETURN VALUE of the call
that asked; it is now a MESSAGE TO THE CONVERSATION that also releases a waiting
call when there is one. Three things the owner picked fall out of that one
mechanism, and a fourth — the undo — rides the same door.

## The mechanism

`internal/session/asklane.go` — the lane's book (`Agent.asks`, one `modelAsk` per
question the model raised), one rendering (`askAnswerText`: a sentence, then the
whole `Answer`), and two deliveries: the call parked on it, or the conversation's
own queue through **`Agent.accept`** — the road a job's ending, a watch's firing
and a landed task already take (step boundary, or a wake on an idle
conversation). No second delivery path. `ResolveQuestion` is still the one door.

**It absorbed #870's book.** `internal/session/askwait.go` held the parked wait
with three endings and a doc warning that two maps holding one question is a
defect; this is one map with those three endings kept word for word plus the
fourth — a call that never waited. `THE ENTRY IS THE OWNERSHIP` became `THE CLAIM
IS THE OWNERSHIP` (`modelAsk.claimParkedLocked`), because a settled entry is kept
so its answer can be changed. Talking past a question still retires the asks a
person's sentence is in the way of — the ones something waits on — and leaves a
non-blocking question standing, which is what asking without waiting means.

**Deleted:** `askWaits`, `askedOfThePerson`, the policy clock inside
`executeAsk`'s `select`, the ask arm that dropped an answer when nobody was
parked, and the refusal in `SetAutonomy` that made a clock length compulsory.

## What a person gets

- **Keep working while asking.** `blocking: {turn: false}` returns at once; the
  question outlives the call and the turn. Omitted or `true` waits exactly as
  before — the zero value waits.
- **A countdown you can stop.** The clock belongs to the lane, not the call, so
  it runs on a question nobody is parked on; it takes the pick through the same
  door, and what the model reads says the answer is **provisional**. Opt-in: no
  clock unless the person set one (`/autonomy`), length by one derivation
  (`autonomyClock`). Any key stops it for good — `Agent.HoldQuestion`, wire
  `Question.Hold`, sent from a `tea.Cmd` — and the question says so itself while
  the clock runs: `any key stops the clock · you can still change the answer
  afterwards`.
- **Change your answer.** `c change` on the receipt asks the question again; the
  new answer carries `Answer.Revises`, the record says `changed from …`, and the
  model is told what changed. Irreversible decisions refuse it in words.
- **Undo a permission.** `u undo` on the receipt of an `always` hands that grant
  back whole — the session memo, the saved settings line, and a connected
  account's capability, which returns to asking rather than to a no nobody said.
  `Agent.undoGrant` is the one door for the stores the engine owns;
  `app.forgetAlways` is the surface's own line. What may be changed is ONE
  reading (`Question.Revisable`), asked by the receipt that offers the key and by
  the door that takes it.

Wire **15** (both halves fail as silence on a v14 engine). Lean prefix 30,833 →
30,968 bytes against a 31,500 budget; fixed prefix unchanged.

## Proof

`make pr-ready BASE=origin/dev` green — laws, and `internal/session`,
`internal/tui3`, `internal/manual`, `internal/e2e`, `internal/remote` with
`-count=1`.

Laws added: a non-blocking ask returns at once and its question stands; a parked
and a messaged answer are the same bytes; a provisional pick says so and runs with
nobody parked; a hold clears the deadline in the engine; a change reaches the model
as a correction (parked and unparked); an irreversible decision refuses a change;
an answer the lane no longer holds is refused in words; an answered question
leaves the desk; a question nothing waits on is not `waiting on you`; a clock that
runs out after `Close` decides nothing; an answer a closed conversation cannot read
records nothing; the second answer to one question records nothing; the countdown
says how to stop it and only while it runs; `u undo` takes the standing yes back
and only a standing yes is offered one.

Driven in tmux as a person against `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, twice — once on
`--no-host` and once over the DEFAULT host road (#690 is closed by #856, and the
idle-woken answer reached the screen). The model chose the non-blocking form,
finished the other files while the question stood, and used the answer when it
came; a change from the receipt made it rewrite the file; the clock took its pick,
said so as provisional, and the model asked the person whether to keep it; a key
press left the next countdown `paused` and undecided a minute later; `u undo`
printed `taken back · this tool asks again` and the next call asked again.

Two earlier drives found two defects the unit tests had not — a correction posted
into a spent channel, and a reopened question that still said `waiting` — both
fixed and pinned.

body:
Two defects, one belief: a task's copy was treated as a detail of where its *worker* stands, rather than as the world its whole life happens in.

## Part 1 — #886: a declared check ran against the person's checkout

`taskCopy.bind` covered `work`, `deliverable`, `acceptance` and `expects`, never `checks`. A check written by a parent standing in the person's folder (`grep -q rewritten /person/folder/report.txt`, which `prompts/system.md` asks for) ran with the copy as its working directory, but an absolute argument is not a working-directory question. It read the untouched original and answered red, and correct work landed `your call · nobody could check it`.

**Found beyond the issue.** The checker does not stand in the task's own copy. It stands in a clean restore (`<tree>-check`). The before-reading stands in a checkout of the base commit, and the progress reader stands in the worker's tree. Binding the check to `trees/<n>` (the issue's acceptance) would fix the checker and break the before-reading, which is already soft on dev today. A check the work really broke comes back "red before this work and remains red", because the base reading also reads the person's folder.

**Fix.** A check is bound onto the copy it is **run** in. It goes through the same `taskCopy.bind`, at the one place a check becomes a door (`auditDoorFor` → `runnableChecks`). The copy is spelled as the directory the command runs in (`.`), which is true in all four run sites. `task_baseline.go` needed no change. The order (shape, then bind, then runnable) also stops a check whose first word is the ground's own script from being dropped silently. `copyOnto` is now the one reading shared by the worker's map and the checker's map. `standingOn` is the identity for the session's reading after a task has landed (the work is home).

## Part 2 — a piece that lands after its parent stopped reading

The seat is withdrawn the instant a worker's reading ends. The node then stays open through its check and landing, minutes away. A piece landing in that window fell through to the person's conversation, and its result never reached the parent's deliverable. The dominant trigger is a parent stopped with pieces out: `stopChildren` cuts them, and they all land during the parent's check.

**Fix.** `taskNoteReaders` asks three readers in order: the parent's worker, then **the parent itself** (`landingFold`, new `task_latefold.go`), then the conversation. `TaskNode.report` is composed under the graph lock from `landed` and `late`, so neither half can erase the other. Only a settled parent sends pieces to the person. A folded piece is marked reported, so nothing is delivered twice.

**Stated limit** (code, design doc, manual): the fold is not a turn, and the check does not see a folded piece. The checker reads the worker's own last words, and re-reading them would mean a second audit of the same tree.

## Proof

- `TestADeclaredCheckIsBoundToTheTaskOwnCopy`: full drive on `newTestRepo` + `routedCompleter` + `Submit`. The door's check passes on what would ship and fails on the base. The command as written still fails, which is the defect itself.
- `TestChecksBindOnlyWhatTheGroundHolds`: under the ground, the ground itself, outside the ground, relative, and a sibling tree (#839). A checker standing on the ground itself gets the identity.
- `TestAGroundCheckThatNamesItsOwnScriptOpensTheDoor`
- `TestAChildLandingAfterItsParentStoppedReadingIsFoldedIntoItsReport` (the probe-branch test, rewritten and renamed) and `TestAChildLandingAfterItsParentSettledReachesTheConversation`
- `make pr-ready BASE=origin/speed/task-start`: result in the report.

Design: `docs/design/task-start/DESIGN.md`, section "A task and its own work agree (lane L)", with the bar's four questions. Manual: `how-tasks-run.md`, two paragraphs in existing sections.

Touches outside lane L's files (few lines each, named for merge order): `task_run.go` (`taskCopyFor` delegate, progress door call, `postTaskMessage` nil-reader mark, `finish` 3 lines, two `TaskNode` fields), `task_audit.go` (door call site).

title: A task and its own work agree: a check runs in the copy the task was given, and a late piece is folded into its parent (lane L)

body:
## What this is

Every question this engine asks now has ONE door onto the questions lane, one reading of what is waiting, and one rule for what a turn may leave behind — and answering a question no longer costs the prompt cache.

Rebased onto `dev` and **targeted at `dev`**: it stands alone, and the pages describe exactly what this pull request's code does.

### One door

`Agent.raiseQuestion(q, announce) letGo` is the whole of a question's life on the lane: bank the words, let the lane say its own row, emit the raise, nudge presence. Eleven lanes go through it. Five of them — connect, the harness offer, the harness design, a sub-harness intake card, a running sub-harness's own question and an adaptive run at its fuel gate — used to reach the questions stream only through the `OpenQuestions` replay and never emitted an answered or a withdrawn event at all, so a window that learned one by replay had nothing that would ever close it. `internal/session/questionlaw_test.go` (an AST law, on `make test-laws`) fails the build if a twelfth lane re-grows half a lifecycle.

### Answering leaves the prompt alone

`recordDecision` no longer rebuilds `message[0]`. The record there is a snapshot, refreshed only when that message moves for a reason of its own; `decisions.jsonl` is read once at open and re-rendered off `a.mu`. Measured on the Spark with `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`: the request after an `allow once` reported **13,568 of 13,861 prompt tokens served from the cache**, across an answer that used to move the first byte of the prompt.

## The review's four blockers

**1 — SECURITY.** A typed API key reached `decisions.jsonl` as the answer's `change`, `message[0]` as `with: sk-…`, the provider on the very next request, and `EventQuestionAnswered` on every `--host` frame. Fixed at the shape, in ONE place, keyed on `Question.SecretAnswer()`: `Agent.ResolveQuestion` strips every typed field from the answer as it leaves, after the lane it was meant for has been handed the real words. `TestASecretAnswerReachesTheLaneAndNothingElse` demands the key's bytes appear in none of the four — the record file, the questions lane's marshalled event, `message[0]`, or anywhere in the session folder — while the connect lane still gets the key it asked for.

**An answered question came back on every attach** (the owner's 2026-09-11 report, folded in here because it is the lifecycle). `internal/remote`'s waiting room dropped a card only when that card's OWN resolve-door was called — a line apiece in `MethodConsent`, `MethodStandingResolve`, `MethodHarness`, `MethodConnect`, `MethodConnectKey` — and since the chat began answering every lane through the one door `MethodQuestionResolve`, which has no such line, nothing dropped anything. A standing proposal answered at 14:55 was back on the block forty minutes later and after every tab switch, conversation switch and new window, with the conversation reading `waiting · your call` and home counting it in `want you`. A door-keyed clear misses every new door, so the room is reconciled against the engine's own `OpenQuestions` every time it is read or counted (`Session.dropSettledLocked`), and the six per-door lines and `settleConnect` go with it. It is **not** a pure mirror of `OpenQuestions` and cannot become one: what a surface is handed on arrival is the lane's own FRAME, which the question object does not carry. Law: `TestAnAnswerThroughTheOneDoorEmptiesTheWaitingRoom`.

**2 and 3 — TWO PREDICATES, TWO NAMES, ONE READING EACH** (agreed with lane A):

- `Question.Waiting()` = `q.Ask.Waits() && q.Blocking.Blocks()` — "is anything stopped on this". The waiting desk, the presence file and `QuestionCap` all read it. The desk answers with its OLDEST row and nothing asked whether that row was waiting for anything, so a standing ratify beside a bash approval put the RATIFY's sentence on home under `waiting on you` and a key press there answered the ratify.
- `questionOutlivesTurn(q)` = `q.Later || len(q.Blocking.Tasks) > 0` — "may the turn end without this". Only the end-of-turn sweep reads it. `Agent.retireTurnQuestions` withdraws everything that fails it, because an unanswered ratify and a question somebody asked back on and never returned to had no withdrawal trigger at all: they stood in `OpenQuestions`, on the desk and against the cap for the rest of the session, about a turn that ended long ago.

`Question.Later` is the model's own word (additive, `omitempty`, no wire bump). `Blocking.Turn` is now **derived** from whether the call actually parks and is never the model's claim, so a model writing `blocking: {turn: true}` beside `kind: ratify` cannot put a row on a desk about a turn that is carrying on.

**4** — the override-memory pass is a tracked background job (`startMemoryJob`/`memoryJobs.Done`) rather than a bare `go`, so `Close` waits for it.

## The rest of the review

- **5 (manual law), now a blocker under the incremental ruling** — the two sentences that described the tui3 follow-ups are rewritten to what is true after this pull request alone: the ratify line no longer claims the open-question count leaves a ratify out, and the ask-back section no longer claims the words reach the asker where it waits. What IS newly true is on the pages: a key you type is never written down (`accounts.md`), and a question the turn leaves behind is taken back when it finishes (`questions.md`).
- **7** — the lean-prefix ledger says honestly what `ask` cost: the schema went 3,844 → 4,235 when its enums began being written from the Go constants, 137 bytes were won back by deleting prose that says a field's own name back at the model, and the lean prefix stands at **31,035 of 31,500**. The changelog's `pairs` claim is corrected: the PROPERTY went, the kind did not.
- **8** — `docs/CHAT-V3.md` described the stuck question as a live rung of the ladder; it was deleted with the rest of the recovery lane, so that section now says what survives (the change ledger, and the revert it makes exact) and what does not. The revert helpers themselves are left in place and are noted in the lane report as still having no production caller.
- **10** — `WithdrawQuestion` reads and takes in one hold (dev had already done this via `claimQuestion`; kept with the reason written down).

## Driven as a person, in tmux, against the real model

Screens under `~/af-qv-reports/F/engine/`.

**The prompt cache survives an answer.** From the call log, tag=turn: the request
before the `allow once` paid 18,119 prompt tokens cold; the request after it paid
**264 fresh of 18,184**, the rest served from the cache. The screen said
`⟲ saved $0.0012 · 47% cached`.

**A ratify that asked to stop the turn stopped nothing, and was retired with its
turn.** The model was told to call `ask` with `kind: ratify` and
`blocking: {turn: true}`. The turn reached its own next sentence, the status line
read `idle` rather than `waiting · your call`, there was no question chip — and
when the turn ended:

```
  decided needs your ok to run ask → allow once · you · 16:48 · c change
   renamed the column to slug — no longer needed · the turn moved on without it
```

That last line is review item 3, live.

**The owner's defect, closed end to end through the real door.** Over the HOST
road, a standing proposal (`wants to keep an eye on: Every day at 9am, check
whether PR 917 is merged into dev.`) was answered `3 just once`:

```
  decided wants to keep an eye on: Every day at 9am, … → just once · you · 16:51 · c change
```

The conversation switcher was then opened and closed three times, a SECOND window
attached to the same engine, and a THIRD. Each is a new arrival number and each
would have been handed that card by `waitingFor`. **None of them drew it** — both
new windows came up on the transcript with `idle` on the status line, no
`waiting · your call` and no question chip.

## Two test fixes, for the two reds CI found

Both are test-only; no product code changed for either.

- `TestTheCapIsCountedAgainstOnePieceOfWorkAndNotTheSession` built a
  subharness-ask question BY HAND with an empty `Blocking` while asserting it
  holds a `QuestionCap` slot. The cap now counts `Question.Waiting()`, so the
  fixture was claiming nothing waited on work it said was stopped; it is given the
  `Blocking{Tasks: …}` its real builder carries. Production is unaffected —
  `executeAsk` is the only caller of `AskQuestion` and its `Blocking` is derived.
- `TestTakingTheKeyboardBackMovesItAndTellsTheOtherWindow` — reproduced and
  diagnosed rather than rerun. It is a TEST bug. The room is told who drives AFTER
  the arriving window's welcome is written (it is that connection's own writer, so
  it cannot be before), so a second window arriving in that gap is told it holds
  the keyboard by the FIRST window's announcement: a true note about an instant
  that has passed, corrected by the next frame, with per-connection ordering
  keeping the correction behind it. The product is right; the test was reading a
  coin flip — about one run in twenty alone, reliable at `-count=400`. It now waits
  for the note that says where the keyboard ENDED UP (`driverSaying`, whose doc
  carries the diagnosis). 500 clean runs after.

## Merge order

`#910` lands first; lane A's `#914` rebases onto it, takes `internal/session/askwait.go` as the one book (`askedOfThePerson.parked` is `map[uint64]*askOpen{q, theirs, wait, letGo}`, `wait` nil for a question that outlived its call), deletes its absorbed copy, and sets `q.Later` in its own `executeAsk`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: questions: one door for every lane, and an answer that leaves the prompt alone

body:
## What was wrong

Since #653 an ordinary `aforge chat` in a workspace takes the engine road: it spawns or joins `aforge engine --daemon` and builds the surface's options with `hostOptions`, the builder written for `--host` and `--at`. That builder deliberately leaves the accounts manager, the harness registry, the profile-write doors and the model-source set out, because over ssh they belong to the far machine. Nobody re-read that list when the road became the default, so on a plain launch:

- `/connect` said `connections are unavailable here` (and the Settings → Connections tab said the same);
- `/harness` said `harnesses are unavailable here`;
- "always" on a consent card was never written to the profile, and `/model` was never remembered;
- the model-service group from #800 was unreachable.

`aforge chat --no-host` still had all of it, which is how it was diagnosed: same build, two roads, two behaviours. The comment above the `Landing` patch in `chatv3_local.go` already named this failure family.

## What this does

- **`localDoors`** in `chatv3_local.go`, applied after `hostOptions` returns on the local road only: the connections manager, `subharness.Default()`, the three profile-write doors, and the resolved model-source set. `--host` and `--at` keep their absences; a test pins both sides.
- **The engine's profile dir travels in the welcome** (`Welcome.ProfileDir`, optional, no version move) and is the authority for every local write, so a daemon that outlives a terminal's profile override is never written past.
- **The daemon re-reads its own profile at doors it already has**: on every hello and immediately before the existing model-set call (`RefreshModelSources`), and before a rule-scoped consent answer is applied (`RefreshApprovals`), so a service connected or a rule banked from the surface is live in the running conversation without any credential crossing the wire.
- **`credentials.json` gets a cross-process lock** around every read-modify-write: the surface and the daemon now each hold a manager on the same file, and the atomic rename alone could lose one side's row.
- **A key named as `$VAR`** is read from the daemon's own environment; the connection receipt says so on the engine road, and the manual names the stop-and-relaunch command when the variable was exported after the daemon started.
- **Manual**: `accounts.md`, `commands.md`, `permissions.md`, `saved-shapes-of-work.md`, `services.md` say where each refusal is true and when a banked rule or a connected service takes effect; two new retrieval probes.

## Validation contract → proof

| Behaviour | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| A plain launch opens `/connect` with connected rows and the models group; `/harness` opens the registry | `TestTUIE2E/plain_launch_opens_connections_and_harnesses` (tmux, real binary, engine road, passed 20 s) and `TestAPlainLaunchKeepsThisMachinesDoorsWhileAHostLaunchDoesNot` |
| `--host`/`--at` unchanged | same unit test asserts the hosted builder leaves every door nil and sources empty |
| A banked bash rule is honoured by the running engine on the next matching call | `TestABankedBashRuleReachesTheRunningEngineBeforeTheAnswer` through `remote.Loopback` + a real `session.Agent` (red before the fix) |
| A service connected from the surface is used by the running conversation | `TestAConnectedModelServiceIsLiveInTheRunningEngineConversation`: real agent, two stub vendors, asserts the stub saw the request with the stub bearer |
| Writes land in the daemon's profile even under a surface-side override | split-profile unit test |
| Two managers cannot lose each other's rows | `TestTwoStoresCannotLoseEachOthersWrites` (red before the lock) |
| A damaged `credentials.json` leaves the accounts absent and the models group drawing, no panic | pinned in `cmd/aforge` |
| The production `bootEngine` carries both refresh doors | asserted on the engine it returns |

Gates: `make pr-ready` green locally; `go test ./cmd/aforge ./internal/connect ./internal/remote ./internal/e2e ./internal/manual/...` green; the one `internal/session` red seen once under a loaded box (`TestATaskWhoseConnectionStaysDownLandsAsLostTheConnection`, not touched here, green on rerun) is noted rather than hidden.

## Out of scope, stated

`ApplyAPIKey` and `ConnectOpenRouter` stay nil on the engine road (that road is only taken on a machine that is already set up). `ApplyApprovals` (the `/permissions` take-back) stays nil there too; the panel's receipt already says `from the next session`, and the manual now says so.

body:
The tasks list was a name and a **ranked tail** of up to six facts —
`2 files · done · 5h · $0.27` — which gave up one fact at a time as the frame
narrowed. So the figure under a person's eye moved sideways on every row and
meant something different on each one, and a list you read DOWN could not be
read down at all.

It is a **table** now. A row is a name and two columns in the same cells on
every row of one frame: `state` at twenty cells, and **the column the list is
sorted by** at six, right-aligned. Only the name flexes (rowfit.go law 1), and
the row's lead — its family connectors and its mark — is spent out of the NAME
rather than out of the room, because a root has no mark and a worker four levels
down has four cells of connectors: a table whose columns move is a tail with
extra steps.

## What is in it

- **The sort key is the column you see.** `age` (default, newest first), `name`,
  `state`, `files`, `cost`. Files and cost draw their own figure; name and state
  show the age, because both are already on the row. The sort runs INSIDE each
  level and the tree never flattens — sections keep their order, conversations
  order by their aggregate, the work under one conversation orders among itself.
  A blank cell is a true answer and sinks to the bottom of its group whichever
  way the column points.
- **`alt+s` walks the keys, `alt+shift+s` turns the column round, and the two
  column labels on the control row are pressed.** Per `ruling-s-key.md`: the
  filter owns every printable key here, so `s` alone would cost `sweep`, `stop`
  and `site`. The chord is declared through the router's `alt+<letter>` class —
  the class a VIEW belongs to — because that class swallows an undeclared letter
  rather than passing it down; written anywhere else it is dead in the product,
  which is how the brief's click-the-label test found it.
- **Everything opens shut** (owner, 2026-09-11). A shut root's state cell is its
  own count in that section — `5 your call`, `9 done` — over every row it hides
  at every depth. A typed filter opens every conversation it matched and gives a
  person their own folds back when it clears.
- **The filter's words are on the control row**, the first line of the list:
  `⌕ ` then what was typed, with the dim `type to filter` standing in it. The
  note line under the list keeps only `nothing matches`. The composer at the foot
  is still the same editor — the two-space door home is armed from it — and only
  its drawing moved (`place.boxOnBody`).
- **Money draws in one place**: the sort-key column, while the list is sorted by
  cost.
- **The reason left the row.** Where there is no pane (#902) the CURSOR's row
  grows one dim line — `your call · nobody could check it`, then a landed row's
  first sentence — starting where its own name starts. `tasksReasonLine` is the
  one function behind it.

## Two things worth a reviewer's eye

- **The pointer reaches `state` and whichever column the list is on, not all
  five keys.** That is what "the sort key is the column you see" costs: there
  are two columns, so there are two labels. `cost` is reached with `alt+s` and
  then pressed. The foot names the chord.
- **A state cell can be blank on a queued node of this window's graph whose
  engine reading has no word.** That is `taskPresenceWord`'s stated law — a
  reading with no word draws nothing, never a fall-through to `done` — and it is
  unchanged from `dev`, where the same row carried no state word either.

## Proof

`make pr-ready` on this head. Driven in tmux as a person at 100×30 and 80×24
against `make demo-home`: opened, `→`, `alt+s` to cost, typed a filter, `esc`,
and a real mouse press on a column label. Four defects came out of that drive
and out of the tests, and each is a commit of its own: `alt+s` unreachable, the
columns not lining up, the grown line costing the body a row, and the foot
naming neither page key on the frame the place opens on.

body:
dev went red on the push of 1d48822b2 (#876). The light gate stayed green; `touched
packages` failed with exactly one test in `internal/session`:

```
--- FAIL: TestOldNamingAndSpendSnapshotsPreserveAnAnchoredWorkspace (0.05s)
    title_meta_transaction_test.go:170: old snapshot undid workspace anchoring:
    {ID:0123456789abcdef Title:parser migration failures ShortTitle: Workspace:/tmp/aforge-ci/T...
```

Internal run id 34616058143 (the PR gate on that push).

## The two commits that collided

- **#695** (`4f8d20a5a`) made a conversation's identity a transaction: `Agent.updateMeta`
  re-reads meta.json under the folder's own lock, each patch owns its fields, and the
  failing test is that transaction's law — an old snapshot must never undo a workspace
  anchored after the snapshot was taken.
- **#876** (`1d48822b2`) moved the opening-message stamp off the person's path:
  `stampUserLocked` now owes its write to `offpath.Write` and settles at
  `Agent.SettleWrites`.

Before #876 the FIRST writer of any conversation's meta.json was always that stamp, on
the path, synchronously. After it, a conversation folder can have no meta.json at all
when something else writes first.

## The contract decision

#695's contract stands and the code is what was wrong. #876 intended to change WHEN the
stamp reaches the disk, not what a metadata transaction owes; its own entry says "the
snapshot is still taken on the path; the disk is `offpath.Write`'s". So the test is
unchanged, and the door that broke the law is fixed.

## What was wrong

`Agent.anchorMetaLocked` is `LoadMeta` → set `Workspace` and `Owned=false` → `SaveMeta`.
As the first writer it therefore saved `{"id": "", "workspace": …}` — and `LoadMeta`
answers a blank `ID` with a blank `Meta`, so that file is invisible whole: the anchoring
was on disk in a record nobody reads. The next transaction carrying a snapshot taken
before the anchoring then met `meta.ID == ""`, took the seeding branch, and wrote the
pre-anchor `Owned` and `Workspace` back over it. The conversation went back to being
project-less.

The failure is scheduling-sensitive, not environment-sensitive: it reproduces on any box
with `-cpu=1` (the deferred stamp loses the race it wins on an idle machine) and is
unaffected by `TMPDIR`.

```
go test ./internal/session -run TestOldNamingAndSpendSnapshotsPreserveAnAnchoredWorkspace -count=20 -cpu=1
```

Lane P of the home-and-tasks wave (#884). The tasks place splits on a wide frame: the list keeps
the left, a dim seam divides it, and the right is the cursor row's record — what it did, what it
cost, where it left the work, what it said, and what can be done about it. Nothing is opened and
nothing is lost.

```
 tasks · 15 chats · 13 subtasks · $2.98                                         shift+← aug 29 – sep 11 →  shift+↑ coarser
                                                                        │ Cut every list on the task surface over to the …
 your call · 4 of 7 shown                                               │ ? your call · nobody could check it
 ▾ Sweeping the Frame Budget                              1m · aforge-v2│
   ▾ ◐ Measure the frame budget in every package that draws a…       55m│ 4 files · $0.52 · 22m ago
     ├ ? Cut every list on the task surface over to the shared r…    22m│ branch task/cut-every-list-to-the-row-fitter
     └ ✕ Rebuild the frame budget report                30m · incomplete│ a branch of your repository
 ▾ The Tab Bar's Counts                                  40m · aforge-v2│
   ▸ ◐ Count the tabs the bar draws          holds 3 more · 2h · 3 files│ The dev server was still up when this window
                                                                        │ last closed, the tui3 suite came back clean, and
 running                                                                │ `make check` stopped on a vet error in
 ▾ The Certificate Rotation                                  now · infra│ tasksplace.go — its log has the line.
      Rotate the wildcard certificate                               now│
                                                                        │ internal/tui3/tasksplace.go
 finished today                                                         │ internal/tui3/jobsview.go
 ▾ Porting the Picker                                     2m · aforge-v2│ internal/tui3/deliverables.go
      Port the picker onto the new list                   40m · 2 files│ internal/tui3/taskrecord.go
 ▾ Standing Up the Watches                                5h · aforge-v2│
      Write the morning sweep down                          5h · 1 file│ enter open
```

## What it is

- **One function decides whether there is a pane at all.** `taskPaneCols(width)`: nothing under
  110 cells, otherwise 40 % of the frame clamped to [44, 64]. Under the floor the pane is ABSENT
  rather than blank, and `taskPaneShowing()` is the one predicate the list asks before it grows the
  cursor row's own line instead (lane T's half).
- **It is not a second renderer.** The record's rows were factored out of the card into shared
  builders — `taskRecordWords`, `taskRecordBranch`, `taskRecordParagraph`, `taskRecordBands`,
  `taskRecordVerbs`, `taskRecordAnswer` — and the card now draws from them too.
- **The seam is the one this surface already draws.** `railSeam`, the rule the roster and the room
  split on. No new mark, no new token slot.
- **Nothing on the draw path touches a disk.** The report is read off the loop once the cursor has
  SETTLED (`taskPaneSettle`, 120 ms, generation-stamped), and kept per row. A held `↓` through
  twenty rows fires no reads at all. Until it lands the slot is empty — no spinner, no `loading`.
- **`1` and `2` answer the row under the cursor**, through the same function the card's own keys
  call. The digit is a second NAME for the landing's own answer — positional, which is
  `questionAnswerParts`' own rule for an option with no key — and `a`/`n` still answer. Where this
  window holds no question for the row, no chips are drawn and the digit is typed into the filter.
- **A click moves the cursor and the pane follows; a second click on the same row opens it.** Under
  the floor there is no preview for a first click to buy, so one click opens as it always did.

## The seam into `place.wheel`

`place.press` answered `(tea.Cmd, bool)` and `place.wheel` answered a bare `bool`, so a place with
work to do about a cursor the WHEEL moved could hear the keyboard and the pointer and not the
wheel. `wheel` now matches `press`. Seven one-line changes.

## Two fixture defects this uncovered

- `cmd/aforge-demo-home` wrote bare transcript **paths**, not `file://` URIs, and
  `session.TaskRecordPath` answers `""` for anything without that scheme — so on the demo home
  **every record card drew a row that named no journal and said nothing the node said**. Fixed.
- Nothing in that fixture carried a branch or a rung, so the card's `branch` row had never been
  drawn there either. The one your-call row now carries `ArtifactURI`, `Rung` and `Mode`.

## Proof

`internal/tui3/taskpane_test.go`: the split floor and the clamp at every width, pane/card
agreement on one fixture row, digits answering through the card's door, the letter still
answering, a digit typed where there is no question, **no journal read on a draw**, one read per
settle, a stale settle reading nothing, click-previews-then-opens and one-click-opens under the
floor, the emptiness law, the file band's `N more`, and the short-frame trim that keeps the head
and the verbs. Manual pages and the e2e needle in the same change; driven in tmux at 122×40,
100×30 and 80×24 against `make demo-home`.

Closes #884

body:
Part of #884. Lane H of the home-and-tasks wave — option A for the `needs you` panel.

## What was true

`needs you` drew three sources as one flat list, oldest first. Every landing carried the
same sub-line — `landed unchecked · enter to look`, nine words repeated on nine rows — so
nine items were eighteen lines and pushed `where you were` off a forty-row frame. A live
consent question sorted UNDER week-old landings. A landing wore the amber `?`, which means
*stopped on you*, over work that had already finished. And the same landing could be drawn
twice on one panel, and again in `since you left`.

## What is true now

One panel, two groups. `needs you` is the live questions — a conversation stopped on a
question or a consent card, a watch that needs somebody — longest wait first, wearing the
mark. Under them a dim group line, `to check · N` at the left and
`finished, nobody has checked it` at the right, holding every task whose call is the
person's, newest first, **one line each**: the name, `N files · age`. The row under the
cursor grows a second line — the report's first sentence and the task's own two answers.

```
 needs you · 1
  tell me when CI goes red on master                     1m
   May I re-run the typecheck job to see whether it i… enter

 to check · 4                finished, nobody has checked it
   Cut every list on the task surface over to… 4 files · 28m
   Read what the four nearest competitors charge          7h
   Take the fortnight's spend apart by model     1 file · 1d
   Write the page about reading a task, and e… 17 files · 1d
   Seventeen sections, each under two… 1 accept  2 not right
   1 older · tasks
```

## The one abstraction

`homePanelGroup` — a run of rows at the FOOT of a panel's list, drawn under a dim line of
its own, which folds before the panel gives up a row above it. It is **the panel's own
shape said one level down**, so the squeeze needed no second rule: the group's rows are
last, the ordinary bottom-up cut spends them first, and when none is left the panel's own
fold reads `4 to check · 1 older · tasks` instead of `4 more`. `shrink()` got simpler as a
result. Any panel can take one.

`homeCell.grows` is the second: a row one line tall whose panel reserves the line it grows
into, so the column keeps its shape whichever row the cursor stands on — no relayout on an
arrow key.

## What it deleted

`needsUncheckedWord`, the amber mark on a landing, `needsItem.answers` and the
draw-the-chips-on-the-first-row flag, and the old `homeGridAnswer` walk. Drawing and
routing now call ONE function (`homeAnswerAt`), so the chip on the screen and the key a
person presses cannot be two different rows.

## Two defects the tmux drive found

- **A live conversation waiting on nothing but its own landing was drawn twice.**
  `Agent.waitingOnPerson` reads a pending decision last and has no question object to write
  for it, so such a session says `waiting on you · your call on <title>` with
  `PresenceQuestion` zero — and that was drawn as a question above the `to check` row for
  the same work. The landing's row is the one that survives; it has the work's own name, its
  files and its answers.
- **`a`/`n` cannot be answer keys on home.** The landing keys are task-states' own letter
  for letter everywhere else, but home's box promises "type to search or start something
  new" and a bare letter there always types. So the WORDS stay the task's own
  (`session.TaskAsk`) and the KEY is the drawn digit — the one printable exception home
  already makes — mapped back to `LandingYesKey`/`LandingNoKey` before the answer leaves
  the surface. Verified on disk:
  `{"kind":"landing","id":1,"key":"a","from":"home","decidedBy":"person"}`.

## Also

- `since you left` drops a landing `to check` is showing, and takes it back when it is
  answered or ages out.
- The pulse's `N want you` is now the sum of both groups, through the panel's own
  `needsCallOf`/`needsAged` rather than a second test.
- The demo home grew four more unchecked landings across three projects, so the fixture
  draws a group rather than a group of one.
- Manual: `home.md` (`needs you` is the questions alone, a new `to check` section),
  `keys.md`, `places.md`; `docs/design/home-mission-control/DESIGN.md` laws 5, 7 and 8.

body:
Closes the first residual of #897, which is not a follow-up: `retireUntouchedTree` is new in #876, merged this afternoon and already in the binary the owner is running.

## What was wrong

The retire's guard was `len(tree.Wrote) == 0`, and `Wrote` has exactly one writer — `noteStandingWrite`, reached only from the belt's `write` and `edit`. A shell command, a script the model ran, or a task working in that ground all leave it empty while the copy holds real work. `git worktree remove --force` then deleted it with no refusal and no sentence.

No key and no test needed to see it: choose a repository folder, ask for a shell command that writes a file into it, then say "actually work in that folder directly". The file was gone.

## The fix

The road that made the copy is asked before anything is removed, which is the move #876 already made for the branch (`git branch -d`, not `-D`) now applied to both halves of the one function:

- **A worktree is removed WITHOUT `--force`**, so the refusal is git's own. git refuses on a modified file, on a staged one and on an untracked one — every way a copy comes to hold something. A refusal is not an error and is not announced: it is the copy being kept, whole. The directory, the branch and the record all stay, because a record dropped here would take the `changes for <name> · /land` chip that leads the person back to the work still sitting in it.
- **A plain folder has no git to ask**, so `mirrorHoldsWork` compares the copy with the folder it was made from: a path the folder does not have, or has at a different length, is work. Its one blind spot — an existing file edited to exactly its old length — is written down in the doc rather than guarded against, because seeing it means reading every file in the folder, which is the cost the copy exists to avoid.

`Wrote` stays as the cheap first answer, and the doc comment now says plainly that it is never the authority.

## Acceptance

- `TestACopyIsKeptWhenItHoldsWorkTheBeltDidNotWrite` — the three ways git itself refuses, each asserting the file survives, the record is kept and the branch is not deleted: a file git has never seen, a file staged but not committed, a tracked file edited in place. The first case is the failing replication from #897, inverted.
- `TestACopyOfAPlainFolderIsKeptWhenItHoldsWork` — the same promise on the road with no git.
- `TestACopyOfAPlainFolderHoldingNothingIsStillGivenBack` and the unchanged `TestSayingInPlaceAfterTheCopyWasCutTakesItBack` are the controls: a copy holding nothing is still given back whole, worktree and branch, which is what proves the un-forced removal still succeeds on a clean copy.

`internal/manual/chat/choosing-a-folder.md`'s give-back paragraph now says the copy is kept when it holds work of any kind, names the shell command and the task explicitly, and says which authority is asked on each road.

Residuals 2 and 3 stay in #897 and nothing else is folded in here.

Part of #884 — lane T, the first of two. Lane P builds the record pane on top of the table
that follows this.

Three defects on the owner's screenshot, and all three were the same shape: **one fact with
two writers**.

### `stopped · stopped`

`internal/session`'s `taskGradeOutcome` spells a stopped node's own outcome as the literal
`"stopped"`, and `tasksMiddle` hung that outcome off `taskStateWord(entry)` — so the page said
one reading twice because each writer thought it was the one saying it.

The fix is not a string. `session.TaskStatus.RowWord()` is the join, written down once: the
word, the reason, and the rule that a reason merely restating the word is not said again. It
is what the column beside a conversation already reads (`tierRowBody`), so the two surfaces
now say the same sentence about one row by construction rather than by agreement. Three
hand-rolled compositions in `tasksMiddle` collapse into it, and `tasksNote` stops spelling a
state word at all — it is now only *which window the work is in*.

Consequence, and it is #884's own ruling for the table arriving a PR early: **the record's raw
outcome sentence leaves the row.** On every row the engine grades, that sentence WAS the state
word in different clothes; where it is real prose it belongs on the record card, which is one
`enter` away. The row's degradation ladder is now `2 files · your call · nobody could check it`
→ `your call · nobody could check it` → `your call`: the word a list is scanned for is the last
thing a narrow frame gives up.

### `one call ran 29.24078975s without answering and was abandoned`

`time.Duration.String` is the engine talking to itself — eight decimal places of a figure
nobody can act on, and the nanoseconds were never a fact about the run, only the resolution of
the clock. `checkerStalled` now spells the bound with `taskSpanWord`, this package's one
spelling of how long something took.

### The `~` at the right of a conversation root

`docs/design/home-mission-control/DESIGN.md` §1 retired `~` as a project name and the project
tag on rows in this window's own folder. Home obeyed it; the tasks place drew both. New
`internal/tui3/projecttag.go` holds `chatProjectWord` — that rule, once — and home's
`chatProjectTag` is now two lines delegating to it.

### The bar

- **One abstraction:** `session.TaskStatus.RowWord()` reused rather than re-spelled, and
  `chatProjectWord` extracted so two pages ask one rule. Anyone drawing a list of work or a
  list of conversations can use both.
- **Deleted:** three compositions in `tasksMiddle`, the state-word branch of `tasksNote`, the
  `session.TaskReasonOf` and `refused()` calls this page made for itself, and the raw-outcome
  fact on the row.
- **Guarded by:** `TestARowSaysItsStateWordOnce`, `TestTheRowTakesItsStateAndReasonFromTheOneJoin`,
  `TestAConversationRootWearsAFolderTagOnlyWhereItIsNews`, `TestAnAbandonedCallIsSaidInWholeSeconds`.
- **Seam reported, not patched:** `checkerRanOut` still says `window.String()` (`5m0s`). That
  window is a configured ceiling rather than a measured elapsed, and `taskSpanWord`'s `5m 0s`
  is not an improvement; it wants a ceiling spelling, which is a different question.
- **Other lane's file:** six lines in `internal/tui3/homepanel_recent.go` (lane H's), turning
  `chatProjectTag` into a delegation.

body:
Closes #878.

## What was true

`runFrontier` took `busy := g.governor.holds()` once per pass, before the lock, behind a one-second cache, and marked **every** ready node running against that one bool. With the fan at twenty, twenty agents, twenty worktrees and — minutes later — twenty builds were admitted against a machine read before any of them existed. Neither half of the reading could catch it: load average is a one-minute decayed figure, and a node's memory arrives with its first build. The same hole was on both roads into the frontier: one pass over twenty ready children, and twenty separate `admit()` calls inside one cache window (the division's road).

A second consultation existed too: `TaskGraph.machineBusy` asked the governor again from the division's receipt, *after* the parts were admitted — a question about a machine that did not include them.

## What is true now

The governor keeps a **reservation** for the work it has let in, and it is asked **once per admission**:

    projected = MemAvailable − max(0, running × footprint − visible)

and one more node starts only while `projected` is at or above `task.min_free_mb`. `running` is the graph's own count, which already includes every node the same pass started, so the second node of a fan is judged against the machine the first one leaves behind. Nothing is counted twice: as a node's memory becomes visible, `MemAvailable` falls by what `visible` rises by.

**The footprint is measured**, never a bare constant: the larger of the peak visible memory per running node any reading of this session has seen (a high-water mark, for `ru_maxrss`'s reason) and one core's share of this machine's memory, `MemTotal ÷ cores` — what a node is assumed to need before anything has been measured, because a node's heaviest act is a compiler, which takes a core and memory in the proportion the machine was built in. **Visible** is this process's own tree, walked through each thread's `children` file (a full `/proc` scan measured 13 ms on this 1,583-process box).

So a quiet machine starts about one node per core's share of the memory above the floor, and holds the rest with `waiting · machine busy`; they start as earlier ones settle or as a reading shows room. `task.parallel` is unchanged and still asked first. The reservation is kept in memory and not in load because memory is the resource that *fails* rather than slows — and bounding admitted nodes by memory already bounds the CPU burst.

## Deleted

`admissionGovernor.holds`, the once-per-pass `busy` bool and its parameter, `hostLoadPerCore`/`hostAvailableMB` (folded into readers that also read `MemTotal`), and `TaskGraph.machineBusy` — the division's receipt now reads what the frontier decided (`machineHolds`) and says *some* of the parts are waiting, because a wide fan is half started and half held.

## Law

`TestEveryStartIsJudgedByTheGovernor` (`go/ast`, so it is on the laws gate): a node is moved to `TaskRunning` in exactly one function; `runFrontier` asks `holdOnStartingLocked` before that move; `admits` and `observe` have one caller each; a node *born* running must be named in `bornRunning` with its reason.

## Tests

Scripted, no real sleeps. Twenty ready parts on a machine with room for four start four and hold sixteen; one reading serving twenty admissions admits three (the defect's own shape); a reading that catches up releases the reservation without double counting; the footprint grows to what this session's nodes were seen to hold and does not fall back; `internal/tui3`: a held **child** row draws the machine word — it previously drew nothing at all, which is 8 lines in `railSaysMore` (lane V's file, named in the lane report).

Manual: `how-tasks-run.md` and `tasks.md` say how many start at once, what a footprint is, and what holds the rest. Design: `docs/design/task-start/DESIGN.md`.

Files outside this lane's region, for merge ordering: `internal/session/task_divide.go` (S2) and `internal/tui3/task.go` (V).

body:
## What was true

A task node made two model calls of its own **in front of** its worker's first request:

- the memory router, as an argument to the worker's constructor (`newTaskAgentOn` → `memoryBlock`): 6 s on node 5 of `de9eabcb10cc1e45`, once per worker a node built;
- the drawn division's reading, between the worker being built and its first request (`divideFromSketch` → `reviewDivision`): 219 s on the same node. The card said `sizing the work` and the worker sat unstarted.

## What is true now

Both are a **reading beside the work** (`task_beside.go`'s `besideWork`): started next to the work, bound to the node's context, cancelled and joined on every road out.

- **Memory** (`memory.go`'s `nodeMemory`): one reading per node run, begun before the working copy is carved, handed to every worker the node builds. A late block rides the next request through the drain every request is assembled by. `newTaskAgentOn` asks no model anything (law test).
- **Sizing**: `divideOnce` is split into `weighDivision` and `admitDivision` with one record written once. The drawing is weighed beside the first worker (`sizeBeside`); the worker's first request goes out at once. Parts are admitted through **the same body** and their receipt queued for the running worker; a refusal changes nothing; work only a person can do stops the worker and lands it on the person; an answer after the worker's last word is dropped (journal word `dropped`). Admission is decided under `Agent.handover` — the lock the runner's tail reads its news under — so parts are never admitted under a worker that will not fold them.
- `sizing the work` is drawn only where the asker waits (`divisionAsker.waits`): a worker inside its own `divide_work`.

Scripted, memory 600 ms + reading 2 s: admitted → first worker request **2,642 ms → 27 ms**.

**Deliberate deviation from the lane brief:** the reviewed parts are NOT handed to the worker to re-propose via `propose_task` — that road has no scope refusal, shared-check lift, family composer or careful tier, and cheap workers were measured never reaching for a verb to hand out a division already written. The harness still admits through the one division body. Consent-window pre-carve (brief item 4) is not done: the worktree/snapshot rungs write into the person's `.git` before consent, and the carve is S1's; the seam is in `docs/design/task-start/DESIGN.md`.

## Tests

- `TestTheWorkersFirstRequestGoesOutBeforeTheDrawingIsWeighed` (real runner; reviewer answers only after the worker's first request — the old code deadlocks it), `TestWorkNoWorkerCanDoStopsARunningWorkerAndLandsOnThePerson`, `TestADrawingWeighedAfterTheWorkerFinishedHandsNothingOut`, `TestADrawingWeighedAfterTheWorkerHandedWorkOutIsDropped`, `TestAReadingBesideTheWorkerMovesNoPhase`
- `TestMemoryThatAnswersLateRidesTheWorkersNextRequest`, `TestATaskWorkerIsBuiltWithoutWaitingForItsMemory`
- Laws: `TestEveryReadingBesideTheWorkHasAJoin`, `TestATaskWorkersConstructorAsksNoModel`, `TestAReadingBesideTheWorkIsCancelledAndWaitedFor`
- Existing sketch/divide tests rewritten to drive `sizeBeside`; `-race -count=3` clean on the new ones.

## Seams for the integrator

`agent.go:170` + `session.go` `Config.memoryBrief` are dead after this (agent.go off-limits); `task_child_run.go:172-192` (S1) comment reason moved; `checkpoint_quick.go:51` (Q) one comment; `runTaskNode` 6 lines; `reading-a-task-page.md` (V) one bullet; `tasks.md` two sketch paragraphs. V's errand hook belongs around `reviewDivision` in `weighDivision`. Full list in `~/af-ts-S2.report.md`.

## What was true

The sizing reading of task 5 (conversation de9eabcb10cc1e45, 2026-09-11) ran for 219 s. Its first token came at 11.5 s, followed by 4,465 reasoning tokens. For all of that time:

- the rail showed `sizing the work` and `asking deepseek/deepseek-…`
- the room showed `nothing on this page yet — it fills in as the task works`
- the pulse file showed `"requests": 0`
- the node's journal held nothing until the bill line landed

Errands run through `callRole` without a stream, so they left none of the traces a worker's request leaves.

## What is true now

`callTrail` (`internal/session/task_calltrail.go`) is one watcher, bound to the node, on every request made under a context. It attaches through `provider.WithCallProgress` (#868). For each request it writes:

- **Pulse:** `taskBeat.began` and `taskBeat.ended`.
- **Journal:** a new evidence-only `flight` line at both ends. The end line carries role, model, machine, how it ended, first-token ms, total ms, and answer and reasoning counts.
- **Phase:** the live request on `TaskPhaseNotice.Call` (a `TaskCall`), beside the ladder sentence. The rail, the room and hosted windows already fold that event whole. The remote task lane carries it as JSON; the new test pins that it survives.

Concurrency:

- The provider's watcher only queues and nudges. The trail's one goroutine does all writing.
- The ladder's sentence goes through the same queue, so the order is total.
- `end()` drains the queue, writes a `cancelled` end for any arm still open, and joins the goroutine. The caller ends the trail before it leaves the phase.

Surface:

- **Rail:** `sizing the work · thinking 41s · ↓ 4,465 · deepinfra`, with the ladder sentence on the row under it.
- **Room:** `✳ asking deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash · 1 of 2 · thinking 41s · ↓ 4,465 · deepinfra`, drawn in place of `nothing on this page yet`.
- The thought glyph comes through `app.icon(tokens.GThought)`. Vocabulary goes through one table (`callPhaseWords`), and `↓` through the shared `tokenDownWord`.

## Laws and tests

- `TestASizingRequestLeavesItsTrailOnTheJournalThePulseAndTheRow` drives a real `provider.Client` against a scripted SSE stream. It asserts the journal lines, the pulse, and the notices that carry thinking and then writing. It fails when the hook line is removed.
- `TestATrailDrawsTheArmNearestAnAnswerAndLeavesNoRequestOpen` covers a hedge arm, a loser still open at the end, and a report after the end.
- `TestATrailsWatcherReturnsWhileTheJournalIsHeld` is the runtime law that the watcher does no work.
- `TestOnlyTheCallTrailWatchesARequestRun` is a go/ast law, on the laws gate: `provider.WithCallProgress` is attached only by the trail.
- tui3: `TestARequestASizingIsWaitingOnIsDrawnOnTheRailAndInTheRoom` (before/after frames in its log) and `TestARequestWithNothingBackDrawsOnlyItsWait` (emptiness law).
- remote: `TestARequestAPhaseIsWaitingOnCrossesTheWire`.
- Manual: `how-tasks-run.md` and `reading-a-task-page.md` are updated, with two new probes in `chat_test.go`.

## Merge order and ownership

- **This branch carries no provider or lane files.** #868's seam is already in
  `speed/task-start`; the stale merge of it was rebased away. `git diff --name-only
  origin/speed/task-start...HEAD` touches nothing under `internal/provider` or
  `internal/lane`.
- **It sits on top of `origin/speed/ts-S2` (#883, 01308b03b).** The hook lives inside S2's
  `sizingWait`: the `sizingLine` struct (`trail` replaces `agent`/`node`), `sizingSaid`,
  the new `watching`, `say` through the trail, `ended` ending the trail before `settle()`,
  and the one returned line `sizing.watching(withErrandWatch(ctx, sizing.tell))`. Merge
  #883 first and this applies clean.
- `tokencol.go`: extracts `tokenDownWord`, shared by a step caption and the rail.
- `task.go`: a field and one clear line. It is disjoint from lane B's `proposeTask` change.
- `Config.auditClock`/`Agent.auditNow` are renamed `Config.clock`/`Agent.now` — the agent's
  one movable reading of the world's time, now that the trail measures a request's length
  against it too.

## The review round (V-fix)

- A question's `CallEnded` is said once and closes **every** request the question had out:
  the named one as it ended, a rescue racing beside it as left.
- A request that walks to another machine is one request to the person — no second pulse
  edge, no second journal line — and the record keeps `journalFlight.Hops` instead.
- `DurationMS` is measured from the **first** attempt's start, off `Agent.now`, never
  `time.Since`; `FirstTokenMS` stays on the last attempt's start, because the counts reset
  when a request moves.
- Two new scripted tests pin both:
  `TestAWalkedRequestIsOnePairOfLinesOnePulseAndItsOwnLength` and
  `TestAQuestionsEndingClosesTheRescueRacingBesideIt`.
- `callFields` stays separate from `phaseFields`, and its doc says why: `CallProgress`
  carries no deadline, so a task row says `paced 6s` rather than inventing a countdown.

`docs/design/task-start/DESIGN.md` is created with section V, including the seams owed for the reflex recall (S2), the handover (checkpoint.go) and tok/s (#868).

title: Task start (V): a request made on a node's behalf is seen while it runs

body:
Lane S1 of the task-start wave. Two findings, both in the ground a task stands on.

## 1. Every node paid for a fork nobody used

On the owner's laptop, 93 of 93 nodes admitted since 2026-09-08 ended up on the snapshot rung. Each one first attached, sealed and forked its whole workspace, then threw the fork away. That cost about 15 s in front of every task's first request. Nothing recorded why the fork failed, and nothing stopped the next node paying again.

- **The rung gives a reason when it falls.** `groundRung` is now `reach()` (asked before anything is touched) plus `carve()`. When carve fails it returns a `rungFell` with the reason. The walk goes into the node's log as each stood-down or fallen rung with its reason and cost, then `its world was made in <time>`. The worker's brief is unchanged.
- **A failed fork is remembered per ground** (`groundfalls.go`, `~/.aforge/v3/universe-falls.json`). The next node on that ground asks furrow nothing, and its log says so. The memory lasts only while the aforge build and the furrow program both stay the same. A successful fork clears it. A stopped task is not recorded as a failure.
- **One door seals the parent's world.** `sealForkWorld` is deleted. The fork is now sealed by the snapshot rung's own `sealGroundWork` (`commit-tree`: runs no hooks, does not sign). A new `standOnSeal` cuts its branch using plumbing only. This cause is proven on the Spark: with a commit-msg hook that rejects machine commits, the old fork fell on every node and the child lost its `.env`. Now the fork succeeds and keeps it. The laptop's own cause could not be reproduced on Linux; its log will now name it.
- **furrow calls are bounded.** `Fork` has a bound (the attach's minute). A merge preview uses the read bound. `WaitDelay` is set, and `Attach` returns furrow's reason. A new law test, `TestEveryCallIntoFurrowIsBounded`, enforces this.

| ground (Spark, real furrow, time per node) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain repo | universe · 0.44–0.49 s | universe · 0.46–0.47 s |
| commit-msg hook refuses | snapshot, **no .env** · 0.81–1.03 s every node | universe, .env · 0.46–0.48 s |
| furrow refuses the fork | snapshot · 0.80–1.02 s every node | 0.98 s once, then 27–30 ms |

## 2. One `git status` per finished tool call

A batch's end events all arrive after the whole batch has run, so every one of those processes read the same tree. `worktreeMoved` is deleted. A `treeWatch` now reads the tree **at most once a batch**. The first call that could have changed the tree triggers the read; the check uses the belt's classes, not tool names. Reading hands, harness refusals and named saves trigger nothing. The read runs off-path as L6's `offpath.Reading` (#876, copied byte-for-byte), settled within `lane.Hysteresis`. The run owns the watch and joins it when it ends. The status now runs with `--no-optional-locks`, so it cannot hold the index lock the worker needs.

| per 8-call step | before | after (edit + 2 bash) | after (read-only) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| aforge-v2 clone, 5,706 files | 61.6 ms | 8.3 ms | 0 |

## Notes for the integrator

- `docs/design/task-start/DESIGN.md` is also created by lane P, so expect an add/add conflict. Keep both sections.
- `internal/offpath/` matches L6's #876 byte-for-byte, so it merges cleanly in either order.
- `task_run.go` changes stay local to `openTaskWorld`, `worktreeDirt` and the `taskTree` struct.
- The manual is updated: `how-tasks-run.md` covers the reported and remembered fall. `forking-and-syncing-a-workspace.md` claimed aforge never runs `furrow watch` itself, which stopped being true when the ladder began attaching folders.

`make pr-ready BASE=origin/speed/task-start` passed (session 182.7 s).

body:
**Lane B of the task-start wave.** `propose_task` is now a staged tool. When its call closes while the rest of the reply is still streaming, the card and its countdown can go up at once. Admission waits until the reply is whole, and the proposal is withdrawn cleanly if the reply does not go through.

## Measured before building
The Spark's 5,562 transcripts contain ten replies with two or more task calls. The stream time left after the first task call closes:

| task calls | est. from wall-time share | est. at 100 tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| 2 (n=8) | p50 11.3 s, p90 60.8 s | p50 4.6 s, p90 12.5 s |
| 3 (n=1) | 13.2 s | 6.1 s |
| 4 (n=1) | 18.7 s | 29.7 s |

The gain for each proposal is capped by its countdown (15 s by default). The work now starts at the later of the countdown ending and the reply ending; before, it started at the reply ending plus the countdown. Method and data: `docs/design/task-start/DESIGN.md`.

## What this PR does
- **`internal/exec/bare/stage.go`**: `StagedTool`, `Staged` (`Commit` or `Withdraw`, exactly one), `Hold` (decided once: release or withdraw), `RunStaged`, and `Tool.Stages()`. The property that lets a tool start early is the tool's shape: `Stages()` reads an unexported field that only `StagedTool` sets, so no tool can claim it with a flag.
- **`propose_task` split** (`task.go`):
  - `stageTask`: refusals, ground, slot, id, preflight, and the card with its clock running.
  - `stagedProposal.Commit`: reads the answer, applies the redirect and the model shortlist, compiles `admissionContext`, admits.
  - Two things moved to keep quality unchanged. The **admission context is now compiled at the commit**, so the node's brief quotes the whole reply, byte-for-byte what the batch compiled. The **answer wait runs from the moment the card goes up**, so a "no" and an expired clock are read in the order they happened.
- **Withdrawal**: the question is withdrawn in one sentence, and the card settles through the new `TaskNotice.Withdrawn` field (`internal/tui3/task.go`: a few lines in lane V's file; V has been told). Late answers are dropped and the fan slot is handed back.
- `quick_task` is **deliberately not staged**. Its commit is the worker's first request, and that request's brief quotes the reply, so nothing about it can run early without changing the brief.

## The loop.go seam (not in this PR)
`loop.go` belongs to another session's lane, so this PR ships only the machinery; without the seam it changes nothing about when a proposal starts. The five-move seam, its loop-level tests (`stageearly_loop_test.go`) and the manual lines that describe the behaviour are one commit on **`speed/ts-B-seam`** (`1eb37f681`), stacked on this PR's commit. The design doc lists every move. Apply that commit after this PR merges, with the owner of loop.go agreeing.

## Tests
- `internal/exec/bare/stage_test.go`: the hold's laws.
- `internal/session/stageearly_test.go`:
  - the card goes up and the clock runs out, yet nothing is admitted before release;
  - the admission quotes the reply;
  - withdrawal takes the card and the question back;
  - withdrawal hands the fan slot back;
  - a "no" given before the clock expired wins;
  - on the belt, only `propose_task` stages.
- `internal/tui3/taskwithdrawn_test.go`: a withdrawn card settles, overrides this window's own clock verdict, and draws nothing when this window never had the card.
- Seam branch: `stageearly_loop_test.go` covers four cases:
  - the first card is up before the second call closes;
  - a cut reply takes back the proposal it had started, and exactly one task is admitted;
  - a reply that ends without the call takes it back;
  - a write before a proposal keeps its order.

  All pass under `-race -count=3`.

## What was wrong (verified on dev 6a3b478cf)

- **Q0** A checkpoint holding a quick node would not load: its empty done-condition failed `decodeTasks` for the whole document, so every conversation that ran `quick_task` resumed with no tasks at all.
- **Q1** The record labelled a quick node and could not rebuild it (`spec.quick == nil` after restore); ticks lived only in memory.
- **Q2** `continue` re-queued a restored quick node, which fell through to `workTaskNode`: worktree, branch, checker.
- **Q3** A running quick task held no claim on files it wrote; `tasks.md` said the first writer owned the file.
- **Q4** The ceiling road built its quick node by hand through `launchRouteTask`: invented acceptance, worktree mode, a naming call, blank `where`, depth 0, no owner, no claim look.
- **Q5** `PresenceTask` had neither kind nor parent, so another window's quick parts read to the model as unrelated jobs.
- **Q6** A restored quick node was counted `interrupted (no branch kept)`; `TaskNode.Expects` was never persisted.

## What is true now

- **One door:** `Agent.admitQuick(quickAsk) (id, spec, refusal)` holds `quickGate`, builds through `newQuickSpec` (the one place mode, ground, `where`, `named`, the empty acceptance, family and model are decided), claims the fan slot and admits. The tool parses a `quickAsk`; the ceiling reads one out of the drawing. `launchRouteTask` lost its `quick` parameter and branch.
- **Record:** `taskRecord.Quick {line, items, done, files}` and `taskRecord.Expects`, both `omitempty`. `restoreNode` rebuilds the body through `newQuickTaskSpec`, and a tick checkpoints. The acceptance rule is #869's `acceptanceHolds` / `kindsWithoutAcceptance`, and this PR merges #869.
- **Restart:** a quick node caught by the close, whether running **or queued**, settles failed. Its report carries the list (`ticked 1 of 3: …`, `not ticked: …`) and its changed list is what it wrote. The recovery line gets a clause of its own, `N quick tasks did not finish`. `reopen` refuses kind quick in the same switch and sentence as harness/subharness.
- **Claim:** one derivation, `TaskNode.holdsTreeLocked`, splits `claimOver` (tree holders) from `fileOwner` (every other running node owns what it wrote). A quick task never holds the folder, only the files it has saved.
- **Presence:** `PresenceTask.Kind`, `.Parent`, and `Done`/`Total` from quick items. `<elsewhere>` folds a window's parts onto their head (`- Survey … · window "x" · 3 quick parts running · files`) and names a non-ordinary kind with `TaskKindWord`.
- **Manual:** `tasks.md` quick sections (claim example, six limits incl. restart and continue, keep-editing correction, elsewhere fold) and `how-tasks-run.md` (recovery bullet and clause, file hold). **Design:** `docs/design/quick-task/DESIGN.md` has a dated section.
- **Complexity:** `rehydrate` went from 18 to 12 (per-record `taskRecovery.reconcile`); its ledger row is deleted. `note()`'s four per-kind clauses became one table.

## Overlap with #869 (already merged into this branch, commit e24357043)

- **Acceptance.** Kept #869's `kindsWithoutAcceptance` / `acceptanceHolds`; this lane's `lacksAcceptance` is deleted.
- **Waiting quick node settles.** Kept #869's `nothingIsComingBackForIt`, which `taskRecovery.reconcile` now calls. Its doc now gives the new reason: the list is on the record, and the node's turn is over.
- **Report on close.** #869's `quickLostReport` wording stays, and `quickReportOnClose(record)` is the one report, now with the list appended. This lane's `quickNeverStartedReport` / `quickClosedReport` are deleted.
- **Tests.** #869's `TestAQuickTaskComesBackFromTheCheckpoint` now asserts the items and ticks it had explicitly deferred to "somebody else's change". Its recovery count expects `quick: 1`, not `interrupted: 1`. This lane's duplicate decode test is dropped.
- **Manual.** *A quick task after a restart* no longer says the checklist "is not written down anywhere". It now shows the ticked/not-ticked list and the recovery clause.

## Touches outside the lane (for merge ordering)

- `internal/session/checkpoint.go` has two one-line call sites. `:3818` becomes `handOverAsQuick(ctx, hub, turn, started, model, *quick)` and `:4058` drops the trailing `, nil`. They follow the two changed signatures. A remaining seam is recommended there but **not** done: move `ahead := a.nameAhead(asked)` (`:3806`) below the quick branch, so the quick road never starts a namer that it then releases.
- `route_judge.go:455` drops `, nil`.
- Comment-only: `task.go` (the `taskSpec.quick` doc) and `task_run.go` (the `TaskNode.Expects` doc).
- `complexity_test.go` deletes the paid-off `TaskGraph.rehydrate` row.

## Tests

New file `task_quick_door_test.go`:
- a tool-door quick node round-trips with its ticks, and both a running and a waiting quick node settle on the close;
- the real `tasks.json` shape (quick 1-4 with `"acceptance": ""` beside ordinary node 5) decodes;
- a table test shows the ceiling node's shape equals the tool node's;
- continue refuses a restored quick node in the harness wording;
- the chat's write to a file a running quick worker wrote is refused with the holder named, through the real road and guard;
- `<elsewhere>` folds a family, and an orphan part stands alone;
- `Expects` round trip, owed only by a node that never ran.

Plus `task_quick_door_law_test.go` (go/ast, laws gate): only `newQuickSpec`/`restoreNode` may put a quick body on a spec, only `newQuickTaskSpec` may build one, only `admitQuick` takes `quickGate`.

Mutation check: reverting the decoder rule or the `fileOwner` filter fails three of them. `make test-quick` is green; `make pr-ready` results are in the lane report.
