title: Quick task as one object: one door, a record that rebuilds it, a hold on what it wrote (task-start lane Q)

body:
Eight measured places where a person's turn paid for work it never asked for. The trap was eight local patches; these are **three shapes**, each one named type with its law in its doc comment, one test, and every caller using it.

## The three mechanisms

**`internal/filememo` — a file read at most once per change.**
`Memo[T]` spends one stat to decide whether it may answer. Used by the profile's `config.json` (`APIKeyConfigured` on every Enter, `FirstPrompt` on every turn, eight readers in `internal/config`) and by a project's `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (re-read whenever the prompt's clock goes stale — the came-back-to-the-terminal turn, and once per attached folder). `Stamped` folds a caller's own write counter into the freshness key, so `internal/config` can never serve back a write it just made, whatever a filesystem's timestamp resolution is.

**`internal/offpath` — the two shapes of work that must not happen on a person's path.**
`Take`/`Reading[T]` is a fact gathered beside the work and settled with a bound; `Deferred`/`Write` is a write a read path owes, coalesced, with `Settle` as the exit door. Three users today: the per-batch `git status`, the fix shelf's counters, the meta.json stamp. **The peer lane's S1 (per-tool-call status on `speed/task-start`) is the fourth** — `offpath.Take` is exactly its shape and the package is named and exported for that.

**`internal/session/toolask.go` — the one door a hand on the belt asks a model through.**
`view_image` and `read`'s three senses each made their own call, and each got the same four things wrong separately.

## What each finding cost, and what it costs now

| | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `read` on media / `view_image` | untagged in the call log (`tag:null`, 2,830 unattributable finishes in ten days), silent for 7–20 s, unbounded in length, bounded at ten minutes | tagged `tool:<name>` + node, `looking at error.png` on screen for the wait, capped at what a tool result shows, bounded by `lane.RoleTool.GiveUp()` |
| `git status` per batch | inline, 10–30 ms small / seconds large | `offpath.Take`, joined at `lane.Hysteresis` |
| `compactToolHistory` | rebuilt the frozen prefix per request | **1.34 ms → 13 µs** (100 rounds), **11.7 ms → 156 µs** (1600) |
| `config.json` | read + parsed per call | one stat per call |
| `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` | re-read per stale clock | one stat per render |
| `fixShelf.consult` | 4 whole-file cycles per fail→fix→succeed, on the READ path | zero writes on the path |
| `stampUserLocked` | LoadMeta+SaveMeta **with the agent lock held**, per user message | snapshot on the path, disk behind it |
| first write into a referred folder | `git worktree add` / recursive copy inside the tool call, silent | started at `ReferPlace`, `preparing · a working copy of <folder>` |

## The `read`-on-an-image decision

**The sense stays; the defect was never that `read` senses.** Decision 20's whole argument is that a model must not have to pick between two verbs for one intention, and `read`'s description has told it `Images, audio and video come back described, never as bytes` since that decision landed — so removing the sense would be removing a working capability, which is not what "a capability that cannot work is absent" says. What was actually wrong: the call was anonymous, silent, unbounded in length and carrying a second ten-minute budget beside the one the dispatcher already derives. All four are fixed at the door. `prompts/system.md` now says `read` **asks another model** on a picture and that it is a real, bounded, shown wait that is free the second time; the manual gained "How long does reading a picture or a recording take, and what do I see while it happens?".

## New role row

`lane.RoleTool` — the properties are derived, not described: somebody **is** waiting (the tool row is open in front of them → `Interactive`), its text is never drawn (`Visible: false`), it is text and is watched as text (`Streams: true`), one shot (`Horizon: 1`), as impatient as talk (`Patience: 1` → 90 s give-up, 10 s ceiling). `viewLookWindow` is deleted.

## Laws now guarding this

- `TestNoHandAsksAModelOutsideTheOneDoor` — `go/ast` over `tools_*.go`, fails the build on a second send site. On the `test-laws` gate.
- `TestAReadOnlyBatchRunsNoWorktreeReading` / `TestAShellBatchTakesOneReadingAndDoesNotWaitItOut` / `TestAFastWorktreeReadingStillReportsMovement`
- `TestConsultingTheFixStoreWritesNothingOnThePath`
- `TestAFrozenPrefixIsReducedOncePerConversationAndNotPerRequest` + `BenchmarkCompactToolHistory` (cold/warm)
- `TestTheProfileConfigIsParsedOncePerChange`, `TestAWriteDoesNotRewriteWhatTheMemoIsHolding`
- `TestAToolsAskIsBoundedByItsRoleAndNotByANumber`, `TestAnAskedModelMayNotWriteMoreThanTheBeltShows`
- `internal/offpath` and `internal/filememo` each carry their law as their own test file.

## Deleted

`viewLookWindow`; `senseOneShot`'s own completion, accounting and error handling; `viewImage`'s own context timeout, role, accounting and no-answer handling; the inline `worktreeDirt` call in `treeMoved`; `saveLocked` from `consult`; the synchronous `updateMeta` in `stampUserLocked`; the per-request view composition in `compactToolHistory`'s two walks; `readProfileConfig`'s and `readInstructionFileWithin`'s own reads; and the comment in `budget.go` saying this package deliberately holds no cache.

## Seams into other lanes' files

- **`loop.go:1379`** — one token, `compactToolHistory(` → `a.compactToolHistory(`. The memo has to live on the agent; there is no other per-session home for it.
- **`internal/lane/roles.go`** — additive: one `Role` constant and one table row.
- **`agent.go`'s `Agent.Close`** *(not made — L1's file)*: it should call `a.SettleMeta()`. Without it, the window in which a process could exit holding an owed meta.json stamp is the length of one small write; with it, zero.

title: No hidden work on the turn: one file memo, one off-path reading, one deferred write, and one door for a hand asking a model

body:
## What was wrong

ARCHITECTURE.md's fourth law is one sentence — **`open` and `tick` may read the disk and `body` may not** — and it was true by habit rather than by anything a build could check. Habit lost three times:

| Where | What it cost |
| --- | --- |
| `imagepreview.go` `(*app).picture` | one `os.Stat` per **visible picture per frame**, because the modification time and the size WERE the preview cache's key. Twelve open pictures at 30 Hz is 360 syscalls a second, taken from inside `View`. |
| `models.go` `CachedModelsFor` | the whole model cache re-read off disk by **every frame that had to name a model** with no catalog behind it — the first-run screen, and every window opened with no key. |
| `app.go` `/workspace <path>` | `git rev-parse` and `git status`, **on the update loop**, under one shared 400 ms ceiling. The surface stopped dead on the keystroke that set the workspace. |

## The one abstraction

The first two are the same shape — *a fact read off the disk under a name, kept until something says the bytes moved* — so there is **one** mechanism for it and both callers use it:

`learned[T]` (`internal/tui3/learned.go`), three doors and a rule about which loop may open each.

- **`of(name)` is the frame's door and it reads nothing.** It answers the memo and writes a miss down.
- **`learn(name)` is the loop's door**: read it now, file it. Every caller is `open`, a tick, or an arrival — the picture call that just finished, the file the person just attached, the mirror's copy landing, the press that asked to see a collapsed picture, the fetch that rewrote the model cache.
- **`refresh()` is the tick's door**, riding the pulse's existing ten-second beat. Nothing on a machine tells a terminal that a png was overwritten; the only way to know is to ask again, on a beat slow enough that asking is free.
- `catchUp()` is the backstop: whatever the last frame asked about, read once, on the loop. It makes the arrival hooks a matter of latency rather than of correctness.

`/workspace` now takes `probeGit` — the road every other reading of the repository already took.

## The law that stops the class

`framedisk_law_test.go` walks this package with `go/ast` from `(*app).View`, following calls on the surface itself, package functions, and func-typed **fields** through whatever this package assigns to them — which is how `a.gitProbe(dir)` is known to be `gitHead`. It fails on `os.Stat`, `os.ReadFile`, `os.Open`, `exec.Command`, `filepath.Glob` and the network. Its sibling asks the update loop the narrower question — no process, no wire, on the loop — and walks every closure **except** the ones handed off to be run elsewhere (returned as a `tea.Cmd`, passed to `tea.Batch`, started with `go`), which is exactly the off-loop escape hatch.

Both were checked against the defects: reinstating either one turns the law red naming the exact line.

**The allowlist is one entry**: `renderPicture`, the decode itself — the work the frame is drawing rather than a fact it is fetching, and `app.previews` pays it once per file per shape.

## Two more of the same class, deleted rather than allowlisted

The walk found them:

- `jobPageSeed` took the job log's first reading **inside the frame**, on the reasoning that the column's enter only records the id. The reasoning outlived its door: `showJobPage` has one caller, `openJobPage`, and it has always followed with `jobPageArm`, which opens the same file off the loop. Deleted.
- `noticeEvent`'s bare board went through the ledger **loader** to conclude it had no ledger. It mints one now (`bareNoticeBoard`).

## Measured

`BenchmarkFramePictures` (new): a dozen expanded pictures on a 100×40 frame, M3 Max, 3000×, 5 runs.

| | median | tail | allocs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stat in the frame | 360 µs | **528 µs** | 1122 |
| the memo | **328 µs** | 370 µs | 1120 |

Twelve syscalls a frame become none; the 528 µs outlier is what a syscall stall in a paint looks like, and it is gone.

body:
Lane P of the task-start wave. PR into `speed/task-start`, not `dev`.

## What changed

- **Caps** (`task_run.go`): `taskFanLimit` 5 → **20**, `taskDepthLimit` 2 → **3**. The comment now says what actually bounds breadth: `task.parallel`, the admission governor and file claims. The fan cap is a runaway stop, not a guess about decomposition.
- **The goal sentence**, stated once, in the picture paragraph of `beltfacts.go`'s `handoffFacts`. That is the one text every agent that can hand work out reads, including the conversation, whose fan-out is uncapped. It tightens the paragraph's `HAND THEM OUT AND KEEP ONE` sentence and absorbs two neighbours that said the same law ("Working through them yourself is the slowest order there is", "What they wait on is wall time, not calls"):
  > THE GOAL IS THE SHORTEST WALL TIME FOR THE WHOLE JOB: when what is ahead has parts that do not need each other, hand them all out at once, however many there are, before you open the first, the way one mind with a team of workers would, and keep one to begin yourself, rather than working through them in turn, the order you fall into unless you choose otherwise.

  It is registered as `handoff.wall-time-goal` (`lawCore`). The law registry now also searches the pages only a task node is handed (`worker.md`, `revise.md`, `fanout.md`, `divide.md`, `quick.md`), so a second copy on any page fails the build. I checked that a planted copy in `fanout.md` fails it.

  The fan-out page (`prompts/fanout.md`) drops "TWO OR THREE PARTS", which anchored breadth at the size of the old cap. It also drops its `WEIGH THE CLOCK AT EVERY STEP` paragraph, which repeated the picture's arithmetic.
- **Depth is read once.** `fansOutAt(depth)` is the one reading of `taskDepthLimit`.
  - `Config.mayFanOut` asks it of the worker itself.
  - `fanoutPage` asks it of the depth one below, so the page's clause about whether pieces may split in turn comes from the same predicate that builds the pieces' belts. Before this, the page asserted "a piece you hand out cannot hand out more" unconditionally.
- **`propose_task`'s description** names both bounds from their constants.

## Two couplings the old numbers hid, cut at their cause

1. **`tasks` listing** (`tools_tasks.go`, S2's file, +8 lines). A node's family was clipped at `taskSearchLimit` = 10 with no "more" line. That was safe only while a family could not pass 5. A node that names no limit now sees its whole family. The test also fails if `taskFanLimit` ever exceeds `taskSearchCeiling`.
2. **Division parts armed by their family's words** (`task_divide.go` +10 lines, `task_divide_compose.go` +13 lines, both S2's area).
   - Every part of a wide division came back `armedBy="counted"`, because `armDivision` read the parent's brief composed around the part, plus the inherited `request`.
   - This was inert while parts had no verb. At depth 3 every part would have been handed the whole job's pile to divide again.
   - Now the judge's yes arms only a root, and the count reads the part's own scope (`partOwnWords`, the inverse of `partBrief`). Restores from a checkpoint answer the same way with no new state.

`briefPieceRule` (`task_brief.go`) now declines "any handing out it asks for" rather than "handing work out". Its pinned phrases are unchanged. The rule and the fan-out page can no longer be read as one forbidding what the other teaches.

## Manual

The bounds are updated in `tasks.md` ×2, `how-tasks-run.md` and `what-i-can-do.md`. The goal's person-facing form is added to *Why several things started at once*. `TestTheManualSpellsTheBoundsTheCodeEnforces` pins every sentence that states a number to its constant.

## Measurements

| page | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| conversation fixed prefix (cap 48,000) | 38,742 | 38,843 (+101: +77 on the page for the goal sentence, +24 in `propose_task`'s description naming both bounds) |
| depth-1 worker page | 28,397 | 28,231 (−166: the fan-out page no longer restates the arithmetic) |
| depth-2 worker page | 22,057 | 28,239 (it now carries the verbs and the fan-out page) |

## Tests

These new tests each fail without their fix, each verified by reverting the fix:
- `TestATreeGrowsToItsDepthLimitAndNoFurther`
- `TestAParentListingItsPiecesSeesEveryOneOfThem`
- `TestAPartIsArmedByItsOwnWordsAndNotItsFamilys`
- `TestTheManualSpellsTheBoundsTheCodeEnforces`

The existing fan-cap tests read the constant and hold at 20.

## For the integrator

- **Files outside lane P:** `tools_tasks.go`, `task_divide.go`, `task_divide_compose.go` (S2), a comment in `session.go`, and a quick section of `tasks.md` (Q).
- **Reported, not fixed:**
  - The admission governor weighs the machine once per frontier pass, so 20 ready children start on one reading. That is #878 (lane G). `docs/design/task-start/DESIGN.md` § *The governor seam* states the shape: per-admission questions, and a reservation per admitted node against the memory floor until a reading taken after it started.
  - The tui3 room header (`roomKinRowCap = 3`, V) cuts off children past three rows with no "+N".
  - The `tasks` family text assumes one level.

  Details are in `~/af-ts-P.report.md` and `docs/design/task-start/DESIGN.md`.

Commits carry the wave's `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1` trailer. The lane itself ran on Claude Opus 5.

body:
## What the log said

Two readings from `calls.jsonl` on 2026-09-11, both on the binary built that morning:

- **09:33.** The reflex tier — `mistralai/mistral-nemo`, in front of every keypress — went from **0 of 245** calls on one machine to **7 of 17** on another, whole-wait p50 1.8 s → 5.5 s, first token 302 ms → 1,032 ms.
- **10:02.** A task step served at a collapsed generation rate ran **219 seconds** after a `cd` tool result while two machines on the same model were writing forty times faster. The person read the `cd` row as stuck for three and a half minutes.

## The mechanism, before the fix

Four things, and none of them is a new failure mode — each is the chooser saying something true in a way that could not act:

1. **A refusal reached `provider.order`.** Which the router may ignore once `allow_fallbacks` is true — #850's own sentence. The 09:33:10 row reads `lane: DeepInfra`, `served: DekaLLM`: we asked for one machine and the router used another. Only `provider.ignore` takes a machine off the table.
2. **The cache affinity pin latches onto whoever ANSWERED** (`affinity.go`) and is prepended to the next request's order. So one router deviation became the head of every order for the rest of the session — which is the whole of 6-of-17.
3. **Whether a person reads an answer was read from the two-valued intent.** A recall is `Interactive` (somebody waits) and `Visible: false` (nobody reads a word of it — it goes into a prompt). Read through the intent, its tokens were counted as text somebody reads, which `PerceivedSeconds` charges only above reading speed: 400 tokens at 15 tok/s were priced at **4 seconds** when the truth is **26**. No chooser reading that number could ever refuse a slow writer for an unread call.
4. **A change point reset the chain and not the flat belief the chooser reads.** A ninefold rate collapse was therefore admitted for five more steps over thirty-three minutes, one of them a nine-minute answer.

Three suspects were cleared by the evidence and are not touched: `sheetDoubtsLast`'s probe never fired for this role (no `mistral-nemo` machine is doubted — a zero uptime doubts nothing and the call carries no tools); the served-keyed ledger struck nothing; the bodies did carry an order.

## The one abstraction

`rolePatience.expected` — how long a request is expected to take to a usable answer on one machine:

> the first-token and rate posteriors, read at the quantile this role is exposed to, widened by how far **one answer** from that machine has been measured to sit from its median, divided by how often it answers at all.

The order is that number sorted. The refusal is that number against the role's own declared deadline. There is no ratio, no threshold anybody picked, and nothing anywhere that names a role or a machine — the policy comes from three columns the role table already declares (`Interactive`, `Visible`, `Patience`) and from measured beliefs. A role added to that table tomorrow is handled with nothing in `internal/lane` edited.

## Laws

- `TestNoProbeRidesARoleSomebodyIsWaitingOn` walks every role in the table, both directions: a role with somebody waiting never promotes a doubt, a role with nobody waiting always can.
- `TestEveryRolesPolicyComesFromItsColumns` fails if two roles declaring the same columns are treated differently.
- `TestNothingIsRefusedWhenThereIsNothingBetter` keeps the bound that may never be crossed.

## Proof

`internal/lane` and `internal/provider` suites, `make test-laws` and `make test-quick` on the Spark; fixtures replay the 09:33 and 10:02 series rather than describing them.

title: A machine is asked only when the answer is expected inside the wait its work will sit through

body:
Three findings from the speed audit, each fixed at its cause rather than where it was measured.

## 1 · The reader reads, and nothing else

`classOrdered` was doing two jobs. It named what a call owes the ones around it — the result frame before the first event of the stream it names, and two calls in the order the surface made them — and it *also* decided the body ran on the goroutine that reads the socket. The second was never part of the first: the reader was supplying the order by not reading.

`MethodSubmit` is what made that expensive. The engine's preamble between Submit and the first request leaving — the client rebind, the person's standing orders, the system prompt reassembly, the journal write, the naming errand — all runs before `session.Agent.Submit` returns, and for all of it the engine was not reading its own pipe. A person who pressed Enter and then Esc was queued behind their own send; so was every getter their surface asks from its update loop.

The fix is structural and not a case for Submit: **`orderedLane` is one named mechanism** — one goroutine, arrival order, a hand-in that never blocks — and `callClass.road()` now has two values, *neither of which is the reader*. Every class runs its body off it. `staysOnReader` is deleted.

- `internal/remote/orderedlane.go` — the mechanism, with its law in the doc comment.
- `internal/remote/callclass.go` — the classification, unchanged in membership.
- `server.detached` / `server.goodbye` become atomics: they are decided on the lane and read by the reader loop, and the reading that matters (`server.leave`) happens after the lane drains.

## 2 · Typing crosses the wire

`internal/provider`'s probe exists so a turn's first token is not also paying for a TLS handshake, and it is bought by a keystroke — through `typingAgent`, an optional interface `*remote.Agent` did not satisfy. The default road holds a `*remote.Agent` (`v3TakeHostRoad` is true for every launch but `--no-host`, `--debug`, first-run setup and a hostless `--once`), so the mechanism was dead on every launch people actually make.

`MethodTyping` is the door, classed like every other method, and it is the one frame on this wire nobody waits for (`Client.notify`). The law test beside it is the deliverable that stops the class: **every optional door the surface asserts that the local engine answers must cross the wire, or be written into a ledger that only shrinks.** Twenty-three others are written down with what a person loses by each; `surfaceDoorLedger` ratchets.

## 3 · The pool is stated, not inherited

`IdleConnTimeout` was the standard library's ninety seconds — shorter than a person reads for — so a think-pause cost DNS, TCP and TLS on the next turn, invisibly, because `ttft_ms` cannot tell a handshake from a slow model. Four values are now set on purpose with one reason each, the idle window derived from a measurement against the live router, and `httptrace` writes `conn_reused`, `dns_ms`, `connect_ms` and `tls_ms` onto the finish row. `make census` grows two columns.

## After the review — `b0e61029b`

Five blockers, each a place where the code did not do what the comment beside it said.

1. **The ratchet turned one way.** A shrunk ledger with the number left up was green. `!=` now, with `ratchetComplaint` saying both directions in `internal/ci`'s voice.
2. **This lane made a keystroke block**, which is the thing it exists to stop. `Client.notify` wrote the frame on the caller's goroutine behind the write mutex, so a hint queued behind an in-flight Submit's body. It hands off now with `orderedLane.hand`'s own shape — one hint in flight, compare-and-swap, the write on its own goroutine. `TestAHintDoesNotWaitForAWedgedLink` hangs the binary without it.
3. **The uncapped queue's invariant was a comment.** `TestEveryNotifiedMethodOwesNobodyAnOrder` reads every `c.notify` site with `go/ast` and refuses a method that classifies to `inOrder`.
4. **`running-on-another-machine.md` promised a page that does not draw.** `standingHereAgent` does not cross, so only the *elsewhere* shelf appears. The page says so.
5. **The typing pre-warm was broken in TWO places.** The second is older and larger: `sessionCompleter` wraps the completer on every construction path and forwarded `CompleteWithMessages` and `FallbackModels` and **not `ProbeLanes`** — so no probe had ever been bought from a keystroke, on any road, since the wrapper landed. The test that covered it built an `Agent` literal and never met the wrapper. Three lines forward it; `TestAnAgentBuiltTheOrdinaryWayCanProbe` goes through `newAgent`, and `TestTheCompleterWrapperForwardsEveryDoorTheAdapterOffers` is the law. That law and the surface-door one are the same shape a layer apart, which is the finding worth keeping from this lane.

**The ledger now carries the split.** Fifteen doors are *silently absent*, which is the design law obeyed. Eight *say a reason that is not the reason* — `a.hosted()` is `a.host != ""`, set only by `--host <dest>`, so on a bare `aforge` every guard is skipped and the local branch runs: `/remember` says memory is switched off, `/land` says nothing is waiting, `/autonomy` says the conversation has no project. Each quoted sentence is checked against `internal/tui3`'s own source so it cannot drift into fiction. **#901** is the parent issue, grouped into five families rather than twenty-three methods.

Spark at `b0e61029b`: `provider` `remote` `enginehost` `calllog` `session` `aforge-census` `manual` all ok; `test-laws` 21/21.

## M1 — a send nobody could find out about (`c56443b87`)

Taking the B5 fix switched on a capability that had **never run in a shipped binary**, with the guard on by default. The bound is fine — eight gates, ≤2 one-token requests per 20 s per model, only while somebody is actually waiting, a few cents an hour of unbroken typing. What was wrong is that the probe deliberately writes no call-log row, and `/cost`, the status line, the spend place and the end-of-run total are all sums over those rows.

A section *did* exist, and **the question did not reach it** — `does aforge send anything while I am typing` landed on `attaching-files`, `questions`, `screen`, `commands`. Complete, correct and unreachable. So:

- **New `## Spend that /cost does not show`** — what is sent, what it comes to, that the provider bills it and aforge counts it nowhere, **why** (the probe hangs up at the first word, so the provider's token count never arrives — there is no measured figure to add up), where the record is (`~/.aforge/v3/lanes.log`), and the switch that makes it zero.
- **The typing section repaired**: it was missing the λ gate entirely, and its heading now carries the asker's words. Three retrieval probes hold both.
- **A false sentence removed**: the `/cost` section claimed `model calls` counts *every* request.

**Should it be in the ledger? Yes — [#903](https://github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/issues/903), not done here.** The obstacle is what makes it a ruling: a probe *cannot report what it cost* — it abandons the stream at the first token so the connection goes back warm, so the usage block never arrives. Every other row in that log carries a measured count; a probe row could carry only a computed one. #903 lays out the three shapes and reads it as the middle one.

Two review notes with it: the dead `token.NewFileSet()`/`_ = set` in `notifylaw_test.go` is gone (the law stays on the gate through `go/ast`), and the completer law **no longer filters by receiver spelling** — it carries the spelling, and a door the adapter answers asserted on something it cannot place is a red naming it, symmetric with the surface-door law. Verified to fire behind a local alias.

Spark at `c56443b87`: `manual`, `session`, `remote`, `tui3` all ok; `test-laws` 21/21; `test-packed-manual` ok.

title: A warm wire, and the socket never waits: the reader reads, typing crosses, and the handshake is on the row

body:
## The law

**THE ONLY WAIT A PERSON EXPERIENCES IS THE MAIN MODEL GENERATING.** Every reading this harness makes on its own behalf — which remembered lines a message needs, what is left of a long answer, whether a message was really work, a name, a caption — runs *beside* the work and may only *interrupt* it. Two figures state it and both are asserted:

| bound | figure |
| --- | --- |
| person's message → the first request on the wire | ≤ 50 ms |
| tool result → the next request on the wire | ≤ 50 ms |

## What that cost before it was a law

From the call census of 2026-09-11:

- The **pre-turn recall** was awaited in front of every message. Sixteen of them, mean **4.3 s**, max **10.7 s** — the person's own model was not asked until a mistral-nemo call returned. Measured gates of 1.7 s, 2.3 s, 3.0 s and one of 20.4 s.
- A **mark's reader** held a turn for **8.1 s** between a tool result and the next step, and the next request went out two milliseconds after it returned. It decided nothing, which is what it decides on nearly every turn it is asked on.
- The **post-turn work-or-words cascade** ran with the answer already on the screen and **no window of its own** — the low tier's two minutes and the mastermind's ten.
- `lane.RoleRecall`'s ceiling **was** its caller's deadline (`internal/reflex`'s `Route` read `Ceiling()` as its timeout), so the two fired at the same instant and no recall in this build's history was ever moved off a slow machine.
- The **safety gate** blocked a tool call for up to ten seconds with no phase word at all.

## One mechanism, not four

`internal/session/sidecar.go` — `readBeside(ctx, ask, act)`. Three verbs: **start** where the question becomes askable, **take** where the answer can still be spent (non-blocking), **end** where nobody can spend it. `act` is the reading's one power over the work: the interruption.

Four readings use it: the recall, the mark's drawing, the pre-turn work-or-words race (whose shape it was taken from), and the post-turn cascade. The three ad-hoc goroutines and the two straight-line awaits they replaced are deleted.

**A reading DECIDES; the turn ACTS.** The post-turn cascade used to start its own task from inside its own `ask`, which meant it could open a task on a turn the checkpoint was about to RE-OPEN. It now answers a `judgeRuling` — a verdict, a turn number and the held name — and `applyRouteJudge` spends it at the take, after the re-open question has been settled. An effect that fires from inside a reading fires at a moment nobody chose. `TestAJudgesRulingIsSpentByTheTurnAndNotByTheReading` takes a yes-ruling in full and asserts zero tasks until the turn spends it, then exactly one.

## Quality is kept by APPLYING every decision, never by awaiting it

- lands before the request is assembled → the request carries it, as before;
- lands before the first token → the request is cut and re-asked **once**, no backoff, nothing on the person's screen (there was nothing there yet), the provider's prefix cache making the second send the cheap one;
- lands after the first token → it rides the **next step** and the turn's journal row records it as late, so the memory ledger still learns.

A drawing with independent parts in it cuts the step in flight through the same door a person's steer uses, so the boundary where it is spent arrives at once. A mark crossed by the round that ENDS a turn has no next boundary, so `runTurn`'s exit defer settles it: a paid-for reading is never a ledger line nobody can count.

## The one named exception

The **safety gate** (`guardian.go`) decides whether a tool RUNS, so it has nothing to run beside and nothing it could be applied to afterwards. It keeps its ten-second window and now draws `checking whether this is safe to run` for the whole of it — and *restores* the batch's `running <tool>` word afterwards rather than clearing it, because phase is one slot.

## Ceilings that could never fire

- `lane.RoleRecall` patience 1 → **0.2**: a 2 s ceiling (above the fastest measured machine's median, 1.7 s; below the slow ones', 4.3 s and 5.5 s) inside an 18 s give-up, which `internal/reflex` now reads as its window so the rescue has somewhere to land.
- `lane.RoleJudge` patience 6 → **1**: 60 s was outside every window its callers set. The ceiling is derived, not chosen — **the tightest caller's window less one measured first token**. That caller is the pre-turn route read at 20 s; the measured p90 first token is 8.4 s; so the ceiling must be above 8.4 s (or a healthy machine is abandoned mid-answer) and below 20 − 8.4 = 11.6 s (or a second machine cannot answer inside the caller's window). Patience 1 puts it at 10 s, inside (8.4 s, 11.6 s). The guardian's own 10 s caller is deliberately excluded from the derivation: its fall-through is to ask the person, not to fail.
- `askRouteJudge` / `confirmRouteWork` now carry `routeRaceWindow` (20 s) and `routeRaceConfirmWindow` (30 s), the same windows their pre-turn twins have always had.

## Laws

- `internal/session/loop_speed_test.go` — the runtime gate. Every reading made three seconds slow; both figures asserted in milliseconds over a twelve-step turn that crosses a mark. Plus the quality half: a recall landing before the first word is re-asked and the answer carries the memory; one landing after it rides the next step and is named late; a mark's drawing cuts the step it rides beside.
- `internal/session/sidecar_law_test.go` — the structural gate (`go/ast`, so it runs on the laws job). The watched set is **derived from the tree**, not a list of three names: every selector called inside a `readBeside` ask is a reading, and every reading must reach the work through the one door. The waiting verb is named `takeAtTheEnd` — the name IS the law — and the same property is pointed at it, so `readBeside(ctx, …).takeAtTheEnd()` inline is refused rather than being a back door that restores the 4.3 s gate. The exemption is a **property, not a list of places**, and it is scoped to the *branch*, not the function: a reading may be awaited only where control is committed to handing the turn somewhere else, because only then is there no next step to apply it to. All three violating shapes are planted in the test and the law is shown naming each one.

## The journal

One `pace` line per turn: `sendMs`, `firstWordMs`, `stepGapMs`, `steps`, and which readings were in flight beside the work. The last audit had to reconstruct those by subtracting request stamps out of `calls.jsonl`, which is how a four-second gate in front of every message went unnoticed for as long as it did.

## The same law read from the other end: a slow listener never holds the turn either

L2's review of #870 found the seam from the far side of this law. `defer phase.done()` at the exit of **every** model call posted the phase down the caller's own stack — `postPhase` → `session.forwardPhase` → `postPhaseNews` → `internal/tui3`'s reader → `p.Send(phaseNewsMsg{})`, and Bubble Tea's `msgs` is **unbuffered**. So the engine goroutine paid a whole Update-and-View cycle before it got its own call back, on every call and not only cancelled ones.

Both news doors (`postPhaseNews`, `postLaneNews`) said in their own doc comments that they never block on a slow reader, and both of them did. They leave the news on a **`desk`** now — the same file and the same law as `readBeside`, read with the producer and consumer swapped: one goroutine per desk at a time, started by the telling that finds it empty and returning when it is empty again, **order kept, nothing coalesced and nothing dropped**. A phase is a state and a latest-wins slot would serve it; lane news is a ledger, and a dropped row is a request nobody can count again — so one honest queue serves both rather than two mechanisms with two ideas of what may be lost.

`internal/provider` needs no change: its own header already names the division ("the one live reader hands the news to a desk and asks for a frame"), and the reader it has is this package's.

Guarded both ways: `TestASlowListenerNeverHoldsTheTurnThatIsTellingIt` stages a listener as slow as every other auxiliary and asserts the same two figures (verified red without the desk — the turn does not merely miss the bound, it stops finishing); `TestAListenerIsAlwaysToldFromADesk` is the structural half on the laws gate.

## Exit settles what it owes

`Agent.Close` now calls `a.SettleWrites()` beside `a.settleDeliveries()`, **before** the `a.mu` it takes (after the lock it would deadlock — `SettleWrites` waits on writes that take that lock, and its doc states the law), and once more at the end for what the close itself sets in motion.

title: Nothing auxiliary blocks the person: one reading beside the work, never in front of it

body:
## The measurement

Two chat turns on 2026-09-10 ended with `decode stream: context canceled` and
then went quiet. Reading the transcripts back, the cancel was not the cause but
the person giving up:

| | conv `b8f5f40f` | conv `f115f3af` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ask` put to the person | 14:46:37Z | 16:51:17Z |
| they typed instead of pressing a key | 14:54:27Z, landing `waiting for the running step` | — |
| the turn was cancelled | 14:54:29Z | 16:53:40Z |
| requests to the model in between | **none** | **none** |

Seven minutes and fifty-two seconds of a person's own sentence sitting in a
queue, then Escape — which dropped it, because a drain must never resurrect a
stopped turn.

## Why

`ask` parks the turn on the person. A parked ask had exactly two endings —
**answered**, or its own lane **let go** — and typing a sentence instead of
pressing a key was neither. The words went down the splice (`Agent.Steer`),
found no generation to cut and no command to adopt, and queued for the next step
boundary. The running step was the question. The turn waited for a tool that was
waiting for the person, and the person had already spoken.

Reproduced as a test before anything was changed: no request ever follows the
steer.

## The change

A parked ask has **three** endings now, and they live in one type with the rule
in it — `internal/session/askwait.go`, replacing a bare `map[uint64]chan Answer`
that was parked in one file, delivered to in a second, counted in a third and
enumerated in a fourth:

- **answered** — they chose; the lane reads an `Answer`.
- **talked past** — they said something else; the lane reads a closed channel,
  the one shape that cannot be mistaken for a choice they made.
- **let go** — the lane itself stopped waiting.

The splice takes the third. The question comes off every surface reading
`you said something else instead`, the person's own line is marked
`took this instead of the question`, the model is told in as many words that
nobody answered and that their sentence is the next thing it will read, and no
decision is recorded. **There is no resume branch**: the turn goes back round
`runTurn`'s own loop, through the same drain and the same send every other step
uses.

And the close-out of a cancelled race is off the person's path.
`hedgeRace.abandon` answered its caller only after draining its arms for up to
`abandonGrace` — a whole second, the whole of `lane.SpokenWithin`, spent in
front of somebody who had just typed a correction. The drain, the offer's
withdrawal and the money are `hedgeRace.accountForTheAbandoned` now, on a
guarded goroutine nobody waits on.

## Proof

| Law | Where |
| --- | --- |
| the next request is on the wire within `lane.SpokenWithin` of the steer, carrying their words | `TestASteerAtAnOpenQuestionPutsTheNextRequestOnTheWireAtOnce` |
| the model reads that nothing was chosen, and no decision is recorded | same |
| the question is withdrawn with their own act as the reason | `TestAQuestionThePersonSpokePastIsWithdrawnWithTheirOwnAct` |
| an answered question is untouched — the three endings stay three | `TestAnAnsweredQuestionIsUntouchedByTheTalkedPastRoad` |
| one sentence retires every question standing at once | `TestOneSentenceRetiresEveryQuestionStandingAtOnce` |
| a cancelled race answers at once and accounts behind the caller | `TestACancelledRaceAnswersAtOnceAndDrainsItsArmsBehindTheCaller` |

The first three and the last fail on `dev` and pass here.

Manual: `internal/manual/chat/questions.md` — the claim that "what you type is a
message to the conversation and the question waits" is gone, and there is a new
section in the asker's own words. `PERF.md` records that the cancelled call's
close-out has left the request path.

## Against the architecture bar

- **One abstraction**: `askedOfThePerson`. Anything that parks a turn on a
  person — a consent request, a landing, a standing card — has the same shape
  and could be moved onto it; they are deliberately not moved in this PR,
  because each means something different by silence.
- **Deleted**: the raw `Agent.askWaits` map and its four hand-rolled
  delete-then-touch sites; the blocking drain in `hedgeRace.abandon`, and the
  stale reason beside it in `spokenWaitExceptions`.
- **No new numbers.** Nothing here has a threshold, a timer or a retry.

## The defect

A quick task is checked by nobody, so `newQuickSpec` leaves its acceptance **empty on purpose** — a "DONE WHEN" with no reader is a contract that is not one (`docs/design/quick-task/DESIGN.md`). The checkpoint's validator asked *every* node for one, and its refusal is whole-document by design. So **one quick task anywhere in a conversation's history threw the entire task graph away on the way back in**: every finished row, every piece of running work, the whole family — gone, and one line in a log file saying the checkpoint was corrupt.

Found on a real checkpoint — four `quick` nodes with `"acceptance": ""` beside three ordinary ones. With this change that file decodes and rehydrates to all 7 nodes, kinds, states and family intact.

## What was true, and what is true now

**Was:** a node with no acceptance is a half-written record, so the file it is in was not written by this code and is refused whole.

**Now:** whether a node owes an acceptance is a **property of its kind**, declared once in `kindsWithoutAcceptance` beside the kinds themselves and read through one rule, `acceptanceHolds(kind, acceptance)` — by the validator, and by a law test that walks the builders. `newQuickSpec`'s deliberate blank and the store's refusal can no longer drift apart, which is the whole of how this happened. No placeholder string was invented for a quick node.

The rule stays **exactly as strict** for ordinary work, for a subharness design and for a subharness run: each of those fills an acceptance, and a record without one is still refused whole.

## The second half: a queued quick node

Making these documents load meant a quick node that was *waiting its turn* would come back on the frontier — and `runTaskNode` dispatches on `taskSpec.quick`, the list the `items` tool ticks while the node runs, which is **not on the record**. That node would have been handed to an ordinary worker: a copy of the folder, a branch and a check, spending real money on work whose whole promise was that it had none of those. It settles instead, saying `the quick task never started before aforge closed, and it does not resume — ask for it again`. `nothingIsComingBackForIt` is where that lives, one named predicate, so `rehydrate` gained no branches and the complexity ratchet holds.

## Tests

- `TestAQuickTaskComesBackFromTheCheckpoint` — end to end through the real door: chat calls `quick_task`, a real worker ticks an item and answers, the checkpoint is written, and it loads and rehydrates. Fails without the fix with the exact defect line.
- `TestACheckpointFromAConversationThatRanQuickTasksDecodes` — the real file's shape: four finished quick nodes with `"acceptance": ""` beside ordinary work with a parent and an edge, plus a queued quick node that must settle.
- `TestOnlyAQuickNodeMayCarryNoAcceptance` — the strictness stays: ordinary, harness and subharness records with no acceptance are still refused.
- `TestEveryKindsAcceptanceMatchesWhatItDeclares` — the anti-drift law: every builder's spec either fills an acceptance or its kind declares it carries none.

## Manual

`tasks.md` gains *A quick task after a restart* (what comes back per state, and that an empty column was a fault that is fixed), the restart section stops implying rows can vanish, and `how-tasks-run.md`'s row 5b names the quick exception. Four probes added.

## Scope

The record's own shape — carrying a quick node's line, items, ticks and files so a queued one can resume as a quick node — is **deliberately not here**; lane Q (`speed/ts-Q`) owns it and merges this branch first. Hunks Q will touch: `nothingIsComingBackForIt` (its queued clause becomes "…and the list is not on the record"), `quickReportOnClose`, `interrupt`'s quick branch comment, `restoreNode`'s spec literal, `recordLocked`, and the *Still waiting its turn* bullet in `internal/manual/chat/tasks.md`.

body:
A task room can draw a worker's call — thinking, tokens climbing, seconds since
it went out — and nothing else. A division, a sizing pass, a mark being read are
each one call through `callRole`, and every one of them draws a blank line while
it runs: measured between 12 and 219 seconds on 2026-09-10, which is
indistinguishable from a process that has stopped.

## What this adds

```go
func provider.WithCallProgress(ctx context.Context, watcher CallWatcher) context.Context
```

`CallProgress` carries the model, the machine that answered, which concurrent
request it is, when it went out, when the first token landed, the visible and
hidden counts, the phase (`started` · `paced` · `thinking` · `writing` ·
`ended`) and, on the last report, how it ended (`answered` · `cut` · `refused` ·
`cancelled`).

## Where it is fed from

Nowhere new. Every streamed reading in this process is already folded into the
hazard controller's watch (`armwatch.go`), where the tokens, the first token,
the heartbeats and the silences are counted for the waiting policy; and every
attempt's two ends are already written down by the model-call log's only writer
(`calllog.go`'s `Client.record`), under a law kept by a `defer` no path can
return past. This forwards what those two places know. There is no second
decoder and no second count of anything, and a `go/ast` law test fails the build
the day one appears.

A race reports each arm under its own `Attempt`; the arm that loses reports
`cancelled` from the race's own cancel site, which is the only place in the
process that knows the difference between exhaust and failure.

## The pacing park is a phase, not a second channel

`dispatch.go`'s three open-coded pacing sites collapse into one `park(bool)`
closure that flips the older `WithPacingNotice` bool and the `CallPaced` phase
together, so the two cannot disagree. `WithPacingNotice` survives only as the
door `internal/session` still calls; retiring it is one line there.

## Proof

- `TestAWatchedCallReportsGoingOutWritingAndAnswering` — scripted router, three
  router comment lines, a first word at 200 ms, forty tokens at forty a second:
  the watcher sees the request go out with no first token, the first token at the
  scripted moment and not at a heartbeat, a count that never goes backwards, the
  forty deltas coalesced, and `answered` carrying the final count and the machine.
- `TestAnAnswerThatStopsHalfwayIsReportedCut` — the connection goes away under
  the answer (new `lanestub.Profile.TearAfter`, the one ending the existing knobs
  could not stage) and it reads as `cut`, not as an answer and not as a cancel.
- `TestEachArmOfARaceIsWatchedAndTheLoserIsNotAFailure` — two arms, two
  `Attempt`s, one `answered` and one `cancelled`, and never both on one arm.
- `TestTheBeatHoldsAFastStreamToTenReportsASecond` — a hundred deltas over a
  scripted second draw ten reports.
- `TestTheCallProgressSeamHasOneFeeder` — the `go/ast` law above.

No person-facing string, key, command or tool changed, so the chat corpus is
untouched. `PERF.md` names no cap this changes.

`docs/design/prompt-diet/BENCH.md` §1a landed with #844 saying **two** subtests regressed on the prompt diet. One did. The page was written while its own confirmation runs were still in flight and merged with the draft's wording; the repeats came back afterwards and said something different.

### What the landed page gets wrong

**`TestTUIE2E/space_in_the_task_room_pages_the_card` was flake**, not a regression — 2/2 pass a side on rerun. Its one red was the model taking a slow road on a nondeterministic flash model: the task landed `your call · ran 2m 8s` where the baseline's landed `done · ran 10s`, so two 30-second waits blew before the paging assertion was ever reached. Anyone acting on the draft would have spent a day hunting a behaviour change that never happened.

**The `· you ·` "elsewhere in the dump" does not exist.** That match was the test's own error text — `the screen never said " · you · "` — counted as though it were screen content. The screen carries `· another window ·` twice and `· you ·` nowhere. This makes the finding *stronger*: there is no frame race, the word was simply wrong.

### What was real, and where it is not

`TestQuestionsE2E/TheOrdinaryRoadCarriesAQuestionAndItsAnswer` **was** a genuine regression on `prompt-diet/integrate` at `2a90be7e8` — 3/3 fail there against 3/3 pass on the `dev` baseline at `6aa6a946e`, the same assertion and the same wrong word each time, on the attribution of an answer the person gave in their own window.

**It is not on the trunk.** The same subtest against `dev` at `c9f24f2b6`, after the wave merged as #844, passes **3/3**. It was fixed before the merge landed, so this is a record of what the bench caught and where — there is nothing to fix in the code, and no action is owed beyond this page.

### Why the page says so itself

Both errors came from reading a grep count instead of the lines it matched — the same shape as the 94%-cut figure §1b already records one layer up, where a median over every request measured the mix of call kinds rather than the size of the prompt. §1a now carries its own account of what it got wrong, beside §1b. A bench whose corrections live only in a changelog is a bench whose next reader repeats them.

### Evidence

On the Spark: `~/bench-diet-out/repeat-{taskroom,askroad}-{dev,diet}-{1,2}.log` (the repeats), `~/bench-diet-out/devnow-askroad{,-2,-3}.log` (3/3 against `dev` at `c9f24f2b6`).

Docs only — no code changes, no test changes.

body:
R3 (#858) left four rows open in `docs/design/recovery/DESIGN.md` §7. This closes them.

**1. The relaxation ladder asks `control.Next` for its rung.** `endpoints.go`'s `for _, step := range c.relaxationPlan(...)` was the seventh of the eleven budgets §2 counts — a private length, under a deadline that could not see it, beside a move generator that already knew the rungs. `recoverFromRefusal` is `dispatch.go`'s now: it asks `Next`, records the `MoveShape` on the same move log the machine walk writes into, and stops at the plan's deadline. `relaxationPlan` stays as the DATA (`Plan.Shapes`). `Plan.ShapeRefused` is the one fact the generator could not work out for itself — "no endpoints found that can handle the requested parameters" answers for every machine the router can see, and such a request's serving set is usually OPEN, which has another machine in it forever.

**2. The race reads the plan's move log.** `hedgeRace.tried` is deleted; the claim, the release and the "where could an arm go now" read all go through `Plan.Moves`, and the machine the primary is about to ask is written on it when the race is built. `MoveLog.Release` is what a shared log needed that a private map had for free. **`maxArms` and `ladderArms` are kept**, with the sentence saying why they are not a retry budget: they bound how many copies of one question are in flight AT ONCE — money and concurrency, Dean & Barroso's tail-at-scale rescue — never how many times it may be asked again.

**And a move is written against the machine that ANSWERED, never the one the body asked for.** `provider.order` is advisory once `allow_fallbacks` is on (R1, #850), so a call that demands DeepInfra and is refused by Parasail has sent nothing to DeepInfra. Leaving the head's claim on the log told `Next` that the one machine we actually wanted had been tried, on the evidence of a machine we never demanded, and the call ended one attempt in with somewhere perfectly good left to go — which is exactly what #859's `TestTheMachineThatAnsweredIsVetoedAndTheOneWeAskedForIsNot` caught on the rebase. The dispatcher gives that claim back through `MoveLog.Release` and writes the pool that really refused in its place.

**3. `response.attempts` scales the deadline instead of counting sends.** `taxonomy.Limits.TransportAttempts` and `DefaultTransportAttempts` are deleted; `Limits.Patience` multiplies `lane.Role.GiveUp` (default 1.0 → today's 90 s talk deadline; `3` → 270 s), published through the one door `lane.UsePatience` from where the profile is resolved. `transportBudget` keeps an allowance only for a cut stream; an ordinary failure asks again for as long as the caller has and says `Evidence.OutOfTime` when it does not — deliberately not `Evidence.Spent`, which claims no shape of the request could be served.

**4. The session's ladders read the same bound, and the laws reach `internal/session`.** The turn loop, the empty-200 re-ask, the errand's rungs (`errandTriesPerRung` deleted) and the naming ladder (`titleAttempts` deleted). The allowlist beside the two new laws is the deliverable as much as the code: five functions and seven constants, each with the line that says what it counts instead of tries. A repair round is not a retry — it sends the model's own bad answer back, which is a different request.

Two things the fold needed and did not have, both in the code with the argument:

- **A failure that asks for no wait still pays one after the first.** Rotation mends an empty 200 at once — kept for the first — but a ladder bounded by a deadline that pays nothing between two requests sends as fast as an endpoint can fail.
- **Whether there is time to ask again is part of the reading.** A ladder that paid its wait and came back to find the give-up gone would give up silently with a chain the person configured unasked (#794's failure).

Manual, `PERF.md` and `DESIGN.md` §7 in the same change: four person-facing numbers were false after this ("up to six attempts or two minutes", "60 attempts or 10 minutes", "three naming attempts", "the three retries a real provider error gets") and `lanes.md` gains the page that says what `response.attempts` means now and what it will never buy.

## dev is red every night between 00:00 and 01:00

`TestTheGreetingsFirstFrameCarriesTheSpend` arrived with #842. It writes the spend row it means to be **today's** at `now.Add(-time.Hour)`:

```go
{At: now.Add(-time.Hour), USD: 1.25, ...},   // "today"
{At: now.AddDate(0, 0, -3), USD: 2.00, ...}, // three days ago
```

An hour before now is **yesterday** for the first hour of any day. So the greeting reads today as `0`, the assertion wants `1.25`, and the test fails — then passes again after 01:00, which is exactly the shape that gets written off as a flake.

Confirmed on a clean `origin/dev` at 00:32 local:

```
--- FAIL: TestTheGreetingsFirstFrameCarriesTheSpend
    home_test.go:1818: the greeting read today 0 and the fortnight 3.25,
                       want 1.25 and 3.25 before the first beat
```

## The fix

Date the row `now`. The current instant is the only time that is always inside today. One line, plus a comment saying why, so the next person does not reintroduce the hour.

`make test PKGS=./internal/tui3 TEST_FLAGS='-count=1 -timeout 15m'` — green.

## One pre-existing red this PR does not touch

`internal/tui3` also fails on **`TestADecayedBeliefDrawsNoTail`** (`lanewalk_test.go:237`), which fails identically on a clean `origin/dev@84bf71d61` with no change under it:

```
lanewalk_test.go:237: a decayed belief has tail 212.71993655648728 (vague=false)
```

It sets `old.At = time.Now().Add(-24 * time.Hour)` — the real wall clock — and then reads the view at `timeNow()`, the fixed test clock. Once real time drifts past that fixed date the belief is no longer 24 hours old relative to it, and the decay never fires. **Same family, different lane**, so it is left for its owner rather than bundled here; this PR is deliberately one commit.

## Why this is worth its own PR

It is offered separately from #861 so the nightly red stops whatever order things land in. #861 carries the same commit.

This is the third fixture on this work to fail with no change under it — #759's legacy cache aged past its TTL overnight, this one crosses midnight, and the decayed-belief test above mixes two clocks. **A test whose result depends on the wall clock reports the calendar.** A small structural law refusing wall-clock freshness in a fixture would catch all three; happy to write it if wanted.

body:
Closes #860. Two `internal/tui3` reds on a clean `dev`, filed together because
they arrived together and fixed together because each is a two-line story.

## The tail — `TestADecayedBeliefDrawsNoTail`

`laneViews` decided a belief had aged past saying anything about its worst case
by catching the **overflow**: before #852 a lane nobody had heard from since
yesterday had a p99 of `+Inf`, and `laneTail`'s `IsInf` arm refused it.

#852 put `lane.MaxSpread` under `Posterior.Predict` — explicitly *"a floor under
the arithmetic and not a judgement"*, so the one unbounded expression in that
package cannot reach a number no reader of it can hold. The clamp is right. What
it took away was the row's crutch: the same yesterday-old belief now arrives at
exactly that ceiling, where σ ≈ 2.4 makes the p99 `212.7` — a couple of hundred
times the median, perfectly finite, under `provider.WallCeiling`, and still
arithmetic rather than a measurement. So the row drew `tail 212.7s`.

`laneTailOf` asks the **belief** instead of the symptom: a spread that has
widened as far as it is allowed to widen draws nothing at all — not a figure and
not `no tail`, which is a claim about the worst case too. `laneTail` keeps its
own arithmetic gate unchanged and is still exercised directly by the test.

## The greeting — `TestTheGreetingsFirstFrameCarriesTheSpend`

Not a regression at all. The test wrote its ledger line an hour before a real
`time.Now()`, and `today` is a calendar day in the person's own zone
(`session.SpendToday`). So the test was green for twenty-three hours a day and
red for the hour after midnight — on any machine, and on CI between 00:00 and
01:00 UTC. It was found red at 00:50 EDT and is red at `c0b204151` (#842, where
it landed), at `baf559e95` and at `dev` alike, if you run it in that hour.

The surface's arithmetic is right on both sides of midnight, so **the code does
not move**. The lab grows a pinned clock (`homeLab.pin`, midday of the day it is
asked for) and the test writes its fixture against that. Verified green at
`23:52`, `00:52` and `04:52` local.

## Proof

- `internal/tui3` in full on the Spark, `-count=1`.
- The two named tests green across a sweep of zones putting the wall clock
  either side of midnight.
- Nothing added to `.github/known-red.txt`; that ledger only shrinks.

body:
## What this is

A vendor can sell the same models twice: a subscription at a fixed price, and metered credit, behind one key. aforge now tries the subsidised door first, because somebody who bought a subscription meant to use it, and falls back to pay-as-you-go when there is no subscription. And a person whose only key is a direct vendor's can now use aforge end to end: one connect, the conversation moves onto the service, the turn runs without an OpenRouter key.

Built on #800 (merged as 6a3b478cf). Verified by hand against a real Z.ai Team Plan key, every request through a TLS-terminating recording proxy so the two Z.ai doors (one host, two paths) could be counted separately.

## What is now true

**A service has ordered billing doors.** Z.ai: `coding plan` at `/api/coding/paas/v4`, then `pay-as-you-go` at `/api/paas/v4`. Connect probes them in order with the cheapest documented model and binds the first that answers; the connect line names the door: `· z-ai-direct is connected · coding plan · 4 models`. MiniMax ships as one door because nothing on the wire tells its plan from its metered balance, and a label about money we cannot check is worse than none.

**A spent window is proof, not refusal.** An exhausted plan binds the plan door and pauses; it never walks, hedges or retries to the metered door. The per-service setting `when the plan is paused` defaults to `wait`; an absent or unrecognised value reads as `wait`; `use pay-as-you-go` lets one turn move there, and the status line names the door while it does. Zhipu's numeric codes decide before phrases, so `1316` ("Insufficient balance for extra usage") is a pause, not "the account cannot pay".

**The plan catalog is the four documented ids**, not the ten the plan host lists.

**A direct service is never chased for an OpenRouter receipt.** A stream ending without its usage block used to fire `GET /generation` at the vendor with Go's default User-Agent and book the call `unbilled`. `settle` returns early for a direct client, and one `applyRequestIdentity` stamps every request `aforge`.

**A region is a choice, not a typed answer.** Z.ai, Moonshot and Qwen ask with two rows (International preselected, arrows, Enter, Esc, first letter jumps). The `your region` box and the `pick one of` sentence are gone. The Providers sheet, which could open this entry but never drew it, now draws it.

**A colliding name connects on the first attempt.** `z-ai` is an OpenRouter author, so the service is stored as `z-ai-direct`; the flow now does that in the same attempt instead of refusing and asking for region and key again.

**A conversation on a connected service sends its turn with no OpenRouter key.** The Enter gate used to open the OpenRouter setup whenever the default key was absent. Now it opens only when the conversation has nowhere else to run, and every crew seat that would resolve to the default service falls to the seated model on the seated service for that turn, through the existing client doors (no second road). With the default key present nothing changes.

**Connecting a service moves the conversation onto it** at once, and says so the way disconnect does: `· this conversation was on ~deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-latest · it is now on z-ai-direct/glm-5.3`. The preferred model is one rule: a plan door's first documented model, else the row's `Preferred`, else the first listed. A running turn is not moved under; the move applies when it ends. It persists like a `/model` choice.

**aforge identifies as aforge.** No borrowed user agent, no impersonation of a supported client.

## Validation contract

| behaviour | test |
|---|---|
| plan accepts → binds the plan door, the turn lands there | `TestAPlanKeyBindsToThePlanDoor` |
| no-plan code → falls back, the plan host gets no turn | `TestAKeyWithNoPlanFallsBackToPayAsYouGo` |
| every door refuses → the existing cannot-pay outcome | `TestEveryDoorRefusingIsStillCannotPay` |
| a bad key stops at the first door | `TestABadKeyDoesNotWalkEveryDoor` |
| window spent, `wait` → paced, metered host receives nothing | `TestAnExhaustedPlanWaitsAndSpendsNothing` |
| opt-in → metered receives it and the line says so | `TestOverflowGoesToTheMeteredDoorAndSaysSo` |
| only an explicit reconnect rebinds | `TestOnlyAnExplicitReconnectRebindsTheDoor` |
| a one-door service is unchanged | `TestAOneDoorServiceIsUnchanged` |
| every documented code decides from the code, not the phrase | the `internal/paymentrefusal` table |
| a direct cut stops at its completion; OpenRouter still chases | `TestContracts1And3ADirectCutStopsAtItsCompletion`, `TestContracts2And4AnOpenRouterCutChasesAnIdentifiedReceipt` |
| a regioned service asks with a choice; walks, takes, backs out; a letter picks | `TestARegionedServiceAsksWithAChoiceAndNotABox`, `TestTheRegionChoiceWalksTakesAndBacksOut`, `TestALetterPicksTheRegionAndTypesNowhere` |
| the chosen region is the one the connection uses; unregioned services unchanged; Providers sheet the same | `TestTheChosenRegionIsTheOneTheConnectionUses`, `TestASourceWithoutRegionsOpensItsOwnBoxAsBefore`, `TestTheProvidersSheetAsksWithTheSameChoice` |
| a colliding name connects first time under the suggested name; models and reconnect keep it | `TestACollidingServiceNameConnectsOnTheFirstAttemptUnderTheSuggestedName`, `TestACollidingServicesModelsUseTheSuggestedName`, `TestReconnectingACollidingServiceKeepsTheFirstSuggestedName` |
| a turn on a connected service sends with no default key; the default service still opens setup | `TestATurnOnAConnectedServiceSendsWithNoDefaultProviderKey`, `TestATurnOnTheDefaultServiceStillOpensSetupWithNoDefaultProviderKey` |
| crew seats and child agents fall to the seated model; keep the default when its key is present | `TestACrewSeatFallsToTheSeatedModelWhenTheDefaultServiceHasNoKey`, `TestAChildAgentFallsToTheSeatedModelWhenTheDefaultServiceHasNoKey`, `TestACrewSeatKeepsTheDefaultServiceWhenItsKeyIsPresent` |
| direct-only `/status` `/cost` `/model` invent no OpenRouter usage | `TestDirectOnlyCommandsInventNoDefaultProviderUsage` |
| connecting moves the conversation onto the preferred model; deferred under a turn; persists | `TestConnectingAServiceMovesTheConversationOntoItsPreferredModel`, `TestAConnectDuringATurnMovesTheModelWhenTheTurnEnds`, `TestTheMovedModelIsTheOneTheNextLaunchOpensOn` |

The two-host tests drive real `session.Agent`s and assert which host received the turn with which bearer; the direct-only tests stand a recording server in for the service and an OpenRouter address that fails the test if touched.

## Hand-verified, live, on the pushed tip

No OpenRouter key, fresh profile, real Z.ai Team Plan key: one connect lands on the three lines above with the status line already on `z-ai-direct/glm-5.3`; `hello` answers in 5.5 s with no setup screen; a tool-calling turn works; 22 of 22 requests to Z.ai on the coding path, zero on the metered path, zero receipt lookups though six streams ended without usage, every request `User-Agent: aforge`; `/cost` shows tokens and calls and no dollars; restart keeps everything; disconnect erases the key and Z.ai receives nothing after it.

## Not in this PR

Only one "Something else" service at a time; the `/connect` filter box drawing typed text unmasked; a "Something else" service at a bare IP is named `0` by `modelServiceSlug`; `/status`'s crew row names the configured crew, not the seat that ran; the exhausted-window pause was never provoked live (it spends the owner's quota) and a pay-as-you-go key was not available to observe.

body:
## What this changes

Five of the six changes in `docs/design/routing/ASSESSMENT-20260911.md` (#857). No new machinery: the belief core is untouched, the policy around it is corrected.

1. **A belief-ordered request drops `max_price`** (`provider/lanes.go` `applyLaneChoice`). The ceiling was list × 1.25 and the list price is the cheapest endpoint, so it vetoed every lane more than a quarter dearer before OpenRouter read the order. The sort-word path, where no belief has spoken, keeps it.
2. **λ has a floor** — `lane.UnattendedValue = AttentionValue / 4` in `Lambda()`. A task node was routed at λ = 0: dollars alone, frontier pruned to 1.25× the cheapest. The routing row's `price` word still means zero.
3. **A refusal is evidence.** `Outcome.Refused` feeds a new `Belief.Availability` Beta (five-minute half-life). The chooser divides the perceived wait by `Belief.Serving()`, so a lane refusing four in five is priced at five sends per answer. `Client.refuseLane` tells the belief for every paced or struck lane. Quality is not charged for an answer that never arrived.
4. **The quality gate reads the mean** once a belief carries twelve observations (`qualityBound`), the upper bound before.
5. **A service floor** — 6 s first token, 30 tok/s, half of requests answered, each only on a belief the ledger is sure about (`ignoreSureVariance`) — and it never empties the set.

Owed: censored timing for cut streams (#6 in the doc).

## Proof

Replay bench (`go test -tags replay`, 2026-09-08..10, λ = 90, refusals recorded):

| model | real router mean regret | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| deepseek-v4.1-flash | 31.9 s (622 picks into a pool that 429'd < 5 min ago) | 1.2 s (181; the oracle itself has 265) |
| glm-5.3-flash | 10.1 s | 3.3 s |
| qwen3.8-27b | 4.8 s | 1.0 s |
| deepseek-v4-flash-0731 | 4.9 s | 3.4 s |

New tests: `internal/lane/availability_test.go` (refusal moves availability not quality, five sends per answer, forgetting, a refusing fast lane ranks behind an answering slower one, the gate closes on evidence, the floor and its never-empty rule) and `internal/provider/routing_fastlanes_test.go` (no `max_price` beside a belief order; a paced pool reaches the belief as a refusal). `TestALatencyAskCarriesACeilingDerivedFromTheModelsOwnListPrice` is untouched and still holds for the sort-word path.

Manual: `lanes.md` no longer says work you are not watching is routed on the cheapest machine.

body:
Wave R3 of the recovery design (`docs/design/recovery/DESIGN.md` §4), on top of
#850 #852 #853 #854 #855.

**One `Plan`.** The hazard's `control.Plan` grows into the call's one budget —
`Deadline`, `SpendUSD`, `Moves`, `Model`, `Role`, `Comeback` and the request's
own relaxation rungs. It is built where a plan has always been built
(`lane.PlanFor`) and stamped on the context at `sendShaped`, so a repaired 400,
a retired pin and every rung of the ladder share one deadline instead of each
restarting it. A race stamps its own and every arm inherits that deadline and
that move log, which is what stops two arms demanding one machine.

**One move generator.** `control.Next` is pure and table-tested, and its order is
the rule's order: another machine, the same machine once after the comeback it
named itself when the set is one wide, a relaxed shape one rung at a time, none.
A set nobody named is an OPEN set, not a set of one — the router picks, each body
carries a longer exclusion list than the last, and the deadline is the whole
bound.

**Six budgets deleted.** `retry.go` is `dispatch.go`, and `maxAttempts`,
`rateLimitAttempts`, `patientAttempts`, `watchedPacingBudget`,
`patientPacingBudget` and `freeMoves` are gone with `outOfPatience` and
`patienceOf`. What replaced them is `lane.Role.GiveUp` — `lane.TurnGiveUp` (90s,
measured) scaled by the same patience column the ceiling is scaled by. R4's
recommendation of 30s/2m for the two pacing budgets is superseded: pacing has no
budget of its own now.

**A relayed refusal is a move.** A 4xx carrying `metadata.provider_name` is one
machine's answer about this request; the model's others have said nothing, so it
walks inside the call instead of ending the turn and waiting for the next message
to rotate. A refusal that named nobody is still our own bytes and still goes back
whole; so does anything `sendRepaired` can fix. A second refusal from a machine
already vetoed means the veto changed nothing, and that goes back too.

**The session keeps one decision.** The turn loop takes the same deadline and
tells the boundary a spent one as a spent ladder, so the one classifier still
answers hop-or-end. `errandWalksOn` reads `!evidence.OurBytes && !evidence.Overflow`
and `taxonomy`'s `seamsOwed` is **empty**.

**Acceptance.** `TestTheScreenshotScenarioAnswersThroughTheFourthMachine` —
policy 404, two 429 machines, a healthy fourth: four sends, each machine once,
an ordinal on screen, no router sentence anywhere. `TestOneDeadlineBoundsEverything`
— 300 randomised scripted pools, no call outliving its deadline by more than one
`maxProviderWait`, sends bounded by machines × shapes + 1.
`TestNextNeverRepeatsAMove` over 300 plans. Three go/ast laws on the `laws` gate:
one place sends a completion, no loop outside the dispatcher counts attempts, no
constant in `internal/provider` bounds one.

**What this deliberately did not fold** is written into `docs/design/recovery/DESIGN.md`
§7 rather than left to be discovered: `maxArms`/`ladderArms`, the relaxation
ladder still being `endpoints.go`'s own loop, `taxonomy.TransportAttempts` still
being a count (its honest fold scales the deadline and lives in `internal/config`),
and six session-side ladders that are bounded but do not read the plan.

## What this is

An assessment, not a routing change. Three days of `~/.aforge/logs/calls.jsonl`, a replay of that log through the real `internal/lane` chooser, a recorded request body, and a live probe of every lane the models in use were served by.

**Verdict: update the policy around the belief core, do not replace the core.** Replayed in isolation at λ = 90 with refusals recorded, the chooser's mean regret on deepseek-v4.1-flash is 0.4 s against the real router's 31.9 s.

## The six defects (details and numbers in the doc)

1. `max_price` = list × 1.25 on the wire filters every lane dearer than the cheapest before OpenRouter reads `provider.order`; for deepseek-v4.1-flash that leaves DeepInfra (18 tok/s, 83% 429s). Recorded and reproduced by hand.
2. Task nodes route at λ = 0: price only, frontier pruned to 1.25× the cheapest.
3. A 429 never reaches the belief; the set-empty release sends the next request back to the same pool 2 s later (825 of 1,010).
4. The quality gate tests the upper bound, so it never closes.
5. Cut streams teach no timing (survivorship bias).
6. No absolute service floor; Morph at 27 s first token stays a candidate.

## What is in the change

- `docs/design/routing/ASSESSMENT-20260911.md` — evidence, the six changes, the acceptance bar.
- `internal/lane/replay_bench_test.go` — build tag `replay`; replays a call log through the real ledger and chooser and scores regret against a ±15 min oracle. Not part of any suite.
- `docs/design/routing/probe.py` — the live per-lane probe and the `order`/`ignore`/`max_price` wire tests.

## Gate

Draft: the touched-package suite for `internal/lane` has not been run on Spark yet. No routing code changes; `go build ./...` and `go vet -tags replay ./internal/lane/` pass.

body:
## What

On a conversation running on the workspace engine daemon (every ordinary local launch, and `--host`), the answer the model writes after a task lands never reached the screen once the window had run one turn of its own. The task card said done; the journal had the sentence; the surface drew nothing. Reopening the conversation replayed it. Seen on 2026-09-10 with three quick tasks landing and the replies to `whats up` after them.

## Why

`watchFollowing` and `watchDriving` captured `app.gen` as "the connection this wait belongs to". But `app.gen` is the turn generation and moves on every turn this window runs (`takeStream`, `startFollow`). The first typed turn therefore made the next `Following` fail the check in `followTurn`, which discards it **and does not re-arm the wait**. From then on `Client.follows` drops every wake because nobody is receiving. The keyboard lane (`drivingMoved`) had the same shape.

## Change

- `app.linkGen`: the connection's generation, bumped only where a switch rebinds `app.link` (`detach.go`).
- Both connection waits capture and compare `linkGen`.
- `TestAHostedWakeAfterThisWindowsOwnTurnIsStillDrawn` and `TestAHandOverAfterThisWindowsOwnTurnIsStillHeard` fail on dev and pass here.

No person-facing string changed; no manual change.

## Also seen while diagnosing, not fixed here

- Every turn in that conversation ended ~30 s after its answer because the `markreader` completion read (deepseek-v4.1-flash via Fireworks/Morph) streamed a 200 and never finished inside `checkpointSketchWindow`. The turn's foot reports that as the turn's time.
- A steer typed into a running turn glues its continuation onto the previous reply's text with no boundary (`…containingNot much — …`).

- #855 had just given the steer lane its own conversation generation (`steerGen`) for the same defect one lane over. This PR folds it and `linkGen` into **one** counter, `app.convGen`, bumped where a switch replaces the conversation.
- **Supersedes #699** (same two-lane fix from 2026-09-09, now in conflict with dev). Its manual paragraph on `how-tasks-run.md` rides here; credit to its author for the diagnosis.

body:
## What was wrong

On 2026-09-10 22:39 the owner asked `whats up` three times over a busy conversation and the screen showed none of the answers. The engine had run every one of them: `transcript.jsonl` holds the replies (`Site is live locally at http://localhost:8001`, `All four pages done, consistency pass finished.`), they were paid for, and reopening the conversation shows them. The live window drew nothing.

A correction typed into a running answer that never reached a boundary **falls through**: the engine lifts it onto its own follow-up queue and carries its stream across the seam (`internal/session`'s `liftSteersLocked`). That news reaches the surface on a lane of its own — and it reaches it **late by construction**, because a fall-through is what happens *after* a turn ends, so by the time the lane is read the next turn has usually already begun.

The lane was stamped with `app.gen`, which counts **turns**. It is bumped by every submit, every adopted stream and every drained follow-up. So the stamp was stale exactly when it mattered, `app.steerFell` drained the channel and threw it away, and a whole turn the engine ran, paid for and journaled drew nothing at all: no question row, no reply, nothing.

## The fix

`app.steerGen` is the steer lane's own generation. It moves only when the conversation on screen is replaced (`detach.go`'s list of every lane generation) — which is the question the check actually means to ask: *is the session these words were said into still the one in front of me?*

## Proof

- `TestACorrectionWhoseFallThroughArrivesLateStillDrawsItsTurn` — the replication, through the real door: the lane's command is taken from `app.holdSteer` so the stamp under test is the one the surface really writes, and it is run after another turn has moved `app.gen`. Red on `dev` (the question row and the whole answer are absent), green here.
- `TestTheSteerLaneStampMovesWithTheConversationAndNotWithTheTurn` — the stamp stands still through ordinary turns and moves when the conversation is replaced.
- `TestAHoppedTurnDrawsItsAnswer`, `TestAHoppedTurnDrawsTheCallsItMadeAfterTheHop` — the other road into the same law, pinned: a turn that hopped to a fallback model draws the answer that model wrote, and the calls it made after the hop keep their rows. (Both were already green; they are now pins.)
- `TestAFellThroughSteerIsNotQueuedOntoATurnSomebodyStopped` now builds its message with the lane's own stamp, so the stop is the only reason it can be refused for.

Full `./internal/tui3` on the Spark.
