body:
`docs/design/recovery/DESIGN.md` §7 row R2. A 404 was classified by three
unrelated rules, a prose regex overruled the verdict forty lines after it was
computed, `Verdict` named two types in packages that call each other, the walk
was a prediction with a compensating repair, two mechanisms hopped the model from
one list, and the empty-200 re-ask was a silent second retry road.

## What changed

**One classifier.** The transport states facts and one function turns facts into
a move. `taxonomy.Evidence` grows `Account`, `Withdrawn`, `OurBytes`, `Overflow`,
`Compacted`, `Unserved` and `Spent`, each decided once at the refusal door
(`markRefusal`, `apiError`) and read nowhere else; `provider.Evidence(err)` is the
one extractor and makes no decision. `session`'s `providerCouldNotServe` status
list and the turn loop's `OurRequest()` early return are gone — both read the
verdict.

**A fourth class, `taxonomy.Shape`:** the request is what nothing will serve. Its
moves are `ActionCompact` (it did not fit — once per turn) and `ActionReshape`
(the router read our own bytes). A spent shape ladder is `Evidence.Spent`:
Transport with its budget gone, whose one move is the caller's chain — it used to
be `Work`, the same word a job that could not be done gets, which is how a turn
ended with the router's sentence on screen while a configured chain sat unasked.

**The regex is deleted.** `isContextOverflow` and its seven-branch pattern are
gone; `isRetryable` stays as EVIDENCE for `Evidence.Wire` and decides nothing. An
overflow is structural now — the request-too-large status and the error
envelope's own `code`, with the sentence kept only as a last-resort hint inside
the transport.

**`provider.Verdict` → `provider.Reading`** (one mechanical commit first).
`internal/lane`'s third `Verdict` is `Advice`: the watch advises, the controller
decides.

**`canWalk` → `takeRefusal`, a commitment.** One call, one lock: the race owns
the refusal and either answers it or climbs the ladder it took. `exhausted()` is
the fulfilment of that promise rather than the repair of a wrong guess, and one
handoff per question — a second door climbs itself, because it holds the shape
that was just refused.

**One model hop.** Both adapter walks (`recoverFromRefusal`'s chain and
`recoverFromPacing`) are deleted; the relaxation rungs stay. `nextFallback` reads
`provider.ModelsTried(ctx)` instead of indexing blind. A model the router no
longer carries is remembered for the process, skipped before any send, and taken
off the chain.

**The empty-200 re-ask** emits one `EventRetrying` with its `RetryNews` and
narrates a non-zero wait on the same phase pipe the ladder uses.

## Proof

- `internal/taxonomy/classifier_law_test.go` (go/ast, on the gate):
  `TestOnlyOneVerdictTypeExists`, `TestOnlyTheTaxonomyTurnsAStatusIntoAMove`,
  `TestTheAdapterNeverChangesTheModel`.
- `internal/provider/classifier_e2e_test.go`: five refusals against the real
  router and a real `Client` — an account policy, an emptied list, our own bytes,
  a withdrawn model, a request that did not fit — move, move, change shape, change
  model, compact; plus the remembered model that sends nothing on the second turn.
- Suites run on the Spark, never on the laptop.

body:
Lane R4 of the recovery wave (`docs/design/recovery/DESIGN.md` §7). Two commits: the measurement the owner asked for, and the hole the coordinator found while it was being written.

## Part 1 — how long is long, measured

The owner asked directly: *"see what are good times to wait — is it 10 or 5, or how long, 2 min or shorter."* Answered against 16,427 finished attempts in `~/.aforge/logs/calls.jsonl` (10,028 with a first token) and `usage.jsonl`'s independent `tps`. The full study with every table is in the wave report; the conclusion:

**Ten seconds was already right and was being used for the wrong thing.** A watched turn's first token is 1.6 s at the median, 8.4 s at the ninetieth and 13.1 s at the ninety-fifth, so `lane.VisiblePatience` at 10 s is this build's own ninety-second percentile — where Dean & Barroso's "hedge near p95" and Nielsen's ten-second attention limit meet. Five seconds is worse on both counts: it touches 28.9 % of calls against 13.9 %, *and* rescues fewer per extra send (17.6 per hundred against 22.1), because under ten seconds almost everything still silent is an ordinary call in progress.

So the number does not move. What moves is that **ten seconds is when we ACT and one second is when we SPEAK**, and until now ten seconds was also the first moment anybody heard anything.

Confirmed and unchanged from the data: every role `Patience` multiplier (each is a percentile of its own roles' first tokens), `firstDeltaBound` 90 s (96 % of calls whose first token came after 90 s still answered cleanly), `midStreamGapBound` 45 s, `streamWallFloor` 5 m, `streamWallCeiling` 20 m (zero clean streams reached it; the longest was 12 m 04 s).

## Part 2 — every wait spoken, no self-inflicted cuts

- **`lane.SpokenWithin` (1 s)** and **`lane.TurnGiveUp` (90 s)** are new, each stated with its measurement. 66 % of the retry chains that recovered in ten days had landed inside 90 s, and 126 of the 167 winners used two distinct machines.
- **The limiter's slot queue speaks.** A burst of rate limits halves the process-wide ceiling and every other call parks there *before* its request is on the wire; it now posts `connecting` within a second, with no countdown, because nothing knows when a slot comes free.
- **A connection wait draws a countdown** to the moment it really ends (`connectionRecoveryWindow`), instead of posting a zero.
- **A law test** (`go/ast`) fails any `select` on a timer in `internal/provider` with no phase in the same function. Three exceptions are named, each with the sentence that says why nobody is waiting on it.
- **`deadline_ms` stops being fiction.** The row now carries the bound that *really* ended an attempt beside the hazard's *planned* one — two questions, two fields.
- **A losing arm of a race is exhaust, not failure** (`cancelled: lost the race`), so a census stops counting 1,204 won races as the largest failure family in the log.
- **The wire is forgiven three times doubling from one second**, down from four and two.

### The census correction

`census-20260910.md` §8 finding 1 attributes 869 `decode stream: context deadline exceeded` rows at exactly 60 s and 90 s — 780 with a first token already taken — to the stream wall. **It is not the wall and it is not in `internal/provider` at all.** `clientFor` already gives a stream `Timeout: 0`, `attemptContext` gives it a cancel and never a timeout, and every bound in `streamguard.go` announces itself as a `StreamCut` with its own sentence rather than as a context error. Those deadlines belong to the caller. What this package owed was the honest record, and three tests now pin the removal so it cannot be undone by somebody restoring a sensible timeout.

## Part 3 — the ceiling that fired and did nothing (second commit)

Acting on a silence meant *hedging*; hedging is purse-gated; so when the purse was empty the ceiling fired and **nothing happened**. 2,186 attempts are in that state and 648 of them ran past six times the silence that had just been refused — p99 272 s, worst case 938 s. Four quick tasks on 2026-09-10 sat on one machine for 260, 370, 375 and 428 seconds before its first token, all past a ceiling that had already fired.

A hedge is the paid way to act; a cut is the free way. **The ceiling now picks one of them and never neither** — but only on a dead wire, and the discriminator is measured: of those 2,186, `drift` ended cleanly 92 % of the time and `ceiling` 75 % (cutting those would throw nine calls in ten away), while `no heartbeat` — not a token, not even a router comment — ends cleanly 31 % against first tokens whose p99 is 505 s.

Two more numbers from the same evening:

- **`bufferedQuietBound` is no longer scaled by the role.** This is why those streams reached six minutes: a task node's 3× made the cap 450 s and a standing pass's 900 s. The first-token and mid-stream bounds are patience and scale rightly; the cap is a measured ceiling on what an *endpoint* may do while keeping its line warm, and a machine does not earn longer because nobody is watching.
- **A late first token from a named machine teaches the ledger again.** The sighting was dropped whenever the act had been charged to the path — but that claim is made from what had arrived at the moment of the act, and a stream that later wrote from a named machine has disproved it. All four streams named their machine and every one was discarded, which is exactly why the sheet went on claiming an eight-second first token.

## Proof

Spark, `internal/provider`, `internal/lane/...`, `internal/taxonomy`, `internal/manual/...`. `make test-laws` green locally. `PERF.md` and `internal/manual/chat/lanes.md` updated in the same commits.

## Seams owed to other lanes

- **R1 (`retry.go`)** — the cut-and-move seam: a `CutSilent` naming its served machine now reaches the attempt loop from a ceiling the purse refused, and the loop should re-ask a *different* machine rather than the same one. Noted in both reports.
- **R2 (`hedge.go`)** — one line at the cancel site: `arm.watch.lostRace()`. The mechanism and its tests are here; without that call the exhaust marking is inert.
- **R0 (`calllog.go`)** — `waitFacts.applied` / `appliedWord` / `exhaust` are the fields to record.

body:
Wave **R0 "see"** of [docs/design/recovery/DESIGN.md](docs/design/recovery/DESIGN.md) §7. Two of that design's twelve problems are that we cannot see, so the first wave is measurement — and the four waves after it each move a number in §1, which is only worth saying if something measures it without being asked.

## The instrument

`cmd/aforge-census` + `make census` reads `calls.jsonl` and prints §1's table as markdown: finishes by status (200-clean / 200+error / 429 / transport / 404 / 400), cause families, the top error signatures under a normalised spelling, the 429 depth histogram, retry chains (tag + node + model, rising attempt, ≤ 15 min gap) with their same-lane share and their ten longest, lane health per (model, **served**) over the recent window, and the checks — every finding of the first census kept as a number a nightly run can move.

Pure Go, no dependencies, tested on a fixture in `testdata/`. `bench/census/README.md` has the Spark recipe (the cron is not set up here and is not this repository's to own; what is here is the target it calls).

Run against the live log it reproduces `docs/design/recovery/census-20260910.md` within noise — same window, 33,735 rows, 75.5 % clean, 54.4 % of multi-attempt chains never leaving the machine they started on, the same three seventeen-deep DeepInfra and Reka chains.

## And the rows it reads are honest now

- **`served`** is the machine that ANSWERED — the stream's own `provider` field, or the one machine a request demanded — and **never** `lane`, which is who was *asked for* and disagreed on 3,728 of 10,107 finishes. Every per-lane belief in the build is keyed on that name, which is how a machine gets struck for another machine's refusal.
- **A failed attempt carries its tokens, its cost and its first token.** 1,884 of 1,887 in-stream failures used to say a cut stream had cost nothing; $201.15 of recorded spend had $0.00 attributed to anything that went wrong.
- **`retry_after`** is recorded on a paced refusal that named one. It was never present on any of 1,106 — so no repeated send could be checked against what the provider itself had asked for, which is the one thing that makes a same-machine retry legal (§3).
- **`deadline_ms` is `hazard_ceiling_ms`**, because it was never a deadline. Nothing ends a call when it passes — it is when a rescue starts being priced — and under the old name the census read 2,720 healthy calls as having run past their own bound.
- **An errand tags its rows with its role**, which is 2,309 of the 2,839 untagged finishes: `internal/session` opens no routing slot, so every naming, captioning and route-judging call landed in the log anonymous.

## `cost_s` is fixed at the source

`Posterior.Predict` doubled variance forever — `2^(dt/10min)`, unbounded — and overflowed to `+Inf` after about seven days of a lane sitting still. `Update`'s gain is `P/(P+R)`, so `+Inf` became `NaN`; `NaN` fails every `> ceiling` test, so nothing repaired it, and the belief file spent days refusing to compact on `json: unsupported value: NaN`. On the way there, a variance of about 673 priced acting at `exp(μ + P/2)` and put **1.99e+146** in the `cost_s` column.

`Predict` is bounded at `MaxSpread`, `Update` treats a belief that is not a number as no belief, `age` clamps unconditionally (it skipped the clamp entirely for every lane the sheet publishes no spread for — precisely the least-known lanes), `control.Measured` answers a non-finite figure as `PastPricing`, and the store drops a value that is not a number rather than the file it is in.

## Acceptance

`internal/provider/calllog_honest_test.go` stages three `lanestub` scenarios: a full pool ranked first and quietly served by the next machine (`lane: A`, `served: B`, and never one filled in from the other); a pool a request DEMANDED refusing with a `Retry-After` (`served: A`, `retry_after: 30`); and a reply that was generated, billed and then judged unusable, whose failure row carries its cost. Plus law tests that the belief store never writes a float that is not a number and that a fortnight of ageing reaches one.

Suites on the Spark, never on the laptop.

body:
Closes #833.

## What was true

Every road that ended a hosted conversation went through one door,
`session retired`, and therefore said one sentence:
`nobody was left watching this conversation, so the reply stopped — ask again to
pick it up`. A person's own goodbye said it, `aforge engine --stop` said it, a
signal said it, a stale build letting go said it, and the idle sweep said it.

And a conversation with no surface attached was unwatched on the instant. A call
that stalled past `internal/remote`'s ten-second `callDeadline` (#832) tears the
window's pipe without the person going anywhere, so the room read as empty a
fraction of a second after they had pressed `1` on a card in it. #833 is that
reply: `bash · cancelled`, and the unattended sentence, on a screen the person
was sitting in front of.

## What is true now

**Presence is renewed by the act itself.** Every call a window makes records the
act — `(*server).dispatch` is the one funnel every keystroke takes — and
`Session.watchedLocked` counts a window that acted inside `watchGrace` as
somebody in the room. The grace is `2 * callDeadline`, derived and never
retyped: one deadline for the call that did not come back, one for the link that
has not been dialled again yet. Both the sweep (`RetireIfIdle`) and the
stand-down reading (`enginehost.Host.idleLocked`, through `IdleSince`) go
through it.

**The door is not disabled.** A room with no surface and no act inside the grace
is still retired, still closed, still flushed — pinned by
`TestAConversationNobodyEverWatchedIsStillRetired` and
`TestAnActThatHasAgedOutStopsCountingAsPresence`, and by every test already in
`internal/remote/idle_test.go` and `internal/enginehost`.

**Every ending names the door it actually came through.** A goodbye
(`MethodClose`) is `conversation left`. A host stopped on somebody's word while a
window is still in the room is a new door, `engine stopped`, with its own
sentence. Only the unattended door says nobody was left watching — and when it
does, the cause carries the window it believed had gone
(`Agent.InterruptNamed`, `stopAs`), so the sentence names it:
`nobody was left watching this conversation from studio, so the reply stopped —
ask again to pick it up`.

The manual page (`internal/manual/chat/models-and-cost.md`) carries all three
sentences and a heading in the words somebody would actually ask.

## Reproduction

`internal/remote/unattended_test.go`, deterministic, no model and no wall clock.
Two of its four tests were red on `dev` and are green here; the other two are the
guards that the door still works.

## Tests

- laptop: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, `make test-quick`,
  `go test ./internal/remote/ ./internal/enginehost/ ./internal/manual/... -count=1`,
  `go test ./internal/session/ -run 'Stop|Resume|Manual|Door' -count=1`
- Spark: the full `internal/session`, `internal/remote` and `internal/enginehost`
  suites, and `TestQuestionsE2E/TheOrdinaryRoadCarriesAQuestionAndItsAnswer`
  six copies in parallel — recorded in a comment below.

The first attempt at this fix was made by the Cursor CLI on Grok 4.6 Fast and
reviewed as a skeptic; what it got right and what was changed on top is in the
lane report.

body:
Wave R1 of `docs/design/recovery/DESIGN.md` §7. It moves two numbers from the census (`docs/design/recovery/census-20260910.md`): the share of multi-attempt chains that never leave the lane they started on (53 %), and the deepest chain of identical sends to one machine (17).

## The measured defect

`internal/provider/retry.go` encoded the request body **once**, above the attempt loop. The body carries `provider.order`, `provider.only` and `provider.ignore`, so every retry re-sent identical bytes to the same machine — `velocity.go` said so out loud: *"the retries of the call that drew the 429 still wait it out, because their body is already written."* Three chains in ten days spent 16 and 17 consecutive sends on one machine over eleven minutes and still ended `429`. Meanwhile GMICloud, which had served the three previous tool calls of the same task in six seconds each, was not a candidate at all, because the fetched sheet marks it `Tools:false` and `lane/frontier.go` gated it out of every tool-carrying request for good.

## What lands

**A body per attempt.** Each attempt of `send` re-encodes through `Client.encodeRequest`, and the machines that have refused *this call* are dropped from the object on the way out (`refusedHere` → `knobs.refused` → `wirePreferences`'s `dropRefusedHere`). A demand is narrowed only while something is left in it; a demand down to its last machine is left alone, which is the one legal same-machine move — and that move waits for the comeback the machine itself named. `Retry-After` is now read out of the **refusal body** as well as the header, because the census found it recorded on not one row in ten days while every fourth failure was a 429.

**One hand-back door.** `retryElsewhere` and `demandedPoolIsFull` (#835) are folded into `Client.handBack`: a strict pin never hands back, a refused demand goes back at once, an account-wide pacing never does, and everything else goes back when the race can fund an alternative.

**The ledger is keyed on who served.** A 429 that names no pool under a demand of exactly one machine is filed against that machine; with nothing demanded it is still filed against nobody. A new structural law, `TestNoLedgerWriteIsKeyedOnTheLaneWeChose`, fails the build the day a ledger write takes a lane we merely chose — the wrong argument compiles, so nothing else would catch it.

**The three configuration gates go.** `velocity.go`'s `c.velocity == nil || !c.carriesPreferences() || routing == RoutingOff` stood on the refusal door and both paces. The ledger always records now; only what is **emitted** from it is configured, and that was already gated at `providerPreferences` and `laneChoiceFor`. A base that is not a router gets a ledger with one row, not no ledger.

**Sheet facts are priors, not gates.** In `internal/lane/frontier.go`, `Tools`, `Uptime5m` and `Status` no longer remove a lane. A doubted lane is ranked behind everything the sheet is happy about (`sheetDoubtsLast`), one request in ten probes it first, and a lane whose own answers have come back usable is not doubted at all — a belief that decays back toward the sheet's prior on `QualityHalfLife` like every other belief there. `Serves` — the wire's own negative — stays the one hard exclusion.

**A blind cut re-asks a different lane.** A stream that died before naming its server is filed against the machine this request *asked for*, which this process wrote itself, so `StreamCut.Rerouted` is true and the one stall shape that could not reroute now does.

## Proof

- `TestRetryNeverRepeatsAMachine` — 200 randomised scripted pools, no call ever sends identical (machine, body) twice while another machine is admissible.
- `TestARefusedMachineIsNotAskedTwiceWhileAnotherIsAdmissible` — three sends, each machine once, answered by the one that had not refused.
- `TestWalkingTheMachinesIsNarratedAsAnOrdinal` — the person reads `2 of 6`; no status code and no `API error` reaches them.
- `TestAPoolOneMachineWideIsReAskedAfterTheWaitItNamed` — exactly one re-ask, after the three seconds it asked for, narrated as paced.
- `TestATaskIsAnsweredByTheLaneTheSheetDoubts` — the screenshot in `lanestub`: a tool-carrying request answered by the `Tools:false` machine, ≤ 4 sends, each machine asked at most once.
- `TestARefusalIsPacedAgainstTheMachineThatServedIt` — a 429 `via DeepInfra` under a choice of `Fireworks` paces DeepInfra.
- Suites run on the Spark, never on this laptop.

**Meanings**
- **D — ↑ is the weight of the request in flight** (`ContextTokens`), not the summed input bill. Re-read off the loop on the usage beat (which now carries `ContextTokens` beside `Usage`); a tool end asks the beat on the next frame. A loop-side `measureContext` outranks a beat that left before it (`ctxSeq`).
- **↓ = billed output + estimate of what arrived since that bill** (`tokenCol.bill`), so it no longer freezes after a bill.
- **↓ counts a call's streamed arguments** (forming bytes / payload).

Closes #839.

## What was true

A contract's addresses were bound to the copy the worker was given for exactly two folders: the node's ground (#566) and the conversation's own `work/` (#804). An address under an **earlier tree of the same conversation** was under neither.

The conversation learns those addresses honestly — the first worker's report names the directory it stood in — so the model that proposes the next piece of work writes `<session>/trees/1/…` into WHAT TO PRODUCE. The worker standing in `<session>/trees/2` followed the address it was given and `taskGroundGuard` answered `is outside your copy` about a directory the harness itself had invented. Under the whole tagged package that fired once in five runs of `TestAWorktreeTaskFollowsItsContractInsideItsOwnCopy`; alone it passed every time.

## What is true now

- `taskCopyFor` reads `Place.Trees()` from the same record the copy was cut from, and `taskCopy.bind` moves another tree of this conversation to the same path under this copy.
- **The ground rule still wins where both could apply.** The sibling rule runs last and only sees what the ground rule left behind. An address already inside this worker's own copy stands as written. A path that is genuinely somewhere else on the machine is untouched and still earns the refusal.
- **`taskoutside.go` is not touched.** #566's guard is unchanged and not widened.
- The brief's copy section states the new mapping — as a rule, not as a headcount, because the document is composed before anybody knows whether this conversation has other copies at all — and `internal/manual/chat/how-tasks-run.md` carries it under a heading in the words somebody would ask.
- **The mode had to move with it.** `groundNamesWorkUnder` read that same address as naming no file under the ground, so `groundMode` made the work a REFERENCE — and a reference binds nothing by law, because its folder is deliberately not a copy of its ground. Naming a file in another tree of this conversation is naming work under the ground, so the task is given a branch of the person's repository and the binding has something to bind to. Provenance does not move: the ground stays the person's repository and the copy stays `trees/<its own id>`.

## Replication and proof

`internal/session/task_contract_sibling_test.go` — `TestASecondTaskIsNotPointedAtTheFirstTasksCopy` cuts two trees for one conversation in the order the tagged package cuts them (the first task settles, then the conversation proposes the second) and asks what the second worker's WHAT TO PRODUCE names. It is red on the first commit of this branch and green on the second. With the bind alone and the mode change reverted it stays red, which is the evidence for the second half.

Also pinned in `task_brief_copy_test.go`: the suffix, the own copy, the trees folder itself, a `trees-old` lookalike, a longer name it is only a suffix of, the ground winning, the legacy layout with no session folder, both spellings of an aliased trees folder, and the sentence the worker is handed.

body:
Closes #832.

## What was true

`internal/remote`'s engine answered every call on one connection strictly in order, on the reader goroutine. A getter that took its time held everything behind it, so a person's keystroke could sit there until `callDeadline` (10s) ran out — and what came back was `the connection to the engine is gone`, about a link that was carrying that turn's events at that very moment, and about an answer the engine went on to apply. `app.answerQuestion` then dropped that error on the floor, so nothing on screen said any of it had happened.

Measured on 2026-09-10: six copies of `TestQuestionsE2E/TheOrdinaryRoadCarriesAQuestionAndItsAnswer` in parallel, one of them ten seconds to the millisecond, the other five one millisecond each. The attribution half — the receipt reading `another window` over a key pressed on that screen — was fixed in #812 (`app.markQuestionSent`). This is the road and the silence.

## What is true now

**The road is classed, not serial.** `internal/remote/callclass.go` holds the one predicate that decides whether `server.invoke` may leave the reader goroutine.

- *Ordered*, and still on the reader in the order the surface sent them: anything that opens a stream or changes the conversation's shape. A stream's first event may not overtake the result frame that names it — `server.pending` is one slot for that reason — and `server.release` now runs only for these.
- *Getters* (`Transcript`, `ListDir`, `FetchFile`, `Ping`, the status-line reads) and a person's *acts* (`ResolveQuestion`, `Consent`, `Take`, `Interrupt`) run off the reader. `server.side` is a `WaitGroup` the serve loop drains before `leave`, so nothing writes into a session that has already closed.
- A method the predicate has not heard of is *ordered* — the allow-list shape `watcherMay` already uses.

The licence for letting a getter or an act overtake an ordered call is stated in the file and is the load-bearing part of the review: **every call on this wire is a synchronous round trip**, so two calls whose order matters were already ordered by their caller, and two made from different goroutines were never ordered by anything. What the reader still owes is the order *within* one call, and that is what stays on it.

**Giving up no longer claims the link is dead.** A deadline that ran out answered with `Client.gone`. It buried nothing — only the reader calls `Client.bury`, on a pipe that actually failed — so the sentence was the whole of the damage, and it was enough. A call that runs out on a live connection now says `<machine> did not answer in time` (`Client.late`); `Client.gone` is kept for a pipe that broke.

**The deadline stays one window, and the branch carries the measurement that says why.** The obvious second half — a longer `actDeadline` for a person's act, since a getter that gives up costs a stale number and an act that gives up costs a decision — was written, measured and taken back out in c8dcd5213. `answerQuestion` asks its door straight from Update rather than from a command, so a 30s act window is 30s a terminal can sit without drawing: eighteen copies of the questions e2e six at a time gave **two 53-second copies against 22 seconds for every other, both losing the receipt**, where twelve copies of this branch's parent gave none over 33 seconds. `callclass.go` and PERF.md both state it, where the next person to reach for that constant will read it.

**The silence is over.** `app.answerQuestion` says the door's own words through `app.note`, the same door every other refused act on this surface uses. The question still stays open — a refusal is not a decision — and the receipt stamped before the door still closes as yours when the engine's news arrives.

**The manual carries both**, and one stale denial is gone: the questions page said a window over `--host` *cannot yet answer* a question. It can, and the ordinary road's own e2e has been proving it.

## Tests

- New `internal/remote/road_test.go`: a fake engine whose `Transcript` is held while a `ResolveQuestion` is sent behind it, asserting the second call returns without waiting out the deadline and without the gone sentence. It fails on the old shape (`the second call did not return; it is waiting behind the getter`), verified by flipping `staysOnReader` to `true`. Beside it, a deadline on a live connection that must not say `gone`, and the class predicate.
- `internal/tui3/question_test.go`: both existing door-refusal tests now pin that the refusal reaches the screen.
- Laptop: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, `make test-quick`, the focused tests with `-race`, `go test ./internal/e2e/` untagged.
- Spark, at c8dcd5213: `./internal/remote/ ./internal/enginehost/ ./internal/pair/... ./internal/relay/ ./internal/furrow/` with `-count=1 -race`, all green; the full `./internal/tui3/` suite; `TestRemoteTwoMachines`, the three-container harness, on real docker — 4 pass, 1 skip, 70s.
- The field acceptance, on the Spark from an isolated clone with `bin/aforge` built there: `TestQuestionsE2E/TheOrdinaryRoadCarriesAQuestionAndItsAnswer`, six copies in parallel, twice — **12/12 with ` · you · ` and no refusal line**, every copy 22–26s.

Three things the prompt-diet wave (#812) left owed, in `docs/design/prompt-diet/BENCH.md` §7 and in lane M's change entry — plus the bench cell that was owed with them, and one rig defect found on the way.

## A `/settings` row for the prompt profile

**What was true:** the profile was derived from the model's context window and from nothing else. There was nowhere to read it and nowhere to correct it — and the derivation is wrong in one recognisable case, an endpoint that reports a window its loaded model does not really have. `AFORGE_PROMPT_PROFILE` was operator plumbing in `OperatorEnvPins`, and `promptprofile.go` and `models-and-cost.md` both said in as many words that there was no settings row.

**What is true now:** `prompt.profile`, under `models` in `/settings` and on tui3's Providers tab beneath `routing`, takes three words — `auto` (the default, which decides nothing and leaves the window to answer exactly as before), `lean`, `full`. The ladder is the pin, then the row, then the window. `AFORGE_PROMPT_PROFILE` still pins for one launch, over the row, and holds the row read-only while it is set — which is why it left `OperatorEnvPins`: it is a row's pin now, not plumbing. The pin and the row share one word list, so a word that is not one of the three is not an answer at all rather than a silent move onto the other arm.

Tests: the row round-trips and honours its pin (`internal/config`), the row outranks the window and loses to the pin, and `auto` renders byte-identically to no row at all on both windows (`internal/session`).

## `ask`'s schema

**What was true:** `ask` is the one verb shelved on a full belt and pre-armed on a lean one, so its schema is what a small model pays for on every request of every turn and what a frontier model never sees. It was 4,277 bytes, thirty percent of the whole lean tool block, and nobody had been through it.

**What is true now:** 3,844. No field left and no enum left. What left is prose saying a field's own name back at the model — `"Block kind"` beside the list of block kinds, `"Subject kind"`, `"Turn waits"`, `"Certainty"` on a low/medium/high enum, and the same six again inside the evidence block, which is spliced into the schema twice — plus the tail of the two long ones. `ask` has no judge paragraph, so nothing was registered in `schemaLawAllowed`.

## The job footer, said once per change

**What was true:** `jobfooter.go` appended one line per outstanding job to **every** tool result while a job was out. A turn with one job out and twenty-one tool results paid for the same three facts twenty-one times; a batch of parallel calls paid for six identical copies inside the same second.

**What is true now:** the footer is appended only when its text differs from the last one this turn sent (`episode.jobFooterChanged`). Nothing is hidden — an identical footer says exactly what the model is already reading further up the same turn, every turn starts with nothing remembered so the first result of a turn with work out always carries it, and the moment a second of elapsed time or a last line or a job moves, it is back. The promise on the page and in the manual was hunted down and made true.

## The bill

| arm | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| full | 38,742 (page 18,807 + tools 19,935) | **38,742**, byte for byte |
| lean | 31,006 (page 16,825 + tools 14,181) | **30,573** (page 16,825 + tools 13,748) |

`leanPrefixBudget` ratchets 32,500 → 31,500, and the ledger in `prefixbudget_test.go` says what paid for it.

## And the bench cell BENCH.md §7 owed

`lean-owed2` at `071d75f2f`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731`, layers A/C/D, against `diet-k` on the same rig and cells. **Parity: yes** — every cell equal, and equal or better against `dev`. **Efficiency per request: yes** — tool block −31.1%, median prompt tokens per turn 13,723 → 12,733 (−7.2%; −28.5% against `dev`). **Per task: no, on this pin** — 19 → 35 turn requests and 84% more spend, because a 128,000-token model does not need sections taken off its page and pays rounds for it. That is the measured argument for `auto` deriving from the window, and §4a says so and says what is still owed: the same cell on a genuinely small window with the profile derived rather than pinned.

**One rig defect fixed on the way.** `bench/prompt-diet/run.sh` assigned its own `CONV_PASS_ENV` flat over the caller's, so §4a's documented lean recipe carried nothing into `bench/conversation` and those cells measured the FULL profile while the e2e cells beside them ran lean. The first run was discarded; §4a has the autopsy.

**And #848 is filed** for the last §7 item, re-aimed: #835 fixed the endpoint hop, so what is left is that a conversation turn ends on a spent provider ladder where a task node with the identical error hops model.

body:
## What

On a bare `aforge` launch, home's first frame drew the `spend` panel as its placeholder line and the head with no `$ / $500`; both filled three seconds later on the first home beat. Captured frame by frame in tmux against a copy of the owner's home: first frame at t, money at t+3.0s.

## Why

`landHome` (the greeting, built before bubbletea exists) took two readings — bands and folders — where `raiseHome` took seven. The ledger read is 26 ms on a 3 MB fortnight; it was simply not asked for on that road. Three lists of "what home reads" existed (`landHome`, `raiseHome`, `refreshHome`) and had drifted, exactly the drift `newHomeView`'s own comment warned about.

## Change

- `newHomeView` is now the one constructor (`raiseHome`'s literal is gone; `claim` and `carrying` moved in).
- `furnishHome` is the one reading list; the greeting, the door and the beat all call it.
- `Init` asks for the card's command readings (repo branch, left-off lines) when home is the first frame, as `raiseHome` does.
- `TestTheGreetingsFirstFrameCarriesTheSpend` pins the panel, the machine's day, and the frame.

No person-facing string changed; no manual change. Launch path gains ~40 ms of reads already paid on the first beat; no catalog read, no unpack.

body:
## The failure

2026-09-10 19:32 EDT, build `839884259`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. A person's turn ended on the router's sentence:

```
· error: API error (404): 0 endpoints out of 1 requested are available matching your
  guardrail restrictions and data policy. … Paid model training violation (account settings) …
```

The wire:
- Arm 1 demanded Fireworks: 404 in 35 ms (the account's paid-training switch).
- The walk demanded DeepSeek: the same 404.
- The walk demanded Io Net: accepted, silent 10 s, then an in-band 429 naming a 74 s wait.

Every arm was dead and nobody had committed. The race settled on the **primary's** 404. The session read a 404 naming no upstream as `work · report · the request itself was refused`, and the turn ended. The ladder that answers this (relax the endpoint filter, let the router choose) never ran: each door that saw the routing refusal predicted the walk would carry it, and the last arm's 429 never reached a door. The same excluded machines were paid for again sixteen hours later in a fresh process.

## What was wrong, and what closes it

Three stacked controllers (race → ladder → session taxonomy) each held their own "is there somewhere left to go", and passed predictions between them instead of facts.

| | Defect | Now |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | The race settled on the primary's error | It settles on the **most actionable** error: an ordinary failure (a 429 with its wait, a 5xx) before a spent ladder before a routing refusal; ties go to the earliest arm |
| D2 | Exhaustion had no owner; `canWalk()` was a prediction | The door writes the hand-off on the race (`deferLadder`). When every arm is dead and nobody committed, **the race runs the deferred ladder itself** as one more arm, narrated `Retry n/N: …` |
| D3 | A router 404 naming no upstream was `Work → report` | The refusal is typed at the one door (`APIError.Routing`, `provider.RoutingRefusal`). `OurRequest()` is false for it, `taxonomy.Evidence.Routing` → **Transport**, and the loop's prose gate skips it. A spent ladder (`RefusalError`) and a malformed request stay Work |
| D4 | Account-policy exclusions were a 30-min per-model in-memory strike | Read from structure (`ineligibility_reasons[].configure_url` / `…-by-account`; the `(account settings)` sentence only as a hint). Learned **for every model**, held a day, persisted in `~/.aforge/v3/account-exclusions.json` (merged across processes), cleared by an answer that machine serves or by a re-pin. `lanes.Serves` reads it, so the frontier, the walk and `canWalk` skip it. A strict pin on such a machine is retired up front on every model |
| D4′ | (found by A8) A price ceiling priced off the excluded first-party machine's own tariff admitted **only** that machine, so every turn paid one 404 before the walk rescued it | The ceiling is not sent when every sheet row under it is ruled out by the serving set, so there is no wider set under it to try (#678's promise kept). A no-demand account refusal teaches the excluded machines when the router's `input_endpoint_count` and the sheet agree exactly |
| — | A rescue demanding a full pool retried it (29 s / 8 calls live) | It hands the 429 back to the race at once (3.2 s / 3 calls) |
| D5 | A cancelled errand was journaled `work · the work did not come back done` | A caller-cancelled errand writes nothing; one cut by an expired deadline is still written down |

D6 (12 minutes of reasoning at `effort: low`) was answered, not fixed here. The knob reaches the wire and Wafer **inverts** it for `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` (Wafer, reasoning tokens: 402/654/1008 at low vs 67/37/37 at high; Z.AI: 6/0/0 vs 22/30/34). The controller already flags `drift`, but its remedy is purse-gated. Filed as #836 (learn the inversion; a volume bound whose remedy is not purse-gated) and #837 (the task room never reads the beat sidecar). A withdrawn tier model found during A8 is #838.

## Tests that replicate it (red on `origin/dev`, green here)

- `internal/provider/recovery_test.go`:
  - `TestTheMeasuredRefusalRaceEndsInAnAnswerOnTheFirstAttempt` (A1: the exact §1 wire through the whole client; on dev the caller gets the 404 verbatim)
  - `TestAnExhaustedRaceSettlesOnTheMostActionableError` (A3)
  - `TestARoutingRefusalIsTypedForTheCaller`
  - `TestAnAccountExclusionIsLearnedOnceForEveryModel` (A4, including a second client on the same home)
  - `TestARescueOnAFullPoolGoesBackToTheRaceAtOnce`
  - `TestAPinOnAMachineTheAccountExcludesIsRetiredOnEveryModel`
- `internal/provider/accountset_test.go`:
  - `TestACeilingOnlyAnExcludedMachineFitsUnderIsPaidForOnce`
  - `TestAKnownExclusionTakesTheCeilingOffTheFirstRequest`
  - `TestACeilingAReachableMachineFitsUnderIsKept`
  - `TestARefusalTheSheetDisagreesWithTeachesNothing`
- `internal/session/recovery_boundary_test.go`:
  - `TestARoutingRefusalIsAskedAgainAndTheTurnLands` (A2)
  - `TestTheBoundaryReadsARoutingRefusalAsTheWire`
  - `TestACancelledErrandWritesNoFailure` (A5)
- `internal/taxonomy`: `TestARoutingRefusalIsTransportAndAMalformedRequestIsWork`.
- `lanestub` can now stage the account exclusion (the live body, metadata and all), a full pool (in-band 429 after heartbeats, or an immediate 429), and `allow_fallbacks: false`.

## Evidence

- `make pr-ready`: green (laws, packed corpora, touched packages lane / lanestub / provider 57.7 s / session 214.5 s / taxonomy).
- **Live router, owner's key** (`go test -tags e2e ./internal/provider -run TestRealRouter -v`, 21:02 EDT):

  | Test | Result |
  |---|---|
  | `TestRealRouterAccountExclusionIsPaidOnceForEveryModel` | pass: 2 models plus a fresh client, DeepSeek demanded once, 1 account refusal, 6 calls |
  | `TestRealRouterTheMeasuredRaceLandsOnTheFirstAttempt` | pass: 3 calls, `Retry 1/2: relaxed the endpoint filter` |
  | `TestRealRouterNeverRefusesItselfTwice` | pass: 22 rounds, 15 machines, 1 refusal |

  The last one was red on dev and here at round 14 (an upstream pool's 429). It now stops thinning on a busy pool instead of failing the refusal law.
- **The real binary** (`bin/aforge` from this branch, throwaway `AFORGE_HOME`, tmux), with a strict pin on DeepSeek, which the account excludes:

  | Run | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Turn 1 | Answered; the screen says `DeepSeek cannot serve this model; routing on auto for this model until you pin again` and never `API error (404)` |
  | `/model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` | 0 × 404 on the new model |
  | Home with the exclusion on file | The primary goes out with no `max_price` and is answered by its first request |
  | Home with nothing on file, no pin | Turn 1 pays one account 404 and writes `deepseek` to `account-exclusions.json`; turn 2 goes out uncapped and is answered first time |
- `make test-e2e-tui` (Spark, 12 min): 21/22 subtests pass. `space_in_the_task_room_pages_the_card` failed once: the task raised a question and its `waiting in this conversation` chip displaced the row's `enter open its room` hint. Rerun alone it passes on both `dev@ef36c3770` (112 s) and this branch (88 s), and no routing path is involved. Filed #840.

Manual: `lanes.md` (refusal section; "Providers switched off on your account") and `models-and-cost.md` ("0 endpoints … data policy").

body:
The first live `Release` run after #813 merged (dev, `ef36c3770`, run 34545146452) had `prepare` and `build` green, six binaries uploaded as a workflow artifact, and `publish` **skipped**. No dev release was created.

**Why.** GitHub skips a job whose dependency chain contains a skipped job unless that job's own condition says `always()`. `test` is skipped on every dev build by design (#813, D11). `build` carried the condition; `publish` did not.

**Fix.** `publish` now reads `if: always() && needs.prepare.result == 'success' && needs.build.result == 'success'`, so a red build still publishes nothing. The law test in `internal/release/workflow_test.go` demands the condition on both jobs under `test`, and it fails against the workflow as it was on `dev`.

**Gates run:** `go vet ./internal/release/`, `go test -count=1 ./internal/release/` (ok), gofmt clean, `yaml.safe_load` of `release.yml` ok, and the new assertion shown failing with the fix stashed.

The next push to `dev` after this merges is the real proof: it should end with a `dev-YYYYMMDD-<sha12>` prerelease on the Releases page.

body:
A completion report saying “no entries were deleted” could trigger an automatic repair because a quoted label still appeared in a file. In a captured benchmark, “all pass, none weakened or deleted” was treated as a claim that the quoted test command had been deleted, launching roughly six minutes of repair.

Remove the keyword-based claim classifiers and their automatic pass/fail decisions. The existing checker receives the original report once, acceptance, assembled files and check receipts, and interprets statements in that context. Explicit declarations in changed notes still arrive with source paths. Remove the duplicate report checklist and the post-check guess about which claims were examined based on shared words.

No extra classifier, model call stage, retry, generation limit or task-specific exception is introduced. Executable checks, restored-tree isolation, child-file assembly and dev's audit-window/second-attempt handling remain. The baseline snapshot preserves its existing 8,000-file bound under its own name. The manual and change entry describe the behavior.

Validation on Spark:
- Fleet433 reproduces the old false refutation with a general release-checklist fixture.
- Fleet435 validates current head `c8fe3da387b2abe7171bedd216b7cf62fefccf26`, integrated with dev `c0b20415129f580794d4ecd810baf4ec8de96e5b`: focused regressions; full uncached session (215.098s) and manual (1.309s) suites; build/vet, formatting, packed manual, structural laws, changelog and manual probes; `make build`.
- Build SHA256: `3d5ed752d5942849b6a2474bf9002d0697a0f8eb68eb79132aba9674d18e53ea`.

The regressions cover negated deletion, declarations interpreted in source context, negative checker findings, a report arriving exactly once and assembled child files. Prior433/434 source and proof are retained separately. No full or live tests ran on the laptop.

**Keep draft pending performance evidence.** A genuine contradiction now reaches the existing checker instead of the lexical fast path; that tradeoff must be measured along with avoided false repairs. Existing benchmark campaigns were interrupted by SIGTERM and remain frozen, with interrupted cells recorded separately. No new quality/cost/speed claim is made and this change is not in those runs.
title: Interpret completion claims in their original context

body:
`release-binaries.yml` waited for a hand-cut `v*` tag and published whatever it
found. Nobody could install a build of `dev` at all, so the only way to try a
change was to clone the repository and build it — and the binaries it did
publish carried no furrow. This replaces it with four channels, an installer,
and a stable release that is still a person's decision.

## What changed

| Channel | Trigger | Tag | Marks on the GitHub release |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dev | every push to `dev` | `dev-YYYYMMDD-<sha12>` | prerelease, not Latest |
| staging | every push to `staging` | `staging-YYYYMMDD-<sha12>` | prerelease, not Latest |
| rc | every push to `main` | `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | prerelease, not Latest |
| stable | a person dispatches `Release` on `main` | `vX.Y.Z` | **Latest**, not a prerelease |

There is **no tag trigger any more**. A tag pushed by hand publishes nothing.
The workflow creates each tag through `gh release create --target <sha>`, so
nothing ever pushes a commit to a branch and `main ⊂ staging ⊂ dev` still holds.

**The order is checked before anything is built.** A candidate or a stable must
already be on `staging`; a staging build must already be on `dev`; the failure
names the fast-forward that fixes it. A re-publish is guarded the same way, and
the workflow refuses to clobber a release whose tag commit is not the one whose
bytes were built.

**Installing.** `scripts/install.sh` takes a channel or a pin, checks the
sha256 against `checksums.txt`, and puts the binary at `~/.aforge/bin/aforge`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --stable
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --rc
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --dev
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --staging
```

and one named build:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/main/scripts/install.sh | VERSION=v0.2.0 bash
```

The assignment sits on `bash`, not on `curl` — a prefix assignment in front of
`curl` never reaches the shell on the other side of the pipe, which is a way of
spelling it that silently installs the wrong thing.

**The furrow defect, fixed in passing.** The old workflow never ran
`internal/furrowbin/cmd/fetch`, so `furrowbin.Embedded()` was false in every
release it ever made and every downloaded aforge fell through to whatever furrow
was on the machine's PATH. The build loop now stages furrow for each target
immediately before compiling it, and clears the stage for windows — which has no
pin — so a windows aforge cannot carry a linux furrow.

**Retention.** After a dev or staging build publishes, that channel's releases
beyond the newest **40** are deleted with their tags. Stable and rc are never
pruned. The number lives only in `cmd/aforge-release`; a test fails if it is
copied into the YAML.

**Concurrency.** `release-<channel>`. Only `dev` is `cancel-in-progress` — a
burst of merges publishes the newest and the skipped commits simply have no dev
build. staging, rc and stable are each allowed to finish.

## How to promote

```sh
git fetch origin && git push origin origin/dev:staging      # dev → staging, publishes a staging build
git push origin origin/staging:main                          # staging → main
```

The first push to `main` cuts `v0.1.1-rc.1` by itself; every later push to
`main` continues that line — `rc.2`, `rc.3`. Opening a new minor line instead:

```sh
gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f channel=rc -f component=minor
```

Cutting the stable, which closes the highest open candidate line:

```sh
gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f channel=stable
```

`component=minor` or `major` on the stable dispatch starts a new line from the
latest stable tag instead. `existing_version=<tag>` rebuilds an existing tag's
commit and replaces its assets — the repair road for a publish that half
finished.

## No token is needed

Publishing already works on the private repository because Actions' own token
creates the release, and the anonymous `curl` line works once the repository is
public.

## Cost

One build job builds all six targets in a loop rather than a six-way matrix, and
uploads one artifact. `dev` is `cancel-in-progress`, so a burst of merges costs
one build rather than one per merge. `dev` also skips the narrow release-surface
test — its pull request gate just ran, and the build is its gate. staging, rc and
stable pay for that test.

## Not in this pull request

- **A PowerShell installer.** Windows here is asset naming only — the `.exe`
  asset installs through MSYS or Git Bash and edits no PATH.
- **The agentfield.ai download route.** That lives in a separate website2.0
  pull request. `scripts/install.sh` keeps the line that route rewrites,
  `CHANNEL="${CHANNEL:-stable}"`, spelled exactly that way on its own line, and
  a test fails if it moves.

## Validation contract, in short

- **Naming.** Stable is the highest stable tag bumped by `component`; a
  candidate continues the highest open line above stable whatever component is
  asked for, and starts a new one otherwise; a stable patch closes the highest
  open line. Ordering is numeric, so `v0.1.10 > v0.1.9` and `rc.10 > rc.9`.
  Tags of any other shape are ignored, never fatal. Usage errors leave with 2
  and put nothing on stdout.
- **Retention.** `prune` prints the disposable tags beyond the newest forty on
  one channel, oldest first, ties by tag; nothing for forty or fewer; other
  channels' tags are untouched.
- **Installing.** Every channel resolves to the newest build GitHub lists;
  `VERSION=` pins any tag on any channel. A channel with no build refuses by
  name and writes nothing. The checksum is checked in a temporary directory and
  a mismatch leaves nothing in the install directory. The install is a `mv` onto
  the old path, never a write through it. The PATH line is appended once and a
  second run adds nothing. darwin and linux on amd64 and arm64, windows through
  Git Bash; anything else is refused by name. curl or wget, `set -euo pipefail`,
  BSD sed/grep/awk.
- **The workflow.** No tag trigger; pushes are exactly dev, staging, main; only
  dev cancels in progress; the guards check the resolved commit; the retention
  count is asked for rather than written down twice.

## Gates

Run in the worktree with `GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false`, outside any sandbox:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go build ./... && make fmt-check && go vet ./...` | exit 0, no output |
| `go generate ./internal/manual && go test -tags=aforge_packed_manual ./internal/manual` | ok `internal/manual` 1.5s |
| `git diff --exit-code` after that generate, post-rebase | exit 0 — no tracked generated file is stale |
| `go test ./internal/manual/ && go test -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/` | ok, ok, ok |
| `make test-laws` | 64 files in 18 packages, 18 packages ok |
| `make test PKGS='./cmd/aforge-release ./internal/release ./cmd/aforge ./internal/manual ./internal/ci ./internal/furrowbin' TEST_FLAGS='-count=1'` | all six ok (`cmd/aforge` 55s) |
| `bash -n scripts/install.sh` | exit 0 |
| `python3 -c 'import yaml; …release.yml…ci-full.yml'` | yaml ok |
| `bash scripts/install.sh --help` | exit 0 |
| `make changelog-check` | all entries well formed |

`.github/known-red.txt`, `SIZE-BUDGET`, `go.mod` and `go.sum` are untouched, and
no dependency was added.

Two adversarial review rounds ran against the diff. The first found the
private-repository asset lookup could not parse GitHub's real JSON (the stub it
was tested against was flatter than the real payload), that `existing_version`
skipped the order guard and could mark a candidate as the stable Latest, and
that an oversized numeric component silently became a negative number. The
second found that the documented `VERSION=` pin never reached `bash`, that the
wget road handed the token to the redirect target, and that an empty known-red
ledger would stop every release. All are fixed, with a test each.

One operational edge is deliberately left as it is: if `gh release create` makes
the tag and then fails, a fresh run resolves the next candidate number and
leaves the broken one behind. `existing_version` is the repair road for exactly
that, and remembering a previous attempt would need state on a branch.

## What this is

The owner's ruling after the 2026-09-10 "task creation" screenshot, where a question the chat was two minutes into answering was moved into a ten-minute task at the round-10 mark (worktree, six-minute worker, two checkers cut by a one-minute window, a third verification by the chat, and the answer left on a branch nobody would merge). The trail is in `ideation/quick-task.md`; the build contract is `docs/design/quick-task/DESIGN.md`.

**Keep the big task exactly as it is. Add one small notion: the quick task.**

A quick task is a task node of kind `quick`. It runs a worker **where the caller works** — no seal, no worktree, no branch. It starts from one tool call that returns at once: no sizing, no shaping, no countdown, no consent. It has a `line` and ordered `items` it ticks on its row (`quick · 2/4 · reading foo.go`). No audit, no landing: **its last message is its result**, delivered as the ordinary landing note. It may name `files` (two quick tasks claiming one path run one after the other; the write guard enforces the claim), `depends_on`, and may itself call `quick_task` and `propose_task` under the graph's fan and depth caps. Steer, stop, page and the room are the ones every task has. A quick node never holds the tree: the person keeps editing while it runs.

The judge is written once, in the tool description:

> A task gets its own copy of the folder, is checked, and lands. A quick task works where you are and its last message is its answer. If you will read the result and carry on, it is quick. If it must be checked and merged on its own, or survive the window closing, it is a task. One edit, one read, one command is a step: do it yourself. Related steps that share what they learn are one quick task's items, not several quick tasks.

## What changes

- **Engine** (`internal/session/task_quick.go` + seams): `TaskKindQuick`, `quick_task` and `items` tools, `runQuickNode`/`landQuickNode` on the harness-design precedent, files-claim serialisation at admission, `quick.md` worker page, belt bullet.
- **Ceiling** (`checkpoint_quick.go`): a turn that has written nothing and whose mark sketch drew parts now starts a quick task from those parts (`this has parts · a quick task is taking them here, in this folder: …`) instead of paying the handoff writer, the carve and the audit. A turn that wrote still takes the watched road. Journal `carry: quick`.
- **Surface** (`internal/tui3`): the row's doing line, no branch/merge on a quick card, honest stop card (`Its work halts; whatever it already wrote is in your folder.`), room setup excluded.
- **Manual**: ten new sections in `tasks.md`, corrections wherever a page said every task gets a copy of the folder, sixteen probes.
- **`fork` is off the belt.** Never seen in use; the scope functions the quick task reuses stay in `fork.go`; hands, the job kind, the five manual sections and their probes go.
- The fixed prefix budget stays at 48,000 (`PERF.md`, `prefixbudget_test.go`): the guidance lane paid for the quick-task bullet by compressing `propose_task`'s schema prose; measured 46,245 at the tip.

## Evidence

Lanes K/S/M/C/F each ran their package suites on the Spark before integration; the integration branch's `internal/session`, `internal/tui3`, `internal/manual`, `internal/e2e` (untagged) and `internal/iconlaw` runs on the Spark are recorded in the PR conversation below. Six new session tests cover the acceptance list in the design (two quick tasks in one batch run at once and both land; a files collision serialises; items tick the row; a quick node under a task reports to its task; a chat write is not refused while a quick task runs; a quick node caught by the close settles rather than resuming), five for the ceiling road, six for the surface.

## Still owed (separate PRs)

The heavy road's own defects from the same investigation: the reading-only audit window (1m split into two 30s calls), the `settle=auto` note ordering a diff read, a document-only task landing on a kept branch, the sketch division paid on read-only work, `context.Canceled` misfiled as failed work, and the surface drawing `idle` over a working wake turn.

On a loaded box that goroutine reached the model first, the reading taken before the loop equalled the reading taken after it, and a turn that did run was reported as one that never reached the model.

**What is true now:** the baseline is read before `Submit`. The law the test pins is unchanged: the turn after an abandoned one answers, ends, and reaches the model at least once.

## What was wrong

The owner's Terminal.app tab for aforge read `/Users/santos…` — the running binary's path — beside a shell tab whose program had set a real name.

**Root cause:** aforge already declared a title (`windowtitle.go`, since 2026-08-24), but Bubble Tea v2 has no `tea.SetWindowTitle` command any more; the title is `tea.View.WindowTitle`, which the renderer writes as **OSC 2** (the window title). Terminal.app and iTerm2 label a **tab** with the icon name, **OSC 1**, and nothing wrote one. tmux, kitty, Ghostty and every window bar read OSC 2 and already worked.

## What is true now

One function owns the sentence: `terminalTitle(a *app) string` in `internal/tui3/title.go` (the old `windowtitle.go` is moved there, not duplicated). `app.retitle` runs after every message in `app.Update` and sends it as OSC 1 **only when it changed** (`a.titleSent`), and `View` declares the same `a.titleSent` as OSC 2, which the renderer diffs itself. A message the pointer fold swallowed (`ptr.still`) is not even asked, so the folded-motion allocation law is unchanged.

| where | title |
|---|---|
| home, nothing waiting | `aforge` |
| home, N waiting | `N want you · aforge` (the pulse's `machineFactsAt` memo and `pulseWantWord`, not a second count) |
| a conversation | `<short title> · aforge` (the tab strip's `chatTabDisplayName`) |
| not named yet | `new conversation · aforge`, re-sent when `EventTitleChanged` lands |
| waiting on the person | `? <short title> · aforge`: the tab strip's own `frontSignal() == tabNeedsPerson`, with `?` from `tokens.ASCII.Glyph(tokens.GNeedsHuman)` |
| a task room | `<task label> · task · aforge` (`roomHereWord`) |
| tasks / standing / memory / spend / search / settings | `<place word> · aforge` |
| over `--host` | `Token counter @ devbox · aforge`; home at rest is `aforge @ devbox` |
| on quit | `titleFarewell` writes an empty OSC 1 after `p.Run()` returns, on every way out (quit, signal, cancelled context); the renderer already clears OSC 2 as it closes |

The title stays within 60 cells: the name is cut with `fit` (`…`) before the suffix, and ` · aforge` is never cut.

## What departs from the ruling, and why

- **The mechanism.** The ruling named `tea.SetWindowTitle`, which v2 does not have. What ships is OSC 1 through `tea.Raw` plus the view's OSC 2. Emitting both is what fixes Terminal.app and iTerm2.
- **"No byte over 0x7f".** The ruling's own sentences carry `·`, and `fit`'s ellipsis is `…`, so a literal byte rule would forbid the table. What the test pins instead: no control character at all (C0, DEL, C1). For an ASCII name, the only non-ASCII runes allowed are those two typographic marks, so no icon glyph can get in. `oscSafe` now drops every control character, including C1 (U+009C string terminator, U+009B CSI), which also hardens the notification it already guarded.
- **Removed:** the old sentence's project prefix, its process-wide `?` (any kept conversation waiting), and the `✓` for a turn that landed while the window was blurred, along with `landedAway`, whose only reader was the title. None of them is in the ruling's table. Home's count now carries the machine-wide "waiting" news.

## Laws

- Manual law: in `internal/manual/chat/screen.md`, the two existing terminal-title sections are rewritten in place (no new `## ` heading to pull search hits away from other probes) under the headings "What the terminal tab says — why my terminal title changes, and why the tab shows a path" and "The ? on the terminal tab — …". Both quote the sentences above exactly. The naming section's two claims about the window title are corrected. Three probes were added to `internal/manual/chat_test.go`.
- Icon law: the mark comes through the glyph door (`tokens.ASCII.Glyph`) and there is no literal. `internal/iconlaw` is green.

## Tests (`internal/tui3/title_test.go`)

- `TestTheTerminalTitleSaysWhereYouAre`: home at rest, home with 3 waiting, named, unnamed, waiting on you, task room (`roomApp` + `clickRail`), `--host`. Each asserts the exact string and the plain-text pin.
- `TestEveryPlaceTitlesTheTabWithItsWord`: the six other places, opened through `everyPlaceTable`'s own labs. A new place with no title fails by name.
- `TestALongNameIsCutBeforeTheSuffix`, `TestTheNeedsYouMarkIsASCIIOnARichTerminal` (NerdFont tier still sends `?`), `TestANameCannotCarryAnEscapeIntoTheTitle`.
- `TestTheTitleIsSentAgainWhenTheNameArrives`, `TestAnUnchangedTitleIsNotSentTwice` (second `retitle` is nil; a repeated `WindowSizeMsg` through `Update` returns no command at all).
- `TestQuittingHandsTheTabBackEmpty`: boots `Run` headless, waits for the title, sends `/quit`, and asserts the last OSC 1 and the last OSC 2 in the stream are both empty. I checked it by mutation: with the farewell commented out, it fails and names the title left behind.

## Spark evidence

Run on the Spark (linux/arm64) at `fb24d2e0a`:

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/manual/`, `gofmt -l internal/ cmd/`: clean
- `go test ./internal/manual/... ./internal/tui3/ -run Manual ./internal/session/ -run Manual`: ok
- `go test ./internal/e2e/ ./internal/iconlaw/... ./internal/tui2/tokens/ ./internal/ci/...`: ok
- `make test-laws`: ok
- the eight new tests, run by name: ok
- full `go test ./internal/tui3/ -count=1 -timeout 25m`: SUITE_PENDING

Context reduction replaces old tool results with file references, but the task finishing phase removed `read` while retaining `edit` and `write`. A worker could therefore be asked to save an accurate deliverable without any way to recover the evidence it had already read.

Keep the existing `read` tool during finishing and tell the worker to retrieve existing evidence as needed. Reading does not count as saving or reset progress rules. The existing stop decisions, permissions, execution budgets and exclusions for asynchronous generation remain in place. The manual describes the changed capability.

The regression test combines actual tool-result archival, successful retrieval, the finishing-tool transition and retrieval again. It uses a general text fixture and no model API, repository-specific instructions or benchmark paths.

Validation passed on Spark: Fleet420 reproduces the exact archived-read failure on the baseline, and Fleet424 passes the same test on the candidate, the full uncached session/manual suites, packed manual tests, and `make build`. All PR CI checks also pass. The ongoing matched benchmark403 is unchanged and does not include this patch. This draft claims a concrete correctness fix, not a measured quality/cost/speed improvement; keep it unmerged until validation and evaluation support it.

Related experiments: #770 removes mandatory progress notes; this fixes a different path that still exists with those notes removed. #763 changes context reduction and should preserve this retrieval contract.

body:
## What was wrong

Both news desks in `internal/tui3` — the phase desk and the lane desk — were keyed by **model**, which is an address and not an identity. Three things followed:

- two tasks running on one model overwrote each other's phase, and each room drew whichever of them had spoken last;
- a node's phase could never be drawn at all, because the only reading (`livePhase`) hard-dropped every role that was not `RoleTalk`, and there was no other reading;
- every rate on the frame was gated on `a.state != stateWorking` — the **conversation's** liveness — so a room showed no throughput whenever the conversation that launched the work was idle, which is the whole of a task's run: you hand the work out and your turn ends.

What a person read inside a task room, with the node writing: no provider, no tok/s, and a stale `running ask · 4m 55s` left over from the conversation.

`internal/session`'s `tellPhase` stamped model, role and `Session: a.newsKey()` — but `newsKey()` is the ROOT conversation, shared by every node in the family, so nothing on the news could tell two nodes apart.

## What is true now

**A news item belongs to a subject, and a window draws its own subject's news.**

- `provider.PhaseNews` and `session.LaneNews` both carry `Subject`. Empty means *the conversation*, which is what every existing producer and every older wire peer sends — so absence behaves exactly as it did before.
- `session.NewsSubject(conversation, node)` mints the one spelling (`<conversation>#<node>`), exported because both sides of the seam have to agree; the surface asks for it rather than rebuilding it. The conversation half is in the name because node ids restart per conversation and a guest room looks at another conversation's node 7.
- `provider.WithNode` is the context stamp beside `WithSession`, set once in the turn loop.
- One key function, `tui3.newsDeskKey(subject, model)`, keys both desks: the subject when there is one, the model when there is not. The lane **rings** stay keyed by model+lane, because those measure a machine and a subject in that key would split one machine's history.
- The window resolves its own subject. The conversation asks for the talk subject and **keeps** the `RoleTalk` requirement — the subject stops a node's news reaching that row, the role still stops the naming errands and memory reflexes that share the conversation's subject. A room asks for its node's subject and accepts a visible leaf role, because the subject already proves whose news it is. **There is no heuristic about a room being open**; two tasks on one model would show each other's rate under one.
- `windowPhase()` / `windowWorking()` are the one place "whose clock is on this frame" is answered. A room's own liveness is its subject's news being fresh, which the held and streaming beats make a real answer, and `roomPhase` has already refused anything past `phaseWindow`.
- The room's identity cluster now carries the node's own attribution — `⠋ Ship the parser fix · task glm-5.2 · via friendli` — on a four-rung width ladder, and the rate stands at the right edge as it does everywhere else. The ledger, meter and job counts on the same row are still the conversation's: those measure a session.
- The subject crosses the wire on both frames and through all four converters, and an older peer that sends none reads as the conversation.

## Tests

New, in `internal/tui3/newssubject_test.go`:

- `TestTwoSubjectsOnOneModelKeepTheirOwnNews` — two subjects on one model keep their own phase and their own served news, and a subject nobody said is still filed under its model.
- `TestARoomDrawsItsNodesRateWhileTheConversationIsIdle` — the room shows `38 tok/s` and `via friendli` with the conversation idle, says neither figure twice, and draws nothing once the news ages out.
- `TestARoomsPhaseIsItsNodesAndNotTheConversations` — `running go test` inside the room while the conversation's own `running ask` sits on the desk; and a room over a silent node draws nothing rather than borrowing that clock.
- `TestClosingTheRoomRestoresTheConversationsOwnLine` — `esc` gives the conversation its own rate back whole, and the node's phase never reached that row even while the room was shut.

`TestANodesOwnPhaseCrossesWithItsRoleOnIt` in `internal/remote` now asserts the subject crosses, survives the read back, and that an absent one reads as the conversation.

## Verification

`go build ./...`, `make test-quick`, `make test-laws`, `go test ./internal/e2e/` (untagged) and the four new tests are green.

`make test PKGS='./internal/tui3 ./internal/session ./internal/provider ./internal/remote' TEST_FLAGS='-count=1'` was first run against this branch's original base (`64dc75f28`): `provider` and `remote` green, `session`'s tests all green, and `tui3` red on four tests — `TestEnterConnectsOpenRouterInTheBrowserAndHandsTheKeyToThisProcess`, `TestAJobsLogReaderTakesOneLastReadingAfterTheJobEnds`, `TestAPathInTheBoxIsNeverChipped`, `TestAnAbsolutePathDoesNotHoldTheCommandListOpen`. Those were #798's harness clock and were fixed on `dev` by #801; this branch is rebased onto that, and all four pass here now. Nothing was added to `.github/known-red.txt`.

One thing worth knowing for anyone running `internal/session` on a laptop: its post-run checkout guard fired twice for me, naming worktrees under `~/.aforge/v3/projects/…/trees/N` that a **live aforge session** on this machine created and removed during the run. The guard filters out a neighbour's work by ignoring anything that is not on a `task/` branch — but the product's own task trees are exactly that, so a running aforge is indistinguishable from the suite writing into the tree. It fired once during a 16-second `make test-laws`, which cannot register a worktree at all.

body:
A conversation hit its checkpoint ceiling, split the rest into a sketch, wrote a
2,641-token handoff and launched the first task. The worker re-read files the
parent had already read and re-derived conclusions the handoff had already
stated.

The tempting diagnosis is that it was short of context. It was not. It had the
handoff, the evidence and the quotes. What it had was **a document that said two
different things about the same work**: the machine-composed line at the head of
the brief, `WHAT IS LEFT, AS PARTS:`, named reading two files as remaining work,
while the calls-already-run section further down named the same two reads, with
their pointers, as done. The worker obeyed the louder and earlier half.

Three sentences, in the three places that were silent. Nothing structural — no
new field on the brief, no new section, no result bytes anywhere near an
admission handle.

### 1. The second reader is told that finished work is not a part

`checkpointSketchAsk` already excluded work handed out. It now excludes work
already done, in the same voice, appended after that clause:

> Work that is already done is not a part either: what the account above shows
> finished is not what remains, and drawing it sends somebody to do it a second
> time.

The measured wording of everything before it is untouched — no digits, none of
the narrowing words `TestTheSketchAskIsTheMeasuredWording` forbids.

### 2. The handoff's writer is told where the line between its first two things falls

`checkpointHandoffWriteAsk` named four things and left this to inference. It now
says it, between the four things and the closing instruction about the person's
own words:

> Nothing that is already done goes under what is left to do: what has already
> been read, run or found out is what they already know, and putting it under
> what is left sends them to do it again.

### 3. The worker is told which half of its own brief wins

`admissionEvidenceRule` described the calls-already-run section without ranking
it against anything, so a contradiction had no resolution. Appended:

> AND THIS SECTION IS WHAT HAS ALREADY HAPPENED, which is what settles a
> disagreement with the work above: where the parts or the brief read as though
> one of these calls were still to be made, it has been made already — read it
> through its pointer instead of running it again, and run it again only where
> the line says it failed or where what you read disagrees with the brief.

**The body-absence law is untouched.** No result bytes or excerpts were added to
a handle; the bytes stay where they are and the worker fetches what it needs.
Entry room inside the 5,000-byte `admissionBudget` follows the rule's length by
itself through `admissionOverhead` — 3,707 bytes, from 4,030, and the budget
test still passes.

### And the folder the same brief could not write to

The same run's brief named `<session>/work/task-creation-flow.md` as its
deliverable, which is what `deliverablesDir` answers with for a conversation
that owns its workspace. That folder is outside the ground, so `taskCopy` rightly
left it alone, `taskGroundGuard` refused the first write there, and the worker
invented an address inside its own copy and reported the deviation. `newTaskCopy`
now takes that folder as a third argument and binds it to the same path under the
copy, and the section that explains the mapping says so outright — which is that
self-correction made the contract instead of a wasted round. The folder is
dropped when the session has none, when it is borrowed, or when the ground or the
copy already holds it.

**Person-quoted paths are still verbatim.** `composeBrief` binds only the
model-authored sections and has never touched the quoted request; that is
unchanged, and a test asserts a person's own `put it in /s/work/flow.md please`
comes through untouched.

### Tests

- `TestBothHandoverAsksSayFinishedWorkIsNotWhatIsLeft` — both clauses word for
  word, and the handoff clause's position before the greeting instruction.
- `TestTheEvidenceSectionOutranksPartsThatNameACallAlreadyRun` — composes a brief
  whose parts name a read the evidence also names as done, asserts the precedence
  phrases render below the parts, and asserts no result body came with them.
- `TestTheConversationsOwnFolderIsWrittenAsThePathInsideTheCopy` — the binding,
  suffix preservation, lookalike siblings left alone, and every constructor drop.
- `TestTheBriefStatesTheConversationsOwnFolderWhereverItIsNamed` — the exception
  sentence, the bound sections, the person's sentence left verbatim, and no
  section for a borrowed session.
- `TestTheCopyTakesTheConversationsFolderFromTheTree` — owned binds, borrowed and
  the zero `Place` do not.

### Verification

- `go build ./...` — green.
- `make test PKGS=./internal/session TEST_FLAGS='-count=1'` — every test green.
  Two guard trips, neither a red in this change: the first run flagged the
  changelog file created while it ran, and the second flagged a branch and
  worktree the shared repository gained from a live session in the main checkout
  (the branch/worktree list is repository-wide, not per-worktree). Both left
  untouched.
- `make test-laws` — green, 18 packages.
- `make test-quick` — green.
- `TestAWindowOneStallClosedIsDecidedByThePosture/left_running_with_a_ceiling`
  fails under load. It is pre-existing: the same test prebuilt from this
  branch's parent fails at the same rate in alternating rounds. Filed as #803
  with a stranger-runnable replication. Nothing added to `.github/known-red.txt`.

### Manual

`internal/manual/chat/tasks.md` said a sketch naming work you have already done
was **not** covered; it is now covered as far as the ask can cover it, and the
page says which half of the brief wins and what genuinely remains uncovered (a
part that lands in the seconds after the account was taken).
`internal/manual/chat/how-tasks-run.md` said a path not under the project stands
exactly as written, with no exception; the conversation's own folder is now that
exception, and the page states it with the before-and-after address.
title: A handover no longer lists finished work as what is left

body:
`RetargetTask` decided what a pick could move from the node's STATE alone. A node is `TaskRunning` across three lives — its own worker, the check reading what that worker left, and every repair round — so the worker's reading is over the moment `runTaskChild` returns, which on a checked node is minutes before anything settles.

A pick made in that window rewrote the frozen `spec.model`, so the row, the checkpoint and the landed card all named a model that never ran a token of the work, while the bill named the one that did.

It reads `node.lifeNow() == TaskPhaseChecking` now — the same word the steering door already uses under *THE CHECK HAS NO READER* — and a pick with no turn left to reach lands in `nextModel`, where a settled node's pick already lands. The room draws `next model <id>` and the sidebar heads itself `Next run setup`, so no surface learns new vocabulary.

Measured on a real run: a node admitted on the install's worker tier with all nineteen of its calls billed there, and a card claiming the low tier — the model that had only ever run the hidden `router`, `taskname` and `caption` roles.

`make pr-ready` exited 0. New tests: `TestAModelPickedWhileTheCheckReadsBecomesTheNextRunsAndLeavesTheRowAlone` and `TestAModelPickedWhileTheWorkerReadsStillMovesTheWork` in `internal/session/taskretarget_test.go`.
