body:
Four `internal/tui3` tests have been red on `dev` since #798 (`f96c7c96f`) replaced `tea.Tick` with the harness clock. Verified by name on the Spark: green at `b9142e747`, red from `f96c7c96f` through `436aa8426`.

| test | what it said |
|---|---|
| `TestEnterConnectsOpenRouterInTheBrowserAndHandsTheKeyToThisProcess` | the key started something other than the panel's beat: `<nil>` |
| `TestAJobsLogReaderTakesOneLastReadingAfterTheJobEnds` | the running beat produced `<nil>`, want a tick |
| `TestAPathInTheBoxIsNeverChipped` | the surface did not settle |
| `TestAnAbsolutePathDoesNotHoldTheCommandListOpen` | the surface did not settle |

**What was true:** `harnessTick` answers any tick longer than `tickBudget` with nothing, by design, so a test whose claim *is* a beat ("the key arms the panel's next beat", "the reader re-arms after the job ends") got `nil` where the old real clock gave a message. And `dropSettled` asked the clock whether the quiet window had passed on every wakeup; under a clock that delivers the wakeup without moving, it re-armed forever and the harness never settled.

**What is true now:** `waitOut(cmd)` is a test helper that runs one delayed command as though its whole delay had passed, costing no wall time, and puts the budget back for the next command; the two beat tests use it. `dropSettled` asks the clock only when a character arrived after the wakeup in flight was armed (`dropFold.stirred`); a wakeup that finds nothing new lands a whole `dropQuiet` after the last character by construction, so the window is over whatever the clock reads. The AST law counting `surfaceTick` callers still holds.

**Verification on the Spark:** the four tests by name, `go vet`, `make test-laws`, and one full `go test ./internal/tui3/ -count=1` on this branch.

## What this carries

One pull request instead of a stack, at the owner's request. It absorbs four in-flight fixes unchanged — their commits and their change entries ride along — and builds Phase 1 of the direct-providers work on top.

Closes #748
Closes #749
Closes #750
Closes #754

Those were open as #759, #752, #757 and #762; each is closed with a pointer here rather than merged separately.

## The goal

A person can connect a second place models come from — a direct DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot or Ollama key, or any OpenAI-shaped base — and every model client in the process is built from the service that serves its model rather than from one global key and one global address.

## What is now true

**The model id decides the account.** `ClientConfigFor` takes the service set rather than a key and a base, so the segment before the first slash chooses where the call goes. An unqualified id still belongs to the default service, so every shipped default, every saved profile and every manual example means exactly what it meant before. A set that is empty *is* one service, resolved through the same door — never a second code path.

**A service is a record, and the record is pure.** `internal/modelsource` reads no file and opens no socket; a `go/ast` law refuses any import of `os`, `net/http`, `internal/config`, `internal/catalog` or `internal/provider`. Five services ship as data. Two publish no model list, which is why the probe has two shapes.

**A key is scrubbed by its exact value, at the moment it is resolved.** A Z.ai key is not `sk-` shaped, so the redaction shape table would never have caught it — and registering at process start would have left a key connected mid-session unscrubbed for the rest of that run.

**A cache belongs to one service at one address.** Keying on the service alone would have put #748's own bug back for anyone on the default service with a custom `AFORGE_BASE_URL`. v3's picker cache is keyed through the same exported derivation, so the two files for one service cannot disagree.

## Validation contract, and the test that proves each item

| # | behaviour | proving test |
|---|---|---|
| 9.1 | a bad key refuses, stores nothing, and the message carries the vendor's own words | `TestABadKeyIsRefusedInTheVendorsOwnWordsAndNothingIsStored` (`internal/config`) |
| 9.2 | a valid key makes that service's models appear in the picker, grouped, **and reachable**, without a restart | `TestAConnectedServicesModelsAppearGroupedWithoutARestart` (`internal/tui3`) — drives a real `session.Agent` across two stub hosts and asserts which host received the turn with which bearer |
| 9.3 | an unqualified id resolves exactly as it did before | `TestAnUnqualifiedIdResolvesExactlyAsItDidBefore` (`internal/config`) — every shipped default through both the scalar and a captured profile, comparing every field. **Passes on the base too; that is the point** |
| 9.4 | a name colliding with a model author is refused with a suggestion | `TestAServiceNameThatCollidesWithAModelAuthorIsRefusedWithASuggestion` (`internal/modelsource`), `TestACollidingServiceWritesNothing` (`internal/config`) |
| 9.5 | harness, subharness, session, standing run, memory consolidation and document read each reach the service that serves their model | `TestTheHarnessReachesTheSourceThatServesItsModel` and five siblings (`cmd/aforge`, `internal/session`) |
| 9.6 | a catalog fetched for one service is never served to another, in all four cache states | `TestACatalogFetchedForOneServiceIsNeverServedToAnother` (`internal/catalog`), sibling in `internal/tui3` |
| 9.7 | no key reaches a trace, transcript, error or log, whatever its shape | `TestNoServiceKeyReachesTheRecordWhateverItsShape` (`internal/config`, `internal/trace`) — drives the production connect path |
| 9.8 | no key or address travels in a `Hello` frame | `TestNoServiceKeyOrAddressCrossesTheWire` + `TestTheHelloAllowlistRejectsAnUnknownCredentialSpelling` (`internal/remote`) |
| 9.9 | disconnecting leaves the conversation on something it can reach, or says it cannot | `TestDisconnectingAServiceLeavesTheConversationOnSomethingItCanReach`, `TestDisconnectingReplacesTheLiveClientBeforeTheNextRequest` (`internal/tui3`) |
| 9.10 | the record reads nothing and dials nothing | `TestModelsourceReadsNothingAndDialsNothing` (`internal/modelsource`) |
| — | one service draws the picker exactly as before | `TestOneServiceDrawsThePickerExactlyAsItDidBefore` — compared against a golden captured from the merged base |
| §1 | **every client is built from the service that serves its model** — a role's model never rides the conversation's account | `TestTheCrewReachesItsOwnServiceWhileTheChatIsElsewhere` (`internal/session`) — a real `Agent` on a stub service with the default crew; the stub must never receive an id it does not serve. `TestOnlyTheClientDoorCanOverrideAModel` is the `go/ast` law that keeps it |
| §5.6 | a connected service's models reach the picker **without a restart** | `TestAConnectedServicesModelsAppearGroupedWithoutARestart` (rewritten to drive the real shelf and the live picker), `TestAConnectedServiceRefreshLandsOnTheProcessShelf` (`cmd/aforge`) |
| §5.6 | a listing-less service draws its heading and the dim row, never nothing | `TestAServiceWithNoListingDrawsNoCount` — a real listing-less stub, then types its model and proves the direct host received it |
| §5.4 | a disconnect says the service went, beside the moved line | `TestDisconnectingAServiceLeavesTheConversationOnSomethingItCanReach`, `TestDisconnectingAnUnusedServiceDrawsOnlyItsAcknowledgement` |
| §5.6 | a direct service's row carries no borrowed lane, and its id stays qualified | `TestADirectModelKeepsItsServiceInStatusAndCarriesNoLane` |
| §15.2 | one row keeps one name in refusal and success | `TestACustomServiceUsesItsWrittenNameOnRefusalAndSuccess` |
| §1 | a **child** — task worker, fork hand, auditor, orchestrated node — resolves its own account, deterministically | `TestTheCrewNeverReachesAServiceThatDoesNotServeIt` (`internal/session`) — a real worker crossed with a real chat on a stub, **five repetitions, all required to agree**. Plus an AST law rejecting a production `newAgent` outside the two account-aware doors |
| §7 | a direct service never owns the process lane sheet | `TestADirectClientDoesNotRepointTheDefaultLaneSheet` (`internal/provider`) |
| §9.9 | a disconnect leaves nothing able to send with the removed key | `TestRemovingAServiceEvictsAndDisarmsItsClient` — every adapter for that account evicted and its bearer cleared, so a stale interface refuses with `ErrNoAPIKey` |
| §5.6 | a "Something else" listing fills its own picker group and both scoped caches | `TestAConnectedServiceRefreshLandsOnTheProcessShelf` — connects the real vendored row through `config.ConnectService` and asserts both cache files exist |
| §8.6 | a placeholder notice is not a model and cannot reach the wire | `TestAServiceWithNoListingDrawsNoCount` — the row carries an **empty id**, so it cannot be selected, pinned or encoded into a URL |
| §1 | the **reflex tier** reaches its own account, per call, including after its ladder falls back | the reflex wire regression in `internal/session/clientdoor_wire_test.go` — drives the reflex path and its fallback against a stub, **five repetitions** |
| §1 | the conversation's raw completer cannot leave the client door | `TestOnlyTheClientDoorReadsTheSessionClient` — the law that ends the class, after three separate routes to one defect |
| §5.3 | the **service** decides whether it has a model list, not our survey | the discovery tests in `internal/modelsource` / `internal/config` — a stub whose listing answers connects on it even when its completion route cannot pay; a stub whose listing 404s falls back to the one-token probe |
| §5.4 | a key that authenticates but cannot pay is connected, and the sentence names the account | the payment-outcome tests in `internal/config` — the service is stored and the line reads `accepted the key but the account cannot pay — <vendor words>` |
| §5.3 | a payment refusal ends the turn once, in the vendor's words | `internal/provider/payment_refusal_test.go` — zero waits, terminal, not paced; **and a control proving a plain 429 still paces and retries** |
| §8.6 | that refusal reaches the screen in the vendor's words, with no status code and no machinery vocabulary | `internal/tui3/paymentnote_test.go` — one composer for the connect row and the turn; the test forbids `error:`, `API error` and the number outright, and its third case proves an ordinary failure is **not** read as a payment refusal |
| §5.3 | a vendored row records what was observed, not what the survey guessed | `TestVendoredListingHintsAndProbeModelsMatchTheProviderSurvey` — Z.ai carries the date it was seen to answer; Moonshot says plainly that nobody has looked |

## An adversarial review round found nine blockers after the gates were green

Worth stating plainly, because it is the reason to trust the table above. Every gate passed and the feature still did not work: connecting a service and picking its model sent to the **old address with the old bearer**, and disconnecting relabelled the conversation while still talking to the service whose key had just been deleted. Both tests drove a `fakeAgent` and structurally could not see it. Also found and fixed: a first-run key that stopped reaching later child tasks (a regression on working behaviour), a redaction test that performed the registration production never performed, a vendor able to echo a submitted key into a visible sentence, a nil key-shape accepting a blank key against its own contract, a key-optional client failing in the tool loop, and a wire law that rejected eight exact spellings so `Key string` sailed past it. `REVIEW-FIXES-1.md` drove the fixes; the tests that missed each one now fail without it.

## A hand run of the real binary then found six more

The gates and the review were both green when a person drove the shipped binary under tmux against three real services — the default one, a real Ollama, and an OpenAI-shaped stub logging every request's path, model and bearer fingerprint. 24 checks: 15 passed, 6 failed, 2 partial.

**What it proved good:** connect-then-chat on both a real vendor and a stub, read off the host's own log; the adversarial 401 that echoes the submitted key renders `(the key you sent was [redacted])`; a 367-file sweep across five HOMEs, both stub logs and the trace records found the keys only in the `config.json` files that hold them.

**What it found, and the worst of it is the phase's central claim.** With the conversation on a stub, the stub received **six unqualified default-service ids carrying the stub's bearer** — the reflex tier, the mastermind, careful work, small work, the worker. Fifteen sites called the conversation's retained client with `ai.WithModel(<role model>)`, which swaps the slug on the wire and keeps the address and the key. So a person who connects a gateway to try one model had their memory consolidation, planner and auditor sent there too. `Agent` now keeps a client per account and `completerFor` resolves from the model being called; a `go/ast` law confines `WithModel` to that door, because fifteen sites is fifteen chances to forget.

The other five: a connected service's models needed a restart to reach the picker; a "Something else" service listed two models and drew no group and no cache; the `is disconnected` line was never drawn because the settings place clipped the second line; an Ollama row said `via akashml`; and the status line dropped the service prefix.

**A second hand run, with both hosts recorded.** The default service was then put behind a recording proxy too, so "the crew went to the *right* place" became provable rather than merely unfalsified. Five of the seven were confirmed fixed; D-3 was partly fixed and had gone non-deterministic, D-2 was unchanged, and the fuller method found two more. Their causes were a **bypass** and a **process-global seam**, neither of which is a `WithModel` site — so the law added the round before was right and not sufficient. `completerFor` returned the conversation's client whenever `managedClient` was false, which every production child agent was; and `provider.NewClient` re-pointed the one process-wide lane sheet at whatever client was built last, which is why a disconnected service kept receiving endpoint probes signed with the key that had just been deleted.

**A third hand run** confirmed D-2, D-8 and D-9 fixed and D-3 deterministic for the task and worker children — and found the reflex tier still riding the conversation's client. `reflexClient` handed the raw completer to `reflex.Session.Bind`, which pins its tier model **inside `internal/reflex`**, so neither existing law could see it: the override was in another package and no agent was constructed. Resolution now happens per call *after* the tier is chosen, because the fallback's last rung is the conversation's own model and a bind-time choice would have relocated the bug rather than fixed it.

**Three routes to one defect, so the third fix is a law about the class**: `a.client` may be read only inside `clientdoor.go`, because a raw completer that leaves that file is one somebody can pin a model onto. It pulled eight further readers onto named doors, and the sweep it required also turned up a harness vision seam nobody had reported.

**This is the second time a fake made a test unable to fail.** The review round fixed the conversation's own client and the auxiliary doors kept the inherited behaviour, because both proving tests drove a `fakeAgent`. Every test added here drives a real `session.Agent` against real stub hosts and asserts which host received which model with which bearer.

## A live run against a real vendor account

A real Z.ai key, both hosts behind recording proxies. **Everything on the wire was right** — the chat, a tool call, `reasoning_content` folded rather than leaked, disconnect silence, secrecy, and the crew doors clean against a *real remote vendor* rather than a stub: Z.ai received `glm-4.5-flash` and nothing else while every OpenRouter id went to OpenRouter. It also settled cache states 3 and 4, which no earlier run had driven.

The account had no credit, and that exposed three faults in our own code. **We had encoded a survey's silence as a fact about the world**: `B-provider-landscape.md` lists Z.ai's `/models` as "no (undocumented)", the live endpoint answers 200 with ten models, and our row's one-token probe was the exact call an empty balance refuses — so a valid key was refused. Discovery now asks the service and the vendored `Listing` is only a hint; the same doubt applies to Moonshot, MiniMax and Qwen, whose rows the survey describes the same way. Z.ai's superseded probe model was corrected and Moonshot's was removed rather than replaced with a guess.

The other two: `refused that key` was the wrong sentence for a valid key on an empty account, and an "insufficient balance" 429 was retried four times over two minutes as *could not be reached*.

## Gates

Run in the worktree, `GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false -p=2`, `GOMAXPROCS=4` — the repository's documented constrained baseline.

```
go build ./... && go vet ./...                  clean
make test-quick                                 green
make test-laws                                  green — 65 files in 20 packages (base: 63 in 18)
go test ./internal/e2e/                         green (untagged needle gate)
internal/modelsource   0.3s    internal/config    82s
internal/catalog      0.08s    internal/router   180s
internal/trace        0.05s    internal/remote    21s
internal/provider       53s    internal/manual   1.5s
internal/session       247s    cmd/aforge         58s
internal/lane            7s    internal/reflex  0.003s
internal/paymentrefusal 0.002s internal/tui3     294s
make build                                      green
```

Re-run in full after the manual-test fixes and after `origin/dev` was merged twice (for #801 and #805). `dev` was merged rather than rebased onto, so the four absorbed fix branches' commits are carried unchanged rather than rewritten.

## Size

`bin/aforge` is 56,172,809 bytes. Against the merged base this branch started from (56,189,193) that is **+532,480 bytes, +0.95 %** — though `dev` has moved twice underneath since, so part of that is upstream's. No vendored catalog in this phase. `SIZE-BUDGET` is 54,600,000 and was already breached by 1,589,193 bytes on a clean `dev` before this branch added a byte (#724); it is **not** raised here, because that number is a reviewable decision that belongs with Phase 2's vendored-catalog question.

## Three deviations from the written spec, taken deliberately

1. **The catalog cache key is the pair (service, normalised base), not the service alone.** The spec argued for the service id so a region change would keep its cache. Keying on it alone would reintroduce #748's own bug for the default service on a custom base. The cost is that a region answer re-fetches once, which is correct — a region is a different account with a different listing.
2. **`ClientConfigFor` takes the service set instead of a key and a base.** #750 landed a door that still let a caller choose the account; the spec named this as the one thing Phase 1 could not work around.
3. **No entries were added to `internal/e2e/tuiwords_test.go`.** That table has a second gate — `TestEveryWordInTheTableIsWaitedForBySomething` reads the tagged tmux suite back and fails on any entry nothing waits for. A needle for this flow would need a tmux subtest driving a real second vendor, and no stub-service harness exists for one. An unwaited needle is exactly the rot that table prevents (#184). The strings are pinned by `internal/tui3`'s own tests, which run on every pull request. The two existing first-run needles are untouched and still match.

## Two failures I could not reproduce

An unconstrained full-suite run reported `TestTaskShortcutRemainsClickableWhenTheLastWorkerNeedsAttention/80` and `TestTheGuardSendsThePagesLineAndKeepsTheConversations`. Neither reproduced under the documented constrained baseline — `internal/session` passed at 232s alongside nine other packages, which is the condition they appeared in — and each passes in isolation. Recorded here rather than added to `.github/known-red.txt`, which is untouched.

## Left for Phase 2

Pricing: a direct call books `Cost == 0` today and that is correct here rather than an invented rate. The vendored models.dev catalog, per-service tiers and roles, coding plans (`Plan` and `KeyPrefix` are on the record but no shipped service sets either), and the Anthropic dialect. A tmux subtest for the connect flow, which is what would let the e2e needles land.

Part of the direct model services plan, phase one of five.

## What was wrong

The owner asked, in a real terminal, for "a card with a diagram block under each option" and saw no question. Measured on the Spark with that exact prompt on deepseek-v4-flash (via deepinfra): the model opens a quote after `"options":` and JSON-escapes the **rest of the argument object** into that string. The outer object arrives with `head/kind/options` only; `pick`, `reason`, `scope`, `stakes` are inside the string. The decoder refused each with `Invalid arguments: options takes a list`, the loop guard ended the turn, and nothing was drawn. Rarer shapes seen the same day: `"pick": 1` (bare key), a number in a `dimensions` cell (a map whose value type the schema never declared), a stray `]` after the tail's closing brace, and a leaked `<｜…｜>` control token plus prose after a complete list.

The `$ref`/`$defs` hypothesis was **not** the cause (dev alone passed a clean steer), but the reference is gone and a law now keeps it out.

## What changed

- **`internal/session/toolargs.go`** (the one decoder, no per-tool paths)
  - `unswallowTail`: a string field that is not JSON alone but closes into an object when put after `{"<field>":` is the object's swallowed tail; its fields are read, and what the model wrote at the top level is never overwritten.
  - `unwrapEncoded`: a string holding the wanted list/object is unwrapped once per level.
  - **The spill law**, stated once: inside a string a model wrapped by mistake, what follows the first complete value is not the value. Nothing is read out of the spill.
  - A number in a cell of a **text map** is its own spelling; a number where a named text argument is wanted (`bash {"command":17}`) stays refused.
  - A self-decoding type's own refusal passes through in the decoder's words.
- **`internal/session/question.go`**: `Pick.UnmarshalJSON` reads `1`/`"1"` as the key; the object form goes back through `coerceArgument`. `Question.Check` refuses an answer with no label by its number.
- **`internal/session/tools_ask.go`**: the evidence block is one constant spliced inline at both places; `dimensions` declares text values.
- **`TestEveryBeltSchemaIsWellFormedAndCarriesNoReference`** walks `offeredTools()` with `json.Valid` and refuses `$ref`/`$defs`. (My first splice had one brace too many; `load_capability` refused the questions group as malformed and the model answered in prose. Only a real-terminal drive caught it. The law catches it now.)
- **`internal/e2e`**: `TestQuestionsE2E/ACardWithABlockUnderEachAnswerArrivesWhole`, steered in the person's own words; the law is read off the journal (one `ask` the decoder read, blocks, zero argument refusals; a question-gate refusal is not counted), and a failed run keeps its journal under `$TMPDIR/aforge-e2e-journals/`.
- Manual `questions.md` lists the new refusal.

## Evidence (all on the Spark, deepseek-v4-flash, real tmux terminal)

| revision | person's prompt, first ask arrives whole | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dev (probe branch) | 1/2 | the miss: `options takes a list`, retry dropped the options, room drew an empty box |
| 77376f9 | 2/4 | misses: swallowed tail; `pick takes an object` |
| 2af8ea9 | 5/6 | miss: swallowed tail with a stray `]` |
| 9fef753 | 5/6 | miss: same `]` shape |
| ea9a78b | 4/6 | misses: pick named `adaptive-hrv` against keys 1–3 (question gate, model's own); complete list then a leaked control token |
| 2711b32 | 6/6 | |
| bb92c0d (rebased on dev) | 2/3 | miss: a diagram's line breaks escaped as backslash + literal newline inside the wrapped string |
| **30fdf90 (this)** | **3/4** | miss: provider stall — `the reply kept going and never finished · asking again`, zero ask calls reached the journal (stream wall, #786's lane) |

Every journal a failed run kept (r4-1, r7-3, diag-150149) decodes on the final revision, with three answers each.

Suites on the Spark (`GOMAXPROCS=4 GOFLAGS=-p=2 -count=1`) on 30fdf90: `internal/session` ok 201s, `internal/e2e` (untagged) ok, `internal/manual` ok, `internal/remote` ok, `internal/tui3` ok 422s (tui3 untouched by this PR).

## The measured failure

Task node 1 of conversation `57d51779f63ac603`, 2026-09-10. A task sat in `sizing
the work` for 3m20s showing one word, then admitted two parts called `read
seam.start in` and `part 2`.

Journal `tasks/20260910-125816.380416_1.jsonl`:

- 12:58:18 — rung 1, `z-ai/glm-5.3` via Reka. First token at 1.0s. Still
  streaming at 90s. Cut: `context deadline exceeded`.
- 12:59:48 — rung 2, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731`. First token at 4.8s.
  Still streaming at 90s. Cut.
- 13:01:18 — the review "unreached" twice; the fail-open road admitted the
  sketch's parts on a line reading `decision: admitted` with no error — byte for
  byte the row a reviewed admission writes.

The ninety seconds was arithmetic: the errand ladder divided the caller's three
minutes between its two rungs and armed each share as a hard
`context.WithTimeout`. **A wall clock cannot tell a rung that is silent from a
rung that is answering, so it killed both** — the exact shape #786 fixed for a
person's turn and left errands out of.

## One recovery machine

**The patience is the errand's, not each rung's.** `callRoleChecked` bounds the
whole errand once at `roles.PatienceFor(role)`. What ends a rung that is not
working is the guard the turn already runs under: `Client.CompleteWithMessages`
serves every completion over the event stream whether or not an observer is
attached, so an errand inherits streamguard's first-delta bound, its mid-stream
gap and its pace-re-arming wall for nothing. **No `internal/provider` change was
needed** — the seam already existed.

What is kept of the arithmetic is a **reserve, not a share**: each rung still
below the one being asked is owed a fifth of what remains (`errandReserve`), so
the first of two rungs gets four fifths rather than half. It exists for the one
shape the guard cannot see — a gateway that answers a whole completion in one
piece and arms no stall watch (`completionInOnePiece`) — and it sits far above
the guard's own five-minute wall floor, so it never cuts a stream the guard was
happy with. `TestAWedgedFirstRungLeavesTheFallThroughTimeToAnswer` is what pins
it.

**The ladder hops on #794's own verdict.** `readErrandFailure` asks
`readLadderFailure` with `transportLadder{fallback: a rung remains}` — the fact
only the ladder has — so `ActionHop` moves it on and `ActionGiveUp` ends it.
`ActionRetry` is read against the **errand's** cap rather than the model's:
`errandTriesPerRung` is one, because the rung below is a better move than another
try and is reached at once with no backoff, so a retry with a rung below is this
ladder's hop. And one failure the taxonomy cannot decide alone — everything
unplaceable lands in `Work`, right for a 4xx that named **no** upstream and wrong
for `that model is down` — so the doomed request is recognised by the evidence,
narrowly, and every other work verdict still falls through one rung.

> Same-rung retry needs the transport budget to be the caller's, which
> `internal/taxonomy` does not take yet: with `allowed=4` it fires on the first
> failure, and a Spark run named six suites for it — the naming job (which
> already has its own retry ladder in `title.go` and cannot see between an
> errand's attempts), both halves of the unattended door's turn, the wedged-rung
> law, and `TestAnErrandsDeadlineIsRetriedOnceThenDroppedWithItsClassOnTheFile`,
> which pins two requests for a two-rung ladder. `taxonomy.ActionHop`'s own
> comment says the cap belongs to whoever holds the chain; `errandTriesPerRung`
> is that cap, and it is a one-line change the day the budget can travel.

**The division review keeps no bound of its own.** `divideReviewPatience = 3 *
time.Minute` is gone; the reading is bounded by its role's tier — ten minutes for
the mastermind — because any figure under the guard's five-minute wall floor is a
guillotine rather than a bound.

**A fail-open admission records why there was no reading.** The word stays
`admitted`; `journalDivision.Error` carries the `unreached…` / `unparseable`
reason, in the field a refusal already writes it in.

**The legend cuts at an inline label as well as at punctuation.** `**A:** …
**B:** …` on one line left A's clause swallowing the whole of it.
`legendInlineLabel` handles `**B:**`, `B:`, `B —`, `B - ` and `(B)`, and demands
a separator after a single letter so `(wired at line 519…)` and `folder-pick`
are not labels.

## And the person can see it

While the reading runs the row under `sizing the work` says, in order:

```
asking z-ai/glm-5.3 · 1 of 2
z-ai/glm-5.3 did not answer in time · asking deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731
nobody answered · going with the parts as drawn
```

A one-rung ladder counts nothing. It rides `EventTaskPhase`'s existing `Text`,
which `internal/tui3`'s `taskphase.go` already draws under the phase line as
`phaseFinding` — **no surface change was needed**, confirmed by reading it.

## Tests

`internal/session/errand_recovery_test.go`. The ladder tests assert on the clock
each call was **handed**, which no machine's load can turn into the other
reading, as well as on the behaviour: a rung still answering past the old even
split is not cut; a rung the guard cut leaves the next one the remainder; a
request no endpoint will serve stops the ladder; `that model is down` still falls
through; an errand whose every rung fails ends inside the caller's patience; a
division admitted with nobody reading it says so on the record; the sizing row's
three lines in order; and the exact legend from the measured run names all four
parts while the shapes the legend already read still read.

`TestTheReadingThatSizesTheWorkIsDrawnAndThenClears` is updated: the reading is
no longer silent under its phase word.

Spark, `b271dbe72`: `internal/session` ok 199.3s · `internal/manual` ok ·
`internal/e2e` ok · `internal/taxonomy` ok · `internal/provider` ok 90.7s.

## The screen this came from

Measured 2026-09-10, conversation `57d51779f63ac603`. A turn ran two bash calls that both came back within the second, then failed the follow-up request four times (502, 429, 429, 429) between 13:00:17 and 13:01:32 and gave up. Two minutes later the conversation showed: the person's message, a step captioned `running 2 commands`, its two rows, and blank. The owner's words were "things are just stuck".

Three defects, one story.

## What changed

**A finished batch is never captioned as running.** `deriveCaptions` decided the words before it decided whether the batch was still open. It now reads liveness first, and a batch whose every row has closed takes the past through one table (`captionPastVerbs`): `ran 2 commands`, `read 3 files in internal/tui3`, `searched the tree`, `edited 2 files and ran the suite`, `built`, `listed github issues`. A title the model narrated itself is left exactly as written — only the floor aforge composes from the calls changes tense.

**Every retry, hop and give-up draws one row in the feed.** New `internal/tui3/failurerow.go` holds a `failure` struct and one composer, `failureRow`. Three doors compose from it and nowhere else spells these sentences:

| door | what it draws |
| --- | --- |
| `feed.retry` (the conversation) | the row for a request being asked again, or moving |
| `app.roomEvent` (a node's page) | the same rows, from the same reducer |
| `app.waitingWords` (the status line) | the short form, via `failureDetail` |

```
· the model went quiet · asking again · 2 of 4
· the reply lost its thread · moving to gpt-5-mini
· gave up after 4 tries · API error (429) rate limited
```

`retryFailure` reads `session.RetryNews` (#794) — `Reason`, `Next`, `Attempt`, `Attempts` — and falls back to `Event.Text` only for an engine that sends no parts, which is a `--host` link to an older build. It is the ONE place in the package that reads a retry event's shape. The reasons are the engine's own spelling (`transportWords`, `cutWords`) and are drawn as they stand; this package composes only the connective words `asking again`, `moving to `, `gave up`.

**A hop draws no arithmetic.** The count is the patience of the model being *left*; `moving to gpt-5-mini · 4 of 4` would read as the new model's.

**The give-up is gated on there having been a struggle.** `gave up after N tries · …` is drawn when a turn that was asked again runs out; a turn that failed on its first and only attempt keeps the plain `error: …` line.

## The finding on the missing error note

It was drawn all along. The reproduction (`TestARetriedTurnThatGivesUpSaysBothInTheConversation`) drives `EventToolEnd` ×2, `EventRetrying` ×3 and `EventError` through `app.event` and finds the note in the rendered frame — no lost note, no `a.gen` mismatch, no echo onto home's message line. What was actually missing: the three identical retries collapsed to one row by the note-repeat rule, the give-up line spoke the engine's arithmetic, and the step above it claimed to be running.

A screen that is genuinely blank after a page switch is a different fact and is outside this change: the surface's notes are surface-side and are never journaled, so a conversation re-attached and replayed from the engine's transcript rebuilds without them.

## Where this does NOT overlap with #796

#796's sizing lines (`asking z-ai/glm-5.3 · 1 of 2`, `<model> did not answer in time · asking <next>`, `nobody answered · going with the parts as drawn`) ride the node's **phase notice** and are drawn under the phase word by `taskphase.go`. These rows ride the node's **event stream**. An errand sends no events at all (`internal/session/auxiliary.go`), so the two cannot say the same thing on one screen. The verbs differ for the reason they differ: an errand's ladder asks a *different* model at each rung, so it says `asking <model>`; a turn's ladder asks the same one, so it says `asking again`. Written down in `room.go` where a wave that wires an errand into the stream will read it.

## What is left out, and why

A node's page draws these rows from its **live** lane. It cannot draw them from a **replayed** journal: `internal/session/sessionfile.go` drops `error` lines on purpose, and `session.Record` carries no field for them, so a room opened after the failure still shows nothing. This lane may not edit `internal/session`; the follow-up is a `Record` field (or a `DisplayEntry` role) for journaled failures.

One small thing for #794's file: `retryNews` fills `Reason` with the single-attempt spelling even on a hop, so a hop row reads `the model went quiet mid-reply · moving to X` where the engine's own sentence said "kept going quiet". `transportKeptWords` already exists for exactly that; a one-line change in `session.retryNews` when `next != ""` would give the row back its "kept".

## Manual

- `screen.md` — a new section on past and present on a step's title, with the whole table; and the `what does "trying again" mean` section corrected to the rows that are actually drawn.
- `models-and-cost.md` — a new section on the retry rows, `gave up`, moving to another model, and a request that did not answer in time; and nine stale code blocks corrected.
- `reading-a-task-page.md` — the room's copy of the same rows.

## Tests

`internal/tui3/failurerow_test.go`: the caption tense both ways and its table; the measured event sequence asserted on the rendered frame; the parts road and the sentence fallback; the same failure rendered through the conversation and a node's page asserted **identical**; a node's page drawing two failure rows instead of `roomYetWord`; the composer's own shapes; the status-line detail off the same struct. Four existing tests were updated honestly where they pinned the present tense on a batch that had closed.

Spark, `5195169d8` / `1f5627601`: `internal/tui3` 290s, `internal/manual`, `internal/e2e` — green except four tests already red on `origin/dev` @ `069038e4d` (#798, owned elsewhere): `TestEnterConnectsOpenRouterInTheBrowserAndHandsTheKeyToThisProcess`, `TestAJobsLogReaderTakesOneLastReadingAfterTheJobEnds`, `TestAPathInTheBoxIsNeverChipped`, `TestAnAbsolutePathDoesNotHoldTheCommandListOpen`. The tmux suite against a real model: `--- PASS: TestTUIE2E/a_real_conversation_and_its_home_card (6.34s)`.

body:
## What was wrong

A chat turn on `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` took one 502 and three 429s between 13:00:17 and 13:01:32 on 2026-09-10 and ended. The journal reads:

```
{"class":"transport","reason":"the endpoint refused","action":"give_up","attempt":4}
```

then `EventError` with `after 3 retries: …`. In that same minute `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` was answering every task-node call in the same session. **The fallback chain was never asked.**

The model hop was reachable only from the stream-cut branch (`provider.CutFrom(err)`). The refusal branch walked `failureLimits().TransportAttempts` with `backoffWait` and then returned. So a turn had two answers to "this model's budget is spent" — one that moved and one that stopped — depending on which kind of failure happened to arrive.

## What this does

**One exit from exhaustion, decided in one place.** The decision moved into the policy object that already answers "what was that failure worth" — `internal/taxonomy`:

- `ActionHop` joins `ActionRetry` and `ActionGiveUp`.
- `transportPolicy.Decide` walks **one budget with two kinds of spending**: an outright failure spends a rung off `Limits.TransportAttempts` with its doubling wait; a cut stream spends a shorter allowance (`SilentCutAttempts`, `BlindCutAttempts`, `DegenerateCutAttempts`) with no wait at all, because the request was served and the *reply* came apart.
- The difference between moving and stopping is `Evidence.FallbackAvailable` — the caller's fact. The policy never names a model.

The turn loop's two roads are folded into one. `cutBudget` and its three constants are gone; the loop reads a verdict and acts on it. A cut and a refusal now differ only in the evidence they arrive carrying.

`movesForFailure` (a task node's tier purchase) already routes through the boundary and is deliberately untouched — that is a *tier* decision, not a chain hop.

## The surface can draw one honest row

`EventRetrying` grows `Event.Retry *RetryNews`:

| field | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Model` | the model whose attempt just failed |
| `Attempt`, `Attempts` | how far into *that model's* patience — the policy's number, not a constant a surface holds |
| `Reason` | why, in the person's words (`the model would not take the request`) — never the journal's `the endpoint refused` |
| `Next` | the model being moved to; **empty on an ordinary retry**, which is the distinction a surface could not draw before |

It is filled on **every** `EventRetrying` the loop sends, cut notices included. `Text` is still the whole sentence, so a surface that reads only `Text` is unchanged. It rides the remote link under its own json key, and a peer built before it exists sees none of it.

## The exits that must not move, and do not

- `provider.IsConnectionUnavailable` — returns as it always did.
- `RefusalFrom(err).OurRequest()` — a 4xx that named no upstream is our own bytes; no retry, no move.
- context overflow and non-retryable shapes.
- `--one-model` — now refused in the loop as well as at the door that empties the chain, so the promise holds against any completer.
- A strict lane pin is untouched: it is a person's answer about a *machine*, and each model carries its own.

## Tests

- `internal/taxonomy`: a spent ladder gives up alone and moves with a model in hand; a move buys no tier, ends no turn and waits for nothing; each cut shape spends its own allowance and ends the same three ways.
- `internal/session`: four refusals then an answer on the fallback — the move is announced with `Retry.Next`, the four journal rows are all on the model that failed and numbered 1..4, the last reads `hop`, and the sealed turn names the model that answered. A walked-out chain names every model tried. `--one-model` never moves. Our own bytes return at once.
- `internal/remote`: the payload crosses the link, and an older peer's retry arrives with none.
- The manual page that said `never moves your model` is gone, replaced by what the turn now does with the three sentences it actually spells.

## Evidence

`make test-laws` green locally (18 packages). `go test ./internal/e2e/` untagged green. Full `./internal/taxonomy/ ./internal/session/ ./internal/provider/ ./internal/remote/ ./internal/manual/` on the Spark — result in a comment below.

body:
## What was measured

A chat turn on `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (conversation `57d51779f63ac603`) died on
2026-09-10 after four transport attempts: one 502 from DeepInfra, then three 429s served by
**Io Net** at 13:00:39, 13:01:04 and 13:01:32. Every one of the three arrived **inside an
already-open HTTP 200 stream** — the journal's rows say status 200 and
`API error (429): Provider returned error (via Io Net)`.

The pacing note lived on the status path alone (`retry.go` read `response.StatusCode`), so a
429 inside a 200 reached **no ledger at all**: not the pace, not the strike. The next encode
carried the same preferences and the router handed the request back to the same saturated
pool, three times in ninety-three seconds.

## What is true now

- **One door.** `Client.refuseLane` is the only place a refusal becomes a ledger fact —
  paced, struck, or nothing — and both transports reach it through the same
  `Client.refuseUpstream`. A structural test (`go/ast`, so it is on `make test-laws`) fails
  the build if a second writer ever appears.
- **A 429 is a class, not an absence.** `refusalPaced` joins the refusal object: a 429 that
  names its pool — in `error.metadata.provider_name`, or by the stream's own `provider`
  chunk — paces that lane for the wait the provider asked for (five minutes when it named
  none), so every request encoded after it routes around the pool instead of queueing
  behind it. The call that drew the 429 still waits out its own retries.
- **The served name is stamped at the door**, before anything reads the refusal, so
  `RefusalFrom(err)` — and through it `internal/taxonomy`'s `Evidence`, read in
  `internal/session/taxonomy_boundary.go` — sees the same status *and* provider whether the
  refusal came as a status or in-stream. No second reader is needed downstream.
- **An account-wide 429 is unchanged**: it names nobody, implicates no machine, and is
  waited out rather than multiplied across machines.
- `retry.go`'s `pacedProviderName` is deleted. `apiError` already reads `provider_name` for
  both transports; two decoders of one sentence is how the paths came to disagree.

Not touched: the session loop's retry count and model hop (`internal/session/loop.go`, lane
B), and `streamguard.go`/`armwatch.go`/`patience.go`/`call.go`/`stream.go` (lane C).

## Tests

- `TestAPacedPoolIsRoutedAroundHoweverThe429Arrived` — **one table, run twice**: as an HTTP
  429 and as an SSE error frame inside a 200. It asserts the next encoded request carries
  the pool in `provider.ignore` and off `provider.order`, and that the surfaced error carries
  status 429 and the provider name on both paths. With the door's paced branch disabled,
  three of its six rows go red.
- `TestOneDoorWritesEveryRefusalIntoTheLedger` — the structural law.
- Full `./internal/provider/` and `./internal/session/` on the Spark, `-count=1`.

## Manual

`internal/manual/chat/lanes.md` gains **"When a machine is too busy — a rate limit, too many
requests, a 429, and how long aforge stays away from it"**: what is stepped around, for how
long, that it counts wherever the message arrived, and that an account-wide limit is waited
out instead.

> **Stacked on #790.** Base is `chore/remove-v2-remnants`, so this diff shows
> only the v1 window. Merge #790 first, or hold this one independently — that is
> why it is a separate pull request.

## The shape of it: 111 lines move, 36,037 go

`internal/tui` (32,669 lines) and `internal/command` (3,368) have been
unreachable from every shipped `main` for weeks, held up by **two thin edges**:

- `internal/command`'s only non-test importer is `cmd/aforge/chat.go`, which names
  exactly four package symbols: `command.NewMediaModels`, `command.LoadPrefs`,
  `command.AttachmentStoreRoot`, `command.NewSessionID`.
- `internal/tui`'s only non-test importer is `internal/command`, and that edge
  carries **no behaviour** — ten data types and two `var _` interface assertions.

So this extracts **111 lines** into a new `cmd/aforge/chatprefs.go`, rewires
`chat.go` in three places, and deletes both packages. **108 files changed, 161
insertions, 37,236 deletions.**

The blank identifier is why this looked alive for so long:
`var _ tui.Commander = (*Commander)(nil)` is not a caller, it is a promise about
a shape — and read as a declaration it keeps every type it names looking
reachable. Any name-based dead-code pass has to special-case `_`.

## Four symbols from the moved ranges were deliberately left behind

Moving them would have moved dead code into a live package, against CLAUDE.md's
"a capability that cannot work is absent, not broken":

| Symbol | Its only callers |
| --- | --- |
| `fallbackModels` | `Commander.Models` (`command.go:400`) |

`loadChatPrefs`, `attachmentStoreRoot`, `newSessionID` — so **no call site
changes** and no name forwards to itself.

```

Three hunks, none between 1000 and 1100.

The rule was **the code under test decides.** A test whose subject survives is
re-pointed; a test whose subject is `*command.Commander` cannot be, because the
subject is what is being deleted.

**Re-pointed:** `TestEveryChatPreferenceIsFrontedByASettingsRow` — a reflection
law over `Prefs`' fields against the rows `config.NewSettings` builds. Both
halves are live; `Prefs` just moved. Its two exemption comments stop citing
`internal/tui2/modelui`, `internal/tui2/chat` and `internal/command`'s
`CurrentModel`; the reasons themselves are unchanged and still true.

**Kept whole:** `chat_test.go`'s other **28** tests — the delivery gate,
learned-facts parsing, the consolidator, reflex envelopes, resident briefs, the
unasked gate, budget-stopped partials. That is live `aforge do` behaviour that
was only ever wearing a v1 driver, and deleting the file would have been the one
real regression in this wave. Only `TestNodeTraceWindowStartsOnALineBoundary`
goes with the trace reader. (`command.Seq` at `chat_test.go:467` is a field on a
local variable named `command`, not the package — it stays.)

**Moved, not deleted:** `voiceRoundTripFunc`, a plain `http.RoundTripper`
adapter that lived in `voice_models_test.go` and is used by
`context_budget_test.go`.

Six behaviours have no current-surface test. They are not regressions — the code
that implemented them is gone, and v3 has its own doors — but if v3's
follow-work/override model preferences, its voice spend ledger or its `/budget
default` and `/budget unlimited today` forms are meant to be pinned, they need
tests of their own. That is a decision worth making knowingly rather than
discovering later.

## The worker trace now has no reader

`Commander.NodeTraceSince` and `NodeTraceTail` were the **only** production
callers of `exec.TracePath` in the module. `internal/tui3` and
`internal/session` contain no reference to it at all — v3 never read a worker's

After this change `internal/exec/executor.go` still **writes** those files and
nothing in production reads them; `exec.TracePath` survives with only its own
test. Not a regression, but a fact the owner should hold: either v3 grows a
reader, or the trace is write-only telemetry whose writer earns its own audit.
`command.go:917-940` documented a repair to exactly this reader, so it is worth
saying out loud that the empty-feed defect it describes cannot recur — there is
no feed.

`internal/tui/charmbubbles/` was the `replace` target for
`github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles`, and its only importers were
`internal/tui/model.go` and `internal/tui/settings.go`. The `replace` and the

`internal/iconlaw`'s `surfaces` drops `"../tui"` — and its comment said "A

body:
**Stacks on #789** (`fix/question-pointer`) and will be rebased onto `dev` once that merges.

The owner opened a question out on 2026-09-10 and reported two things about the page (`internal/tui3/questionroom.go`, the page `o` opens): "once its opened the layout org and everything seems really bad and no arrow or click or bugs please clean all those", and "make sure there is some textual hierarchy in design in options like the same line and next line in options look same and a bit weird".

Both were true. The foot said `[←→] choose` and neither arrow moved anything on the page; no key opened or folded a section but `o`; nothing on it answered to a mouse at all; and an open answer drew its body, its consequence, the asker's reason and what would change its mind as four identical grey rows at one indent — one of which read `would switch if If you are targeting…`, because the model's sentence was capitalised and the prefix is a clause.

### The pointer

- `↑`/`↓` walk the answers. The foot names **that** pair now (`[↑↓] choose`): this form's answers stand in a column of sections, and the pair it was naming walked nothing.
- `→` opens the answer under the pointer, `←` folds it. They state what they want rather than toggling, so holding one down is safe. Where the question carries a shape of its own — a dial, a hole with choices — the side arrows are still that shape's.
- `enter` takes the answer the pointer is on, which is #789's law arriving on the page. It costs nothing on a fresh room: the room opens standing on the asker's pick, so `enter` straight away still takes the recommendation.
- **A click on an answer's row** moves onto it and opens it; a **second click on that same row** is `enter`. One press to read, one to decide — a page where the first click answered would answer with evidence somebody had not read. Only an answer's own row answers to the mouse, and it is the only row that lights under the pointer (hover.go's law); its body, its diagrams and your own notes are prose.

### The hierarchy

Three tiers, and every row says which it is:

- the **label** — bold in the question hue, exactly as the card already spells an answer's word; it was the body's own ink, so a heading and its paragraph were one column of identical grey
- the **body** — the prose ink
- the **asides** — all dim, each behind its own word: `then ·` what taking it would leave true, `why this one ·` the asker's reason, `would switch if` what would change its mind
- one blank row closes an open answer, so the next label is not merely a different indent

`would switch if If you are targeting…` is gone: a leading `if` the reader is about to read twice is dropped and the opening capital lowered, with a word whose second letter is also a capital (`SQLite`, `HRV`) left alone.

### The evidence

An answer's own blocks stay under that answer at its body's indent, with a blank row above each. The question's own `Attach` is now **one dim-titled section** — `what it showed you` — above the answers, indented under its title, rather than a run of unowned pictures starting at the gutter after them.

### And one safety fix found on the way

Two tests in this package were already red on `fix/question-pointer`, and one of them was red for a reason: `enter` now takes the answer the pointer is on, and the pointer started on the first answer of a **consent gate** — so on the gate for `rm -rf *`, `enter` meant `allow once`. Measured, not reasoned.

`questionPointerStart` now opens on the answer that loses nothing wherever nobody but a person may answer — a confirmation, an irreversible act, or a permission that is not cheap to take back. That condition is `questionHandsOnly`, which is the predicate `d`/`D` were already reading, lifted out so the two cannot disagree. Every other kind still opens on its first answer: on a landing row or a proposal the safe answer is the one that does nothing, and a pointer parked there would make `enter` mean "no" on every card. Both stale tests are rewritten to the law that is now true.

### Also

- `internal/manual/chat/questions.md` — two new sections under the room's page (`Moving around the page — the arrows, and clicking an answer`, `What each line under an answer means`), the page's own list grew the evidence section, and the key table says what the arrows and `o` do inside the page.
- `docs/design/questions/DESIGN.md` — the **room** bullet and the **HUE** law.

### Checks

- `make test-laws` green
- `go test ./internal/manual/ ./internal/e2e/ -count=1` green
- full `./internal/tui3/` on the Spark — result posted as a comment
- driven as a person in tmux against a real model — screens posted as a comment

## What this removes

Everything the v2 chat surface left behind that nothing has drawn with since it
went on 2026-08-31 (entry 111). **65 files, 17,906 lines deleted; 96 files
changed, 177 insertions, 18,713 deletions.** No behaviour changes.

| What | Lines | Why it is dead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `internal/tui2/modelui` — the chip and the picker, 6 files + 6 tests | 4,773 | the only symbol any package outside `internal/tui2` names from `modelui` is `ModelWord`, in `word.go`, called once from `internal/tui3/spendplace.go`. `word.go` and `word_test.go` stay. |
| `internal/tui2` root — the shell, compositor, layout solver, panes, placeholder, capability probe, OSC writer, 19 files | 5,576 | its only non-test importer was `modelui/picker.go`, deleted above |
| `internal/tui2/blocks` — the whole rendering engine | 6,864 | `internal/tui3` and `cmd` never imported it. After the two rows above its only non-test importer was `tokens/styler.go`, and only for two `var _` assertions and the four methods written to satisfy them |
| `internal/tui2/tokens/breakpoints.go` + tests | 442 | after the rows above, no symbol declared in it is named from outside `internal/tui2`. `ContextToken`'s one external caller was `modelui/chip.go:162`; the footer registry, `FitFooter`, `SplitDiffAtWidth` and `HUDRowCap` had none |
| `internal/tui2/tokens/identity.go` + test | 251 | `IdentityFor`, `IdentityNext`, `AssignIdentities` have no production caller anywhere in the module — a dead file inside a live package |

Also removed from `tokens/styler.go`: `Paint`, `PaintGlyph`, `PaintIdentity`,
`Token(state, hue)` and the two `blocks` interface assertions. Nothing outside
`internal/tui2` called any of them. `PaintToken`, `PaintOn`, `PaintRowOn`, `Fg`
and `Glyph` — what v3 paints through — are untouched.

**What stays, and why:** `internal/tui2/tokens` is the icon and colour
vocabulary v3 draws with and carries its own law; `internal/tui2/prose` renders
v3's markdown; `internal/tui2/reltime` is v3's and `internal/subharness`'s; and
`modelui/word.go` holds `ModelWord`. `internal/tui`, `internal/command`,
`internal/head` and `internal/resident` are **not touched** by this pull request.

Reachability was measured file by file and symbol by symbol, not package by
package: every one of `internal/tui2`'s packages is package-reachable from
`cmd/aforge`, so package reachability was the wrong question.

## Two laws re-pointed rather than deleted

The `blocks` removal touches six `tokens` test files. Assertions that only
pinned a `tokens` constant to its deliberate twin in `blocks`, and tests of the
four deleted methods, go with their subject. Two that were laws about **tokens**
and merely used `blocks` to build a sample are re-pointed:

- the tier width-parity golden (`parity_test.go`) now composes its sample rows
  from `Glyph` and `PaintToken` instead of `blocks.Header`/`Disclose`/`CutRule`.
  The golden is regenerated with `-update-glyph-parity` and still records every
  codepoint, so the shapes stay reviewable in the diff.
- `TestUpgradeChromeIsAnExplicitDoor` uses token literals.

`TestPaintNeverChangesWidth` survives as `TestPaintOnNeverChangesWidth` and
`TestTierChangesTheGlyphAndNothingElse` as `TestTierDoesNotChangeTokenPainting`.
`TestPaintResolvesTheAxes` is gone, and what it asserted — the state × hue
composition rule — is still checked by `state_test.go`'s `TestHueAlwaysWins` and
`TestStateAxisPicksTheTier` against `ResolveToken` directly.

## One row of the plan was dropped, and why

The plan behind this wave also listed `internal/head/absorb.go` and
`internal/head/aside.go` as dead. **`absorb.go` is not:**
`internal/head/head.go:353-354` calls `deliveredRow` and
`h.absorbDeliveryBounded`, both declared there, so deleting it would not
compile. `aside.go`'s `Head.Ask` genuinely has no production caller, but it
belongs to the same conversational `Head` cohort that is a separate follow-up,
and removing it alone would gut `aside_test.go` and assertions in three more
head tests for no gain. **`internal/head` is untouched here.**

## No open pull request touches any deleted path

Checked against all 36 open pull requests. `internal/tui2` appears in none of
them. #693 touches `internal/lane` but only `choose.go`, `frontier.go`,
`workload.go` and `unknownanswer_test.go` — not `structure_test.go`. #740, #775
and #783 touch `CLAUDE.md`, at hunks near lines 234, 224 and 170; the one line
edited here is line 12.

## Gates — run in this worktree, results verbatim

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go build ./...` | pass, exit 0, no output |
| `go vet ./...` | pass, exit 0, no output |
| `make fmt-check` | pass, exit 0, no output |
| `make test-laws` | pass — `laws: 63 files in 18 packages`, 18 × `ok` |
| `go test ./internal/manual/` | pass — `ok … internal/manual` |
| `go test -run 'Manual' ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/` | pass — `ok` both |
| `go generate ./internal/manual && go test -tags=aforge_packed_manual ./internal/manual` | pass — `ok … 1.495s`, and `git diff --exit-code` clean afterwards |
| `make test-packed-manual` | pass — `ok … internal/manual 1.520s` |
| touched packages, the CI shape: `make test TEST_FLAGS='-count=1 -p 1' PKGS='./internal/tui2/modelui ./internal/tui2/tokens ./internal/lane'` | pass — `ok` ×3 (`lane 7.368s`) |
| `go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/tui3/` | pass — `ok … internal/tui3 424.724s` |
| `go test -count=1 ./internal/e2e/` (untagged) | pass — `ok … 0.190s` |
| `go build -tags=aforge_packed_manual ./...` | pass, exit 0, no output |
| `make check` | running at the time of opening; the result is posted as a comment |

`.github/known-red.txt`'s single entry
(`TestEveryLockInTheGuardedTreeUnlocksFromADefer`) is the only red anywhere, and
it is skipped by the same target CI uses. No other test failed. `SIZE-BUDGET` is
a ceiling, so a smaller binary cannot fail `size`; the number is left alone
deliberately — lowering it after a deletion is a policy choice for the owner,
not a gate.

## Follow-ups this uncovered

- `internal/tui2/tokens`' exported `Hue`, `State`, `ResolveToken`, `Identity`,
  `IdentityCount` and `BandFor` now have no caller outside the package. They are
  public API of a live package with their own laws, so nothing was removed —

  anywhere) needs a `go/types` dead set, and
  `internal/registry/registry_test.go` parses `internal/head/toolbelt.go` **by
  path**, so that law has to move before `toolbelt.go` can.

Five stale artifacts, none of which any open pull request touches. Nothing here
changes behaviour: no Go file, no module file, no manual page, no slash command,
no default. Every path was checked against the paths of all 38 open pull
requests before it was touched, and **no open pull request touches any of
these paths**.

## What this removes and changes

1. **`harness-design` — a tracked binary at the repository root, 9,245,154 bytes.**
   An unstripped ARM64 ELF with `debug_info`, committed 2026-08-17 and never
   read: no Makefile target, no workflow, no script and no Go file names the
   root file. Every other mention of the name is the source directory
   `cmd/harness-design`, which `go build ./cmd/harness-design` produces on
   demand. It also carried a build machine's home paths inside it.
2. **`harnesses/` — 8 files, 24,052 bytes, tracked against the ignore rule that
   was meant to exclude them.** `.gitignore:16` already ignores `harnesses/`;
   these page and run JSON files were committed before that line arrived, so
   the rule never applied to them. The directory is an *output* of
   `cmd/harness-design`, and the only thing that names it is that tool's own
   comment. The store the running program reads is `~/.aforge/harnesses/` — a
   different place, and untouched here.
3. **`docs/BRANCH-ARCHIVE.md` — 4,831 bytes, 66 lines, last written 2026-08-30.**
   Nothing links to it, and it disagrees with `CLAUDE.md` about the branch
   model: it calls `master` the release line, says `dev` is cut from `staging`,
   and presents per-person `santosh/<topic>` branches and a personal worktree
   path as the convention.
4. **`scripts/frame.sh:12` — one line.** `ROOT` defaulted to one person's
   working copy, so on any other machine the script looked for `bin/aforge`
   under a directory that does not exist. It now defaults to
   `ROOT="${ROOT:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}"`, so `OUT` and `BIN`
   resolve inside whichever clone it is run from. Setting `ROOT`, `OUT` or `BIN`
   still overrides, exactly as before, and `bash -n` is clean.
5. **`audit-notes/headless-regression-audit.md` — three lines redacted.** Both
   "how to reproduce" sections spelled out a rented pod's address and port and
   the filename of the private key that opens it. They now read
   `root@<pod-host> -p <port>` and `~/.ssh/<key>`. Nothing else in the file
   changed; the paths on the pod are left as written so the account still reads
   as a whole.

Five commits, one per concern.

## Owed, and deliberately not done here

## What a person can now do

With `/model` open, press **`ctrl+r`** to fetch today's model list from the router, so a model a provider shipped this morning shows up now instead of after the 24-hour cache runs out. The picker keeps working while the fetch runs. The conversation gets `models · 612 · 9 new · a, b, c` (or `models · 612 · nothing new`). If the fetch fails, the list stays exactly as it was and the note is `could not fetch the model list · <reason>`. `aforge models --refresh` does the same from a script.

## The rules, one line each

1. **Key:** `ctrl+r` = `refreshModelsKey` (internal/tui3/modelrefresh.go). It is free inside the picker, which owns the keyboard before spell-it-out or `/files` reveal are read.
2. **Named:** the placeholder gains `ctrl+r refresh` between `ctrl+t effort` and `enter · esc` (on 60 cells `enter · esc` drop first). The empty list reads `no model matches · ctrl+r fetches the newest list`.
3. **Door:** `tui3.Options.RefreshModels`. Nil means absent: the key does nothing and no line names it. Both chat doors (local and `--host`) wire it through `v3ModelShelf`, one atomic pointer refilled by `catalog.Refresh`, which also writes `~/.aforge/v3/models.json`.
4. **While running:** the list's first line reads `fetching the newest list…`. The fetch runs as a tea.Cmd under the catalog's 15 s ceiling, every key still works, and a second press does nothing.
5. **Landed:** the list is re-ranked with the filter kept and the cursor back on the model in use. The note shows the count, the number new and up to three new ids. A model that vanished is never mentioned.
6. **Failed:** the shelf and the picker are unchanged, the note is one line with the transport's own reason, and the key is offered again.
7. **Script:** `aforge models --refresh` makes the same fetch, writes both caches, and prints the same failure sentence on stderr.

The vision gate and the task-model list also read the shelf. Without that, a model picked from a freshly refreshed list would be refused photos as unknown.

`catalog.Refresh` is `Load` plus the fetch error that `Load` drops on purpose.

## The defect, measured 2026-09-10 (the owner's own session)

A task on `moonshotai/kimi-k3` asked for ONE self-contained HTML file (the existing one is 33 KB ≈ 9k tokens; the model was going for more). It ran 20+ minutes and produced nothing.

| attempt | lane | ran | output streamed before the cut | journal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | DigitalOcean | 2m30s | 5,510 tok (~37 tok/s, steady) | `the reply ran past 2m30s without finishing and was cut` |
| 2 | DeepInfra | 2m30s | 3,576 tok (~24 tok/s, steady) | same |
| 3 | Morph | 10m39s | 26,145 tok (~41 tok/s, steady) | `the reply ran past 10m39s without finishing and was cut` |
| hedge arm during 3 | – | – | 18,233 tok, discarded | `hedge_waste_usd` 0.30 |

$1.46 of the task's $1.74 was discarded output. Every cut reply was streaming at its lane's normal rate. The error rows carried no token count.

## Three causes, all in code

1. **The wall was blind to progress.** `stallWatch.wallTimer` was a pure elapsed-time timer at `wallFor(longest)` — 5× the longest reply the lane had COMPLETED, floored at 2m30s. This lane had only finished 5–9s tool-call turns, so 2m30s ≈ a hard cap of 6k output tokens at 40 tok/s. A 9k-token write could never fit; the retry ran the identical request into the identical wall.
2. **A tool-call fragment was hidden.** `visible, hidden := 0, 1; if answerText != ""` — a call's argument delta has no answer text, so the controller stayed in `PhaseThinking`, measured a ten-minute `write` against the model's THINKING distribution, and raised a rescue arm that wrote 18k tokens nobody kept. `stampCut` counted answer text only, so the row said zero.
3. **The wall could only learn from a completed reply** — a consequence of (1), fixed by (1) without a second mechanism (the design section says so).

## The ruling

**THE WALL BOUNDS A REPLY THAT IS NOT WORKING, NEVER A REPLY THAT IS LONG.** A tool call's arguments are the answer arriving: `Reading.Visible`, phase writing (both clocks), and counted in the cut's `Tokens`; the one-voice rule counts a call forming on screen as the answer being read, so a rescue's first fragment cannot take the voice. When the wall fires it asks whether the stream kept pace: tokens delivered over the period (from the first write, then each re-arm) against what the lane's measured rate would have produced. At least `1/streamWallFactor` — the wall's own spread argument, not a new number — re-arms it for another period, up to `streamWallCeiling` (20m), which stays absolute. Less is cut exactly as before, same sentence, naming the whole bound reached. A lane with no measured rate (and every lane under `routing off`) is held to `LagRate` (so 6 tok/s); a stream's own first-period rate was rejected because a drip keeps pace with itself. The rule never cuts earlier than the old wall. The cut's `Tokens` is the watch's own count of everything written (one estimator, `tokensOf`). Non-streamed completions keep their hard wall.

## Alternatives rejected (docs/design/waiting/DESIGN.md §L)

- **A `max_tokens` wall** — some routes send none (`document.go`, `relaxMaxTokens`), and the failure is a drip: a rate, which a count catches only after the whole budget.
- **Raise `streamWallMeasuredFloor`** — a band-aid; the chicken-and-egg stays and a slower lane or bigger file hits it tomorrow.
- **Push the wall on every chunk** — already rejected by the file; the pace re-arm is re-derived once per period from a measurement and cannot pass the ceiling.
- **Salvage the partial `write` across the cut** — out of scope, owed; seams `hedgeRace.flip` and `internal/session/salvage.go`.
- **Reuse the controller's drift test as "keeping up"** — over thousands of tokens it condemns a stream 20% under median; right for gating credit, wrong for a cut.

## Files

- `internal/provider/streamguard.go` — the law, `paceFor`, `keptPace`, `overrunVerdict`, `tokens`, `progress(bytes)`, `rewall(wall, pace)`
- `internal/provider/client.go` — call args visible + writing phase; progress bytes; cut tokens from the watch
- `internal/provider/hedge.go` — `shown`: a forming call counts as the answer on screen
- `internal/provider/{sse,lanes,velocity}.go` — `callText`/`written`, `tokensOf`, `streamPace`
- `internal/lane/control/contract.go` — `Reading` doc
- Tests: `internal/provider/streamwall_pace_test.go`, `internal/provider/toolcall_answer_test.go`, `internal/lane/control/toolcall_test.go`; two existing wall tests re-shaped to what they meant (drip → first wall; gusher → ceiling)
- `docs/changes/unreleased/786-stream-wall-keeps-pace.md` — the change entry
- `PERF.md` wall row; `internal/manual/chat/{models-and-cost,what-i-can-do}.md` + a reach test in `internal/manual/chat_test.go`; design §L

## Suites (Spark, linux/arm64, `-count=1`)

```
$ go build ./... && go vet ./internal/...          # clean
$ go test ./internal/provider/ ./internal/lane/... -count=1 -timeout 30m
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/provider	60.294s
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/lane	7.185s
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/lane/control	0.239s
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/lane/lanestub	0.591s
$ make test-laws        # laws: 63 files in 18 packages — all ok
$ make test-quick       # build, vet, gofmt, packed manual, laws — ok
$ go test ./internal/e2e/ -count=1
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/e2e	0.268s
$ go test -tags e2e ./internal/provider/ -run TestRealRouter -v
    e2e_ignore_real_test.go:159: WALL 1m41.224s  HTTP CALLS 32  MACHINES 15  REFUSAL ROWS 1
--- PASS: TestRealRouterNeverRefusesItselfTwice (101.22s)
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/provider	101.232s
$ go test ./internal/session/ -count=1 -timeout 30m

**What a person can see or do**
- `→` (or `tab`) on a model moves the cursor **into** its lanes — onto the pinned lane, else `auto` — and the list scrolls so the model and every lane are on screen. `←`/`tab` walks back out. Enter inside pins, as before.
- A model nobody has measured opens onto `auto` and `openrouter` with one dim line — `no machine has been measured for this model yet — machines show up after its first answer` — and asks the beat for its sheet.
- The hint slot follows the cursor: `→ lanes · enter switch · esc` on a model, `enter choose · ← back · esc` inside (with `tab` in place of the arrow where typed text is in the way). The settings panel's foot does the same.

- A. `→` walks in, `←` walks out — `unfoldHere` → `cursorToPin` + `revealFold`; both doors read `foldKey`.
- B. A fold always has its two answers — `unfoldAt` no longer refuses an empty fold; `lane.WantSheet` on unfold.

## What was wrong (two screens from the owner, 2026-09-10)

1. A model asked a checklist of eight as `form: line` with keys like `landscape`, `still-life`. The block drew one row cut at the edge — `[landscape] Landscapes & seascapes · [portrait] Portraits · … [surrealis…` — no key a person could press past the fourth answer, nothing under the pointer, the card's own per-row layout skipped because of a second cap (`questionCardOptions = 4`) under the engine's.
2. The withdrawn line for that question — `⊘ Which painting genres do you like? — no longer needed · it is no longer needed` — then sat above the box of a DIFFERENT conversation after a switch.

## What is true now

- **The asker's `line` is a wish; the evidence decides.** Structured input (checklist, blanks, pairs, dial) or an answer with a consequence/body beside it is a card whatever was asked for; plain answers stay a line as long as they fit (the existing width fallback).
- **Every answer is a row.** The card's second cap is gone; the engine's (4, 8 on a checklist) is the bound. A long label wraps, never `…`, and every row it takes presses the same answer (hover band + click).
- **A checklist is answered on the card.** Rows wear their ticks; a digit ticks its row (again unticks), `space` ticks the cursor's, `tab`/`shift+tab` walk, `enter` sends what is ticked in row order and nothing when nothing is; the key row says `[enter] send what is ticked` once something is.
- **Keys are digits.** `ask` renumbers whatever the model wrote to `1`… in order (`askDigitKeys`), and the answer goes back to the model in its own names with `labels` beside them (`askInTheirKeys`, `Answer.Labels`). The schema says so.
- **A conversation switch forgets the questions and records of the one left** (`forgetQuestions` in `attachConversation`); the new lane replays its own.
- **A withdrawn `ask` says `the turn moved on without it`** instead of `it is no longer needed` twice.
- Manual: *How a question looks*, *Pick several*, and the keys page; DESIGN.md's card line.

## Verified

- New: `TestAChecklistAskedForAsALineIsACardWithARowPerAnswer`, `TestALongAnswerWrapsOntoRowsThatPressTheSameAnswer`, `TestThreePlainAnswersStillDrawAsOneRow`, `TestSwitchingConversationsLeavesTheOtherOnesQuestionsBehind`, `TestAnAskWithWordKeysIsRenumberedAndAnsweredInTheAskersOwnKeys`.
- Targeted tui3/session/manual/laws/word-gate green locally; full `internal/tui3` and `internal/session` on the Spark — results in a comment.

| panel | what it holds | door |

| `needs you` | questions from any chat or task, your-calls under two days old; older ones fold as `N older · tasks` | a digit answers the top row from anywhere on home; `enter` opens |
| `running` | every session's live tasks and jobs, a firing standing item; one spinner | `enter` brings it here; `s stop it` / `ctrl+x` on work this window holds |
| `since you left · Nh` | tasks landed, files made, watches fired, what memory learned since the look stamp | each line opens its record, file or place |
| `where you were` | this window's chat first with your own last words under it, then the most recent; the previous chat is preselected on `space space` | `enter` opens; typing searches through every fold |
| `projects` | the launch folder first (always a row), then folders with counts and the repo clause, paths cut from the left | `enter` starts a chat there; `ctrl+o` opens the folder |
| `spend` | `today $X of $Y`, a fourteen-day block sparkline with the loudest day, top models, chats and tasks today | `enter` opens spend |
| `next up` | reminders and routines, soonest first | `enter` opens standing |

Laws the branch pins with tests: stable order and flexible height; a short frame squeezes by priority and a whispering panel drops before any panel with rows; a tall frame grows panels to their budgets, `spend` never; an empty panel whispers what arrives there and how, never that it is empty (the emptiness law narrowed for panels only); one head shared by home, every place and the chat (pulse · strip or bar · rule · blank), so nothing above or below the body moves between them; a four-place bar `home tasks spend settings`; one click is `enter` on every surface, a heading is a door, hover previews; `←→` cross columns and `→` opens a row's verbs only where no column lies to its right, the foot naming the chord otherwise; a whisper wraps and is never cut; the age outranks the tail of a title; `~` and temp folders never tag a chat row.

Zero new model calls. The engine seams are `PresenceTask.Activity/Done/Total`, `SessionPresence.Jobs`, `TaskIndexEntry.StartedAt`, `ArtifactsSince`, `LandedSince`, `SpendToday`/`SpendShare`, and a worker-report prompt rule instead of a receipt role.

Retired: the flat ranked list and its fold, the resting card and its bands on home, the three-column card tier, `alt+g`/`alt+q`, `ctrl+t` as the way to another folder, the seven-place bar and `alt+5…7`, the chat head's adaptive blank rows. The band registry stays for the typed search, the standing-item card and the phone sheet.

Places got the same pass (audit in `docs/design/home-mission-control/PLACES-AUDIT.md`): heads and feet that never jump, teaching empty states, one text and component hierarchy, exact hit maps after a squeeze or scroll, focus waking at the center of mass.

The manual's home, keys and places pages are rewritten; the tmux suite's home subtests and needles are re-pointed at the panels.

**Verification, all on the Spark, at the tip that carries dev's own tip (`98fe03311`, dev `6a8816ae7` with #809 and #810 merged in):** `internal/tui3` full suite green under CI's serial command (`-p 1`); `internal/session` full suite green except one 0.00s race in a test's own baseline reading, fixed on dev by #810 rather than listed as known-red; `TestTUIE2E` fifteen subtests green (one, `narrow_window_ask_here`, waited out a model reply while two other e2e runs shared the box and passed in sixteen seconds alone), including three that were red on dev before this branch (`the_firing_reaches_the_person`, `a_nested_landing_asks_and_a_key_answers_it`, `one_figure_on_every_spend_surface`) and are fixed here. On the way, four `internal/tui3` tests #798's harness clock left red on dev were fixed by #801 and dev's two nightly reds by #805, so the branch merges onto a green trunk.

Also on the way: the shared test home's `artifacts.jsonl` was being written by export tests and read by the home lab, which made one test order-dependent; the lab now roots its own index. The same pollution had reached both machines' real `~/.aforge/v3/artifacts.jsonl` from test runs before 2026-09-02; the junk rows were removed with a `.bak-2026-09-10` copy kept beside the file.
