body:
`internal/tui2/tokens` holds every mark a person sees, in three spellings, behind
one door. The law that keeps it that way landed in #711 covering `internal/tui3`
**alone** — which left the older window and the resident free to spell marks for
themselves, and v1 did:

| v1 drew | For | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `◌` | a pending node waiting on a sibling | `GWaitsOn` — `⚑` |
| `⚑` | a card or brief row waiting on a **person** | `GNeedsHuman` — `?` |
| `✗` | failure, in five places | `GFailed` — `✕` |
| `–` | cancelled, so it would not read as broken | `GStopped` — `■` |
| `✓ ◐ ○` | done, working, queued | `GSettled` `GWorking` `GQueued` (same shapes) |
| `⚙ $ ✎ ⌕ ⌾ ♪ ▶ ▤` | the tool-call gutter in the activity feed | the action-family and file-kind slots |

The two at the top are the reason this is a defect and not a tidy-up: v1's flag
meant *waiting on you* while the vocabulary's flag means *waiting on a sibling*,
so the same shape said two different things on two screens of one product.

## The law is its own package now

`internal/iconlaw` walks `internal/tui`, `internal/tui3`, `internal/head` and
`internal/resident` on one list, so a fifth surface joins the law by being added
to that list rather than by somebody remembering to copy a test. It fails on any
private-use codepoint and on any vocabulary shape used as a mark. The one
carve-out is `resident.NoteMark` — a job-board note is written with `⚑` and read
back by prefix, so that byte is a **protocol byte in the journal**, not a cell on
a screen, and routing it through the tier would make stored bytes depend on the
terminal that wrote them. `TestEveryExemptionIsStillReal` fails if that carve-out
ever stops naming a real line. `make test-laws` runs both.

## How v1 picks the tier

The same two facts v3 folds together, folded the same way (`internal/tui/icons.go`):
the Display row `step icons` over `tokens.DetectGlyphSet`. One terminal, one tier,
everywhere. It detects **at `RunWithCommander`** — the one door that knows a real
terminal is on the other end — so a window an embedder or a test builds keeps the
designed plain floor, and the suite is not asserting against codepoints it cannot
print. `internal/head` and `internal/resident` draw no marks of their own, so they
hold no tier; they are on the list to keep it that way.

## Four slots joined the vocabulary

The attachment and media chips draw a closed set of four kinds together, and one
of them was already `GActionRead`'s byte — half a chip row upgrading is the exact
mixed-repertoire line the tier exists to end. So: `GFileDocument` `▤`,
`GFileImage` `⌾`, `GFileAudio` `♪`, `GFileVideo` `▷`, on Font Awesome 4's outlined
file family. The video mark moves off the filled `▶`, which is `GQueuePill`'s
byte: one plain glyph may upgrade exactly one way.

## One defect found in the pinned extract

`testdata/nerdfont_glyphnames.json` pinned `nf-fa-file_text_o` at `f15c`. In the
release it names (ryanoasis/nerd-fonts 3.2.1) `fa-file_text_o` is **`f0f6`**;
`f15c` is `fa-file_text`. The shipped glyph is right and the NAME was not the
contract it claimed to be, so `GActionRead` is renamed to `nf-fa-file_text` and
the extract regenerated from the release. No drawn character changes. The other
47 entries check out.

## Verified

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `go test` over `internal/tui`, `internal/head/...`,
  `internal/resident/...`, `internal/tui2/...`, `internal/iconlaw` and
  `internal/tui3` on the Spark
- `make test-laws`

v1's restraint is intact: no hue moved, and a shape changed only where the shared
vocabulary already had a different character for the meaning the window was drawing.

body:
## What was wrong

`PriceOf` (`internal/orchestrate/fuel.go`) cut a `:variant` or `@build` suffix
off a model id and then walked the price table matching a **bare** name against
any **vendor-qualified** key ending `/<name>`. Every key in that table is
qualified, so a bare `deepseek-v4-flash` — which is the id a vendor's own base
serves, as against the router's `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` — resolved to that
row's list price of $0.14 in and $0.28 out.

That is not a missing price, it is a confident wrong one, and it looks right.
The adaptive run's fuel tank meters and gates on this number: at the run's own
metering door a million prompt tokens billed **$0.14** where the documented
`unpriced` fallback charges **$1.25**, so the 80% warning and the 100% gate
arrived some nine times too late. The comment above `unpriced` states the law
this broke — a model the table has never heard of is the case where the tank
matters most, because nobody has checked what it costs.

## What is true now

**A bare name is not a vendor's row.** The suffix-matching loop is deleted. The
exact lookup above it already priced every qualified id, suffixes and all, so a
bare id now falls to `unpriced` like any other model nobody has priced.

The suffix cutting, the `unpriced` figures and every qualified row are
untouched, and **no rate was added to the table** — every vendor's model line
has rolled over since it was written, and a guessed row would be the same defect
with a different number. No shipped default needs one: the shipped chat model
and all five crew-tier models are vendor-qualified ids.

This is deliberately **not** a redesign of the id grammar. A bare id staying
unpriced is the honest answer until service-qualified identities exist.

Nothing a person reads changes. The manual describes the tank, the 80% mark, the
three answers at the gate and the $100 default, and says nothing anywhere about
how an id is matched to a price row — the fallback table is machinery a person
never sees. This is a wrong number behind an unchanged sentence.

## Validation contract

Tests derive from these, not from the implementation.

- **A bare id is not a vendor's row.** `PriceOf("deepseek-v4-flash")` reports
  unknown and returns `unpriced`; likewise the bare form of every key in the
  table, with and without `:free` / `@2026-01`. *Fails on `dev`, passes here.*
- **Every qualified id prices exactly as before.** Table-driven over `prices`
  itself, so a row added later is covered: each key, and each key with a
  `:free` or `@2026-01` suffix, returns its own figures and reports known.
- **An id in no row is still unpriced,** with a non-zero `Out` — an unpriced
  model is not a free model, and no new path to `$0.00` is created. The empty
  and whitespace ids behave as before.
- **The run's own metering door agrees.** `orchestrateCost` with usage and no
  reported `Cost` returns `1.25` for a bare `deepseek-v4-flash` and `0.14` for
  the qualified `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`; a response that *does* carry a
  `Cost` still returns that figure verbatim for both — the provider's own number
  still outranks the table.

Proven against `origin/dev` before the fix: the same three tests fail there.

```
--- FAIL: TestMeter
    fuel_test.go:27: a bare model name is not its vendor's row
--- FAIL: TestABareNameIsNotAVendorsRow/bare_deepseek-v4-flash
    fuel_test.go:45: PriceOf("deepseek-v4-flash") = {In:0.14 Out:0.28}, true; want {In:1.25 Out:10}, false
--- FAIL: TestOrchestrateCostKeepsABareNameOutOfAVendorsRow
    orchestrate_cost_test.go:19: orchestrateCost without a reported cost for "deepseek-v4-flash" = 0.14, want 1.25
```

`internal/orchestrate`'s `TestMeter` asserted the old behaviour on purpose
("a bare model name matches its vendor's row"); it asserts the new law instead.
That belief is what the change entry invalidates.

## Gates

All run in the worktree with `GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false`.

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go build ./... && go vet ./...` | PASS, silent |
| `make test-quick` | PASS — 18 packages `ok` |
| `make test-laws` | PASS — 17 packages `ok` |
| `make test PKGS='./internal/orchestrate ./internal/session' TEST_FLAGS='-count=1'` | PASS — `ok internal/orchestrate 0.236s`, `ok internal/session 270.004s` |
| `make build` | PASS |

No line was added to `.github/known-red.txt`.

Closes #749

body:
## What was true

Who holds a landed-but-unsettled task's decision — `TaskAskOwnerModel` vs the
person — lived ONLY on the live `TaskNode`. The checkpoint did not carry it, on
the argument that a node coming back from disk should be the person's anyway.

That was the right answer arrived at by accident, and it cost three things:

- a restart or a re-attach drew the card as the zero value, which *happens* to
  read as the person (since #743) rather than because anything decided it;
- no fixture or e2e could seed "aforge is deciding", which is why the acceptance
  lane (#698) could not provoke shape 5 at all;
- an engine that died mid-turn while the model held a question dropped the
  hand-back it owed, because `handBackUnsettled` only ever runs at the end of a
  turn that got to end.

## What is true now

**The checkpoint carries the holder.** `taskRecord.Decider` (task_store.go),
written by `recordLocked`, read by `restoreNode`, with the emptiness law: a
missing field — every file written before this, and every node nobody handed
over — reads as the person.

**The floor fires on the way in.** `TaskGraph.handBackOnLoad`, called out of
`rehydrate`, hands every node the record says the model was holding back to the
person *as the checkpoint is read*: before the frontier turns, before anything
is drawn, and before `recoverTasks` rewrites the file, so the disk stops saying
it too. The landings still waiting on a decision come back on `taskRecovery` and
`recoverTasks` publishes each as one ordinary task update — the same lane and
the same shape the end-of-turn floor uses.

`readsTheDecisionLocked`'s question is not asked on that road, and the comment
says why: there are no turns on it, and every agent that was holding anything
died with the process.

**Conflicted and shifted landings are still never model-held.** `taskAskOf`
already forces the person on that road whatever a caller says, and a test now
pins it across a restore too.

**The project index deliberately does NOT carry the decider**, and that is
written down rather than forgotten: the index is what work *came to*, appended
once and never rewritten, while who holds a question lasts at most one turn — a
row on disk saying `aforge is deciding` about a conversation that closed hours
ago would be a claim nothing could correct. It is `TaskIndexEntry.Activity`'s
own rule about a present that ends seconds after it is recorded.

## How it composes with the Questions wave (#712 / #728)

**One holder, two vocabularies — no second store and no second timer.** A landed
`your call` is DERIVED as a `Question` (`landingQuestion`), and its `Policy` is
now read off `TaskAsk.Owner` through `landingPolicy`: the model holding it is
`PolicyDecide`, the person is `PolicyAsk`. The holder itself stays exactly where
task-states put it — on the node, in the notice, and now on the checkpoint.

`PolicyRecommendThenAuto`, `Question.Deadline` and the one timer in this program
(`tools_ask.go`) belong to the `ask` tool's timed assumptions and are untouched:
the floor is the end of a turn, not a clock, so a landing question carries no
deadline and starts nothing. A test pins that.

## Tests

- store round-trip of the decider, and the floor applied on rehydrate;
- an older record with no `decider` field reading as the person;
- a restored conflict that is still the person's;
- the whole resume: the node comes back the person's, the update goes out on the
  task lane, and the file on disk stops saying the model is deciding;
- the landing question's policy moving with the holder, with no clock;
- **e2e shape 5 is now deterministic.** `the_auto_settle_floor_hands_a_restart_back`
  seeds a checkpoint saying `"decider": "model"`, opens the conversation on it,
  and asserts the attached surface draws `[a] accept · [n] not right · [s] tell it`
  and NOT `aforge is deciding`. It pays for no model. The live subtest keeps its
  skip path, because no fixture can catch a window whose length is however long
  the model takes.

## Docs

`docs/design/task-states/DESIGN.md`'s floor section gains the load rule, the
index ruling and the one-holder derivation. `internal/manual/chat/tasks.md` and
`task-rooms-after-restart.md` each gain the sentence a person needs — after a
restart it is yours again — with a probe for it.

## Verified

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `make test-laws`, `go test ./internal/session/
./internal/tui3/ ./internal/e2e/ ./internal/manual/...`, and the tagged
`TestTaskStatesE2E` on the Spark.

## What changes

**The conversation's foot** (`internal/tui3/foot.go` is the law):
- The conversation's name and model move from the status row onto the legend above the box: `─ porting the parser · glm-5.3-flash · ⠿ high · via deepinfra · main* ─`. The model is pressable (picker); the thinking rung is pressable (walks one step) and hoverable. The ladder for a narrow frame: branch → cut the name to seat the `via` rider → rider → rung whole → cut the name → model → name.
- The status row is a ledger grouped by question: bill (`$0.27 · ⟲ saved $0.0038 · 58% cached`), meter (`66.8k/1.3M · 5%`), elsewhere (`2 jobs`), posture (`YOLO`); the right edge is the LIVE stream rate (`38 tok/s`, never the burn average), the link and the state word. Every figure is a door: bill and cache → Spending, meter → /status, YOLO → /permissions.
- Off the row, still in /status and the phone sheet: crew, session delta, burn, sparkline, `2 open`. `◦ 2 standing orders` draws at the foot of the task column (pressable, opens /standing). The task column's foot no longer repeats the bill and drops the `Σ`.
- `⟲ saved $…` is derived from the cache totals, so a resumed conversation shows it on its first frame.
- `via <machine>` is always on the seam whoever served; the jump chip is at the left edge; the prompt is directly under the rule.

**Thinking on the seam**: the tray chip is gone; the rung sits beside the model, reads `⠿ auto` until a rung is chosen, a press or `ctrl+v` walks it, `/effort` (`/think`, `/thinking`) opens the six-row ladder or sets a rung (`/effort max`, `/effort auto`). Conversation effort crosses the wire (`Effort`/`ResolvedEffort`/`SetEffort`, `Welcome.Effort`), so hosted conversations have the dial too.

**Phase and lane news over the wire** (the real cause of "no tok/s, no via"): bare `aforge` in a workspace runs against the machine's engine host, and `PhaseNews`/`LaneNews` never crossed. New `phase` and `lane` push frames, session-scoped on the host (`provider.WithSession`, `Agent.NewsKey`), never blocking the stream; `endPhase` now stamps its session; `MethodAnswerLaneOffer` so the offer road is honest over a host.

**Home's foot**: the rule above home's box is a legend saying where the sentence lands and on what model (`→ new conversation in ~/src/parser · glm-5.3-flash`, `alt+w` / `alt+o`). `/model` at home pins the next conversation's model. `/folder` opens the folder browser aimed at the target; `/attach` and `/image` land on home's tray and ride into the new conversation; every command in the `/` list says its fate on its row before it runs (`opens a conversation here first`, `opens the page`, `answers here`, …).

**Recall**: ↑/↓ history recall works in every conversation the fleet opens beside (the History store was not wired into the bundle).

Design records: ideation/home-input-groom.md and the two option artifacts shared in session.

## Checks (all full runs on the Spark, per the owner's standing order)
- [x] `internal/tui3` (4657 tests), `internal/session`, `internal/provider`, `internal/remote`, `internal/enginehost`, `cmd/aforge`, `internal/tui2/tokens` — all `ok` with `-count=1` at the dev-merged commit
- [x] tagged tmux TUI e2e suite against a real model: 14 of 15, identical to dev's baseline run the same night (`the_firing_reaches_the_person` is red on dev too); `one_figure_on_every_spend_surface` went red once by crossing midnight mid-run and passed on rerun
- [x] the Spark found two things the laptop could not: a test whose room was sized off a macOS temp path, and the e2e foot finder that home's worded rule had outgrown — both fixed here
- [x] manual gates · e2e needles · tokens · laws · gofmt · vet · changelog-check · `make build`
- [x] change entries: 747-status-foot.md, 747-home-target.md, 747-seam-effort.md, 747-wire-news.md, 747-recall-beside.md
- [x] verified on the real binary in tmux: `30 tok/s · ⠋ working · 8s` mid-answer, `⠿ auto · via relace` on the seam (the name cut to seat it), `served via relace · 1.2s` in /status, the `/effort` ladder, `⟲ saved` on resume
- [x] dev merged in twice (through #776); six conflicts resolved by keeping both sides

body:
Streamed reasoning text was replayed as many separate detail objects with the same block index. In the captured CPF run, an 89-character reasoning block became 16 objects. The next tool step should receive the completed logical block, as OpenRouter’s client assembles it.

Join compatible adjacent text and summary fragments once when capturing the completed assistant reply. Preserve distinct block identities, opaque/encrypted bytes, signatures and unknown metadata. Keep the streaming path, model provenance, request settings and generation defaults unchanged. The manual and a CRITICAL invariant comment describe the contract.

A real Submit regression and a mixed-block regression fail before the fix and pass afterward. Focused tests also cover 1,000 fragments, reset/snapshot independence, different IDs/indices, late signatures and opaque data. body:
## What was true

`ctrl+t` in `/model` walked a list of its own — `off, low, medium, high`
(`internal/tui3/palette.go`'s `reasoningCycle`) — while the effort ladder has five rungs and
the `thinking` row of `/settings` offers all five plus `auto`. `nextReasoning` returned `""`
for any word not on its list, so a level it did not recognise was **cleared rather than
climbed**: `aforge --reasoning xhigh` lost its pin to one keypress and the next turn went out
with no `reasoning` object at all. `xhigh` and `max` could not be reached from the picker at
any number of presses.

The same dial was spelled two ways in one corpus. A task's own control already walks
`auto → low → medium → high → xhigh → max → auto` and `task-controls.md` says so; `commands.md`
and `models-and-cost.md` said the picker walks `off → low → medium → high → off` and "does not
offer `xhigh` or `max`". Absence was `auto` in the settings row and `off` in the refusal a
task's thinking change prints. Three manual gates were green through all of it, because they
ask whether a **name** is mentioned and never whether the sentence around it is true.

## What is true now

One walk, off `effort.Rungs`, wherever a person can move this dial.
`internal/tui3/effortscope.go` grows `effortNextClearing` — the wheel for the two scopes whose
absence means "hand this back to whatever stands above it" and which the surface is the only
door onto: a task's rung, and the level dialled onto one model. The picker and the task control
now take the same step from the same rung. The conversation chip keeps `effortNext`, which
never lands on absence, because that rung is cleared from the settings row instead.

Absence is called `auto` in everything a person reads: the refusal ends `, or auto` (`off` and
`""` are still read, because a profile written by an older build means what it meant), and the
`thinking` row names the doors that exist — including `ctrl+t` in `/model`, and no longer the
home resting card that was retired with `↑` reaching the tab bar.

The walk, the words the row offers and the shipped default are rows in
`internal/manual/truth_test.go`'s table now, so they are written once in code and filled into
the pages at test time. `effort.Ship` stays `effort.None`; #653 decided that deliberately and
this is not that argument.

## Validation contract

1. With `xhigh` dialled onto the model in use, one `ctrl+t` on that row leaves it reading
   `max` — one step up — and never nothing.
2. From no level, successive presses visit `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` in order.
3. The press after `max` clears the level, so a per-model pin can still be cleared from the
   picker without `/new`.
4. The step the picker takes and the step a task's thinking control takes are one step, read
   off one list.
5. `ctrl+t` still does nothing at all, silently, on a model whose catalog row takes no
   reasoning knob, and on a window with no agent.
6. Absence has one name in what a person reads: `auto`.
7. A page still spelling the walk `off → low → medium → high → off`, or the default as
   anything but `config.EffortWord(effort.Ship)`, goes red with its owner named.

Not changed: `effort.Ship` is still `None` (#653); a pinned rung still reaches the wire as it
did (#643 — `xhigh` → the 32,000-token budget, `max` → 64,000, absence → no reasoning object),
and `internal/provider/effortladder_test.go` is untouched and green; the conversation chip's
five-rung wrap; the picker hint; the `<id>:<level>` spelling.

One existing test changed expectation rather than shape:
`TestCtrlTCyclesTheLevelAndSkipsModelsThatTakeNone` asserted the four-step cycle this issue
names as the defect, so its `want` is now the ladder's six stops.

Fixes #738

## Gates

Run in the branch's worktree, `GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false`, on `HEAD` rebased onto `dev`:

```
go build ./...                                   build ok
go vet ./...                                     vet ok
make fmt-check                                   fmt ok
make test-packed-manual                          ok  internal/manual  1.349s
make test-laws                                   ok  internal/tui3 10.021s (all packages ok)
go test -count=1 ./internal/manual/              ok  internal/manual  1.318s
go test -count=1 -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/
                                                 ok  internal/tui3 0.172s · ok internal/session 0.264s
go test -count=1 -timeout 20m ./internal/tui3/   ok  internal/tui3   423.717s
go test -count=1 -timeout 20m ./internal/session/ ok internal/session 222.456s
go test -count=1 ./internal/config/              ok  internal/config  81.483s
go test -count=1 ./internal/e2e/                 ok  internal/e2e      0.219s   (the tui words table)
go test -count=1 ./internal/effort/              ok  internal/effort   0.002s
```

## Driven in a terminal

`bin/aforge chat --no-host --reasoning xhigh --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, in tmux
against an isolated profile, then `/model` and `ctrl+t`.

**Before, on `dev@df3153e5b`** — the marked picker row, one press apart:

```
=== /model open ===
› deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash:xhigh   via baidu · ▲0.8s · $0.07/$0.14 per M · 1M · 70t/s · elo 1221
=== after one ctrl+t ===
```

And the `thinking` row, found by typing `thinking` into `/settings`:

body:
The four things the real-terminal acceptance of the task-states wave (#698) found, closed.

Closes #706. Closes #707.

## #706 — a landing card with a reason and no answers

The root cause is not the fixture and not the surface's layout. **v3's ordinary launch
talks to an engine host over `internal/remote`**, and `internal/remote`'s agent had none of
the four doors that decide a landing — `ResolveUnverified`, `ResolveConflict`,
`HandUnverifiedToModel`, `TakeBackDecision`. `app.settleDoors()` asserts them on the agent
the window holds, the assertion failed, and the absence law then did exactly what it is
written to do: it removed the whole answers row, leaving

```
? ◆ Review the pull request diff · your call · 42s · 1 file
  nobody could check it
```

and nothing to press.

**The path length is why it read as a fixture bug.** A host is only reachable where its
socket path fits (`enginehost.socketLimit`, 104 bytes), and the temporary home a subtest
runs in is named after the subtest — so `TestTUIE2E/a_refused_landing_is_incomplete` got a
host and drew no chips, while `TestTaskStatesE2E/your_call_asks_in_three_columns…`, whose
name is thirty characters longer, fell back to the in-process engine and drew all four.
Same binary, same run, two answers. On macOS the temp root is long enough that neither ever
reaches a host, which is why the subtest passes on a laptop.

So the four verbs cross: `Task.Settle` carries all five acts, a `Welcome.TaskSettle` flag
says whether the engine behind them has them, and `internal/tui3` asks that flag before it
draws a chip — an engine too old to answer draws the reason and no chips, which is where
the absence law wants it. A reading window is refused by the existing allow-list.

## #707 — "the rail row names the work and stops"

**The rail row was never the row that was measured.** The column stands to the right of the
conversation, so no line of a capture that has one begins with a tier cell —
`statesRailRow` matched on the whole line, found nothing, and `statesRail` then pressed
ctrl+g "because there was no column", closing the very column it was measuring and reading
the tab strip that appears in its place. The column was saying
`your call · nobody could check it` one row below the name the whole time:

```
│ ? Port the parser         #1
│   your call · nobody could
│   check it
```

So the reader reads the column, and a row is read WITH ITS BLOCK — thirty cells will not
hold a name and a reason side by side. `tierRowBody` is split over a new `tierRowParts` so
the two lists of work can paint the title and the reading apart, and a `internal/tui3` unit
test pins the glyph, the name, the word and the reason on the column.

## The conflict shape

It was unreachable, and the engine was right. The repository the harness builds is on
`main`, which is on the protected list, so the landing kept its branch and never merged and
nothing could clash. The subtest now moves the checkout onto `work` first — and leaves the
person's clashing change **uncommitted**, because a commit while the work is out moves the
branch, and a branch that moved since the cut is one aforge will not write either. A
landing that keeps its branch off a plain unmoved checkout is now a failure rather than a
skip.

`docs/design/task-states/DESIGN.md` said `branch kept` appears "only when keeping was asked
for". It appears whenever the landing kept the branch — asked for, a protected or detached
checkout, or one that moved since the cut — and the card's own report says which.

## Stale needles

The setup door's title counts two steps (`setupStepsFor` builds at most two) and the suite
waited for three. `waiting on you` was checked and is **not** stale: `internal/tui3`'s
`notifyAskWord` still spells it and home draws `session.PresenceWaiting`, which is the same
string — so those two subtests' reds have another cause and were left alone.

body:
Fixes #729.

## What was true

The **add context** sheet is the one surface here that COVERS the conversation instead of
replacing it: `contextModalOver` fades the finished chat frame and writes the sheet into it,
so while the sheet is up every row it lands on is full width. The frame that comes after the
close is the ordinary chat frame, whose rows end wherever their content ends — usually well
to the left of where the sheet's right edge was — and the terminal keeps whatever the
frame-to-frame diff does not overwrite. Nothing in the closing path asked for those cells
back, so the sheet's right-hand slice stayed on the screen over whatever was drawn beneath
it. It survived typing and cleared only when something else repainted those cells full width.

At the other end of the size range the same sheet built one row more than the terminal had.
`contextSheet` forced a row of names even where there was no room for one, so a four-row
terminal got `head, box, thin rule, one name` and the foot rule — the row that carries
`esc · cancel` — fell off the bottom. The window it recorded said otherwise: `win.height`
counted the rows it BUILT, so `contextWin.holds` answered true for a row the terminal does
not have and the cancel target was offered on a cell nobody could click. The manual page
already promised the opposite, and was right.

## What is true now

**One door out, and it asks for the whole screen back.** `esc`, the `esc · cancel` words and
the action row that adds and closes all go through `closeContextSheet`, which closes, touches
and answers with a full repaint. The action door keeps the work it was carrying (the repaint
and `folderTakeCmd` travel together in one batch). Padding our own rows cannot repair this and
was not attempted: the renderer clears its cell buffer before every frame, so explicit
trailing spaces and absent cells produce exactly the same diff — the only lever is the
repaint, and this is the one moment this surface has a layer to undraw.

**The sheet draws no row the terminal does not have.** Rows yield in order — the browser's own
rows, then the thin rule under the box, then the box — so the head rule and the foot rule are
the last two things to go: four rows give `head, box, thin, foot`; three give `head, box,
foot`; two give `head, foot`; one gives the way out alone. `contextWin` then records what was
painted: `holds` is false below the last drawn row, the cancel target is offered only on a
foot rule that was actually drawn, and with no box on screen there is nowhere to type, so the
frame hides the caret rather than blinking it at a row that is not there.

Two small things found in the same corner, each in its own commit:

- `scripts/context-modal-native-fixture.sh` wrote a 79-byte `pixel.png` whose IHDR and IDAT
  both failed CRC32 (`png: invalid format: invalid checksum`), so the one script written to
  exercise the half-cell picture renderer never exercised it. It writes a valid 16x8
  true-colour PNG now.
- `docs/remote-access-testing.md` still listed `/attach takes a path` and `<name> is a folder`
  as "refusals to try". #657 deleted both; a reader following that runbook recorded a false
  PASS. It says what those two inputs do now instead.

## Validation contract

1. After the sheet closes — by `esc`, by a press on the `esc · cancel` words, or by the action
   row adding what was chosen — no cell of the sheet is left on the screen.
2. The failing round is the acceptance: open at 150x42, resize to 52x30, resize back, `esc` →
   `capture-pane | grep -c 'esc · cancel'` answers `0`.
3. Every door out asks for the same repaint, and the action door still carries its work.
4. A terminal too short for the sheet still shows the way out: the last row the sheet draws is
   its foot rule with `esc · cancel` on it.
5. The pointer is offered only cells the paint put on the screen: `holds` is false below the
   last drawn row, and the cancel target only where the foot rule was drawn.
6. The fixture script writes a `pixel.png` that `image/png` decodes as 16x8.
7. The remote runbook lists only refusals this build gives.

What does not change: the sheet's look while it is up, its five constants, the centring, every
key and person-facing word, and `close`'s promise that nothing chosen in an abandoned sheet
reaches the conversation.

## Manual test — the real binary, in tmux, no model

`bin/aforge chat --no-host --yolo` in a fresh git repo with `HOME=$(mktemp -d)`, driven with
tmux: open the sheet at 150x42, resize to 52x30, resize back, press `esc`. Then reopen it and
resize the window to four rows. Three rounds each on the `dev` build and on this branch.

Closing after the resize, on `dev` — the start page's rows with the sheet still over them:

```
                                       Understand this folder alt+m choose · ctrl+u search   │
                                       Make or fix something                          folder │
                                       Compare two options──────────────────────── esc · cancel ─╯
```

The same three rows on this branch:

```
                                       Understand this folder
                                       Make or fix something
                                       Compare two options
```

`grep -c 'esc · cancel'` after the close: **1, 1, 1** on `dev`; **0, 0, 0** on this branch.

The sheet on a four-row terminal, on `dev` — no way out drawn:

```
    · still╭─ add context ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /tmp/… ╮
    · openr│  › search folders and files · or type a path · alt+p preview · alt+h hidden  │
 ›         │  ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
tmp.GXLEuAN│                  ›   ▸ docs/                             nothing below here   │
```

and on this branch:

```
    · still╭─ add context ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /tmp/… ╮
    · openr│  › search folders and files · or type a path · alt+p preview · alt+h hidden  │
 ›         │  ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
tmp.mQtJLyG╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── esc · cancel ─╯
```

`grep -c 'esc · cancel'` with the sheet open at four rows: **0, 0, 0** on `dev`; **1, 1, 1**
on this branch.

## Gates

Run in this worktree, on the branch as it stands:

```
$ go build ./...                                          # no output, exit 0
$ go vet ./...                                            # no output, exit 0
$ make fmt-check                                          # no output, exit 0
$ make test-laws
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/tui3	10.118s
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/workspace	0.034s
$ go test ./internal/manual/
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/manual	1.363s
$ go test -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/tui3	0.340s
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/session	0.926s
$ make test-packed-manual
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/manual	1.371s
$ go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/tui3/          # the one package this diff touches
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/tui3	473.198s
$ make build
go build -tags=aforge_packed_manual … -o bin/aforge ./cmd/aforge
```

Two things said plainly rather than hidden:

- The **first** full `./internal/tui3/` run failed one test —
  `TestSteeringANodeWaitingOnItsPiecesSaysWhatTheLineJustDid`, `enter steered 0 times, want 1`
  — and it did not recur. The same tree re-ran green (473s, above), the test passes alone,
  and a control run of the full package on `origin/dev` in a detached worktree was green
  (`ok … 487.729s`, 0 failures). It is a task-room steering test; nothing in this diff runs
  unless the chooser is open. Recorded here rather than dismissed.
- `make size` is red, and was red before this change: `bin/aforge` built from `origin/dev`
  at the base commit is 55,656,713 bytes against a 54,600,000 budget. This branch's binary
  is 55,660,809 — 4,096 bytes more. That is #724, which is open, and `make size` is not one
  of the PR gate's steps.

## Not fixed here, and why

The QA sweep filed four more faults on this browser. They are not this change and are left
for their own:

- **`folderCutWord` is dead.** `more of this folder is not shown` is declared and
  `folderListing.cut` is set three times and read never, so a listing bounded at
  `folderRowsCap` says nothing about being bounded. The cap is also applied per half, so a
  listing can offer twice the rows the constant names — which is a decision about the cap, not
  a wiring fix.
- **A directory that changes under the sheet is never noticed**, and there is no re-read key.
  Only `alt+h` twice drops the cache. Adding a key is a new chord and a manual page.
- **Trailing spaces are trimmed off a path by the engine and the tray.** A folder named
  `keep me ` is answered `· /tmp/sp/keep me is not there`, because `Agent.placePath`
  (`internal/session/places.go`) and `attachChipTo` both `TrimSpace`. That is an engine change
  and belongs to whoever owns that trim.
- The sheet's yield order at four rows is a choice: the thin rule is kept and the last name
  row given up. Keeping one name and dropping the rule would fit too, and is a one-line change
  if the owner prefers it.

body:
Fixes #735.

## What was true

#658 landed `make test-report`, `make test-quick`, `scripts/test-report.sh` and
`internal/ci/testreport`, whose own doc comment says a timing artifact that lies is
worse than no artifact. Five of its claims were not:

- `make test-report` with no `REPORT` wrote `test-report.json` into the repository root
  and nothing ignored it, in a checkout several sessions share.
- `"cached": true` was written for any package whose output contained `(cached)`
  anywhere. A two-file module whose only test calls `t.Log("see (cached) here")`, run
  with `go test -json -count=1 ./...`, reported
  `{"name":"cf","action":"pass","seconds":0.003,"cached":true}` — the package had just
  executed, uncached, one line earlier.
- A stream cut mid-line was a parse failure: `unexpected end of JSON input`, exit 2, no
  file — and `scripts/test-report.sh` had already `rm -f`'d the previous report, so a
  killed run destroyed the last evidence and left none of its own. CLAUDE.md's promise
  that the report "lists incomplete packages after an abrupt end" held only when the kill
  landed on a line boundary.
- `kill -9` on `scripts/test-report.sh` orphaned the heartbeat: `trap cleanup EXIT` does
  not run, so the `while sleep 30` subshell reparented to init and reported forever.
- `make test-quick`'s own comment called it "the deterministic light half of the
  pull-request gate" while it ran neither `go run ./cmd/aforge-changes check` nor two of
  the three manual gates. `git show origin/dev:Makefile` line 150:
  `test-quick: build-check vet fmt-check test-packed-manual test-laws`. Add a slash
  command with no manual page and it stayed green while the pull request went red.

## What is true now

- The default report is ignored by git.
- Go's package summary line — `ok  <package>  (cached)`, and the `-cover` form with a
  fourth field — is the only witness to the build cache. What a test logs is not evidence.
- A cut stream is a cut run, not a malformed one: the report is written, `"truncated":
  true` and `incomplete_packages` say what did not finish, the unfinished packages are
  named on stderr, and the command still exits 2. An empty stream and a whole line that
  is not JSON are refused exactly as before, with no file. The report's `schema` is 2.
- The heartbeat asks each tick whether the script it speaks for is still there, so a
  SIGKILL costs at most one interval. `TEST_REPORT_HEARTBEAT` sets that interval, which
  is how the repository's own test drives it in five seconds.
- `test-quick` runs the changelog check and all three manual gates — about twenty seconds
  more on a cold cache, nine on a warm one. The half of the changelog check that asks
  whether THIS branch adds an entry needs the pull request's base commit, and the comment
  says only CI can answer it. **This was the one call in the item**: the alternative was
  to weaken the sentence in the Makefile, in CLAUDE.md and in `docs/design/test-speed/PLAN.md`.
  Making the target true is the reversible half — the target is a convenience, nothing
  gates on it, and a `make test-quick` that predicts the light gate is the only version
  worth having.

## Validation contract

1. When a package's tests actually executed, its row says nothing about caching, whatever
   any test logged.
2. When Go really reused a cached result, the row still says `"cached": true`.
3. When the stream ends mid-line, a report is still written, lists every package that
   started and never finished, says `"truncated": true`, and the command exits 2 with
   `test-report: the go test stream ended mid-line; the run did not finish`.
4. An empty stream, and a complete line that is not JSON, are still refused with no
   report and exit 2.
5. Packages that did not finish are named on stderr, not only inside the JSON.
6. After `make test-report` with the default `REPORT`, `git status` shows nothing new.
7. A `kill -9` on `scripts/test-report.sh` leaves no heartbeat alive past one interval.
8. `make test-quick` runs every deterministic step the light gate runs, and its own text
   says which.

Unchanged on purpose: `make test`, `make test-focus`, `make check`, the known-red ledger
and how it is read; the report's existing field names and slowest-first ordering; the
strict refusal of empty and malformed streams; the `rm -f` in `scripts/test-report.sh`,
because an older report must never masquerade as this run's evidence.

## Gates

All run in this branch's worktree with `GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false`, after the rebase onto
`dev`:

```
go build ./...                                          exit=0
go vet ./...                                            exit=0
make fmt-check                                          exit=0
make test-packed-manual                                 ok  …/internal/manual  exit=0
git diff --exit-code (packed corpora)                   exit=0
go test ./internal/manual/                              ok  …/internal/manual  exit=0
go test -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/  ok  …/tui3  ok  …/session  exit=0
make test-laws                                          laws: 60 files in 17 packages  exit=0
go run ./cmd/aforge-changes check                       371 entries, all well formed  exit=0
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/ci/            ok  …/internal/ci  11.295s
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/ci/testreport/ ok  …/internal/ci/testreport  0.002s
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/ci/cmd/testreport/   exit=0
make build                                              exit=0
```

## Driven by hand, on the real doors

`make test-report` with the default REPORT, then `git status --short`, then
`git check-ignore`:

```
test-report: wrote test-report.json; 8 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
git status --short:   (only this branch's own edits; no test-report.json)
git check-ignore -v test-report.json
.gitignore:21:/test-report.json	test-report.json
```

The two-file module, run and then re-run so Go really caches it:

```
fresh run  : "packages":[{"name":"cf","action":"pass","seconds":0.002}]
cached run : "packages":[{"name":"cf","action":"pass","seconds":0,"cached":true}]
```

The same stream cut at 900 bytes, over a report that already existed:

```
test-report: wrote …/cut2.json; 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
test-report: packages that did not finish:
  cf
test-report: slowest completed tests:
  0.000s cf TestOne
test-report: the go test stream ended mid-line; the run did not finish
exit=2
{"schema":2,…,"incomplete_packages":["cf"],"truncated":true,"packages":[],"tests":[{"package":"cf","name":"TestOne","action":"pass","seconds":0}]}
```

An empty stream, unchanged:

```
test-report: go test produced no JSON events
exit=2
ls: cannot access '…/never3.json': No such file or directory
```

A real sixty-five-second run at the DEFAULT thirty-second interval, so the liveness check
is proved not to have broken the cadence:

```
test-report: still running (30s)
test-report: still running (60s)
test-report: go test produced no JSON events
```

and after `kill -9` on the script, with the interval at one second:

```
heartbeats before the kill: 1
heartbeats 5s after kill -9: 1 -> 1
surviving heartbeat processes: 0
```

`make -n test-quick`, which is what the new test asserts:

```
go build ./...
go vet ./...
…gofmt…
go run ./cmd/aforge-changes check
go test ./internal/manual/
go test -run 'Manual' ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/
./scripts/laws.sh
```

And `bin/aforge` from this tree still opens — the Makefile changed, so the binary was
driven in tmux at 150x42: the setup page, then Escape, then

```
   Home      [Untitled] ×   +
                                     aforge
                                     What would you like to work on?
aforge · deepseek-v4-flash-latest              crew balanced · YOLO · idle
```

## Left alone, and why

Three cosmetic things sit in the same area of #658 and are not touched here, so this
change stays one defect wide:

- `make test-focus PKGS=./internal/tui3 RUN='^TestEveryLockInTheGuardedTreeUnlocksFromADefer$'`
  runs `-run '^X$' -skip '^(X)$'` on a known-red test and prints `ok … [no tests to run]`
  with exit 0. A green that ran nothing is its own defect and wants its own ruling about
  whether a focused run may reach past the ledger.
- `drive`'s two settle guards in `internal/tui3` fail with the identical string
  `the surface did not settle`, and the newer wait guard is wall-clock bounded at about
  seventy-five seconds where the old step guard failed in milliseconds.
- `CLAUDE.md` and the Makefile quote the pre-change 563-second `internal/tui3` baseline
  as current guidance. Correcting it needs a fresh uncached measurement on the
  constrained-runner caps, which this change has no business making up.

body:
## What was true

The tasks place has counted two different partitions of the same rows since conversations
became its structure. The sections file a conversation and everything under it under where
the CONVERSATION stands — its most urgent member's answer — while the foot counts what each
piece of work IS. The heading standing between them claimed to reconcile the two, and could
not: it stated a per-section TOTAL in the foot's own words.

On `make demo-home`, `alt+2`, at `dev@c85e10a1`:

```
tasks · 14 chats · 16 subtasks · $3.32

your call · 2 of 10 shown
› ▾ Sweeping the Frame Budget
    ▸  Measure the frame budget in every package that draws a…   holds 3 more · 55m · 1 file
  ▾ The Tab Bar's Counts
    ▸  Count the tabs the bar draws                              holds 3 more · 2h · 3 files
…
 1 your call · 1 running · 2 waiting · 9 finished today · 3 earlier
```

`10` and `1` for the same two words, one frame apart. `tasksSectionHead`'s own comment said
"Open the fold and the numbers agree by themselves"; they cannot, because the difference is
mostly the filing and only partly the fold. Three things drifted with it in #653:

- `internal/manual/chat/tasks.md` documented the opening heading as
  `tasks · 148 pieces of work since aug 11 · $34.10`. That branch is taken only when the
  page holds NO conversation at all — the form every ordinary machine draws,
  `tasks · 15 chats · 13 subtasks · $2.98`, was nowhere on the page.
- The manual explained the foot/heading difference as folds alone, which is the same false
  claim in prose.
- `railGroupWords` became `{needs you, running, queued, waiting, done}`, and the ALL-CAPS
  law above `app.roomKinWord` still read "AND THAT ONE WORD IS `parked` AND NOT `queued`" —
  a word the table no longer has, forbidding the word that is now its neighbour's. Four
  manual passages still taught the retired roster words, and the roster footer was quoted as
  `1 need you · 3 running` / `148 parked · 12 done` where the code builds
  `3 running · 1 needs you` / `148 waiting · 12 done`.

## What is true now

The foot keeps its basis. That is deliberate and it is the one thing this change refuses to
touch: a conversation stopped on a question with three workers out must not read
`4 your call`, which is the defect #653 fixed at the row level.

What goes is the claim that the two partitions are one number. A section heading now says
only what its folds are holding back — `your call · 8 folded away` — and says nothing when
they hold nothing, which is the emptiness law applied to a fact that has stopped being one.
The comments that told the next reader the heading reconciled the foot with the rows say
what is actually true instead, and the manual gains the section a person searching *why does
the count at the bottom not match the rows* can reach: the foot counts what each piece of
work is, the sections file work with its conversation, so a `✓` row can sit under `waiting`
and the foot can name a state the page draws no heading for. Each row still says what it is
with its own mark and its own words.

## Validation contract

- **C1** — a section heading never states a total a person can read as the foot's number for
  the same word. It is the section word alone, or the word and what its folds hide.
- **C2** — where a fold is holding rows back the heading says exactly how many, and that
  number is the work the laid-out page really withheld; opening every fold makes it go.
- **C3** — where nothing is behind a fold the heading is the section word alone.
- **C4** — the foot still counts what each piece of work IS: a conversation asking its own
  question with three workers out still reads `1 your call · 3 running · 1 waiting ·
  1 finished today`, and every row keeps its own mark.
- **C5** — both of the page's opening headings are quoted in the manual, exactly as the code
  spells them.
- **C6** — the manual says why the foot can name a section the page did not draw.
- **C7** — a child blocked behind its own parent wears the roster's `waiting` and never its
  `queued`, and the law above that code names both words as the table spells them today.
- **C8** — every roster group word the manual quotes is the word the table spells, in the
  footer's own order.

Not changed, on purpose: `tally()`'s basis and arithmetic, `tasksTreeOf`'s filing, any row's
mark or words, the opening heading's own arithmetic, and the family column — the four cells
in front of a work row on an attributed page are the indent under its conversation row,
which is the tree and not emptiness, so
`TestAnUnattributedPageWithNoFamiliesDrawsNoFamilyColumn` stands as it is.

Fixes #727

## Gates

```
go build ./...                                      exit 0, no output
go vet ./...                                        exit 0, no output
make fmt-check                                      exit 0, no output
make test-packed-manual                             ok  internal/manual  1.416s
make test-laws                                      ok  internal/tui3 10.425s (last of 20 packages, none red)
make test PKGS=./internal/tui3 TEST_FLAGS=-count=1  ok  internal/tui3  416.718s
go test -count=1 ./internal/manual/                 ok  internal/manual  1.345s
go test -count=1 -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/
                                                    ok  internal/tui3 0.205s · ok internal/session 0.253s
```

The manual pins were checked by breaking them on purpose: with the footer example left in
its old order the run says
`the chat manual does not quote the roster footer "3 running · 1 needs you" in the table's own words`.

## Driven in tmux, against `bin/aforge` and a `make demo-home` home

Opening `alt+2` on the same fixture, on this branch:

```
your call · 8 folded away
```

`→` on the first folded family — three rows arrive, the foot does not move:

```
your call · 5 folded away
 1 your call · 1 running · 2 waiting · 7 finished today · 5 earlier
```

`→` on the next two, then the last:

```
your call · 1 folded away
your call
 1 your call · 1 running · 2 waiting · 7 finished today · 5 earlier
```

The heading is the word alone the moment nothing is behind a fold, the foot never moved
through any of it, and `grep -c ' shown'` over the whole captured frame answers `0` — the
retired clause is nowhere on the surface.

## The owner decision this does not make

There are two defensible bases for the foot and this change keeps the one that is already
tested. If the foot should instead count the page's own partition — every word on it naming
a heading actually drawn — that is `tally()` reading `tree.filed` rather than `item.section`,
about four lines, and `TestTheRunningCountSurvivesAConversationsQuestion` is the test that
would have to move with it. It is not made here because that test states an owner's decision
about not turning a conversation's finished siblings into more decisions for a person.

Also looked at and left alone: the QA note that an attributed page with no families spends
four cells of every work row on nothing. It does not — those cells are the indent under the
conversation row above them, and removing them would put a conversation's work at the same
column as its title.

Lane S2 of the questions wave. Builds the **room form** from `docs/design/questions/DESIGN.md` on top of lane E1's `session.Question` (#712).

## What lands

**The page** (`internal/tui3/questionroom.go`) — a view over the conversation in the task-room idiom. Head with the amber `?`, the four attribution facts (`asked by · why now · what waits on it · what goes on without it`), answers as `▸`/`▾` sections opening on the asker's pick with its reason, confidence and `would switch if…`, and a foot pinned above the box exactly where every other question on this surface sits.

It is **never modal**: the turn keeps streaming, the box stays live, a bare letter is an answer only over an empty box, `esc` is *later* and restores the conversation with its scroll untouched. The settle guard drops the first 250ms of keys.

**`x` compare** (`questioncompare.go`) — the asker's `Dimensions` as a table, **differences only**, with the fallback deriving rows from the `+`/`−` consequence lines askers actually write. Stacks under 80 columns. Not offered at all where there is nothing to compare.

**`c` comment · `?` ask back** — a note under the part it was pressed on in the person's ink led by `›`; one exchange per answer sent through the ordinary turn with the question still open, the reply drawn in place with `↳` and read **live** off the transcript rather than frozen on the first frame. Both ride the answer into the record.

**`d` you decide** shows the pick and the asker's reason before the second press hands over, and records `DecidedBy: asker`. **`n`** returns `Answer.Reframe`.

**The four input shapes** (`questioninput.go`) — blanks as a sentence with holes validated by their kinds, a checklist that ticks/suggests/orders, pairs whose third answer is `=` (it does not matter), and a dial with a sentence under it saying what the setting does — drawn as a number on the reader tier.

**Six block kinds** (`questionblocks.go`) — text, diagram (never reflowed), table, diff (the diff glyphs and tokens), image (reuses `app.pictureRowsFor`; path + `o open` where it cannot paint), layout (two panes above 100 cols, stacked below).

**The key table** (`questionkeys.go`) — DESIGN.md's `ONE KEY GRAMMAR` spelled once, read by the offer row and filtered by the emptiness law. Lane S1 should import this rather than write a second one.

## Beyond the lane, and why

- **`internal/remote` gains `ResolveQuestion`** — one wire frame carrying `session.Answer` whole, with the optional-door pattern the task and sub-harness frames already use. Every local chat window holds a `*remote.Agent`; without this the page could be read and answered nowhere. Found by running the real binary.
- **`tokens.GReplyIn` (`↳`)** — a new prompt slot, geometry, one cell under both rulers, with the icons DESIGN.md table updated in the same change.
- **`welcomeFits`** returns false under the page, or the greeting is drawn through it.

## Manual

`internal/manual/chat/questions.md` gains ten sections and loses the denial that said no such page existed. Nine new probes; `task-rooms-after-restart.md` got the asker's own words back into one heading so `it says aforge is deciding` still reaches it.

## Verified

`go test ./internal/tui3/ -count=1 -timeout 15m` (419s), `./internal/remote/`, `./internal/manual/`, `./internal/tui2/tokens/`, `make test-laws`, `make test-quick`, `go vet ./...` — all green. Thirteen screens captured from `bin/aforge` in tmux against `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` and rendered to PNG (`screens/`, not committed): reading, compare wide + narrow, comment + a live ask-back reply, composing, you decide, blanks, checklist, pairs, dial, layout wide + narrow.

Two bugs were found by **looking at the screens**, not by the tests: the page ate the first two letters of every comment (`c` then `only…` lost the `o` to the fold and the `n` to the reframe), and an ask-back reply froze on `↳ Let me` because it was snapshotted out of a still-streaming entry. Both are fixed and pinned.

## Owed

- `D` (decide this kind from now on) says it is not built. The dial lives in lane E2's `autonomy.json`.
- `AnswerOption` has no `Suggested bool`, so `a` on a checklist takes the pick and whatever is marked `Safe` — the closest honest reading of the object as it stands.
- `internal/tui3/questiondemo.go` is a fixture door (`AFORGE_QUESTION_DEMO`) in the spirit of `make demo-home`, so the page could be looked at before anything raises a real room-form question. It goes when E2's `ask` tool and S1's cards land.

A plain `aforge` in a workspace whose engine was already holding conversations could be refused **by that engine** — about a journal the engine itself had the flock on:

```
~/.aforge/v3/hosts/<hash>/host.log
connection: engine: this conversation is open in another window — open aforge here and press enter on it to move it here, or run aforge engine --stop --workspace … to let go of it
```

The window then fell back onto the **in-process** road with a brand-new conversation, where `tui3.Options.EngineAnswers` is nil — so the instant move from home (#691) was unavailable and `enter` on the held row took the two-enter asking road that a daemon never answers.

### Why

The key a nameless hello resolved to was the **empty string** (`engine.go`'s `Key`). That worked exactly as long as the `""` slot held the workspace's latest. Once its conversation ended — moved to another window, left behind by `/new`, retired by the idle sweep — while the host went on holding another, the next plain hello found nothing under `""`, booted, and the boot resolved this workspace's latest… which is the journal this very process had the flock on.

### What this does

**1. The host never collides with itself.** `engineHelloKey` resolves a hello that names no session to a **transcript path**, using `v3LatestTranscript` — the same resume order the boot applies, through one shared `v3PickFolder`, and touching nothing on disk. The host consults its map and `openLocked` before it boots, and nothing is filed under `""` any more; the empty key is an *alias resolved at lookup*, never an identity.

**2. A host refusal never pushes the window in-process.** When the engine answers an `ErrSessionLocked`-shaped refusal for the conversation it was asked for, the launch **stays on the engine road**: it asks again with `Hello.New` and lands on home with the held row armed — the same landing `v3TakeOverInstead` gives, and a better one, because `EngineAnswers` is wired. The genuine fallbacks (host unreachable, wrong wire version, onboarding, `--once`, `--debug`, `--no-host`) are untouched.

**3. The sentence names the right workspace.** For an OWNED conversation `session.Config.Workspace` is that session's own `work/` folder under `~/.aforge/v3/projects`, so `aforge engine --stop --workspace X` pointed at a host that does not exist. `v3Launch` carries the project separately, and a structural test keeps every `openV3Agent` call off `.Workspace`. No person-facing string changed spelling.

### Verified in a real terminal

Scratch `AFORGE_HOME`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, two tmux shells, both builds:

| | dev (df3153e5b) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain launch beside an engine holding the latest | `host.log`: `connection: engine: this conversation is open in another window…`; window falls in-process, its own home row reads **`open in another window`** | sits straight down in the held conversation; the other window says **`moved to another window · enter on home brings it back`**; host log empty |
| plain launch beside a `--no-host` window genuinely holding the journal | own row **`open in another window`** (in-process) | own row **`open in the engine`**, held row armed |

### Tests

- `internal/enginehost`: a plain hello after the nameless slot's conversation ended joins the one the host still holds, with no second boot, and nothing filed under `""`. (Fails on dev with `a conversation is filed under the empty string`.)
- `cmd/aforge`: a plain hello keys to exactly the journal the boot would open (and to the empty folder a boot just minted); a named hello keys to the boot's spelling; the refusal is recognised after a trip over the socket and keeps the engine road, while an answered engine, an unreachable one and `--once` keep the road they had; a structural law over every `openV3Agent` call site.
- Manual: `home.md`, `keeping-an-eye.md`, `sessions-and-rewind.md` say what is true now, plus two probes in the asker's own words.

Green locally: `go vet ./...`, `make test-laws`, `cmd/aforge`, `internal/enginehost`, `internal/remote`, `internal/session`, `internal/manual`, `internal/tui3`.

The **block half** of `docs/design/questions/DESIGN.md`. Lane E1 (#712) landed the
object — `session.Question`, `ResolveQuestion`, `OpenQuestions`, `WatchQuestions` —
with no surface change. This is the surface.

## What is here

**`internal/tui3/question.go`** — the ONE renderer, fed by the engine's standing
question subscription and answering through its one door. Three forms, drawn
exactly as the file's header states them:

```
  ╰─▶ bash rm -rf build
? allow this? [1] allow once · [2] always · [3] deny · [esc] later
  bash pattern "rm -rf *"
  2 more
```

```
? wants to start a task: rewrite the packer
  it will run on its own branch · aforge
    1  start it   on a branch of its own
  ▸ 2  not now    nothing runs
  [enter] take the pick · [esc] later · [d] you decide · start it in 9s
```

```
✓ renamed 12 files under src/ · [esc] later · [c] change · [u] undo
```

**`internal/tui3/questionkeys.go`** — the ONE key table, read by the renderer, by
the manual page, and by lane S2's room. A narrow row gives its keys up by RANK
rather than by position, because dropping from the end took `[r] make it a rule
for everywhere` off a hundred-column row to keep `[c] change`, which a person
reaches by simply typing.

## The laws this enforces

- **`esc` is LATER.** The rows fold to the chip, nothing is cancelled, the turn
  stays paused on the question and the count does not drop. That is what retires
  the consent block's *"IT SUSPENDS THE KEYBOARD"* for everything on the block:
  the block takes only the keys it draws, letters are the question's only over an
  empty box, and words typed under a blocking question are the answer.
- **The settle guard.** A key pressed inside 250ms of a question appearing is
  dropped, never applied late to the wrong question.
- **The box is never moved under a hand.** A question arriving on a half-typed
  sentence is open and counted and takes no rows until the box is clear or the
  hands have been still for three seconds.
- **The answer is the record.** The receipt is built from
  `session.DecisionRecord.Line`, so the line above the box and the line in
  `decisions.jsonl` are one sentence.
- **Withdrawn, with a reason**, once, dim, never called cancelled.
- **Rules are offered, visible, forgettable** — the third same-shaped yes, with
  its scope written on the key before it is pressed.

## The chip

`? N questions · alt+a`, amber, on the status row, reachable from every page.
`alt+a` is free in this surface's whole key table and **verified in tmux** —
`› xy` after `M-a` with nothing open, no stray character. `ctrl+?` is DEL in most
terminals and was never a candidate.

## Three lanes get a surface for the first time

A running sub-harness's own question, an adaptive run at its fuel gate, and a
ground-shift conflict each had a resolver and nothing anywhere that drew them.
`app.questionDrawnHere` is the one place that says which lanes have moved, with
a test so it cannot rot.

## Audit finding 1

`switcher.go`'s answer strip took its keys off the option's POSITION, drawing `y`
on whatever answer came first — which on the consent lane, whose answers are
`1 allow once · 2 always · 3 deny`, put a **widening approval under the key a
person presses for yes**. It reads `AnswerOption.Key` now. The two tests that
pinned the old shape are rewritten to pin the new one.

## Also

`internal/tui2/tokens` gains `GWithdrawn` (`⊘`, `nf-fa-ban`, tertiary and never
amber — nobody is being waited on by a question that has been taken back), added
through the vocabulary's one door with its provenance pinned.

## What is owed

Named in full in the lane report. In short: the consent block, the task-proposal
clock, the standing card, the harness card, the takeover confirm and the stop and
tab-close cards are **not** migrated in this PR — each is a block with its own
laws and its own test surface, and moving them half-way would have put one
decision on the screen twice. The manual page says so rather than claiming the
new grammar reaches them.

## Verified

`go test ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/tui2/tokens/ ./internal/manual/ ./internal/session/`
green; `make test-laws` green; `go vet ./...` clean. Twenty-two new tests in
`question_test.go`, one screen per form captured through the real renderer and
looked at.

body:
Lane S3 of the questions wave (`docs/design/questions/DESIGN.md`). Where a question is
seen and answered away from the conversation that raised it, and when it arrives.
Builds on #712 (the object) and #734 (the block).

## What changed

**One delivery rule** — `internal/tui3/questiondelivery.go`. Presence, the away boundary,
the boundary batch and the bell are decided in one place and read by the block, by home,
by the notification and by the terminal, so "away" and "blocking" cannot mean four things.
On the page it pins; on any other page of this window it pins and one dim row says
`<head> · waiting in this conversation · alt+a`; with nobody at this keyboard for ten
minutes the project's rule takes what it may (recorded as decided by the dial) and
everything else goes to home, the desktop notification and — once, for a blocking
question only — the bell.

**The sheet** — `internal/tui3/questionsheet.go`. Quiet questions raised inside one step
arrive together at its end, grouped by the kind of decision, each row wearing its own
answers. `1`–`9` answer the focused row in that question's own keys and walk on, `enter`
takes a row out onto the block, `s` sends what is answered and delegates the rest to
their own picks, `g` gives the last answer to every row of that shape that offers the
same key, `esc` puts the whole thing off without dropping the count.

**`/autonomy`** — the project's rules per question kind, through the engine's door.
`D` on a question now writes the rule its own word promises instead of answering exactly
one question, and a row a rule is about to take wears `· your rule` beside its countdown.
Confirmation and clarification are refused a clock at the engine's door, on the write
**and** on the read.

**First answer wins, drawn.** A window that learns somebody else answered writes
`another window` on the receipt rather than `you` (`session.DecidedByWindow`), and two
answers inside a second leave both lines with `two windows answered that · the first one
is the decision` — nothing merged.

**Home answers every lane.** It looked the key up in three lanes it knew and dropped the
rest; it now looks it up in that question's own options and goes through
`Agent.ResolveQuestion`.

## Four things a real run against `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` found

1. **A batching deadlock.** The `ask` tool blocks its own turn, so a question held for
   "the model speaking again" was held behind a boundary that could not arrive. The hold
   is bounded by three seconds and fires on whichever comes first.
2. **The sheet was unanswerable.** `enter` took the row *out*, so `✓`, `s`'s count and `g`
   were all unreachable. Rows are answered in place now.
3. **`session.QuestionAsk` reached no surface at all** — every `ask` call stopped the turn
   on a question no window in the product could show.
4. **`Agent.AskQuestion` banked the word book and not the presence row**, so home drew a
   conversation with three questions waiting on it as `working`.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/tui3/ -count=1 -timeout 15m` — green (424s)
- `go test ./internal/session/ -count=1` — green (193s)
- `go test ./internal/manual/ ./internal/tui2/tokens/ ./internal/e2e/ -count=1` — green
- `make test-laws`, `go vet ./...`, `make changelog-check`, `make build` — green
- Driven in tmux against `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`: the model's own `ask` calls raise
  a sheet, it is answered in place, `g` spreads an answer, `s` sends, and the model
  reports receiving them. `/autonomy` reads, writes, reads back and prints the engine's
  refusal of `confirmation decide`.
- Screens looked at: `screens/autonomy.png`, `screens/sheet.png`,
  `screens/sheet-one-answered.png`.

## Owed

Answering over `--host` (`ResolveQuestion` is not on the wire, so a hosted window draws
no engine question rather than one nobody can resolve — the manual says so); the harness
room's foot from the object (that lane's object carries `run it`/`not now`, not
`save it`/`drop it`, so sourcing the chords from it today would be wrong); the task
room's foot (its files belong to the task-states lane); captures for home, the withdrawn
line and the away note; and DESIGN.md's five numbers.

Two `make build` runs on one commit made two engines out of one program.

`buildinfo.Identity()` was `revision/dirty/builtAt`, and `builtAt` is the second
the linker ran (`BUILD_AT := $(shell date -u …)`). `clearStaleEngineHost` compares
that string for equality against the engine already holding the workspace, and
`HostSelf.Busy` is "a surface attached, a turn running, or a question waiting" —
so with any window open, every window opened after a rebuild read a line about an
older aforge that was this same commit. Verified live on `dev@c85e10a19`, two
builds thirteen seconds apart:

```
$ /tmp/one version
aforge c85e10a19 built 2026-09-09 17:09 · go1.26.5 linux/amd64
$ ./bin/aforge version
aforge c85e10a19 built 2026-09-09 17:09 · go1.26.5 linux/amd64

daemon whois: {"version":12,"build":"c85e10a19/false/2026-09-09T21:09:01Z","busy":true}
this window:                    c85e10a19/false/2026-09-09T21:09:14Z
```

**What is true now.** A build that can name its source — a revision from an
unmodified tree — is that source and nothing else, so a rebuild of one commit is
one engine and a window from either binary attaches to it without a word. A build
that cannot name its source — a modified tree, or no stamp at all — keeps the
moment it was made, because that is the only thing left that tells one rebuild
from the next and somebody rebuilding what they just edited must still get a new
engine. The tree had already reached this answer once, for the news channel, in
`buildStamp` in `internal/tui3/notice.go`.

Nothing a person reads changed wording, and no sentence stopped firing for the
case it was written for.

Fixes #730

## Validation contract

- Two builds of one commit from an unmodified tree are one engine: a window from
  either binary attaches to the engine the other started, with no sentence.
- Another commit is still another engine: idle, it is replaced without a word;
  busy on this wire, it is joined and the `an older aforge and is still holding
  work … it picks up this build the moment it goes quiet` line is said; busy on
  another wire it is still refused with `run aforge engine --stop on <machine>`,
  and its work is not ended.
- A rebuild from a modified tree is still another engine.
- A build with no revision at all is never called the same engine as another such
  build made at a different moment.
- A host that answers with an empty build stamp, or one too old to answer at all,
  is treated exactly as before.
- `aforge version` and every displayed build stamp keep today's wording and
  precision — `buildinfo.String()` is untouched.
- Unchanged: the two sentences' wording, the protocol-version refusal, the whois
  frame's shape, and a host retiring itself when the file it was started from is
  replaced and it is holding nothing.

## Manual test — the real door, in tmux

Two binaries of one commit; a window open on a workspace (which is what makes the
engine busy); a second window opened from the other binary in the same folder.

Before, on `dev@c85e10a19` (both binaries `aforge c85e10a19 built 2026-09-09 17:09`):

```
· another window is on this conversation — typing is here now · the engine on Abir is an older aforge and is still holding work — it picks up this
build the moment it goes quiet
```

After, on this branch (both binaries `aforge 5887dfa97 built 2026-09-09 17:27`,
linked 31 seconds apart):

```
· another window is on this conversation — typing is here now
```

`grep -c 'older aforge'` over the after frame: `0`.

Control, same run with the engine started from the earlier commit's binary
(`c85e10a19`) and the window from this branch — the line is still said, and the
engine keeps its work:

```
· another window is on this conversation — typing is here now · the engine on Abir is an older aforge and is still holding work — it picks up this
build the moment it goes quiet
```

## Gates

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go build ./...` | ok |
| `go vet ./...` | ok |
| `make fmt-check` | exit 0 |
| `make test-packed-manual` | `ok github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/manual 1.403s` |
| `make test-laws` | exit 0 (every law package ok) |
| `go test -count=1 ./internal/buildinfo/` | `ok … 0.003s` |
| `go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./cmd/aforge/` | `ok … 58.770s` |
| `go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/remote/` | `ok … 21.151s` |
| `go test -count=1 ./internal/enginehost/` | `ok … 13.491s` |
| `go test -count=1 ./internal/manual/` | `ok … 1.368s` |
| `go test -count=1 -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/` | `ok … 0.175s` / `ok … 0.272s` |
| `make build` | writes `bin/aforge`; both manual-test binaries came from it |

`make check` was not run end to end: its last step is the binary-size ratchet,
which is red on `dev` for everybody right now (#724).

## Notes for the reviewer

- The door's yardstick is a parameter one layer down (`clearStaleEngineHostFor`)
  because the law needs two builds of one source and a test binary is only ever
  linked once. The public shape and both call sites are unchanged.
- The *Three things can be true* bullets on the manual page still describe the
  same-wire busy host as refused, which stopped being true in #691. That drift
  belongs to #722 and is deliberately left alone here.
