body:
Fixes #719.

## What was true

Every step caption was cut at the first `.` in the line, whichever token that dot
belonged to. `captionSentences` walked the line and treated every `.`, `!` and `?` as a
sentence end with no guard for a terminator sitting between two non-space characters.

Worse than a short caption: the fragment left in front of the dot is usually a word or
two, and `shortCaption` passes over any sentence under three words — so the caption a
person read often began *after* the dot, in the middle of a word.

On `dev`, through the exact function the live step row draws with:

```
"Reading livesteps.go now."                            -> "Reading livesteps"
"I will update config.json and then run the suite."    -> "I will update config"
"Bumping the pin to v1.2.3 across the three services." -> "Bumping the pin to v1"
"searching ~/.aforge/v3/projects for the transcript"   -> "aforge/v3/projects for the transcript"
```

The splitter existed **twice**, byte for byte — `internal/tui3/caption.go` and
`internal/session/caption.go` — which is why one defect had to be found in two places.

## What is true now

A `.`, `!` or `?` closes a sentence only when what follows it, past any closing quote or
bracket, is a space, a tab, a newline, or the end of the line. Every other dot belongs to
the token it sits in. The same four lines:

```
"Reading livesteps.go now."                            -> "Reading livesteps.go now"
"I will update config.json and then run the suite."    -> "I will update config.json and then run the suite"
"Bumping the pin to v1.2.3 across the three services." -> "Bumping the pin to v1.2.3 across the three services"
"searching ~/.aforge/v3/projects for the transcript"   -> "searching ~/.aforge/v3/projects for the transcript"
```

And the rule stops being two rules: `session.ShortCaption` is now the single home of it,
and `internal/tui3` calls it.

## Validation contract

The tests were written from this, before the fix, and they were red for it.

1. A caption naming a file keeps the extension — `Reading livesteps.go now.` draws
   `Reading livesteps.go now`.
2. A dotted token mid-sentence does not end the sentence — `I will update config.json and
   then run the suite.` draws whole.
3. A version number keeps its parts — `v1.2.3` is not `v1`.
4. A dot inside a path with no sentence end at all leaves the whole line, and a caption
   never begins mid-token.
5. A real sentence boundary still ends a caption: `Good leads. Fetching the key pages to
   confirm which are open.` still draws `Fetching the key pages to confirm which are
   open`. A newline still ends one. `?` and `!` at a real sentence end still do.
6. The length cap still holds at ten words, still with trailing glue words dropped and
   still with no ellipsis.
7. Both doors answer identically — the narrator's `cleanCaption` and the surface's
   `captionWords`.
8. Unchanged on purpose: the under-three-words fallback, `captionSpan`'s whole-line
   consumption rule, `captionWordMax` at 10, and `captionTrimDangling`'s word list.

## Gates

Every command below was run in this worktree; `bin/aforge` is the binary from `make build`
here.

```
go build ./...                                              (no output)
go vet ./...                                                (no output)
make fmt-check                                              (no output)
make test-packed-manual        ok  …/internal/manual   1.378s
make test-laws                 ok across 60 law files in 17 packages
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/tui3/     ok  …/internal/tui3     426.337s
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/session/  ok  …/internal/session  231.732s
go test ./internal/manual/                         ok  …/internal/manual
go test -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/   ok / ok
make build                     -> bin/aforge
```

Re-run after the rebase onto `dev@c85e10a19`:

```
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/session/  ok  …/internal/session  227.569s
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/tui3/     ok  …/internal/tui3     417.699s
```

One note in the interest of not overclaiming: on a first post-rebase pass I ran both
suites *concurrently* on this box and `TestAClosedCorrectionSurvivesRestartWithoutRestoringPlainDrafts/close_kept`
failed with `no send crossed`, alongside `tui3: 1777 goroutines still parked`. It passes
in isolation on this branch (2.926s) and on `dev@c85e10a19` untouched (2.925s), and the
full tui3 suite run on its own is green above. It is a load shape, not this change, and
it is not in `.github/known-red.txt` — no line was added there.

## Driven in a terminal, not just in a test

Real binary, tmux, DeepSeek V4 Flash, a scratch home and a two-file scratch workspace.
Same prompt, same model, same workspace on both sides — the model was asked to write
`Reading notes.txt in /tmp/w-B22 now.` before its tool call, then read the file.

**Before** (`dev@475a48473`), `ctrl+e` on the finished turn:

```
    ▾ worked 5.3s · thought 0.7s · 1 tool call · ctrl+e
    ▸ txt in /tmp/w-B22 now                                                     1 call
```

The caption begins in the middle of `notes.txt`.

**After** (this branch):

```
    ▾ worked 8.7s · thought 0.6s · 1 tool call · ctrl+e
    ▸ Reading notes.txt in /tmp/w-B22 now                                       1 call
```

A second pair on a two-step turn, where the model narrated each step itself. Before, the
`.txt` was gone:

```
    ▸ I'm about to open /tmp/w-B22/notes                                        1 call
```

After, both steps keep their filenames:

```
    ▸ step one: reading /tmp/w-B22/config.json                                  1 call
    ▸ step two: reading /tmp/w-B22/notes.txt                                    1 call
```

## The manual

`internal/manual/chat/reading-a-task-page.md` promised only that a caption is never cut
with an ellipsis — true, and beside the point, since it was being cut at the first dot
instead. It now says what a person can rely on: a caption ends where its sentence ends,
so a filename, a version number or a path keeps its whole self, and a caption never
begins in the middle of a word.

`internal/session/prompts/system.md` promises nothing about captions and is untouched.

## What was true

`make check` — the end-of-change ritual `CLAUDE.md` sends everybody to — stopped
at its last step on `dev`, for every change, whatever that change touched:

```
bin/aforge is 55542025 bytes. The budget in SIZE-BUDGET is 54600000. Over by 942025.
```

Nobody caused it and nobody could clear it from inside their own work. `#624`
was the last merge that weighed in under the cap; by `dev@8d8cd6c8` the binary
had grown 1,908,736 bytes and crossed a number nobody moved.

## What is true now

`SIZE-BUDGET` is 57,488,000 — two percent above darwin/amd64 at 56,360,432, the
heaviest of the four platforms, which is the headroom every figure in `PERF.md`'s
size-ratchet section was given. That section gains the fifth reset in the same
commit as the number, per its own standing rule: the per-merge attribution, what
grew and what did not, and the four-platform table the figure came from.

**Nothing a person sees in the running program changes.** No manual page moves —
nothing about the running chat changed. No Go file is touched.

### The attribution (linux/amd64, Go 1.26.5, each figure a `make build`)

| merged | bytes | added |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #624, the last merge under the cap | 53,633,289 | |
| #653 | 55,234,825 | 1,601,536 |
| #658 | 55,271,689 | 36,864 |
| #673 | 55,382,281 | 110,592 |
| #689 | 55,501,065 | 118,784 |
| #721 (`8d8cd6c8`) | 55,542,025 | 40,960 |

#653 is 84% of it and crossed the cap by itself. The rest is the ordinary
accretion of twenty-odd merges, none over 120 KB.

### The shrink was looked for first, and is not there

`PERF.md` names two honest moves and the first one is unavailable:

* **No dependency was added.** The only `go.mod` change across the range moves
  `github.com/rivo/uniseg` from indirect to direct; it was already linked.
* **Nothing new is embedded unpacked.** The one embed that grew is
  `internal/manual/chat.pack.gz`, 707,105 → 782,330 — the manual learning about
  the features that landed, already gzipped, and required by the manual law.
  `internal/manual`'s raw and packed sources are behind mutually exclusive build
  tags, so the shipped binary carries the corpus once.
* **The weight is compiled first-party code.** Section by section between the two
  binaries: `.text` +1,030,464, `.gopclntab` +592,718, `.rodata` +198,176,
  `.noptrdata` +75,200, everything else under 7,000 each. The source says the
  same: +26,203 net non-test lines in `internal/tui3`, +13,011 in
  `internal/session`, +2,509 in `internal/remote`, +1,210 in `cmd/aforge`.
* **The dependencies were weighed too.** Ranked by the file bytes their symbols
  occupy: `modernc.org/sqlite` 1,807,889, `github.com/dop251/goja` 1,791,194,
  `golang.org/x/text` 1,538,848 (of which `x/text/collate` is 1,267,813, pulled
  in by goja). Each sits behind a shipped capability — the store, and the
  JavaScript a saved program is written in (`internal/jsrun`). Dropping either is
  a product decision, not a size fix, and taking **all** of goja and its
  collation tables would still leave darwin/amd64 over the old cap.

### The four platforms, each with its own furrow staged

| platform | bytes |
| --- | --- |
| linux/arm64 | 51,052,706 |
| darwin/arm64 | 52,082,226 |
| linux/amd64 | 55,542,025 |
| darwin/amd64 | 56,360,432 |

### Two lines that named the wrong platform

The refusal in `Makefile` and the informational job in `ci-full.yml` both still
said the budget was set on linux/arm64. That stopped being true at #235 — the
number has been set on darwin/amd64 since the reset that came down. The refusal
was telling whoever hit it to reset against an architecture the figure was never
taken from. Both now say darwin/amd64, and the CI comment says why that job stays
informational: linux/amd64 weighs about eight hundred kilobytes less, so a hard
compare there would pass a tree that is over the cap on the platform the cap is
measured on.

## Validation contract

1. `make check` on a clean checkout runs to the end; its last step prints
   `bin/aforge: <bytes> bytes, under the SIZE-BUDGET budget of <budget>.` and the
   `Over by` block is not printed.
2. `make build` alone is still ungated: green, and silent about bytes, on a tree
   deliberately over the cap.
3. When the binary next crosses the new cap, `make size` fails with the same
   words it fails with today. The gate is moved, never loosened.
4. `SIZE-BUDGET` still holds one integer and nothing else — `cat` of it is what
   `[ … -gt … ]` compares, so the attribution lives in `PERF.md`.
5. `## The size ratchet` in `PERF.md` accounts for the number in the same commit:
   before-and-after, what grew, and the four-platform table.
6. Where CI prints which platform the budget was set on, that is the platform it
   was set on.
7. Nothing a person sees in the running program changes: same commands, same
   strings, same capabilities, same manual.

**What must not change:** no test edited to pass, no line added to
`.github/known-red.txt`, no manual page moved, `internal/session/prompts/system.md`
untouched, the furrow embed still fetched-at-build-time and uncommitted.

Fixes #724

## Gates

Run in this worktree, `GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false`, Go 1.26.5, linux/amd64.

```
$ go build ./...                                     exit 0
$ go vet ./...                                       exit 0
$ make fmt-check                                     exit 0
$ make test-packed-manual                            exit 0, ok  internal/manual  (packed-corpus path)
$ make test-laws                                     exit 0, "laws: 60 files in 17 packages", every package ok
$ go test -count=1 ./internal/manual/                ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/manual  1.579s
$ go test -count=1 -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/
                                                     ok  .../internal/tui3  0.171s
                                                     ok  .../internal/session  0.161s
$ go test -count=1 ./internal/ci/                    ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/ci  1.073s
$ go test -count=1 ./internal/furrowbin/...          ok (the pin, the fetch, the staging)
$ make size                                          bin/aforge: 55542025 bytes, under the SIZE-BUDGET budget of 57488000.

No Go package is touched by this diff, so "touched packages" has none to run.
internal/ci (the known-red ratchet) and internal/furrowbin (the embed the
measurement depends on) were run anyway. .github/known-red.txt is unchanged.
```

## Manual test

**Contract 1 — before, on the branch's base tree:**

```
$ make size
bin/aforge is 55542025 bytes. The budget in SIZE-BUDGET is 54600000. Over by 942025.
make: *** [Makefile:244: size] Error 1
```

**Contract 1 — after, with the new number:**

```
$ make size
bin/aforge: 55542025 bytes, under the SIZE-BUDGET budget of 57488000.
```

**Contracts 2, 3 and 6 — `SIZE-BUDGET` temporarily set to `1000`, then restored:**

```
$ make build ; echo "build exit=$?"
build exit=0                      # green, and it says nothing about bytes

$ make size
bin/aforge is 55542025 bytes. The budget in SIZE-BUDGET is 1000. Over by 55541025.

Shrink what you added — pack a corpus (internal/packed), drop a
dependency, stop embedding what can be fetched — or raise the number
in SIZE-BUDGET IN THIS COMMIT, so the extra weight is a decision somebody
signed for rather than a drift nobody saw. PERF.md states the policy.

The budget is set on darwin/amd64, the heaviest of the four
platforms, with the toolchain of the day. A new Go release moves
this number on its own; that too is a reason to reset it
deliberately, never to ignore red.
```

**Contract 7 — the binary this budget weighs, driven in tmux against an isolated
home on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, a real turn:**

```
  › in one short sentence, what is aforge?

  aforge is a working colleague that helps you think, make decisions, and turn requests
  into useful results using tools and delegated work.
                                                    · 16:50 · 4.7s · $0.0014 ·

aforge · deepseek-v4-flash · via digitalocean · 2.8s      crew balanced ·  $0.0014 · 14.9k/1M · 1% · YOLO
```

and `/help` on the same run still draws its whole key table:

```
    ctrl+e         open the model's thinking, streaming or finished
    ctrl+t         a new chat start page · your draft stays put · esc back
    ctrl+w         close this tab · select the last open chat · keep your draft
    alt+t          the task roster · ↑↓ move · →← fold · enter opens · esc back
```

## Owner decision

Opened as a **draft**: 57,488,000 is a 2.9 MB rise and the ratchet exists so a
rise is somebody's signature rather than a drift. The safe reversible option is
what is implemented — the number moves, nothing is removed, and every figure it
was taken from is written down so the decision can be re-litigated against real
bytes rather than an argument.

The one lever this change deliberately does not pull is `internal/jsrun` and its
goja + collation tables, about 3.06 MB behind the JavaScript a saved program is
written in. That is a product decision about a shipped capability, it belongs to
its own change, and on its own it would not have kept darwin/amd64 under the old
cap.

body:
## What was true

`/help` still described the `ctrl+e` that existed before #653:

```
ctrl+e         open the model's thinking, streaming or finished
```

The key does something else now. The `case "end", "ctrl+e"` arm in `input.go` calls
`toggleLatestWorkfold()` first and reaches `toggleLatestThought()` only as a fallback —
and `toggleLatestWorkfold` states the law in its own comment: *"THE RUNNING TURN'S WINDOW
IS THE NEWEST CHIP THERE IS … it is asked first"*. The rows either side of it on the sheet
were all rewritten in that wave; this one was missed, and the doc comment over the arm
said the same stale thing. `internal/manual/chat/keys.md` already had the new wording, so
the sheet and the manual disagreed with each other on the same machine.

Seven manual pages stated things the build does not do. The three manual gates were green
throughout: they check that a NAME is MENTIONED, never that the sentence around it is
true, which is exactly how these pages went stale.

| Page | Said | The code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keys.md`, the switcher's `ctrl+w` row | a working row is asked `keep running` / `stop work` / `cancel` | `hopAway` routes only `row.here` through `tabDismiss`; every other row goes to `tabShutKey` with no card, and the switcher says `tab closed` |
| `running-on-another-machine.md` | `this build speaks protocol 3 and the surface speaks 4` | `internal/remote/wire.go`'s `Version` is 13; the sentence is `fmt.Sprintf`ed from it and no shipped build a person meets has ever said 3 or 4 |
| `permissions.md` | pre-approved bookkeeping is `note`, `track`, `recall`, `forget` | `v3BuiltinApprovals` seeds `remember`, `track`, `recall`; no belt has a `note` or a `forget` |
| `choosing-a-folder.md` | the pane says `more of this folder is not shown` | `folderCutWord` is declared and drawn nowhere, and `folderListing.cut` is set in three places and read in none |
| `when-the-connection-drops.md` | "My wifi died in the middle of a reply" gets the five-minute redial | that is the `--host` link policy; an ordinary local chat gets `waiting for connection` and a two-minute wait, stated four paragraphs earlier and never reached |
| `screen.md` | the strip stands down "under 12 columns wide, or on a terminal too short for a blank row above the message box" | `tabsHeight` stands down under 12 columns **or under 16 rows** — `breathingRows() < 2`, and the second blank row arrives at `airyFloor` |
| `sessions-and-rewind.md` | the full name is capped at 80 **characters**, the label at 32 | `clip` bounds BYTES on a rune boundary; a CJK name fits about 26 and 10 |

And two questions asked in a person's own words reached the wrong pages: *"how do I
preview a file before attaching it"* never returned `choosing-a-folder` — #657's headline
capability — and *"scroll the tab bar"* returned `places` three times over, because "tab
bar" belongs to the seven-places row while the chat strip is only ever a "tab strip".

Separately, `658-faster-test-feedback.md` was the only entry for #658 and named only
`make test-focus` and `make test-report`. The same commit added
`internal/tui3/harnessdriver_test.go` and rewrote `drive`/`runCmd` so waiting overlaps
inside one call. Anyone catching up through `docs/changes/unreleased/` — the use
`CLAUDE.md` prescribes — would debug the next tui3 flake against a serial harness that no
longer exists.

## What is true now

The sheet's row reads in the router's own order, and the comment over the arm names both
functions it calls. Every page above says what the code prints, quoting its strings
exactly. The two questions have their askers' words in the headings that answer them, and
ten probes in `internal/manual/chat_test.go` hold all of it. #658 has its second
`kind: changed` entry.

**No behaviour moves.** The only Go edits are one string in the help sheet, three doc
comments, and the probe table.

## Validation contract

1. `/help` in a conversation describes `ctrl+e`'s actual order — the running turn's
   compact steps first, then the newest worked chip, then the thinking — and the sentence
   `open the model's thinking, streaming or finished` appears nowhere.
2. The comment over `case "end", "ctrl+e"` names the running turn's compact steps as the
   first thing an empty-box press reaches.
3. Asked what `ctrl+w` does on the switcher card, the page says a row that is not the one
   you are in is dismissed at once with no question and the card says `tab closed`, and
   only the conversation you are in raises `keep running` / `stop work` / `cancel`.
4. The protocol-mismatch page shows the sentence's shape without pinning two version
   numbers that move with nearly every release.
5. The pre-approved bookkeeping list names `remember`, `track` and `recall`, and no page
   claims a `note` or a `forget` tool exists.
6. No page claims the folder pane prints a sentence nothing draws; the bound is stated
   instead.
7. Somebody on an ordinary local chat asking about a dropped connection is answered with
   `waiting for connection` and the two-minute wait first, with the five-minute `--host`
   redial beside it as the separate connection it is.
8. The tab strip's floors read 12 columns and 16 rows.
9. The name caps read bytes, and the page says what that costs a name not written in
   Latin letters.
10. *"how do I preview a file before attaching it"* reaches `choosing-a-folder`, and
    *"scroll the tab bar"* reaches `screen`.
11. `docs/changes/unreleased/` records the tui3 harness rewrite #658 shipped.

**Not changed:** any behaviour, any key binding, `.github/known-red.txt`, the shape and
column of the help sheet, or the rows either side of the one rewritten.

Fixes #722

## Gates

go vet ./...                                          ok (no output, rc=0)
make fmt-check                                        ok (no output, rc=0)
make changelog-check                                  docs/changes/unreleased: 366 entries, all well formed.
go test -count=1 ./internal/manual/                   ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/manual  1.346s
make test-packed-manual                               ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/manual  1.422s
go test -count=1 -run Manual ./internal/tui3/         ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/tui3    0.228s
go test -count=1 -run Manual ./internal/session/      ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/session  0.320s
go test -count=1 ./internal/e2e/                      ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/e2e     0.174s
make test-laws                                        ok  (every package; internal/tui3 10.155s, internal/session 3.284s)
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/tui3/        ok  github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/tui3    437.642s
```

## Driven in a terminal

`make build`, then the real binary under tmux at 150×45 against a fresh `HOME`, `Escape`
past setup, `/help` typed at the box.

Before, on a `dev` build:

```
    ctrl+q         hand this to the session now, to run after the current turn
    ctrl+e         open the model's thinking, streaming or finished
    ctrl+t         a new chat start page · your draft stays put · esc back
```

After, on this branch:

```
    ctrl+q         hand this to the session now, to run after the current turn
    ctrl+e         open the running turn's compact steps · the newest worked chip · or the thinking
    ctrl+t         a new chat start page · your draft stays put · esc back
```

`grep -c "open the model's thinking, streaming or finished"` over the captured frame is
`0`, and the rows either side are unchanged.

The pages were driven through the real door too — the same binary against a live model,
which reads them with the `manual` tool. Asked *"what happens if I press ctrl+w on a
different chat in the ctrl+k switcher list?"*, the chat now answers:

```
  `ctrl+w` on a different (inactive) row in the switcher closes that tab — the card stays
  open, you see `tab closed · <title>`, and you can keep putting away others in
  succession.
  …
  If you aim `ctrl+w` at a row below the fold (a conversation not open on this terminal),
  nothing happens — `that one is not open here — enter opens it`.
```

Asked *"My wifi died in the middle of a reply. This is a normal local chat, not --host.
What does aforge do?"* — the question that used to be answered with the remote redial —
it now answers:

```
  In a normal local chat, the only connection that dropped is the model request itself —
  the line between aforge and the API.

  aforge waits up to 2 minutes while the internet is gone.
```

## Out of scope, deliberately

- `folderCutWord` and `folderListing.cut` are left in place: making the folder pane say
  the bound is a behaviour change and belongs to whoever fixes that pane. The comment on
  the constant now says plainly that nothing draws it, so no page may quote it.
- `collections.md` says nothing about a locked collections database — that refusal's
  wording is still moving.
- Asked *"how do I group my chats into folders?"* without naming aforge, the chat still
  answers from its own priors without calling `manual` at all. The page is reachable and
  correct when the product is named; the trigger vocabulary lives in the prompt, not here.

body:
The namer is asked for two lines — `full:` a descriptive title, `tab:` a compact
label. #671 taught the parser to take the markdown off a line *before* it looks
for the label, which fixed bold, backtick, heading and quoted labels. Two shapes
were still unread, and both of them reach a person.

**What was true.** A markdown **list marker** survived `stripMarkup`, so the
label test never matched behind one:

- `- full: … / - tab: …` lost the tab label entirely and drew a word-clipped
  copy of the full title in the tab strip. Same for `1. `, `1) `, `+ ` and a
  bold label inside any of them.
- `- tab: … / - full: …` made the **tab label** the conversation's name and
  threw the title away.
- a one-line `- porting the parser` was journaled and drawn with the dash still
  on it — the tab read `[- porting]`.

And a label line that opened with the throat-clearing a model agrees with a
request in — `Sure! full: …`, `Okay, full: …` — never matched either, so the
whole pair was discarded, the conversation stayed `Untitled`, and the errand
paid every rung of the ladder and all three `titleAttempts` for nothing.

**What is true now.** A list marker comes off with the rest of the markup — one
marker, and only when a space separates it from the words, so `-v flag handling`
and `v1.2.3 release notes` keep every character they have. And the interjection
cut `stripOpener` already applied is a named rule both readers share, so the
label reader and the plain-name reader cannot drift apart about what `Sure,`
means. Nothing else moved: a labeled answer with no usable `full:` is still
refused, which is what leaves the conversation drawn under the person's own
opening words and the namer free to ask again.

Fixes #718

### Validation contract

1. Two labels behind a markdown list marker — `- `, `+ `, `* `, `1. `, `1) `,
   with or without bold — name the conversation exactly as the bare pair does:
   `full = agentfield star growth`, `short = star growth`.
2. The `full:` line decides the conversation's name whichever line it is on.
3. A label line that opens with an interjection still mints both names. It is
   never left unnamed.
4. A one-line answer carrying a list marker is named without it: `- porting the
   parser` mints `porting the parser`.
5. Nothing that parses today changes — the bare, UPPERCASE, bold, backtick,
   heading and quoted forms, and a legacy one-line answer.
6. A name a marker rule must not touch keeps every character: `-v flag
   handling`, `v1.2.3 release notes`, `port-b failures`, `fix: nil map crash`.
7. The refusals stay refusals: `tab: inventory`, `full:`, `full:\ntab:
   inventory`, `nothing to name`, `Untitled`, `no title`, and the instruction
   handed back.

`TestConversationNamingReadsLabelsThroughFormattingAndKeepsRealNames` is that
table, row for row; `TestAListedNamingAnswerPublishesAndReplaysBothNames` runs a
listed answer through the Agent and asserts what the **replayed session file**
carries, because the leak this is about is what gets journaled and drawn.

### Manually tested

Two real `bin/aforge` binaries — one built at `origin/dev`, one from this branch
— driven under `tmux`, each against its own isolated state root and a scripted
OpenAI-compatible endpoint behind `AFORGE_BASE_URL` (`test/remote/stub` with the
naming ask answered from a flag), so the namer's exact answer is the variable
and no key or money is involved.

The namer answers `- full: agentfield star growth` / `- tab: star growth`:

```
before   Home      [agentfield star] ×   +
         {"type":"title","title":"agentfield star growth","shortTitle":"agentfield star"}

after    Home      [star growth] ×   +
         {"type":"title","title":"agentfield star growth","shortTitle":"star growth"}
```

The namer answers the one line `- porting the parser`:

```
before   Home      [- porting] ×   +
         {"type":"title","title":"- porting the parser","shortTitle":"- porting"}

after    Home      [porting the] ×   +
         {"type":"title","title":"porting the parser","shortTitle":"porting the"}
```

The namer answers `Sure! full: agentfield star growth` / `tab: star growth`:

```
before   Home      [Untitled] ×   +
         no title line in the transcript at all; the stub was asked to name the
         conversation 3 times — the whole ladder spent

after    Home      [star growth] ×   +
         {"type":"title","title":"agentfield star growth","shortTitle":"star growth"}
         the stub was asked once
```

### Gates

Run on this branch, rebased on `dev`:

```

go vet ./...                                      (no output, exit 0)
make fmt-check                                    (no output, exit 0)

make test-packed-manual                           ok  internal/manual  1.524s
make test-laws                                    ok  … 17 packages, internal/session 3.422s
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/session/  ok  internal/session  266.330s
go test ./internal/manual/                        ok  internal/manual  1.482s
go test -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/
                                                  ok  internal/tui3  0.395s
                                                  ok  internal/session  0.807s
```

Touched packages: `internal/session`, `internal/manual`. No line was added to
`.github/known-red.txt`.

body:
Fixes #708.

## What was true

The tab strip and the `ctrl+k` switcher answered the same question twice, differently.

The strip read `behindWatch.tasking` — the watcher's fold of every task notice, running or
queued. The card built its own second answer in `hopKept`: the turn and job flags only
(`turning := held.watch.turning.Load() || held.watch.jobbing.Load()`, with `tasking`
omitted — the very flag `keeper.go`'s `noteTask` exists to keep) plus `runningTasks`, which
reads the project index and counts only nodes whose status is `running`. So a conversation
with a queued node wore `◐` on its tab and `○ … nothing new` on its row, on one frame.

`hopFront` set neither `needs` nor `moving`, so the row a person is standing on could never
wear a mark at all — the conversation the status line was calling `working` drew `○` on the
card describing it.

And an unnamed chat was called `Untitled` on its tab and in its breadcrumb root, and
`new conversation` on the card and the entry line. The constant for the second one carries a
comment saying it exists "rather than a ninth spelling of it".

## What is true now

**One reading.** `behindWatch.signal` is the whole of what a held conversation is doing —
needs a person, working, or nothing — and both the strip and the card ask it. The row in
front asks `frontSignal`, which is what its own tab is asking this instant. `hopSlide`, which
had a third reading for the row being left behind, asks the same one.

**One reading for the words too.** `hopNote` takes that signal instead of deciding a second
time, so the count refines the working word where the project index has one (`3 tasks
running`) and never contradicts it: work that index cannot count — a queued node, a
background job — says `working`. The row you are standing on keeps `you are here`.

**One spelling.** `unnamedConversationWord` is the only word for a chat with no name yet;
the tab, the breadcrumb root, the card and the entry line all draw it. `Untitled` is gone.
`main` is still the conversation as a place, and the `+` page still says `New chat`.

## Validation contract

- **C1** A held conversation with a task node running or queued wears the same mark on its
  tab and on its card row, on one frame; neither says `nothing new` while the other says
  working.
- **C2** The same for a turn in flight and for a background job with no task nodes.
- **C3** A working conversation in front wears the working mark on its own card row, and
  that row keeps `you are here`.
- **C4** Needing a person outranks working on both surfaces, held and in front.
- **C5** A conversation with nothing happening draws no mark on either surface and keeps
  `nothing new` / `it finished while you were away` / `open in another window` / `that
  folder is gone`; a conversation with no watcher claims nothing and does not panic.
- **C6** A chat with no name is spelled `new conversation` on the strip, in the breadcrumb
  root and on the card. `Untitled` is drawn nowhere.
- **C7** A conversation that has a name is never redrawn as unnamed — the namer's own, one
  somebody typed, one that arrived welded.
- **C8** The unnamed word is not the place word, and the start page keeps `New chat`.
- **Unchanged:** the strip still opens no file and crosses no wire per frame; the card may
  read the index because it is drawn on a keystroke. `hopRest` and every other note wording
  are untouched.

New tests in `internal/tui3/hopsignal_test.go` assert C1–C6 as an *equality between the two
readings* rather than a fixed expectation, so a future third state cannot slip between them.

## Gates

GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false go vet ./...                                (no output)
make fmt-check                                                      (no output)
make test-packed-manual        ok  internal/manual  1.363s
make test-laws                 laws: 58 files in 17 packages;  ok  internal/tui3  9.929s, all 17 ok
go test -count=1 -timeout 15m ./internal/tui3/     ok  internal/tui3  417.378s
go test -count=1 ./internal/manual/                ok  internal/manual  1.339s
go test -count=1 -run Manual ./internal/tui3/ ./internal/session/
                                                   ok  internal/tui3 0.179s   ok  internal/session 0.270s
make build                                          bin/aforge
```

No line was added to `.github/known-red.txt`.

## Driven in tmux, on the demo home

`make demo-home`, open **Sweeping the Frame Budget** (it ships with a queued node), `ctrl+t`,
one message, `ctrl+k`.

Before, on `dev@57940a813` — one frame, two answers per conversation and two names for one
chat:

```
   Home     ◐ Sweeping the      ◐[Untitled] ×   +   Chats ▾
      │>  1 ○ Sweeping the Frame Budget    nothing new              aforge-v2  now│
      │   2 ○ new conversation             you are here             aforge-v2  now│
aforge-v2 · deepseek-v4-flash-latest   crew balanced · 2 open · $0.00 · ⠧ working · 4s
```

After, on this branch — one frame, and every conversation described the same way twice:

```
   Home     ◐ Sweeping the        greeting exchange      ◐[new conversation] ×   +   Chats ▾
      │   open                                 3 of 12 · enter open · esc cancel · ↑↓ choose │
      │>  1 ○ greeting exchange with a friendly…nothing new                     aforge-v2  now│
      │   2 ◐ Sweeping the Frame Budget         working                         aforge-v2  now│
      │   3 ◐ new conversation                  you are here                    aforge-v2  now│
```

`Untitled` appears nowhere on that frame. The conversation at rest keeps `○` and `nothing
new`; the two that are working wear `◐` on the strip and `◐` on the card; the unnamed one is
called `new conversation` on the strip, on the card, and on the entry line's `· new
conversation · aforge-v2`.
